nodes.s: GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, QZSS, NavIC: signals, receivers, positioning.
Carrier-phase differential and precise point positioning, corrections (RTCM, SSR, NTRIP).
Acquisition, tracking, navigation-message decoding in software on SDR front-ends.
GNSS interference, spoofing simulation, detection, mitigation, monitoring, anti-jam antennas (CRPA).
Architectures that keep position, navigation and timing trustworthy under denial and deception.
Clocks, holdover, PTP/NTP, GNSS-disciplined oscillators, chip-scale atomic clocks.
Strapdown mechanization, IMU error models, calibration, dead reckoning.
Kalman filters (EKF/UKF/ESKF/IEKF), factor graphs, smoothing, multi-sensor integration.
Loosely, tightly and deeply coupled GNSS/INS.
Camera-IMU, LiDAR-IMU extrinsics, intrinsics, time offset, Allan variance.
VO/VIO from monocular, stereo, event cameras with IMU.
Mapping and localization with loop closure from cameras.
LiDAR(-inertial) odometry, scan matching, LiDAR mapping.
Radar odometry, radar SLAM, radar altimeters, Doppler velocity.
Global descriptors, image retrieval, LiDAR place recognition.
Keypoints/descriptors and learned matchers (SIFT, SuperPoint, LightGlue, LoFTR).
Matching UAV/ground imagery to satellite orthophotos or maps for absolute position without GNSS.
TERCOM/TRN/DSMAC-style matching of altimetry or imagery against DEM/terrain databases.
MagNav: matching magnetometer readings to crustal anomaly maps; aircraft compensation.
Star trackers, sun/sky polarization, celestial fixes.
Positioning from LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, DVB, LEO satellites (Starlink, Iridium), eLoran, other non-navigation RF.
UWB, TDOA/AOA, direction finding, emitter geolocation, beacons.
PDR, foot-mounted INS, dismounted soldier navigation, indoor positioning.
Flight stacks, control loops, estimation inside autopilots, firmware.

nodes.n: MAVLink, ground control and C2 links
nodes.s: MAVLink protocol, SDKs, ground control stations, telemetry radios.
Global/local planners, sampling and search based planning, trajectory optimization.
Route networks, waypoint missions, coverage, terrain-aware and threat-aware routing.
Reactive avoidance, sense-and-avoid, DAA.
Cooperative localization, swarm control, multi-robot SLAM, formation flight.
Map engines, tiles, DEMs, orthophotos, coordinate systems, geodesy.
Datums, projections, ECEF/ENU/NED, MGRS, geoid models.
TAK/CoT, MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 symbology, blue force tracking, common operating picture.
Surface vessel navigation, AIS, ECDIS/charts, USVs.
DVL, USBL/LBL acoustics, AUV navigation, underwater SLAM.
UGV/off-road autonomy stacks, localization and navigation for ground robots.
Orbit determination, LEO-PNT, spacecraft navigation.
Physics and sensor simulators, software/hardware-in-the-loop, GNSS signal simulators.
Public datasets, evaluation tools, leaderboards for navigation and localization.
ROS ecosystem packages for navigation and localization.
Detection, segmentation, depth on embedded hardware supporting navigation.
Multi-target tracking, MHT/JPDA, track fusion (for nav-relevant awareness, not weapon guidance).
Detecting, tracking and identifying drones (Remote ID, RF, radar, vision) - defensive.
Operating comms and navigation under EW: spectrum monitoring, LPI/LPD links, fallback modes.
ICDs, STANAGs, RTCM, NMEA, MAVLink, CoT, ASTERIX, interoperability specs.
ITAR/EAR, dual-use rules, PNT policy, responsible military AI.

nodes.n: LLM agents for robotics and navigation
nodes.s: Language models driving robots, mission planning, MCP servers for drones/ROS/GIS.

Python pipeline that localizes a drone by matching its downward camera frames against georeferenced satellite map tiles with SuperGlue, then converts the best match into GPS coordinates. Companion code to the 'Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild' paper.
nodes.w: The canonical small, readable reference for absolute visual localization over non-urban terrain - exactly the 'visual GPS' building block a GNSS-denied team needs.
nodes.h: Clone, drop in your own map tiles with corner coordinates and a few drone photos; runs on a laptop GPU. Brute-force tile search is slow - add a retrieval stage (AnyLoc/SALAD) to prune candidates.

nodes.s: A cleaner reimplementation of the WildNav idea: match UAV images to satellite tiles with SuperPoint/SuperGlue-style matchers and estimate geographic position.
nodes.w: Packaged, modular take on the WildNav approach that is easier to extend with newer matchers.
nodes.h: Good starting skeleton if WildNav's scripts feel too ad hoc; swap the matcher for LightGlue or XFeat for speed.

nodes.s: Geo-localization system for aerial platforms that first retrieves the right satellite map region with a deep descriptor and then aligns the drone orthophoto to it to extract coordinates; evaluated on reorganized public AgEagle datasets and a field test.
nodes.w: Shows the two-stage retrieve-then-align architecture end to end with field data, the design most practical systems converge on.
nodes.h: Use its pipeline layout as the backbone of a demo; datasets need a separate download. Conda env file provided.

nodes.s: Benchmark and code for UAV absolute visual localization under low-altitude, multi-view (oblique) observation, comparing retrieval and matching combinations against aerial and satellite reference maps.
nodes.w: One of the most up-to-date (2025) systematic comparisons of what actually works for low-altitude drones, which is the regime of small tactical UAVs.
nodes.h: Read its results before choosing a retrieval/matcher combo; reuse its evaluation scripts to score your own pipeline.

nodes.s: Scale-aware cross-view geo-localization method for matching UAV views to satellite imagery when the altitude-driven scale difference is unknown.
nodes.w: Scale mismatch is one of the main failure modes when flight altitude is uncertain; this targets it directly.
nodes.h: Research code; useful if your demo flies at varying altitudes and fixed-scale tiles break.

nodes.s: Project page for a UAV geolocalization system that combines image matching, visual odometry and a terrain-weighted constraint optimization, intended to work day and night. The repo holds only the README, result figures and demo video links - no code is released.
nodes.w: Fuses absolute map matches with relative VO and terrain constraints - the hybrid structure a real GNSS-denied nav stack needs.
nodes.h: No code, data or weights are released (README, figures and videos only); use it only as a reference for the fusion design.

nodes.s: Recent project fusing visual odometry with satellite-map matching in a particle filter for GNSS-denied UAV flight, with an explicit notion of when the map match should not be trusted; evaluated on UAV-VisLoc flights and with a browser demo.
nodes.w: Directly addresses the practical problem that per-frame map matching often fails (water, farmland, repetitive texture), and shows how to bridge with VO.
nodes.h: Very recent single-author project; good blueprint for a 48h demo combining VO drift with intermittent absolute fixes. Verify numbers yourself.

nodes.s: 6-DoF absolute visual localization for UAVs built on deep homography estimation between the drone view and a reference map, smoothed with a Kalman filter.
nodes.w: Homography-based registration gives full pose, not just a location, which helps when the camera is not nadir.
nodes.h: Pair with the STHN family for comparison; expect to retrain on your imagery.

nodes.s: Map-matching-based visual localization software for UAVs in GNSS-denied settings, shipped with a GUI front end and demo.
nodes.w: One of the few projects packaged as an operator-facing tool rather than a paper repo.
nodes.h: Useful for UI inspiration and a quick demo; inspect the matcher it uses before relying on accuracy.

nodes.s: Absolute drone positioning by image retrieval (SelaVPR-style ViT features) over cropped satellite tiles followed by registration with SIFT+RANSAC or SuperPoint+SuperGlue.
nodes.w: Clean example of a retrieval + registration pipeline that compares classic and learned matchers side by side.
nodes.h: Training described used a multi-GPU server; for a hackathon reuse pretrained weights and the pipeline code only.

nodes.s: Code for the paper 'Assisting UAV Localization via Deep Contextual Image Matching': locates an aerial template inside a larger georeferenced map with a SIFT pipeline and a deep variant built on Neighbourhood Consensus Networks, then reads GPS coordinates with GDAL.
nodes.w: A zero-training baseline to compare learned matchers against; mirrors classic DSMAC-style scene correlation in spirit.
nodes.h: Runs instantly; good as a fallback or ablation baseline in a demo.

nodes.s: CVPR 2022 cross-modal visual representation learning for absolute camera localization of aerial imagery, trained largely on synthetic data rendered from geodata.
nodes.w: Shows that synthetic renders from DEM/orthophoto can train localizers for real flights - a cheap way to cover new terrain.
nodes.h: Older and heavy to set up; read for the synthetic-data idea.

nodes.s: Real-time visual localization framework for planetary UAVs that jointly uses relative and absolute pose estimation against orbital maps.
nodes.w: Planetary flight is the purest GNSS-free case; the joint relative+absolute design transfers to Earth.
nodes.h: C++ build; mostly a design reference.

nodes.s: Dataset and baseline code for drone-based geo-localization across drone, satellite and ground views of university buildings worldwide.
nodes.w: The standard drone-to-satellite retrieval benchmark; most cross-view papers report on it.
nodes.h: Dataset is sent on emailed request from an academic address, after agreeing to research-only use, no sharing with third parties and no profit (Request.md); the synthetic drone views are building-centric, not wide-area terrain.

nodes.s: Multi-height, multi-scene drone-satellite cross-view dataset and evaluation code, capturing drone imagery at several altitudes.
nodes.w: Adds altitude variation that University-1652 lacks - closer to real flight profiles.
nodes.h: Comparable training pipeline to University-1652. The dataset is for academic research only, despite the repo's MIT code licence.

nodes.s: Dataset and baseline (TIP 2023) for UAV self-positioning in low-altitude urban environments using dense sampling of drone and satellite views.
nodes.w: Targets self-positioning (where am I) rather than target retrieval, with dense reference sampling.
nodes.h: Good dataset for training a retrieval head for urban flights.

nodes.s: Cross-view geo-localization training with hard negative sampling, reporting strong results on drone-satellite and street-satellite benchmarks with a simple contrastive setup.
nodes.w: A strong, simple baseline that is easy to retrain for your own drone/satellite pairs.
nodes.h: Pretrained checkpoints help; fine-tune on your tile set if time allows. No licence file, so code and weights are all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: PyTorch implementation of a cross-view geo-localization method that pools features in rings around the image center to capture contextual local patterns.
nodes.w: Widely used baseline in drone-satellite retrieval; useful to understand rotation-robust pooling.
nodes.h: Mainly as a comparison baseline.

nodes.s: Large-scale dataset of real UAV flight imagery with satellite reference maps for UAV visual localization across varied terrain.
nodes.w: Real nadir-ish drone frames with ground truth over large, non-urban areas - the closest public match to a GNSS-denied flight test.
nodes.h: Best dataset to test a visual-GPS demo; pick one flight and its map, run your matcher, plot error vs ground truth.

nodes.s: IROS 2023 code for long-range UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite RGB imagery, using domain adaptation to bridge thermal and visible imagery; comes with the Boson-nighttime dataset.
nodes.w: Night flight is when GNSS-denied UAVs are most exposed; this is the main open line of work for thermal-to-satellite matching.
nodes.h: Dataset on Hugging Face (gated). Use the pretrained model to show night-time matching in a demo.

nodes.s: Deep homography estimation for aligning UAV thermal images to satellite maps (RA-L 2024), refining coarse geo-localization into precise alignment.
nodes.w: Turns a coarse thermal match into an accurate position fix.
nodes.h: Combine with the IROS 2023 retrieval stage from the same lab.

nodes.s: ICRA 2025 extension of STHN that adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography, so the system can say when a fix is unreliable.
nodes.w: Calibrated uncertainty is what lets a nav filter safely ingest visual fixes.
nodes.h: Feed its uncertainty into your EKF measurement covariance.

nodes.s: Zero-shot UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite imagery without thermal-specific training.
nodes.w: Zero-shot avoids collecting paired thermal data, a common blocker.
nodes.h: Very recent; check release completeness.

nodes.s: Training code for a learned image transform that makes aerial imagery robust to seasonal appearance change for visual terrain-relative navigation.
nodes.w: Reference maps are often from a different season than the flight; this attacks that gap.
nodes.h: Older; reference for appearance-change preprocessing.

nodes.s: Event camera localization in prior lidar maps with confidence weighting.
nodes.w: Event cameras keep working in low light and fast motion, relevant for night localization against a prior map.
nodes.h: Requires event camera data; mostly a reference.

nodes.s: Universal visual place recognition using foundation-model (DINOv2) features with VLAD/GeM aggregation, working across aerial, underwater, indoor and outdoor domains without task-specific training.
nodes.w: Training-free retrieval that already works on aerial imagery - the fastest way to get a coarse 'which tile am I over' stage.
nodes.h: Extract descriptors for your satellite tiles offline, query with drone frames; then refine with LightGlue/RoMa.

nodes.s: Toolbox for hierarchical visual localization: global retrieval (NetVLAD etc.) to find candidate images, then local feature matching (SuperPoint, LightGlue...) and PnP against an SfM model.
nodes.w: The standard plumbing for coarse-to-fine localization; ready-made wrappers for most retrieval and matching models.
nodes.h: Use its retrieval + matching APIs even without the SfM part; pip-installable.

nodes.s: ICCV 2023 visual place recognition training method for viewpoint-robust descriptors.
nodes.w: Viewpoint robustness matters when drone heading and tilt vary against nadir satellite tiles.
nodes.h: Pretrained models loadable via torch.hub.

nodes.s: CVPR 2022 large-scale visual geo-localization treating place recognition as classification over geographic cells.
nodes.w: Scales to very large maps, a useful framing for country-sized reference databases.
nodes.h: torch.hub weights available.

nodes.s: Place recognition descriptor using optimal-transport aggregation of DINOv2 features.
nodes.w: Among the strongest off-the-shelf retrieval descriptors; good drop-in for the coarse stage.
nodes.h: Load via torch.hub, compare with AnyLoc on your tiles.

nodes.s: WACV 2023 place recognition descriptor built by MLP feature mixing; lightweight and fast.
nodes.w: Compact descriptors suit embedded retrieval on a drone.
nodes.h: Fast inference; good for an onboard-feasibility story. No licence file, so code and weights are all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: CVPR 2024 place recognition with a bag of learnable global queries over backbone features.
nodes.w: Recent strong retrieval model with simple usage.
nodes.h: torch.hub available.

nodes.s: ICLR 2024 method adapting pretrained foundation models for place recognition with lightweight adapters, producing both global and local features.
nodes.w: Global+local output lets one model do retrieval and re-ranking.
nodes.h: Used by Visual-Locator for UAV retrieval.

nodes.s: Wrapper exposing many state-of-the-art place recognition models behind one interface so you can switch models with one parameter.
nodes.w: Fastest way to benchmark several retrieval models on your own drone/satellite set.
nodes.h: Format your data as database/queries folders with UTM in filenames; GPU recommended.

nodes.s: Fast learned local feature matcher (ICCV 2023) that adapts its depth to pair difficulty; works with SuperPoint, DISK, ALIKED and SIFT features.
nodes.w: The default fine-matching stage for drone-to-tile registration today: accurate and fast enough for near-real-time.
nodes.h: Not on PyPI: install with `git clone https://github.com/cvg/LightGlue && pip install -e .`, or use the Hugging Face Transformers port. Use SuperPoint+LightGlue between a drone frame and top-k retrieved tiles, then RANSAC homography.

nodes.s: Training library for local feature detection and matching (trains LightGlue and others).
nodes.w: Lets you fine-tune a matcher on aerial/satellite pairs if off-the-shelf models struggle.
nodes.h: Training takes longer than a hackathon; use for post-event work.

nodes.s: Pretrained SuperGlue graph-neural-network matcher with SuperPoint features (CVPR 2020).
nodes.w: Used by WildNav and many UAV localization repos; non-commercial license limits reuse.
nodes.h: Prefer LightGlue (permissive license, faster) unless replicating WildNav exactly.

nodes.s: Pretrained SuperPoint keypoint detector and descriptor.
nodes.w: Feature front end for SuperGlue/LightGlue pipelines.
nodes.h: Most users get SuperPoint via LightGlue/hloc now.

nodes.s: Detector-free transformer matcher producing dense-ish correspondences, good on low-texture scenes.
nodes.w: Low-texture terrain (fields, desert) breaks keypoint matchers; detector-free matching helps.
nodes.h: Also available in kornia for easy use.

nodes.s: Robust dense feature matcher (CVPR 2024) estimating pixel-dense warps with certainties, strong under large appearance change.
nodes.w: Handles season, lighting and sensor differences between drone frames and satellite imagery better than sparse matchers, at higher compute cost.
nodes.h: Use as the accurate-but-slow verifier on the top retrieval hit; GPU recommended.

nodes.s: Matching grounded in 3D: predicts dense correspondences and 3D pointmaps from image pairs, building on DUSt3R.
nodes.w: Robust to extreme viewpoint change (oblique drone view vs nadir satellite) because it reasons in 3D.
nodes.h: Heavy model and non-commercial license; good for offline demos.

nodes.s: Lightweight local feature extractor and matcher (CVPR 2024) designed for speed on constrained hardware.
nodes.w: Fits onboard compute on small drones where LightGlue on GPU is not available.
nodes.h: Runs on CPU in real time; good for an embedded/Jetson story.

nodes.s: Wrapper exposing 50+ image matching models behind one interface (formerly image-matching-models).
nodes.w: Swap SIFT, LightGlue, LoFTR, RoMa, MASt3R etc. with one line to find the best matcher for your imagery.
nodes.h: Best first stop for matcher selection during the hackathon.

nodes.s: Python demo of TERCOM terrain contour matching: simulate a radar-altimeter profile over a DEM and correlate it against the map to recover position.
nodes.w: Smallest end-to-end TERCOM sim to understand and extend for a DEM-matching demo.
nodes.h: Load an SRTM/Copernicus DEM tile, generate a profile, show the correlation surface; an afternoon's work.

nodes.s: ROS 2 (Humble) package for GPS-denied fixed-wing UAV navigation: a TERCOM node correlates baro + rangefinder terrain profiles against a GeoTIFF DEM and feeds fixes into a 15-state error-state Kalman filter driven by IMU, baro and velocity updates.
nodes.w: Bridges batch terrain matching into a recursive filter that a real autopilot stack could consume.
nodes.h: Tested against PX4 SITL + Gazebo via MAVROS (no ArduPilot setup documented); colcon build, then launch with a GeoTIFF DEM path and world origin. GPS is used once to initialise the filter. Needs a rangefinder and barometer, real or simulated.

nodes.s: MATLAB SIR particle filter estimating UAV position from terrain contour matching in GPS-denied flight.
nodes.w: Particle filters handle the multimodal ambiguity of terrain matching better than a single correlation peak.
nodes.h: Port the filter loop to Python for a demo.

nodes.s: A single short OpenCV script that locates a Google Maps crop inside a larger map image with SIFT matching and a RANSAC homography, framed as DSMAC-style scene matching. Despite the repo name there is no terrain contour (TERCOM) code.
nodes.w: Minimal scene-matching (DSMAC-style) baseline; the TERCOM half exists only in the name.
nodes.h: Small educational code; use for concept slides and quick baselines.

nodes.s: Preprocessing tools for terrain-referenced navigation, generating DEM tiles with controlled noise for training and evaluation.
nodes.w: Saves time preparing DEM data for TRN experiments.
nodes.h: Use to build synthetic DEM test sets.

nodes.s: Julia package from the DAF-MIT AI Accelerator for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: flight/INS data import or simulation, anomaly maps, aircraft magnetic compensation (Tolles-Lawson and neural models) and navigation filters.
nodes.w: Official code behind the AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge; magnetic navigation is a leading GNSS-independent, unjammable PNT approach in DIU and AFRL programs.
nodes.h: Install Julia, Pkg.add("MagNav") and run the documented examples on the challenge flight data; compensation + EKF in a day. The DAF-MIT project has concluded and the package now gets maintenance-only changes, so do not expect fixes for new issues.

nodes.s: Community Python port of MIT's MagNav.jl: loads flight, INS and magnetometer data and magnetic anomaly maps (with upward continuation), runs Tolles-Lawson and neural-network aircraft compensation, and provides an EKF / MagNav filter with CRLB analysis and plotting.
nodes.w: Lowers the language barrier to the MagNav data and algorithms for Python-heavy teams.
nodes.h: Community port; install from the repo (despite the README badge, magnavpy is not on PyPI) and sort out GDAL first. Verify outputs against MagNav.jl examples.

nodes.s: Python package (Magnetic Anomaly Map Matching Airborne and Land) for simulating and processing aeromagnetic survey data and building anomaly maps for MagNav.
nodes.w: Map creation is the hidden half of MagNav; this covers it in Python.
nodes.h: Use to generate maps or simulated surveys feeding a particle filter.

nodes.s: Sample data for MagNav work: MIT-AIA anomaly maps, a challenge flight, North American magnetic anomaly grids and geoid files.
nodes.w: Ready-made data so a team can start without hunting for maps.
nodes.h: Grab these files first.

nodes.s: MATLAB code for Rao-Blackwellized particle smoothing for SLAM, including magnetic field mapping and map-matching localization with a magnetometer.
nodes.w: Clean academic reference for magnetic field SLAM and particle-filter matching at small scale.
nodes.h: Good for understanding magnetic map matching quickly.

nodes.s: Deep-learning approach to aircraft magnetic disturbance compensation built around the MagNav challenge data.
nodes.w: Compensation quality dominates MagNav accuracy; shows a learned alternative to Tolles-Lawson.
nodes.h: Unmaintained since 2023; dependencies may need pinning.

nodes.s: Hardware + firmware design for a drone magnetic-anomaly navigation board (ESP32-S3, magnetometer, IMU, baro) running particle-filter matching against a global anomaly map and feeding position to a flight controller over MAVLink. Proprietary: the LICENSE grants no rights to copy, modify or use it.
nodes.w: Rare example of MagNav pushed down to cheap drone hardware with an autopilot interface.
nodes.h: Very recent single-author project; the board has not been built and the firmware has not run on real hardware (README status). Proprietary licence, so read it for ideas only - do not reuse code or designs. Global anomaly maps are coarse, so expect km-level, not meter-level, results on small drones.

nodes.s: Fast lost-in-space plate solver for star trackers from ESA: identifies stars in an image and returns attitude using a precomputed pattern database.
nodes.w: Star-based attitude (and with time + gravity vector, position) is jam-proof; tetra3 is the easiest open solver.
nodes.h: Not on PyPI: pip install git+https://github.com/esa/tetra3.git; solve sample images in minutes. Combine attitude with a level sensor and clock for a celestial fix demo.

nodes.s: Actively maintained fork of tetra3 with speed and robustness improvements, used in the Cedar telescope-aiming product.
nodes.w: More maintained than upstream tetra3 for new work.
nodes.h: pip install cedar-solve. Keeps tetra3's API but is not quite drop-in: follow the repo's migration notes when porting tetra3 code.

nodes.s: Open-source star tracker using a Bayesian star identification approach, developed by the University at Buffalo Nanosatellite Lab.
nodes.w: Full camera-to-attitude pipeline with calibration, proven on small-satellite hardware.
nodes.h: Calibration step needed for your camera; budget a few hours.

nodes.s: Open-source star tracker (C++) covering centroiding, star identification and attitude estimation, from the UW CubeSat team.
nodes.w: Compiled, modular alternative for embedded targets.
nodes.h: Build with make; it can generate synthetic star images for testing (no real test images ship in the repo).

nodes.s: NASA software for building a star tracker from commercial off-the-shelf cameras, including calibration and attitude solution.
nodes.w: Directly aimed at cheap COTS cameras - the hardware a hackathon team will have.
nodes.h: Follow its calibration workflow with a phone or Pi camera.

nodes.s: Exploratory project on automating celestial navigation with deep learning and edge inference on synthetic sky images.
nodes.w: Shows a learning-based route from sky images to position.
nodes.h: Concept reference.

nodes.s: Python toolkit for classic celestial navigation sight reduction, usable offline on a phone.
nodes.w: Ground-truth math for turning star/sun sightings into a position.
nodes.h: Pair with a star tracker output to compute position.

nodes.s: Header-only C library for processing sky polarization images to support heading estimation; successor to compyss.
nodes.w: Polarization compass gives heading without magnetometers or GNSS, robust to magnetic disturbance.
nodes.h: Needs a polarization camera (or simulated images).

nodes.s: Passive positioning using Starlink downlink signals as signals of opportunity: SDR capture, blind OFDM analysis, Doppler extraction, TDOA/FDOA solver and EKF with TLE-based orbits.
nodes.w: One of the very few open end-to-end attempts at Starlink-based PNT, a hot GNSS-alternative topic.
nodes.h: Needs an SDR that covers Ku-band via LNB, or use the simulation path with TLEs. Treat claims as unverified.

nodes.s: Diploma thesis materials on signals-of-opportunity positioning from LEO satellites using Doppler shift and TLE-based orbits.
nodes.w: Readable derivation plus code for Doppler positioning from LEO constellations.
nodes.h: Use as the math reference for a Doppler-positioning simulator.

nodes.s: Open toolkit for LEO/MEO/GEO constellation simulation and single/multi-satellite positioning.
nodes.w: Lets a team simulate LEO-based positioning geometry and accuracy without hardware.
nodes.h: Desktop PySide6 app with Cesium 3D views (browser or embedded WebView); good for visualizing LEO coverage in a pitch.

nodes.s: Factor-graph positioning combining real GNSS pseudorange/Doppler with simulated LEO satellite measurements, extending GraphGNSSLib.
nodes.w: Shows how LEO observations slot into a factor graph alongside degraded GNSS.
nodes.h: C/ROS build; reference.

nodes.s: MATLAB simulation code accompanying an IEEE tutorial on 5G positioning (timing, angle and multi-cell methods).
nodes.w: Cellular positioning is a fallback PNT source; this is a didactic, runnable starting point.
nodes.h: MATLAB with the 5G Toolbox and Phased Array System Toolbox is needed, so Octave will not work; only the outdoor scenario is included.

nodes.s: Web-accessible shortwave SDR receiver (10 kHz - 30 MHz) with built-in software GPS and a Loran-C/eLoran monitor extension.
nodes.w: Public KiwiSDR network offers remote access to LF signals for eLoran/Loran experiments without owning hardware.
nodes.h: Use public KiwiSDR receivers to look at LF navigation signals; not a positioning solver.

nodes.s: Dronecode flight stack for multirotors, fixed-wing, VTOL, rovers and boats, built on NuttX with a uORB pub/sub middleware. Its EKF2 estimator fuses IMU, GNSS, baro, magnetometer, optical flow, range finders and external vision.
nodes.w: The most common permissive-licensed (BSD) autopilot base for defense and commercial UAS; EKF2 external-vision and flow fusion is the standard route to GPS-denied flight.
nodes.h: Run `make px4_sitl gz_x500` for SITL with Gazebo in under an hour. Feed VIO/SLAM poses via the ROS 2 uXRCE-DDS bridge or MAVLink ODOMETRY; disable GPS with EKF2_GPS_CTRL to test GPS-denied behaviour.

nodes.s: GPL autopilot covering Copter, Plane (incl. QuadPlane VTOL), Rover, boats and ArduSub, plus AP_Periph CAN peripherals. EKF3 supports switchable source sets, so GNSS, optical flow, beacons, wheel odometry and external vision can be swapped in flight.
nodes.w: Very broad vehicle coverage and mature non-GPS navigation docs; EKF3 source switching (EK3_SRCn_*) is directly useful for GNSS-loss and spoofing-resilience experiments.
nodes.h: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map` gives SITL in minutes. Lua scripting lets you add behaviour on the flight controller without a fork. Use SIM_GPS1_ENABLE=0 / EK3_SRC1_* to simulate GNSS denial.

nodes.s: Navigation-focused fork of the Cleanflight/Betaflight lineage for small multirotors, fixed-wing and rovers, adding GPS position hold, return-to-home and waypoint missions on cheap F4/F7/H7 boards.
nodes.w: Lowest-cost path to GNSS waypoint navigation on FPV-class airframes; useful to show how small drones behave on GNSS loss and how RTH failsafes work.
nodes.h: Configure with INAV Configurator; supports MSP and a MAVLink telemetry subset. SITL exists but is less polished than PX4/ArduPilot. Good for physical demos on cheap hardware.

nodes.s: Racing/freestyle-oriented flight controller firmware focused on attitude control and low-latency filtering. GPS Rescue was long its only navigation mode; releases since 2025 add altitude hold, position hold and waypoint flight plans (AUTOPILOT mode in 2026.6).
nodes.w: Dominant firmware on FPV drones seen in current conflicts; its navigation is still limited (GPS Rescue plus newer altitude/position hold and basic waypoints), which matters for C-UAS and EW-impact analysis.
nodes.h: Not a navigation platform; use for FPV-class hardware or to study how small drones react to link loss and GNSS jamming.

nodes.s: Long-running academic autopilot (ENAC, TU Delft and others) for fixed-wing, rotorcraft and hybrids, with its own ground segment, flight-plan language and INS modules.
nodes.w: Strong research heritage in fixed-wing and micro air vehicles, including vision-based and swarm experiments; a non-MAVLink reference architecture.
nodes.h: Toolchain and ground station setup takes hours; pick only if you know it already. Flight-plan XML is a nice example of declarative mission logic.

nodes.s: GitHub mirror of LibrePilot, the community continuation of OpenPilot for CC3D/Revolution boards, with the GCS bundled. Main development was on Bitbucket and has been quiet for years.
nodes.w: Historical reference for the OpenPilot-era INS13 estimator and UAVTalk protocol; not a base for new work.
nodes.h: Read-only reference. Hardware is end-of-life.

nodes.s: Mirror of the original OpenPilot flight controller project (not comma.ai's openpilot), frozen since 2015.
nodes.w: Origin of the TauLabs, dRonin and LibrePilot family; historical only.
nodes.h: Historical reference only.

nodes.s: Single-file Arduino/Teensy flight controller for small VTOL and multirotor craft, written to be read and modified by students.
nodes.w: Easiest flight-control code to understand end to end; good for teaching attitude estimation (Madgwick) and control loops in a weekend.
nodes.h: Flash to a Teensy with an MPU6050/9250 IMU; no navigation or MAVLink, so pair with a companion for anything beyond stabilisation.

nodes.s: Espressif's mini quadcopter firmware for ESP32/ESP32-S2/S3, derived from Crazyflie code, controlled over Wi-Fi.
nodes.w: Very cheap, hackable airframe with Wi-Fi control; usable for indoor swarm or RF experiments.
nodes.h: Builds with ESP-IDF; supports optical-flow deck style positioning only with extra sensors. Expect tuning effort on DIY frames.

nodes.s: Firmware for the Crazyflie nano quad, Bolt and the Roadrunner positioning tag, with EKF and complementary estimators supporting UWB Loco positioning, Lighthouse, Flow deck and mocap.
nodes.w: Mature indoor research platform where UWB/Lighthouse localisation and GPS-free estimation are first-class; widely used in swarm papers.
nodes.h: If you have Crazyflies, the Python lib gets you scripted flights in an hour. UWB Loco anchors make a good GNSS-denied testbed. Simulation via crazyswarm2 or the official SIL.

nodes.s: Python API to connect, log, set parameters and send setpoints/high-level commands to Crazyflies over Crazyradio or USB.
nodes.w: Fastest way to script autonomy experiments on nano drones.
nodes.h: pip install cflib; Swarm class runs parallel commands.

nodes.s: ROS 2 framework for flying many Crazyflie nano-quadrotors with motion capture or onboard localization, including simulation backends.
nodes.w: Ready-made multi-agent testbed for coordinated indoor flight and formation experiments.
nodes.h: Simulation works without hardware; with Crazyflies plus Loco or Lighthouse you can fly a small swarm in a day.

nodes.s: Lean research autopilot (BYU) that keeps only attitude estimation and low-level control on the flight board and pushes everything else to a ROS companion.
nodes.w: Clean split between embedded and onboard autonomy; good for teams who want full control of the estimator on the companion.
nodes.h: Use with rosflight_ros_pkgs; includes a simulator so hardware is optional.

nodes.s: ROS 2 interface, simulator and utilities for the ROSflight autopilot.
nodes.w: Companion-side half of ROSflight, where navigation and autonomy live.
nodes.h: Start with the sim launch files.

nodes.s: Former home of PX4's estimation and control library including the EKF2 navigation filter; archived after the code moved into PX4-Autopilot.
nodes.w: Its history and docs remain a readable reference for the EKF2 derivation (SymPy-generated equations).
nodes.h: Read the current EKF2 in PX4-Autopilot src/modules/ekf2 instead; use this for history.

nodes.s: Algorithms for computing optical flow from a downward camera to produce velocity inputs for a position estimator.
nodes.w: Optical flow plus range finder is the cheapest GNSS-free velocity source for low-altitude hover and drift control.
nodes.h: Library only (PX4Flow SAD block matching and an OpenCV KLT variant behind calcFlow()); there is no executable or MAVLink output, so you write the camera capture and OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD publishing yourself. The Gazebo Classic flow plugin is the reference user. Light maintenance commits in 2026.

nodes.s: Message definitions (XML dialects) and the pymavlink-based generator for the MAVLink micro air vehicle protocol, used by PX4, ArduPilot and most GCS tools.
nodes.w: The lingua franca of open-source UAS; any GCS, companion, Remote ID or C-UAS sensor integration ends up speaking it.
nodes.h: Add a custom dialect XML and regenerate bindings to prototype new messages (e.g. a jamming-detection report).

nodes.s: Source of the mavlink.io documentation: protocol, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, Open Drone ID) and message reference.
nodes.w: Canonical reference when wiring new sensors or services over MAVLink.
nodes.h: Read the microservice pages before implementing anything stateful.

nodes.s: Python MAVLink implementation plus tools for connections, log parsing (DataFlash/tlog) and code generation.
nodes.w: Quickest path to scripting a vehicle or parsing flight logs to evaluate estimator behaviour under GNSS loss.
nodes.h: pip install pymavlink; mavutil.mavlink_connection('udp:...') against SITL works in minutes.

nodes.s: C++ SDK exposing high-level MAVLink plugins (action, mission, offboard, telemetry, camera) with a gRPC server for other languages.
nodes.w: Clean API for companion-side autonomy against PX4 (and to a degree ArduPilot) without ROS.
nodes.h: For hackathon speed use the Python binding: since MAVSDK v4, `pip install mavsdk` installs a native binding built in this repo (sync API in `mavsdk`, asyncio in `mavsdk.asyncio`), with no mavsdk_server process. The older gRPC-based MAVSDK-Python with a bundled mavsdk_server lives on as `mavsdk-grpc`.

nodes.s: Asyncio Python client for MAVSDK that wraps a bundled mavsdk_server.
nodes.w: Probably the fastest way to script missions or offboard control against PX4 SITL.
nodes.h: pip install mavsdk-grpc and import mavsdk_grpc (the PyPI name 'mavsdk' now means the native binding with a different API); examples cover takeoff, missions, offboard velocity.

nodes.s: ROS/ROS 2 node bridging MAVLink to ROS topics and services, with GCS proxy; widely used to push vision/SLAM poses into PX4 or ArduPilot.
nodes.w: Standard glue between ROS-based VIO/SLAM and a flight controller for GPS-denied navigation.
nodes.h: apt install ros-<distro>-mavros, then run install_geographiclib_datasets.sh; current MAVROS targets ROS 2 (Humble and newer). Feed your odometry into /mavros/vision_pose/pose.

nodes.s: Lightweight C++ daemon that routes MAVLink between serial, UDP and TCP endpoints with filtering and logging.
nodes.w: Typical companion-computer plumbing to share one flight-controller link between GCS, autonomy and loggers.
nodes.h: Build with meson; one config file. Run it before attaching multiple clients.

nodes.s: Single-binary Go MAVLink router/proxy supporting serial, UDP and TCP with deduplication.
nodes.w: Zero-dependency alternative to mavlink-router; easy to drop on any companion.
nodes.h: Download the release binary and run; no build.

nodes.s: Go MAVLink v1/v2 library with dialect generation and multiple transports.
nodes.w: Good for writing small, robust Go services (telemetry relays, sensor bridges).
nodes.h: Go modules; examples for reading/writing messages.

nodes.s: Rust implementation of MAVLink with generated dialects and serial/UDP/TCP connections.
nodes.w: Memory-safe option for ground or embedded services.
nodes.h: cargo add mavlink.

nodes.s: TypeScript/Node.js MAVLink bindings and tools.
nodes.w: Handy for web dashboards and Node-based ground tools.
nodes.h: npm install; works over serial/UDP/TCP.

nodes.s: Older high-level Python API for MAVLink vehicles, built on pymavlink; maintenance has slowed (last push 2024).
nodes.w: Many tutorials still use it; fine for simple ArduPilot scripts but prefer pymavlink or MAVSDK for new work.
nodes.h: The PyPI release 2.9.2 (2019) fails to import on Python 3.10+ (it uses collections.MutableMapping); pin Python 3.9 or install from GitHub master, which has the fix. Better to avoid for new work.

nodes.s: Command-line, module-based ground station and MAVLink proxy with map, console and many plugins.
nodes.w: Default SITL console for ArduPilot; scriptable modules make it easy to prototype operator-side tools.
nodes.h: Comes with sim_vehicle.py; write a module to add custom displays or alerts (e.g. GNSS anomaly warnings).

nodes.s: Qt/QML cross-platform GCS (desktop, Android, iOS) for PX4 and ArduPilot: setup, mission planning, video and telemetry.
nodes.w: Most common open GCS; a base for custom operator UIs, including Remote ID display.
nodes.h: Use prebuilt binaries for SITL; custom builds take a few hours to set up Qt.

nodes.s: Windows-centric C#/.NET GCS for ArduPilot with deep parameter, log-analysis and mission tooling.
nodes.w: Feature-richest ArduPilot GCS; the EKF and GPS status views are useful during GNSS-denial tests.
nodes.h: Windows best; runs under Mono on Linux/mac with caveats.

nodes.s: Qt-based cross-platform ArduPilot GCS, now largely in maintenance mode.
nodes.w: Alternative GCS mainly of historical interest.
nodes.h: Prefer QGroundControl or Mission Planner.

nodes.s: Web app for uploading and plotting PX4 ULog flight logs, including estimator innovations and test ratios.
nodes.w: Fast way to judge whether EKF2 is healthy when fusing a new vision or flow source.
nodes.h: Use the hosted instance or run locally with Docker.

nodes.s: Browser-based viewer for ArduPilot DataFlash (.bin) and MAVLink telemetry (.tlog) logs, also DJI .txt logs, with 3D replay and plotting.
nodes.w: Quick post-flight review of EKF3 innovations and source switching.
nodes.h: Hosted at plot.ardupilot.org; no install.

nodes.s: Guided step-by-step parameter configuration tool for ArduPilot vehicles; the sequence is complete for ArduCopter, while Plane, Heli and Rover guides are still incomplete.
nodes.w: Reduces setup mistakes on new airframes, which matter more than code in short builds.
nodes.h: Use when building physical ArduPilot vehicles.

nodes.s: ROS 2 message definitions mirroring PX4 uORB topics, used with the uXRCE-DDS bridge.
nodes.w: Required to talk to PX4 natively from ROS 2 (e.g. VehicleOdometry for external vision).
nodes.h: Match the branch to your PX4 version or messages will mismatch.

nodes.s: Example ROS 2 nodes and helpers (frame transforms) for interfacing with PX4 over DDS.
nodes.w: Starting templates for offboard control and sending odometry into PX4.
nodes.h: Clone alongside px4_msgs into a colcon workspace.

nodes.s: Agent that bridges DDS-XRCE clients on microcontrollers into a full DDS / ROS 2 graph; PX4 and ArduPilot use it for native ROS 2.
nodes.w: Core link in the PX4 and ArduPilot ROS 2 (DDS) paths.
nodes.h: Install via snap or build from source; run MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 for SITL.

nodes.s: C++ library for writing PX4 flight modes and navigation-data sources in ROS 2 on a companion computer, registered with PX4 as first-class modes.
nodes.w: Lets a team ship a custom autonomy mode or inject a local/global position estimate (e.g. a visual geolocalisation fix) cleanly into PX4.
nodes.h: Needs recent PX4 (1.15+) and matching px4_msgs; examples include custom modes and external navigation interfaces.

nodes.s: Small example of driving PX4 velocity setpoints from ROS 2 teleop, with SITL launch files.
nodes.w: Good minimal starter for a ROS 2 offboard demo.
nodes.h: Runs against PX4 SITL in about an hour (README pins PX4 release/1.15, ROS 2 Humble, Ubuntu 22.04). The README says the tutorial has moved to ARK-Electronics/ros2_px4_teleop_example (C++, PX4 custom modes); use that for current PX4.

nodes.s: ROS 2 integration examples for ArduPilot, including Cartographer-based non-GPS navigation and Nav2 setups.
nodes.w: Directly targets lidar-SLAM-fed GPS-free flight on ArduPilot.
nodes.h: Use with ardupilot_gz for simulation; follow the wiki ROS 2 pages.

nodes.s: ROS 2 + Gazebo packages for ArduPilot SITL integration and testing.
nodes.w: Gives a ready simulated vehicle with lidar/cameras for ROS 2 navigation experiments.
nodes.h: Target ROS 2 Humble + Gazebo Harmonic per the README.

nodes.s: Gazebo Sim plugins that connect ArduPilot SITL to Gazebo physics, with example Iris copter and Zephyr plane models and worlds.
nodes.w: Brings ArduPilot vehicles (copter, plane, rover, boat) into gz-sim with realistic sensors for nav and autonomy testing.
nodes.h: Follow the ArduPilot wiki Gazebo guide; works best on Ubuntu (macOS also supported). No rover or boat models ship here, so a USV/rover test needs a model from elsewhere, such as ardupilot/SITL_Models.

nodes.s: Plugins, vehicle models and worlds that connect PX4 SITL/HITL to Gazebo Classic, including GPS, IMU, magnetometer, barometer and optical-flow plugins.
nodes.w: Large existing corpus of tutorials and research setups still target it; the GPS plugin is a common starting point for spoofing and jamming experiments in sim.
nodes.h: Works with Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 and Gazebo 11. Gazebo Classic has reached end of life, so prefer gz-sim for new builds unless you need a specific legacy model.

nodes.s: Archived ROS nodes for local planning, global planning and safe landing using depth sensors with PX4.
nodes.w: Still a useful reference for obstacle avoidance architectures, but unmaintained.
nodes.h: ROS 1 only; read for design ideas.

nodes.s: Web-based companion-computer manager for MAVLink vehicles: telemetry routing, video streaming, logging and network config on Raspberry Pi/Jetson.
nodes.w: Turnkey companion setup so the team spends time on navigation code rather than plumbing.
nodes.h: Flash the prebuilt image to a Pi; manage routing in the browser.

nodes.s: Blue Robotics' onboard software platform for ROVs and USVs: web UI, ArduPilot management, MAVLink routing and a Docker extension system on a Raspberry Pi companion computer.
nodes.w: Strong base for maritime/underwater vehicle builds; extension system makes adding a nav service easy.
nodes.h: Most useful with a BlueROV2; extensions are Docker images, so a nav add-on can be packaged quickly.

nodes.s: Rust service that exposes cameras as MAVLink camera components and streams video (RTSP/UDP) to GCS.
nodes.w: Makes onboard cameras discoverable to QGC and BlueOS without custom code.
nodes.h: Runs standalone or inside BlueOS.

nodes.s: ROS and Python scripts that convert external localisation (fiducials, T265 VIO, SLAM, depth) into MAVROS/MAVLink pose messages, tested on ArduPilot.
nodes.w: Proven recipe for feeding vision-based localisation into ArduPilot EKF3 for GPS-denied flight; came out of GSoC work.
nodes.h: Old (2022) but simple; adapt the non-ROS T265 script to any VIO source.

nodes.s: Precision landing using visual fiducial targets, sending LANDING_TARGET messages to ArduPilot.
nodes.w: Example of vision-based terminal approach for recovery/landing without GNSS accuracy.
nodes.h: Discontinued by its authors (README: academic/learning use only). Needs OpenCV, the aruco library and DroneKit on the companion; inactive since 2023.

nodes.s: Open-source long-range digital HD video and telemetry link over Wi-Fi adapters in monitor mode (wifibroadcast-style), for air and ground units.
nodes.w: Low-cost resilient video/telemetry downlink for situational awareness; also a reference for link behaviour under interference.
nodes.h: Needs supported Wi-Fi cards (RTL8812AU) and SBCs; budget a few hours for imaging.

nodes.s: Long-range packet radio link over raw Wi-Fi injection with FEC, carrying video, MAVLink and IP tunnels.
nodes.w: Unidirectional broadcast-style link with FEC is more robust to interference than plain Wi-Fi; useful for EW-resilient telemetry experiments.
nodes.h: Install on Linux with compatible RTL8812AU/EU cards (patched drivers required); key pairs per link. Code is GPL-3.0, but the author's paid support excludes military usage.

nodes.s: Open-source LoRa/FLRC radio control link (2.4 GHz and sub-GHz) with high packet rates, telemetry and MAVLink passthrough modes.
nodes.w: Dominant open RC link in FPV; its behaviour under jamming and its telemetry options matter for EW-resilience and C-UAS work.
nodes.h: Flash with ExpressLRS Configurator; receivers are cheap.

nodes.s: LoRa-based bidirectional link carrying RC and full MAVLink serial data on 2.4 GHz, 868/915 MHz and 433 MHz.
nodes.w: Combines control and telemetry over long-range LoRa for ArduPilot/PX4, which is useful where Wi-Fi links fail.
nodes.h: Supports several off-the-shelf modules; read the hardware list first.

nodes.s: Firmware and tools for Si1000-based telemetry radios (3DR/RFD900 class) carrying MAVLink.
nodes.w: Classic serial telemetry radio stack; frequency-hopping config is relevant to link robustness.
nodes.h: Mostly use stock firmware; configure via AT commands or Mission Planner.

nodes.s: ESP32-based Remote ID transmitter firmware implementing ASTM F3411 broadcast (Bluetooth and Wi-Fi) fed from MAVLink or DroneCAN.
nodes.w: Cheap compliant Remote ID broadcasting, and the transmitter side of any Remote ID-based C-UAS awareness demo.
nodes.h: Flash an ESP32-S3/C3 dev board; pair with opendroneid receiver-android to show detection end to end.

nodes.s: Reference C library for encoding and decoding ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN Remote ID messages (location, operator, system, auth) for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi broadcast.
nodes.w: Remote ID is the cooperative layer of airspace awareness and counter-UAS; this library is the canonical message implementation.
nodes.h: Builds with CMake in minutes; pair with an ESP32 or phone receiver to decode drone broadcasts and push them to a map or TAK.

nodes.s: Example Android app that listens for Remote ID broadcasts over Bluetooth 4/5 and Wi-Fi Beacon/NaN and shows drones and operators on a map.
nodes.w: Fastest way to get a working cooperative drone-detection sensor in a hackathon using only phones.
nodes.h: Sideload on a recent Android phone; Wi-Fi NaN support depends on handset. Extend to forward detections as CoT to a TAK server.

nodes.s: Example Linux transmitter for Remote ID over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
nodes.w: Lets a companion computer broadcast Remote ID for testing receivers.
nodes.h: Needs compatible Bluetooth/Wi-Fi chipsets; dormant since 2023.

nodes.s: Arduino classes for several UAV electronic ID formats (ASTM/EU Remote ID, French ID) and UTM interfaces, with ESP32 examples.
nodes.w: Small, readable alternative Remote ID implementation, including receiver-side sketches.
nodes.h: Arduino IDE; the id_open examples are transmitters (ESP32, ESP8266, nRF52) and id_scanner is a receiver sketch.

nodes.s: Minimal C implementation of the DroneCAN protocol used for GNSS, compass, airspeed and other peripherals on CAN.
nodes.w: Needed to build custom CAN sensors (e.g. an alternative nav sensor) that ArduPilot/PX4 can consume.
nodes.h: Use with dronecan/DSDL; mostly for hardware teams.

nodes.s: ROS 2 framework for autonomous single and multi-aerial-robot systems with behaviours, state estimation plugins and platform adapters (Gazebo and a multirotor simulator in this repo; PX4, Crazyflie and DJI adapters in separate as2_platform_* repos).
nodes.w: One of the few ROS 2 native UAV mission frameworks that spans simulation to several real autopilots, good for multi-drone mission demos.
nodes.h: Binary packages for Humble; Python mission API lets you script takeoff/goto/land for several drones quickly.

nodes.s: Official training and evaluation code for the GSV-Cities visual place recognition dataset (about 530k street-level images of 62k+ places across many cities), including the Conv-AP aggregator and evaluation notebooks for standard VPR benchmarks.
nodes.w: The standard large training set for modern VPR descriptors; training without offline triplet mining makes fine-tuning on your own imagery fast.
nodes.h: Dataset is on Kaggle under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (research only); the code repo has no licence file. Use it to pretrain or fine-tune a descriptor, then adapt to aerial tiles. Last push 2024.

nodes.s: Modular PyTorch framework for training VPR models as data -> backbone -> aggregation -> loss, with one-command download of GSV-Cities / GSV-Cities-light, metric-learning losses, TensorBoard logging and retrieval visualizations.
nodes.w: Fastest route to training or fine-tuning your own place-recognition model with swappable aggregators.
nodes.h: Conda environment install; GSV-Cities-light is the quick start. MIT licence on code, but the GSV-Cities data is CC BY-NC-ND. No commits since mid-2024.

nodes.s: Benchmark tool accompanying the aerial VPR survey by Moskalenko et al.: downloads satellite map tiles, localizes UAV imagery against them with AnyLoc, CosPlace, EigenPlaces, MixVPR, NetVLAD, SALAD or SelaVPR, and optionally re-ranks with LightGlue, SuperGlue or SelaVPR.
nodes.w: Ready-made drone-to-satellite VPR pipeline with many descriptors behind one interface, plus evidence on how tile zoom and overlap affect recall.
nodes.h: Start from example.ipynb (download map, localize a sequence, compute recall). Some weights come from a Google Drive link, others via TorchHub. Tested on Python 3.10. Apache-2.0.

nodes.s: Official code for the CVPR 2022 benchmark: a configurable training and evaluation framework for visual geo-localization where backbone, aggregation, negative mining and pre/post-processing can be swapped and measured.
nodes.w: Lets a team compare VPR design choices on equal footing, including runtime and memory, before committing to an onboard model.
nodes.h: Datasets must be arranged in its directory layout; the VPR-datasets-downloader repo helps. MIT licence.

nodes.s: MATLAB implementation of Lagrangian grid-based (point-mass) filters for terrain-aided navigation, compared against other filters on real-world-based TAN models, with code for several related papers including the tensor-decomposition variant.
nodes.w: State-of-the-art grid filters for terrain-aided navigation that run in real time; a strong alternative to particle filters for radar-altimeter TRN.
nodes.h: Needs MATLAB; a mex file speeds the FFT time update and can be switched off. AGPL-3.0 licence matters if you ship derived code.

nodes.s: MATLAB code for the efficient point-mass filter (FUSION 2023) for systems with linear state dynamics, illustrated on terrain-aided navigation.
nodes.w: Small, readable reference implementation of a fast grid-based TAN filter.
nodes.h: Needs MATLAB; no licence file. The pesslovany/Matlab-LagrangianPMF repo is the maintained successor.

nodes.s: Dataset, ROS nodes and DWM1001 firmware from the IROS 2020 paper on UWB localization for autonomous UAV flight: several anchor configurations, flights inside and outside the anchor hull, and an anchor auto-positioning method.
nodes.w: Cheap Decawave hardware recipe plus real flight data for UWB-aided GNSS-denied flight.
nodes.h: Use the data to tune a UWB EKF before buying hardware. No licence file. Not updated since 2022.

nodes.s: Drone UWB dataset: six flight sequences with two-way ranging to four anchors, stereo VIO, motion-capture ground truth for drone and anchors, CSV exports and an analysis tool; rosbags on Google Drive.
nodes.w: Shows how anchor and tag orientation bias UWB ranges, which is what breaks naive UWB models in practice.
nodes.h: CSV files are usable without ROS. No licence file, so reuse terms are unstated.

nodes.s: C++ core library and Python bindings for Luxonis OAK cameras: on-device stereo depth, neural inference and feature tracking pipelines.
nodes.w: OAK cameras give a small UAS or UGV onboard stereo depth and feature tracking without a GPU, a cheap input for VIO and obstacle avoidance when GNSS is gone.
nodes.h: The luxonis/depthai repo is a placeholder; real code and examples live here. Needs OAK hardware.

nodes.s: Open-source Python framework from UK Dstl and partners for developing, running and evaluating tracking and state estimation algorithms: Kalman variants, particle filters, JPDA, MHT, GM-PHD, track management and metrics.
nodes.w: A government-backed, permissively developed tracking toolkit - the closest thing to a reference library for situational-awareness fusion that defense judges will recognize.
nodes.h: pip install stonesoup; tutorials run in Jupyter. Good for fusing ADS-B, Remote ID or DF bearings into tracks on a common picture within a day. Keep it to air-picture awareness, not fire control.

nodes.s: The DoD's public source release of the civilian Android Team Awareness Kit: map engine, Cursor-on-Target messaging and plugin SDK.
nodes.w: TAK is the de facto common operating picture across US/NATO units, so a plugin or CoT feed is an instantly legible demo for defense judges.
nodes.h: Archived; use the TAK Product Center repo for current code. Building ATAK from source is heavy - develop a plugin against a prebuilt SDK instead.

nodes.s: Source of the civilian Android Team Awareness Kit maintained by the TAK Product Center: map client, plugin SDK and CoT handling.
nodes.w: The most widely used open tactical map client; plugins let you inject nav and sensor data into a fielded UI.
nodes.h: Plugin builds need the matching SDK version; budget half a day for toolchain. Many teams instead feed CoT from Python and just use stock ATAK/iTAK.

nodes.s: Open-source Python server compatible with TAK clients (ATAK, WinTAK, iTAK) that relays Cursor-on-Target positions, chat and data packages.
nodes.w: Gives dismounted users and robots a shared map picture; common endpoint for drone-detection and blue-force feeds.
nodes.h: pip install or the ZeroTouch installer; activity slowed since 2024, so check OpenTAKServer as a more active option.

nodes.s: Actively developed open-source TAK server for ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK with web UI, video streaming integration, Meshtastic support and certificate enrollment.
nodes.w: Quick, modern backend for a common operating picture demo linking several sensors and phones.
nodes.h: Installer scripts for Linux/RPi; get clients connected in an hour, then focus on your sensor feed.

nodes.s: Python asyncio package for TAK integration: CoT send/receive over TCP, UDP, TLS and multicast, with helpers for building events.
nodes.w: The glue that turns any sensor script (GNSS monitor, Remote ID sniffer, DF array) into a TAK layer in a few lines.
nodes.h: pip install pytak; write a CoT generator for your detections. Lowest-friction way into the TAK ecosystem.

nodes.s: Gateway that converts ADS-B traffic from dump1090/readsb or aggregator APIs into Cursor-on-Target so aircraft show in TAK.
nodes.w: ADS-B also carries NIC/NACp integrity fields - the same signal GPSJam uses - so this is a ready bridge for a live GNSS-interference overlay.
nodes.h: Run alongside readsb on an RTL-SDR; add a filter that flags low NIC aircraft as an interference indicator.

nodes.s: ADS-B/Mode S decoder for RTL-SDR and other receivers with networking, JSON output, MLAT support and aggregation features.
nodes.w: Gives a team its own receiver for aircraft positions and navigation-integrity reports, the raw material for crowd-sourced jamming maps.
nodes.h: Install on a Pi with a cheap RTL-SDR and 1090 MHz antenna; JSON output is easy to parse for NIC/NACp statistics.

nodes.s: Improved web interface for readsb/dump1090 with track history, filtering and overlays.
nodes.w: Ready-made visualization layer for an ADS-B based interference or airspace-awareness demo.
nodes.h: One-line install on top of readsb. Fork the JS to color aircraft by NIC to show degraded GNSS.

nodes.s: FlightAware's maintained Mode S/ADS-B decoder (dump1090-fa), a GitHub fork and successor of dump1090-mutability, supporting RTL-SDR, bladeRF, HackRF, LimeSDR and SoapySDR devices.
nodes.w: Widely packaged alternative to readsb for the same ADS-B situational-awareness use.
nodes.h: apt-installable on Raspberry Pi OS from FlightAware's own package repository (it is not in Debian main), or build the .deb from source; pick either this or readsb, not both.

nodes.s: Multi-user web SDR receiver with waterfall display and many built-in digital decoders.
nodes.w: Shared, browser-based spectrum view is a simple way to demonstrate RF situational awareness, e.g. watching the GNSS L1 band for interference with a suitable front end.
nodes.h: Docker image available. Upstream activity slowed after 2024; the luarvique fork is more active.

nodes.s: Actively developed fork of OpenWebRX adding decoders, bookmarks and packaging improvements.
nodes.w: Same browser spectrum-monitoring capability with current maintenance.
nodes.h: Use the provided packages/Docker; works with RTL-SDR, Airspy, SDRplay, HackRF.

nodes.s: Desktop SDR receiver built on GNU Radio and Qt with FFT/waterfall and demodulators.
nodes.w: Quick local spectrum inspection when characterizing a jammer test signal in a shielded lab or checking band occupancy.
nodes.h: Available via brew/apt. Only transmit-free monitoring; never radiate in GNSS bands outside licensed test ranges.

nodes.s: Direction-of-arrival processing and web UI for the five-channel coherent KrakenSDR, producing bearings to RF emitters.
nodes.w: Passive DF of interference sources (or drone control links) is a core defensive-EW capability and maps well to a hackathon demo.
nodes.h: Needs KrakenSDR hardware (or recorded IQ). Prebuilt Raspberry Pi images exist (check the KrakenRF docs). Multiple stations plus Stone Soup gives triangulated emitter tracks.

nodes.s: Coherent multichannel SDR acquisition chain (sync, calibration, decimation) underneath KrakenSDR DoA and passive radar apps.
nodes.w: Useful if you need raw coherent IQ for your own DF or interference-localization algorithm.
nodes.h: Installed as part of the KrakenSDR image; modify only if building custom DSP.

nodes.s: Ruhr University Bochum receiver for DJI DroneID that works live with an SDR or offline on captures, released with their NDSS 2023 security analysis.
nodes.w: Shows how passive decoding of drone telemetry supports detection and localization of DJI aircraft, a common C-UAS need.
nodes.h: Requires a wideband SDR (e.g. USRP/BladeRF) and recorded or live captures; sample captures ease offline work.

nodes.s: Gateway that takes drone Remote ID / DroneID detections from WarDragon-style sensors and publishes them as CoT to TAK and other outputs.
nodes.w: Working example of a passive drone-detection to common-operating-picture pipeline.
nodes.h: Read it as a reference architecture even without the WarDragon kit; reuse its CoT mapping for your own detector.

nodes.s: ESP32 firmware and a Python/Flask mapper that capture Remote ID broadcasts over both BLE and Wi-Fi, relay detections over a Meshtastic LoRa mesh and plot drones and pilots on a live, offline-capable web map.
nodes.w: Cheap, distributed, off-grid drone-awareness network - very hackathon friendly hardware.
nodes.h: ESP32 boards plus Meshtastic nodes cost little; flash and map in an afternoon.

nodes.s: A public submission repository for the JuliaCon 2020 MagNav signal-enhancement challenge, implementing a learned aircraft-field compensation.
nodes.w: One of the few open challenge entries - shows what a competing compensation pipeline looks like end to end.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2022; useful as a template for a challenge-style submission on the MagNav data. Needs both Julia (Tolles-Lawson pre-filter) and MATLAB with the Deep Learning Toolbox (the learned filter in runs/main.m).

nodes.s: Gazebo worlds, robot models, ROS interfaces and scoring tools from the virtual track of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge.
nodes.w: Ready GNSS-denied underground environments with official scoring - a credible simulation testbed straight out of a DARPA challenge.
nodes.h: Dockerized, ROS1-era; heavy GPU/CPU needs. Use the hello-world repo as a starting point.

nodes.s: Graph-based exploration planner from NTNU ARL; the main branch is now OmniPlanner (GBPlanner 3.0) for aerial, ground and underwater robots, and GBPlanner 2.0, the planning core of Team CERBERUS, winner of the DARPA SubT final, is kept on the gbplanner2 branch.
nodes.w: Winning-team open code for autonomous exploration of GNSS-denied spaces with legged and aerial robots.
nodes.h: The default branch is now OmniPlanner (GBPlanner 3.0, aerial/ground/underwater); GBPlanner 2.0 is on the gbplanner2 branch. ROS workspace with Gazebo worlds; heavy but realistic. Licence is BSD-3, but the README says it is intended for civilian use only.

nodes.s: Motion-primitive based exploration planner for fast aerial robots in confined spaces, used in CERBERUS flying platforms.
nodes.w: Aerial complement to GBPlanner for drone exploration without GNSS.
nodes.h: ROS1, not updated since 2023.

nodes.s: Team CoSTAR's large-scale multi-robot lidar SLAM back end with robust loop closure, from the NASA JPL-led SubT entry.
nodes.w: Open component of the NeBula stack that won the SubT Urban circuit; shows multi-robot GNSS-denied mapping done at challenge scale.
nodes.h: ROS1 and dormant since 2023; run on the NeBula multi-robot dataset rather than live hardware.

nodes.s: Index for CoSTAR's multi-robot SubT lidar datasets (Tunnel, Urban, Finals Prelim2, Kentucky Underground): processed keyed scans and incremental pose graphs sent to the base station, g2o/pcd exports and ground truth.
nodes.w: Real GNSS-denied field data from SubT for testing SLAM or loop closure without building robots.
nodes.h: Bags are large; pick one sequence. Data is processed LAMP front-end output, not raw sensor streams. No licence file or data terms are given (all rights reserved by default); cite LAMP 2.0 and ask the authors before reuse beyond research.

nodes.s: Hierarchical exploration planner from CMU's Team Explorer, which earned the most-sectors-explored award at the SubT final.
nodes.w: Well-documented, high-performing exploration planner that runs on top of a ready simulation stack.
nodes.h: Install the companion development environment first; ROS1 and ROS2 branches exist. Runs in sim on a laptop.

nodes.s: CMU ground-robot development environment with simulated worlds, terrain analysis, local planner and waypoint tools used for exploration research (TARE, FAR planner).
nodes.w: Fastest route to a GNSS-free autonomy demo: drop-in base for planners like TARE and FAR.
nodes.h: Download the Unity/Gazebo environment and run; the local planner and terrain analysis nodes are reusable standalone.

nodes.s: Visibility-graph route planner for known and unknown environments from the CMU SubT team.
nodes.w: Long-range routing companion to exploration planners in GNSS-denied environments.
nodes.h: Runs in the same CMU development environment.

nodes.s: Code for computing time-optimal quadrotor trajectories through waypoints, from the UZH group that placed second in AlphaPilot and built Swift.
nodes.w: Insight into how top drone-racing teams plan; transferable to fast inspection or reconnaissance flight planning.
nodes.h: Python/CasADi, offline only. Inactive since 2021.

nodes.s: Quadrotor simulator from UZH RPG with a decoupled Unity renderer and fast dynamics, aimed at RL and vision-based agile flight.
nodes.w: Simulation lineage behind UZH's drone-racing work; useful for training vision-based navigation without hardware.
nodes.h: Last updated 2024 and ROS1-oriented; expect dependency fixing. Unity renderer binaries are separate downloads.

nodes.s: PyTorch baselines and domain-bridging methods for spacecraft pose estimation on the SPEED+ dataset used in ESA Kelvins SPEC2021.
nodes.w: Open code tied to an ESA competition on vision-based relative navigation and sim-to-real gap.
nodes.h: Dataset download is large; start with a subset. Inactive since 2023. The code is MIT, but the SPEED+ dataset on the Stanford Digital Repository is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).

nodes.s: Cross-platform open-source chartplotter and navigation application that displays raster and S-57 vector charts, ingests GPS and AIS feeds, and runs waypoint routes. Large plugin ecosystem.
nodes.w: The de facto open maritime nav display; a ready-made situational awareness front end for any surface-vessel or GNSS-denied maritime demo.
nodes.h: Install the packaged build, feed it NMEA over UDP/TCP from your own nav filter or a simulator and you have a chart display in minutes. Writing a plugin needs the plugin SDK and a full C++ build.

nodes.s: OpenCPN plugin that connects to Navico and some Garmin and Raymarine marine radars and overlays radar imagery and ARPA-style targets on the chart.
nodes.w: Shows how real marine radar returns are pulled into an open nav display, useful for radar-aided navigation and contact tracking demos.
nodes.h: Needs a supported radar on the network to be interesting; without hardware, study the protocol decoding and overlay code.

nodes.s: Python library for decoding and encoding AIS NMEA sentences (AIVDM/AIVDO), including multi-part messages and streaming from sockets or files.
nodes.w: The quickest path from raw AIS sentences to typed vessel positions for maritime picture building or AIS spoofing/anomaly detection.
nodes.h: pip install pyais, point it at a public AIS TCP feed or a recorded NMEA file, and you have vessel tracks in an hour. Pair with AIS-catcher for live RF.

nodes.s: Pure-Python AIS decode and encode library from a long-time AIS researcher, with message definitions and utilities for working with NOAA and coastal AIS data.
nodes.w: A reference-quality alternative decoder, handy for cross-checking pyais output and for older message types.
nodes.h: Use mainly as a cross-check; pyais has the friendlier API.

nodes.s: AIS receiver and decoder for cheap SDRs (RTL-SDR, Airspy, HackRF, SDRplay, SoapySDR) with a built-in web map, JSON/NMEA output and feed sharing.
nodes.w: Turns a 30-dollar dongle into a live maritime picture sensor, the cheapest real RF input for a maritime awareness build.
nodes.h: Prebuilt binaries and Docker image; plug an RTL-SDR with a VHF antenna, run with the web viewer enabled, forward NMEA to pyais or OpenCPN. Inland sites may see few ships.

nodes.s: Node.js server implementing the Signal K open marine data standard: it ingests NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 and other boat buses and republishes everything as a JSON data model over REST and WebSocket, with a plugin ecosystem.
nodes.w: A modern data bus for a vessel; ideal glue between sensors, your own nav filter and displays.
nodes.h: Run via Docker or npm, enable the sample data playback, subscribe over WebSocket. Write a plugin to inject an alternative position source.

nodes.s: The JSON schema and specification for the Signal K marine data format covering navigation, environment, propulsion and other vessel data paths.
nodes.w: Gives a common vocabulary for maritime nav data instead of inventing one during a hackathon.
nodes.h: Read the navigation.* paths before designing your own message format.

nodes.s: Signal K server plugin that converts Signal K data back into NMEA 0183 sentences for legacy displays and autopilots.
nodes.w: Lets a custom position or heading source reach any off-the-shelf NMEA consumer such as OpenCPN or a chartplotter.
nodes.h: Enable in the Signal K admin UI, choose sentences, output over TCP.

nodes.s: Long-running autonomy middleware (MOOS) plus the IvP Helm behaviour-based multi-objective decision engine, used widely for autonomous marine vehicles, including COLREGs-aware collision avoidance behaviours.
nodes.w: The academic and navy-adjacent reference for marine vehicle autonomy; much published USV/UUV collision avoidance work is built on it.
nodes.h: Builds on Linux/macOS with CMake; the bundled alpha and heron missions run in simulation with pMarineViewer. Pair with the MIT 2.680 labs.

nodes.s: MOOS-IvP applications from a 2025 master's project at Universidade de Sao Paulo implementing COLREGs-compliant collision avoidance for USVs, including a modified A* planner, a velocity-obstacle method and a virtual-contact spawner for test encounters.
nodes.w: Recent, field-validated COLREGs avoidance code that plugs straight into MOOS-IvP.
nodes.h: Build against a MOOS-IvP tree; use pContactSpawn to stage head-on/crossing/overtaking cases. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default. The README says terms are 'specified in the repository' but none are.

nodes.s: Python framework from the NTNU Autoship centre for simulating and evaluating autonomous ship collision avoidance controllers, open-sourced in autumn 2025, with scenario generation and evaluation tooling.
nodes.w: One of the few open, evaluation-oriented COLAV simulators from a leading autonomous ship lab; good test bench for COLREGs logic.
nodes.h: Python with uv; define scenarios and swap in your own planner. Pair with its VIMMJIPDA tracker for realistic target estimates.

nodes.s: Interface that runs the VIMMJIPDA multi-target tracker (visibility, interacting multiple models, JIPDA) inside the NTNU colav-simulator; open-sourced November 2025.
nodes.w: A maritime-grade multi-target tracker connected to a collision avoidance loop, closing the sense-track-avoid chain.
nodes.h: Install with uv alongside colav-simulator; the VIMMJIPDA core tracker code is vendored in vimmjipda/code (also published on Code Ocean).

nodes.s: Collision avoidance simulator for COLREG-compliant autonomous ship navigation intended for use as a digital twin under varied weather and day/night conditions. Distributed only as a Windows binary release (v1.11); the repo holds no source code.
nodes.w: Another research testbed for COLREGs logic with environmental variation.
nodes.h: Binary only: download the v1.11 Windows release and run the .exe. Source is not published, so there are no build steps and nothing to modify or run on Linux. Little activity since 2023.

nodes.s: Gazebo-based simulation environment for the RobotX maritime autonomy competition, with a WAM-V USV model, waves, wind, sensors and scored tasks such as station keeping, wayfinding and perception.
nodes.w: Ready-made surface-vessel sim with nav and perception tasks; good for maritime autonomy demos.
nodes.h: Current branch targets gz-sim and ROS 2. Task worlds (station keeping, wayfinding) work as hackathon challenges out of the box.

nodes.s: Example Python code for talking to Water Linked DVLs over their serial and TCP/JSON protocols, parsing velocity and dead-reckoning reports.
nodes.w: DVL velocity is the core GNSS-free aid for underwater dead reckoning; this is the shortest route to real DVL data.
nodes.h: Archived by Water Linked and no longer maintained, but the serial (wldvl) and TCP parsers still work as examples. Needs a DVL or recorded JSON; protocol is simple JSON over TCP so a replay mock is easy. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.n: Water Linked DVL A50 ROS driver
nodes.s: ROS 1 driver publishing Water Linked DVL A50 velocity and beam data as ROS messages; now archived.
nodes.w: Reference ROS integration for DVL-aided navigation.
nodes.h: Archived; port the parsing to ROS 2 or use dvl-python directly (also archived). No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: Python library and examples for Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 scanning sonar using the Ping protocol.
nodes.w: Cheap altimeter and sonar input for underwater navigation and obstacle sensing.
nodes.h: pip install bluerobotics-ping; requires the hardware or Ping Viewer logs.

nodes.s: Desktop application to view and record data from Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 sonar.
nodes.w: Fast way to record sonar logs for offline SLAM or odometry experiments.
nodes.h: Prebuilt releases; logs can be replayed into ping-python.

nodes.s: ROS package that drives the Ping360 scanning sonar and publishes scans as images and laser-scan style messages.
nodes.w: Gets low-cost scanning sonar into a ROS SLAM or obstacle pipeline.
nodes.h: Needs the sonar; the laser-scan output plugs into standard 2D SLAM tools.

nodes.s: Gazebo-based underwater simulation environment from the Naval Postgraduate School and partners, extending UUV Simulator with DVL, sonar, bathymetry and manipulation models.
nodes.w: Navy-funded underwater sim with realistic DVL and sonar sensors for testing AUV nav without water.
nodes.h: ROS 1 Noetic + Gazebo 11 via Docker; setup is heavy, budget half a day. No push here since 2024-08; the ROS 2 port continues in the IOES-Lab/dave fork.

nodes.s: GPU (CUDA) multibeam sonar simulation plugin for Gazebo producing physically motivated sonar imagery.
nodes.w: Synthetic sonar data for testing sonar odometry and SLAM.
nodes.h: Needs an NVIDIA GPU; used within DAVE.

nodes.s: Gazebo/ROS packages for underwater vehicle simulation with hydrodynamics, thrusters and sensors; archived.
nodes.w: Many underwater-nav papers and DAVE build on it; useful for reference models.
nodes.h: Archived and tied to old ROS/Gazebo; use Stonefish or DAVE instead.

nodes.s: C++ simulation library for marine robotics with hydrodynamics, underwater rendering and sensors including DVL, USBL, multibeam and forward-looking sonar; has a ROS wrapper.
nodes.w: One of the few open sims with credible underwater nav sensors for AUV dead reckoning and sonar-based localization work.
nodes.h: Build with CMake; use stonefish_ros for ROS integration. Good for a DVL+USBL EKF demo.

nodes.s: ROS bridge for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal Engine based underwater simulator with DVL, IMU, depth, sonar and acoustic modem sensors.
nodes.w: Photo-realistic underwater sim with multi-agent acoustic comms, useful for cooperative AUV nav.
nodes.h: HoloOcean itself is not installed from PyPI (that package is an old 0.5.x): the source repo is only visible to a GitHub account linked to Epic Games, then pip install the client and run holoocean.install('Ocean') for the world package. The bridge is ROS 2 (Humble/Jazzy), Docker recommended. Needs a decent GPU.

nodes.s: C++ library and ROS 2 (Humble) node that simulates ultra-short baseline acoustic positioning measurements; a Gazebo plugin is only listed as a planned feature.
nodes.w: USBL is the main absolute fix for submerged vehicles; simulated USBL lets a team test an aided-INS filter.
nodes.h: ROS 2 colcon build; generate USBL fixes to fuse with DVL dead reckoning.

nodes.s: Work-in-progress AUV state estimator fusing DVL, IMU and barometer two ways, a 15-state EKF and a GTSAM factor graph with custom DVL and barometer factors, with ROS 1 (Kinetic/Melodic, Python 2.7) wrappers.
nodes.w: Small, readable DVL-aided INS example to start a GNSS-free underwater nav filter from.
nodes.h: Dormant since 2021; treat as a starting template, not a dependency. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: Localization and SLAM components for the SMARC AUVs (KTH), including EKF localization with IMU, DVL and multibeam sonar against a feature map.
nodes.w: Research AUV navigation from a Swedish maritime robotics centre, showing map-aided underwater localization.
nodes.h: Fork of smarc-project/smarc_navigation frozen in 2021; the upstream was updated until 2024, so start there. ROS 1 era; read for architecture.

nodes.s: Underwater SLAM for robots with multibeam imaging sonar, from Stevens Institute research on BlueROV-class vehicles, combining sonar feature extraction and pose-graph optimization.
nodes.w: One of the more complete open sonar SLAM pipelines; directly relevant to GNSS-free underwater navigation.
nodes.h: ROS 1 with sample bags; budget time for dependencies.

nodes.s: BlueROV underwater SLAM and exploration code from Stevens Institute, combining sonar-based SLAM with active exploration planning.
nodes.w: Predecessor to sonar-SLAM; shows SLAM-driven exploration underwater.
nodes.h: Dormant since 2020.

nodes.s: Direct imaging sonar odometry: estimates vehicle motion directly from forward-looking imaging sonar frames without feature extraction.
nodes.w: Sonar odometry is a key aid when DVL bottom-lock or vision fails in turbid water.
nodes.h: C++ with ROS; try on the provided datasets first.

nodes.s: Guidance, navigation and control software from NTNU's student Vortex team for competition AUVs and ROVs, built on ROS 2.
nodes.w: A complete, actively maintained student AUV GNC stack to borrow structure from.
nodes.h: ROS 2 workspace; sim integration via their companion repos.

nodes.s: Meta-repository for Autoware, the open-source ROS 2 autonomous driving stack covering localization (NDT, EKF), perception, planning and control.
nodes.w: The biggest open ground-vehicle autonomy stack; its localization modules are a mature map-based alternative when GNSS is degraded.
