nodes.h: Heavy: use the Docker images and the planning simulator. For a hackathon, lift single packages such as NDT scan matcher or the EKF localizer.

nodes.s: The broad package collection of Autoware with experimental and production-candidate modules, including localization add-ons such as YabLoc, landmark-based localizers and the pose estimator arbiter.
nodes.w: Holds Autoware's extra localization modules; the core NDT scan matcher and EKF localizer have moved to autoware_core.
nodes.h: Pick packages and run them standalone with rosbags; autoware_ndt_scan_matcher and autoware_ekf_localizer now live in autoware_core, not here.

nodes.s: Unity-based digital-twin simulator for Autoware with simulated lidar, camera, GNSS and IMU.
nodes.w: Lets a team exercise Autoware localization without a car.
nodes.h: Prebuilt binaries for Ubuntu with an NVIDIA GPU. Licence is split: code Apache-2.0, but assets (including release content) are CC BY-NC, so non-commercial use only, and the docs may not be publicly re-hosted.

nodes.s: Baidu's open autonomous driving platform, including the multi-sensor fusion localization module combining GNSS RTK, IMU and lidar map matching.
nodes.w: Its MSF localization design is a well-documented reference for GNSS/INS/lidar fusion in vehicles.
nodes.h: Very heavy to build; read the localization module docs and code rather than deploy.

nodes.s: C++ library and ROS integration for multi-layer 2.5D grid maps, widely used for elevation and traversability mapping.
nodes.w: Standard data structure for terrain-aware off-road navigation.
nodes.h: apt install ros-<distro>-grid-map; convert DEMs or point clouds to layers quickly.

nodes.s: Robot-centric elevation mapping for rough terrain navigation, started at ETH Zurich and now maintained by ANYbotics, that fuses range data into a probabilistic 2.5D map. This entry is the leggedrobotics fork of ANYbotics/elevation_mapping.
nodes.w: Classic baseline for terrain mapping on legged and wheeled robots.
nodes.h: ROS 1; this fork is dormant since 2022, while upstream ANYbotics/elevation_mapping was updated in 2024. Prefer the GPU version.

nodes.s: GPU-accelerated elevation and traversability mapping from ETH Zurich, supporting semantic layers and learned traversability, used on ANYmal robots.
nodes.w: Terrain-aware planning for off-road robots needs a live elevation and traversability map; this is the modern GPU version.
nodes.h: Needs CUDA; Docker image available. Feed a depth camera or lidar and get a traversability layer.

nodes.s: ETH package that computes traversability from elevation maps using slope, roughness and step-height filters.
nodes.w: Simple, explainable geometric traversability baseline.
nodes.h: ROS 1, dormant; reimplement the filters with grid_map.

nodes.s: System that learns visual traversability online from pre-trained vision features and robot self-supervision, deployed on legged robots in forests.
nodes.w: Learned traversability that adapts in minutes, relevant for unstructured off-road nav.
nodes.h: Needs a GPU and a camera bag; offline demo scripts help.

nodes.s: Self-supervised traversability prediction for wheeled field robots that learns from RGB-D, with labels from kinodynamic traction estimates. The repo holds only the network models, one training notebook and a dataset download link; the traction estimator and navigation stack are not included.
nodes.w: Agricultural/field traversability learning without hand labels.
nodes.h: Dormant; use for method reference. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: Gymnasium-based PyTorch simulator for benchmarking off-road navigation planners under uncertain, probabilistic traversability, with synthetic terrain generation.
nodes.w: Lightweight way to compare off-road planners without a robot.
nodes.h: Docker setup via make build-gpu or build-cpu, or pip install from the clone (not on PyPI); fetch the dataset and models with scripts/download_dataset_and_model.sh, then run the tutorial notebooks. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: Multi-modal off-road dataset from Texas A&M with lidar, camera, IMU and GNSS plus semantic annotations collected on a ground robot.
nodes.w: A standard benchmark for off-road perception and localization.
nodes.h: Download only the sequences you need; ROS bags are large. Unmaintained since 2022; the data itself is static and still usable. Data and code are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, so non-commercial use only.

nodes.s: Tools and utilities for the TartanDrive off-road driving dataset from CMU's AirLab, recorded on an ATV with multi-modal sensors.
nodes.w: Large-scale off-road vehicle dynamics and perception data for learning traversability.
nodes.h: Data is large; use the provided loaders and a subset.

nodes.s: Autonomy stack for a small-scale high-speed off-road vehicle from the UW MuSHR group, with BeamNG simulator integration and Jetson Orin deployment.
nodes.w: Affordable off-road platform with sim-to-real tooling.
nodes.h: Docker-based install; real hardware optional. BeamNG license needed for sim.

nodes.s: Firmware for Bitcraze Loco Positioning UWB anchors and tags (DW1000), supporting two-way ranging and TDoA modes.
nodes.w: Off-the-shelf UWB infrastructure for GNSS-denied indoor positioning tests.
nodes.h: Needs Loco nodes; configure anchors with the Crazyflie client.

nodes.s: Minimal simulation models and tooling for Crazyflie in Webots and Gazebo; the README says it is not actively maintained and not realistic in dynamics.
nodes.w: Hardware-free swarm prototyping.
nodes.h: Webots is the easiest entry.

nodes.s: Czech Technical University's multi-robot UAV platform with control, estimation (including GNSS-denied modes), planning and simulation, field-tested in outdoor swarm deployments.
nodes.w: Mature outdoor-swarm stack with several localization back-ends to choose from.
nodes.h: Install via apt; simulation tutorials are good. Moving between ROS 1 and ROS 2 versions, so check the branch.

nodes.s: Mutual relative localization for UAV swarms using blinking ultraviolet LEDs and UV-sensitive cameras, from CTU MRS.
nodes.w: Radio-silent relative localization, attractive when RF is jammed or must stay off.
nodes.h: Needs special UV hardware for real use; simulated in the MRS Gazebo setup.

nodes.s: Domain-specific programming language for robot swarms with swarm-level primitives such as neighbour queries, virtual stigmergy and swarm membership.
nodes.w: Expresses swarm behaviours compactly; used with ROS and drones in MIST Lab research.
nodes.h: Builds cleanly; bindings to real robots require extra work.

nodes.s: ROS 2 package providing a library of swarm behaviours (aggregation, dispersion, flocking) and an easy-to-extend framework, tested on TurtleBot-class robots.
nodes.w: Ready-made ground swarm behaviours in ROS 2.
nodes.h: Launch in Gazebo with multiple TurtleBots. Not maintained any more (README); branches target ROS 2 Dashing, Foxy and Galactic.

nodes.s: Sparse, decentralized collaborative SLAM for multi-robot systems on ROS 2, supporting lidar, stereo and RGB-D with inter-robot loop closures under limited communication.
nodes.w: Shared map and relative localization across a team without central infrastructure.
nodes.h: ROS 2 with heavy deps; try on the provided datasets before robots.

nodes.s: Distributed collaborative lidar SLAM for robotic swarms with lightweight LiDAR-Iris descriptors for inter-robot place recognition and minimal data exchange.
nodes.w: Low-bandwidth multi-robot lidar mapping.
nodes.h: ROS 1 package; test with multi-robot bags.

nodes.s: Placeholder repo: it only holds a README pointing to zhongshp/Co-LRIO, where the code lives. CoLRIO is ROS 2 centralized lidar-ranging-inertial state estimation for robotic swarms that offloads optimization to a server and uses UWB inter-robot ranges (ICRA 2024).
nodes.w: Shows how UWB ranging tightens swarm state estimation when GNSS is out.
nodes.h: Use zhongshp/Co-LRIO (Apache-2.0, C++). ROS 2 Foxy and GTSAM 4.2a8; build is sensitive to versions.

nodes.s: Index repo for Kimera-Multi, a distributed multi-robot metric-semantic SLAM system with robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
nodes.w: Multi-robot mapping with peer-to-peer communication is core to swarm and team operations.
nodes.h: Multi-repo install; budget a full day. Use their datasets for a demo.

nodes.s: Decentralized omnidirectional visual-inertial-UWB state estimation for aerial swarms from HKUST, combining VIO, UWB ranges and map-based place recognition.
nodes.w: Shows fusing UWB ranging with VIO for drift-bounded relative swarm localization.
nodes.h: Dormant since 2022; superseded by D2SLAM.

nodes.s: Decentralized and distributed collaborative visual-inertial SLAM for aerial swarms from HKUST.
nodes.w: Swarm-scale relative localization and mapping for UAV teams.
nodes.h: Needs a CUDA GPU and the provided Docker images; runs on a quad fisheye rig, RealSense stereo or TUM datasets. Study rather than deploy.

nodes.s: Decentralized multi-quadrotor extension of EGO-Planner with inter-agent collision avoidance and trajectory sharing over a network.
nodes.w: Open reference for drone swarms that coordinate paths without a central server, relevant to contested comms scenarios.
nodes.h: Simulation launches many drones on one machine; trajectory broadcast assumes reliable comms - an interesting knob to degrade in a hackathon.

nodes.s: ROS library fusing UWB ranging with IMU for accurate 3D localization of MAV swarms, used in a 2017 drone light show.
nodes.w: Compact UWB+IMU fusion reference.
nodes.h: ROS 1 and dormant since 2018.

nodes.s: Infrastructure-less relative localization for decentralized swarm formation of nano-drones using UWB ranging (IROS 2023).
nodes.w: Relative positioning without anchors, the realistic case for field swarms.
nodes.h: The repo holds only a Python demo of the algorithm (demo.py) and a PDF supplement; no Crazyflie or UWB firmware is included.

nodes.s: FreeRTOS UWB library for DW1000 on Crazyflie providing double-sided two-way ranging and UWB data messaging between drones.
nodes.w: Peer-to-peer ranging building block for anchor-free relative localization.
nodes.h: Flash as Crazyflie app; ranging between two nodes in a few lines. Fork of iGNSS/uwb-software-library, tested against a pinned crazyflie-firmware commit. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default.

nodes.s: Lightweight STM32 drone control and multi-agent localization system combining a flight controller, UWB relative localization and a monitor tool.
nodes.w: Low-cost hardware+software reference for UWB relative swarm localization.
nodes.h: Custom hardware; dormant since 2023.

nodes.s: Dataset and scripts for UWB time-difference-of-arrival measurements from Bitcraze's Loco Positioning System, collected by University of Toronto.
nodes.w: Real UWB data for testing ranging-based estimators without hardware.
nodes.h: Download and run the provided EKF example as a baseline. Unmaintained since 2021; the data itself is static and still usable.

nodes.s: Track-oriented multi-hypothesis multi-target tracker in Python developed for maritime radar tracking research.
nodes.w: Compact MHT implementation for comparison against Stone Soup.
nodes.h: Dormant; useful as a readable algorithm reference.

nodes.s: Simple Python library for tracking-by-detection multi-object tracking with Kalman filters and IoU/feature association.
nodes.w: Fast, minimal tracker to sit behind a drone detector in a demo.
nodes.h: pip install motpy; a few lines to track YOLO boxes.

nodes.s: Pluggable collection of modern multi-object trackers (ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, OC-SORT, StrongSORT and others) for detector outputs, in Python and C++.
nodes.w: Drop-in visual tracking for camera-based drone detection.
nodes.h: pip install boxmot and wrap your detector; pick ByteTrack for speed.

nodes.s: ECCV 2022 multi-object tracker that associates both high- and low-confidence detections, improving tracking through occlusion.
nodes.w: Strong baseline for tracking small, intermittently detected drones in video.
nodes.h: Use via BoxMOT or Ultralytics tracker configs rather than the original training code.

nodes.s: Widely used Python package for YOLO-family detection, segmentation and tracking with training, export to edge runtimes and built-in trackers.
nodes.w: Fastest route to a custom vision drone detector trained on Anti-UAV or similar data.
nodes.h: pip install ultralytics; fine-tune on a drone dataset in hours with a GPU. Check AGPL licensing for deployment.

nodes.s: Official repository of the Anti-UAV challenge and benchmark for detecting and tracking UAVs in RGB and thermal infrared video, with dataset links (Anti-UAV300/410/600) and baselines.
nodes.w: The main public benchmark for vision-based C-UAS tracking, including thermal.
nodes.h: Download a subset, train a YOLO detector plus tracker, report on their metric.

nodes.s: Code and configs for benchmarking drone detection and tracking across Anti-UAV, Drone-vs-Bird and MAV-VID datasets, including format converters.
nodes.w: Saves time on dataset wrangling for a vision C-UAS comparison.
nodes.h: Use the COCO conversion scripts first. No LICENSE file, so all rights reserved by default. The three datasets keep their own terms.

nodes.s: Lua Wireshark dissector that decodes Remote ID broadcast frames over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
nodes.w: Debugging aid for Remote ID sniffers.
nodes.h: Drop the Lua into the Wireshark plugin folder.

nodes.s: ESP32 Remote ID receiver built on opendroneid-core-c and a fork of sxjack's electronic ID classes.
nodes.w: Ten-dollar Remote ID sensor node.
nodes.h: PlatformIO project for VS Code (not the Arduino IDE), developed on a TTGO ESP32 board with a 1.14-inch LCD; it shows lat/lon of one UAV on the display.

nodes.s: Documentation hub for WarDragon, an SDR-based RF sensing appliance for drone detection; open components are documented here, while commercial kits add closed features.
nodes.w: Useful architecture reference for a low-cost RF C-UAS sensor.
nodes.h: Docs only; follow links to the open component repos.

nodes.s: GNU Radio based scanner that checks known analog FPV video frequencies for energy and publishes alerts over ZMQ; the optional confirmation detector is closed source.
nodes.w: Simple, explainable RF detection of FPV drones, a growing threat class.
nodes.h: Needs GNU Radio 3.10, gr-inspector and an SDR such as Pluto.

nodes.s: Decodes DJI DroneID (OcuSync 2.0) frames from SDR I/Q recordings, building on proto17's reverse engineering and Kismet.
nodes.w: Recovers DJI drone and pilot location telemetry from RF, filling the gap for drones without standard Remote ID.
nodes.h: Needs high-rate I/Q captures; decoding is slow with interference.

nodes.s: Original reverse engineering of DJI DroneID with MATLAB/Octave scripts that demodulate frames, C++ turbo-code helpers and a GNU Radio correlation test flowgraph.
nodes.w: Foundational work behind open DJI DroneID decoders.
nodes.h: Use for understanding the PHY; prefer samples2djidroneid for decoding.

nodes.s: Code for the RFUAV benchmark dataset for UAV detection and identification from RF signals, using a two-stage STFT spectrogram detection and classification model.
nodes.w: Recent learned RF drone classification with a public dataset.
nodes.h: Start from the provided spectrogram models; raw data size is large.

nodes.s: LabVIEW programs to record RF signals plus MATLAB and Python code for drone detection and identification, accompanying the DroneRF dataset (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0).
nodes.w: Widely cited RF detection baseline.
nodes.h: Dormant since 2021; good for a quick baseline classifier.

nodes.s: Open-source acoustic drone detector that listens for propeller noise; explicitly detection and alerting only.
nodes.w: Acoustic sensing covers drones that emit no RF, such as fibre-optic FPVs.
nodes.h: Breadboard build guide; new project, verify claims on your own recordings.

nodes.s: Low-cost edge-only acoustic drone detector on ESP32-S3 with encrypted LoRa or Ethernet alerting.
nodes.w: Cheap distributed acoustic sensor network for perimeter awareness.
nodes.h: ESP-IDF build; tune thresholds per site.

nodes.s: Python package that aligns an estimated trajectory with ground truth from CSV files, associates timestamps and reports position/attitude error metrics, including NEES from pose covariance.
nodes.w: Consistency checks (NEES) matter as much as RMSE when judging a GNSS-denied filter; this tool computes both from plain CSV.
nodes.h: pip install cnspy-trajectory-evaluation; estimated CSV must carry pose covariance. Use evo for quick plots, this when you need filter consistency.

nodes.s: End-to-end structure-from-motion pipeline built on GTSAM, with pluggable front-ends (classical and learned matchers) and distributed execution via Dask.
nodes.w: Builds georeferenceable 3D maps from drone or ground imagery, which can serve as prior maps for visual localization.
nodes.h: No compilation: `uv tool install .` (or `pip install .` in Python 3.12) from a recursive checkout, then `gtsfm run` opens a browser workspace with sample scenes; `gtsfm execute` is the CLI path for your own image folders. Expect long runtimes on large sets - downsample.

nodes.s: Toolkit for NMEA 2000 networks: a PGN decoder/analyzer plus utilities to read, write and convert N2K and NMEA 0183 messages, used largely for reverse-engineering marine bus traffic.
nodes.w: Gives raw access to ship sensor buses (GNSS, heading, AIS, depth), useful for maritime nav integrity monitoring and spoofing detection research.
nodes.h: Build analyzer and pipe candump/actisense logs through it to JSON. Needs a CAN or N2K gateway for live data; sample logs work offline.

nodes.s: Modern C++17 library of Monte Carlo Localization algorithms with a ROS 2 node that is a drop-in replacement for the Nav2 AMCL package.
nodes.w: Map-based particle-filter localization for ground robots operating without GNSS; easier to extend than legacy AMCL.
nodes.h: Swap beluga_amcl for nav2_amcl in a Nav2 launch file; same parameters. Good base for adding custom sensor models.

nodes.s: Real-world GNSS interference recordings from Jammertest 2025 at Andoya, Norway, covering jamming, spoofing, meaconing and multi-emitter scenarios, with metadata for classification, characterization and direction finding.
nodes.w: Rare open real-world interference data from live jamming trials, suited to training and testing interference detectors and classifiers.
nodes.h: Data is chunked HDF5 under dataset/ (Git LFS; the README points to an identical GitLab mirror for the full download) plus train/test split lists. There are no loader modules - the README only gives an h5py inspection snippet, so budget time to write your own loader before building a jamming/spoofing classifier on one scenario class.

nodes.n: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (2nd ed.) code
nodes.s: Companion code for the second edition of Gao Xiang's visual SLAM textbook: Lie groups, nonlinear optimization, feature VO, direct methods, back-end and loop closure examples in C++.
nodes.w: One of the most-used hands-on routes into visual SLAM internals; good for bringing a team up to speed fast.
nodes.h: Each chapter builds standalone; dependency versions (Pangolin, Sophus, g2o) are old - use the bundled 3rdparty or a Docker image.

nodes.s: University of Colorado Boulder collection of MATLAB software-defined GNSS receiver code-bases, organized per constellation (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou), with linked sample data sets.
nodes.w: Teaching-grade multi-constellation receivers you can read end to end, from acquisition to tracking and navigation.
nodes.h: Point the settings file at one of the provided IQ data sets and run. MATLAB licence required; slow on long recordings.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial estimator that fuses raw GNSS pseudorange and Doppler with VIO in a factor graph, giving drift-free global poses and smooth local tracking.
nodes.w: Shows how raw GNSS measurements degrade gracefully into VIO when satellites are blocked, a core pattern for contested or urban PNT.
nodes.h: ROS1 (Melodic/Noetic) only; run on the GVINS dataset bags. Porting to ROS 2 is non-trivial.

nodes.s: Joan Sola's MATLAB SLAM toolbox with EKF-SLAM (`ekf` branch) and graph-SLAM (`graph` branch) variants, landmark parameterizations (points, lines, inverse depth) and simulated or real sensor support, written for teaching and prototyping.
nodes.w: Readable reference for EKF-SLAM landmark handling, by the author of the widely cited Lie theory and quaternion kinematics notes.
nodes.h: Runs in MATLAB with simulated worlds out of the box; not maintained, use for understanding rather than deployment.

nodes.s: ROS framework for sensor fusion as factor-graph optimization: plugin sensor models, motion models and publishers on top of Ceres, supporting both smoothing and fixed-lag estimation.
nodes.w: A more flexible alternative to robot_localization EKF when you need delayed measurements, robust losses or custom constraints.
nodes.h: Use the fuse tutorials or the ROSCon UK 2025 workshop Docker image; plugin config in YAML. Ceres dependency builds slowly.

nodes.s: Materials for an eight-task ROS 2 state estimation workshop at ROSCon UK 2025, with a Docker image, recorded bags and step-by-step exercises using robot_localization and fuse.
nodes.w: Ready-made, containerized curriculum for wiring wheel odometry, IMU and GNSS into a ROS 2 estimator.
nodes.h: docker compose run with the provided compose file; work through tasks in order. Fastest way to get a fused ROS 2 pose estimate running.

nodes.s: TypeScript/JavaScript renderer for MIL-STD-2525 (D and later) military symbology, producing single-point and multi-point tactical graphics for web maps.
nodes.w: Standard-conformant symbols are the expected visual language for any common operational picture or C2 demo.
nodes.h: npm package; render SIDC codes to SVG/canvas and drop onto Leaflet/Cesium/OpenLayers layers. Multi-point graphics need control-point ordering per the standard.

nodes.s: Pointer repo for the ROS bag files used in MIT's Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles course exercises.
nodes.w: Supplies the datasets that make the VNAV labs runnable outside MIT.
nodes.h: Only a README with a download link; fetch bags alongside VNAV-labs.

nodes.s: Lab assignments for MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles: ROS, 3D geometry, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, VIO and place recognition.
nodes.w: A structured, graded path from ROS basics to visual-inertial navigation, built by the SPARK lab behind Kimera.
nodes.h: Labs assume Ubuntu + ROS; pick individual labs (feature tracking, two-view geometry) as warm-ups.

nodes.s: Motion planning framework for ROS 2 manipulators: kinematics, collision checking, planners (OMPL, Pilz, STOMP) and real-time servoing.
nodes.w: Relevant when a vehicle carries an arm or gimbal-like mechanism; outside pure navigation but the ROS 2 standard for manipulation planning.
nodes.h: Binary install via apt; use the MoveIt Setup Assistant for a new robot. Overkill unless your platform has an arm.

nodes.s: Official test catalog and plan for Jammertest, Norway's annual live GNSS jamming and spoofing event, maintained by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration.
nodes.w: The reference for which interference scenarios were transmitted when, needed to label any Jammertest recording.
nodes.h: Use the per-year plan to map timestamps in Jammertest datasets to emitted scenarios.

nodes.s: ROS 2 package wrapping NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated cuVSLAM for stereo visual(-inertial) odometry and SLAM on Jetson and x86 GPUs.
nodes.w: Real-time VIO on embedded Jetson hardware with low CPU load, a practical GNSS-denied odometry source for drones and UGVs.
nodes.h: Use the Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense or ZED stereo works out of the box. Jetson Orin recommended.

nodes.s: Tutorial packages referenced by docs.nav2.org: example planner, controller and behavior-tree plugins, SLAM and GPS waypoint following setups.
nodes.w: Shortest path to custom Nav2 plugins and GPS-based outdoor navigation in ROS 2.
nodes.h: Clone into a ROS 2 workspace matching your distro branch; the GPS waypoint follower demo runs in Gazebo.

nodes.s: Release repo for the SLAM Handbook (Cambridge University Press), edited by Carlone, Kim, Barfoot, Cremers and Dellaert, published incrementally in three parts from late 2024.
nodes.w: Current, expert-written reference covering factor graphs through spatial AI; free drafts for the whole team.
nodes.h: Download chapter PDFs from the release page; factor-graph chapter is the best starting point.

nodes.s: University of Vaasa public GNSS dataset recorded at Jammertest 2024, released in batches from autumn 2025 under a Finland-NSF project on secure satellite navigation.
nodes.w: Second independent real-world interference dataset, useful for cross-dataset validation of detectors.
nodes.h: Check README for which batches are released; pair with the Jammertest plan for labels.

nodes.s: Simultaneous Trajectory Estimation and Mapping engine from UTIAS: a C++ nonlinear least-squares library with continuous-time Gaussian-process trajectory priors on Lie groups.
nodes.w: Continuous-time estimation handles asynchronous, motion-distorted sensors such as spinning radar and lidar.
nodes.h: Library, not an application; see steam_icp for a ready odometry pipeline built on it.

nodes.s: NASA JPL's LangChain-based AI agent that lets operators query and command ROS 1 and ROS 2 systems in natural language through a set of ROS introspection and control tools.
nodes.w: A credible, lab-backed reference for putting an LLM in the loop of a robot stack, with tool boundaries an operator can audit.
nodes.h: pip install jpl-rosa; demo runs against turtlesim in Docker. Add custom tools for your MAVROS/Nav2 topics.

nodes.s: Model Context Protocol server that exposes ROS topics, services and parameters (via rosbridge) to LLM clients such as Claude or GPT, for ROS 1 and ROS 2.
nodes.w: Fastest way to let an LLM inspect and drive an existing robot without changing robot code.
nodes.h: Run rosbridge on the robot and point the MCP client config at the server; works with sim (Gazebo/Isaac). Add safety limits before anything flies.

nodes.s: Standalone demos for driving robots with natural language through the ROS MCP server: a Tugbot in a Gazebo warehouse, a Unitree Go2 with the CHAMP controller, a PX4 drone via MAVROS (Gazebo and real hardware) and TurtleBot3 in Ignition Gazebo.
nodes.w: Worked examples shorten the path from install to a talking robot demo.
nodes.h: Each sub-folder is a self-contained project with its own README; the PX4 demo (takeoff, patterns, orbit, RTL via MAVROS) is the most relevant. Run one demo end to end before customizing the server.

nodes.s: MCP server that lets AI agents discover and operate ROS 2 robots: topic echo/publish, services, actions and introspection, implemented natively in ROS 2 rather than through rosbridge.
nodes.w: Native ROS 2 alternative for LLM control without a rosbridge hop.
nodes.h: Fastest path is the Docker image (wisevision/ros2_mcp:jazzy or :humble) as the MCP client's stdio command - ROS 2 does not need to be installed on the host. Start with ROS2_MCP_READONLY=1 so the agent can inspect but not publish.

nodes.s: ROS 2 MCP server from the Lincoln Centre for Autonomous Systems: tools to list and echo topics, inspect message/service/action interfaces, fetch camera images for VLM analysis and send simple drive commands, plus canned analysis prompts. Runs as a ROS 2 package or via Docker Compose (SSE on port 8000).
nodes.w: University-maintained option for agricultural/field robot agent experiments.
nodes.h: Smaller project; compare with ros-mcp-server before committing.

nodes.s: MCP server bridging an LLM to a drone over MAVLink, exposing arming, takeoff, waypoint and telemetry tools via MAVSDK.
nodes.w: Direct template for a natural-language drone mission interface on PX4/ArduPilot SITL.
nodes.h: Pair with PX4 or ArduPilot SITL; never point at a real vehicle without geofence and human confirm.

nodes.s: MCP server for flying ArduPilot vehicles from AI agents over MAVLink, covering missions, camera vision and SITL workflows.
nodes.w: Another ready LLM-to-autopilot bridge, oriented to ArduPilot missions.
nodes.h: Young project; test thoroughly in SITL.

nodes.s: SITL-first MCP server for talking to ArduPilot vehicles over MAVLink, with explicit safety gating of commands.
nodes.w: Its safety-gate design is a useful pattern for keeping an LLM from issuing unsafe flight commands.
nodes.h: `pipx install ardupilot-mavlink-mcp`, point it at SITL (tcp:127.0.0.1:5760). Read-only by default; arming needs `--enable-actuation`, and real (non-loopback) links also need `--allow-real-vehicle`. Its prearm-diagnosis and single-reader-thread design are worth copying.

nodes.s: MCP server plus QGIS plugin that lets an LLM create projects, load layers, run processing algorithms and execute PyQGIS code in QGIS Desktop.
nodes.w: Natural-language GIS analysis for terrain, route and coverage products in a mission-planning demo.
nodes.h: Install the plugin, start the socket server in QGIS, add the MCP server to the client. Arbitrary code execution - sandbox it.

nodes.s: MCP bridge that lets AI agents drive QGIS Desktop: a QGIS plugin runs a TCP socket server inside QGIS and a FastMCP server exposes about 125 tools (layers, feature editing, processing, rendering, styling, layouts/atlas, cross-layer SQL). Supports QGIS 3.28 to 4.x; the plugin installs from the QGIS plugin manager and the server runs via uvx.
nodes.w: More recent alternative if the original QGIS MCP lags behind QGIS releases.
nodes.h: Same plugin-plus-server pattern; check QGIS version compatibility.

nodes.s: MCP server giving LLMs geospatial operations through Shapely, PyProj, GeoPandas and Rasterio: geometry ops, CRS transforms, distances and raster analysis, without a desktop GIS.
nodes.w: Headless geodesy/GIS tool layer an agent can call for coordinate conversion and spatial reasoning.
nodes.h: pip install gis-mcp; no QGIS needed. Good for an agent that must reason about coordinates and areas.

nodes.s: Research prototype of an LLM-driven 'autonomous GIS' that turns a spatial question into a solution graph, generates code and executes the analysis to return maps and numbers.
nodes.w: Early worked example of LLM planning over geospatial workflows, a building block for agentic mission planning.
nodes.h: Notebook-driven; needs an LLM API key. Use as design reference rather than a dependency.

nodes.s: LLM-based robot control framework: an OpenAI model turns a natural-language request plus a YOLO scene description into a short Python plan built from the robot's registered skills, which is then executed. Ships wrappers for a virtual webcam robot, DJI Tello, Unitree Go2 and Petoi.
nodes.w: Shows how to constrain LLM output into a small, verifiable command language for drones, cutting latency and risk.
nodes.h: `pip install -e .`, add an OpenAI key and run `typefly-run`; the default virtual robot uses a webcam, so no hardware is needed. A Tello needs both a Wi-Fi and an ethernet adapter. Swap in a MAVSDK-based robot wrapper to target PX4.

nodes.s: Microsoft's collection of prompts and an AirSim-based ChatGPT drone simulator accompanying the 'ChatGPT for Robotics' work.
nodes.w: Classic starting point for prompting LLMs to produce drone control code in simulation.
nodes.h: No longer updated and AirSim itself is archived; mine the prompts, run elsewhere.

nodes.s: Framework for natural-language interaction with ROS robots, letting an LLM call robot functions and chain behaviors.
nodes.w: Earlier ROS-native LLM integration; useful comparison to MCP-based designs.
nodes.h: Not updated since 2023; prefer ROSA or the MCP servers for new work.

nodes.s: Platform for outdoor aerial vision-language navigation: multi-engine simulators (UE, GTA V, Google Earth, 3DGS), automated data collection toolchain, a large benchmark and a keyframe-aware VLN model.
nodes.w: Largest open aerial VLN benchmark, for agents that fly to places described in words.
nodes.h: Heavy downloads and GPU; use the released dataset with the baseline model rather than regenerating data.

nodes.s: Benchmark and simulator (AirSim/UE-based) for vision-and-language navigation by UAVs in city-scale environments, with baseline agents.
nodes.w: The first widely used aerial VLN benchmark; baseline for language-commanded drone navigation.
nodes.h: Large simulator assets; plan download time. Linux + GPU.

nodes.s: Language-goal aerial navigation dataset over real-city 3D point clouds with geographic information, plus baselines that use map-based landmark grounding.
nodes.w: Links language goals to real geography, close to how operators describe destinations.
nodes.h: Dataset plus training code; GPU needed for baselines.

nodes.s: Scalable benchmark and platform for long-horizon UAV vision-language navigation built from satellite imagery (NeurIPS 2026 Datasets track).
nodes.w: Satellite-imagery grounding matches what a real UAV can carry as a prior map, so results transfer better to GNSS-denied ops.
nodes.h: New release; check README for data availability before planning around it.

nodes.s: UAV vision-language navigation method that feeds high-resolution front and downward views plus a coarse 3D target direction, updated online, into waypoint prediction for precise see-and-reach flight. Releases the UAV-VLN-FOV benchmark (2,717 trajectories, seen/unseen-object/unseen-scene splits), code and weights; runs in AirSim with TravelUAV environments.
nodes.w: Recent aerial VLN method to compare against benchmark baselines.
nodes.h: Research code; reproduce only if you need a SOTA aerial VLN baseline.

nodes.s: PyTorch toolbox for embodied navigation on Habitat and Isaac Sim, covering vision-language navigation (VLN-CE and continuous-trajectory VLN) and point, image or trajectory goal navigation, with 10+ baselines, 6 benchmarks, the InternData-N1 dataset and the InternVLA-N1 dual-system model.
nodes.w: Brings recent VLA-style navigation models into one toolkit.
nodes.h: Large models and simulators; use the provided checkpoints.

nodes.s: Evaluation code for NaVid and Uni-NaVid, video-based VLMs that plan the next navigation step from monocular RGB history in continuous VLN environments.
nodes.w: Shows map-free, camera-only language navigation, relevant when maps and GNSS are unavailable.
nodes.h: Requires Habitat and large checkpoints; evaluation only.

nodes.s: Code and checkpoints for general visual navigation foundation models (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD) that drive robots from camera images toward image goals or explore, with ROS deployment code.
nodes.w: Pretrained camera-only navigation policies that run on small robots, a ready learned navigation baseline.
nodes.h: Deploy NoMaD on a Jetson-class robot with a fisheye camera; topological graph from a teleop run.

nodes.s: Code for LM-Nav, which composes a language model, CLIP and a visual navigation model to follow natural-language route instructions without language-annotated robot data.
nodes.w: Early demonstration of building language navigation from off-the-shelf pretrained parts.
nodes.h: Mostly notebook-level; read for the architecture.

nodes.s: Builds visual-language maps by fusing pretrained visual-language features into a 3D reconstruction, enabling open-vocabulary landmark navigation from natural language.
nodes.w: Language-queryable maps are a natural interface for operators tasking robots.
nodes.h: Habitat-based data; GPU needed for feature extraction.

nodes.s: Builds open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs from RGB-D by associating 2D foundation-model detections across views, then lets an LLM plan over the graph.
nodes.w: Object-level semantic maps an LLM can reason about, useful for tasking and situational awareness.
nodes.h: Heavy dependencies (SAM, CLIP, GroundingDINO); start from Replica examples.

nodes.s: Purely LLM-based vision-and-language navigation agent that reasons explicitly over textual observations to choose actions (AAAI 2024).
nodes.w: Readable baseline for LLM reasoning in navigation, with prompts you can adapt.
nodes.h: Needs an LLM API and R2R/Matterport data.

nodes.s: Multi-robot exploration and object search where an LLM assigns frontier goals to robots from a merged semantic map.
nodes.w: LLM as a multi-agent tasker, a pattern for swarm search missions.
nodes.h: Habitat simulation; adapt the goal-assignment prompt for your own swarm sim.

nodes.s: Python implementation (one 9-state script, plus ESP32 logger firmware) of a foot-mounted INS with EKF and zero-velocity updates for pedestrian dead reckoning, with sample datasets from two foot-mounted MPU6050 IMUs.
nodes.w: Compact reference for the standard ZUPT pedestrian tracker that underpins dismounted soldier navigation.
nodes.h: Runs offline on included data; reproduce with any cheap IMU strapped to a boot.

nodes.s: Arduino library forked from MPU6050_tockn that reads and calibrates an MPU6050 and streams angles and time series to Python plotting scripts. The README says foot-mounted INS / ZUPT support is planned but the repo is under construction; no zero-velocity detector or INS code is in it yet.
nodes.w: Low-cost hardware path to a working foot-mounted INS demo.
nodes.h: Only the IMU reading and calibration part exists; you would write the ZUPT detector and INS yourself (see pajaraca/IEZ or OpenShoe for the algorithm). Needs an MPU6050 and an Arduino-class board; expect heading drift without magnetometer aiding.

nodes.s: Planned device-independent pedestrian dead reckoning platform that never got past its outline: the repo holds MATLAB ellipsoid-fit accelerometer and magnetometer calibration scripts with sample logs, an Allan-variance note, and reference papers on filtering and AHRS. No step detection or step-length code is present.
nodes.w: Simple step-and-heading baseline for phone-based indoor navigation.
nodes.h: Unmaintained since 2017. Only the ellipsoid-fit IMU/magnetometer calibration scripts are reusable; for actual PDR code look elsewhere.

nodes.s: Android app implementing pedestrian dead reckoning with step detection and orientation from phone sensors.
nodes.w: Phone-native PDR demo you can install and walk with during a hackathon.
nodes.h: The author marks it unmaintained (written in 2014). It is an Eclipse ADT project, so expect to import and migrate it into Android Studio, and the manifest lacks a Google Maps API key. Use the step-detection and heading code as reference; fuse with Wi-Fi or UWB for correction.

nodes.s: Code for RIDI, which regresses velocity from smartphone IMU data with learned models to reduce inertial drift for pedestrian navigation.
nodes.w: Ancestor of RoNIN/TLIO-style learned inertial odometry.
nodes.h: Old dependencies; prefer RoNIN for new work.

nodes.s: Data and baseline code from Microsoft Research's Indoor Location Competition 2.0: smartphone IMU, Wi-Fi, BLE and magnetic traces across many buildings with floor maps.
nodes.w: Large real indoor dataset for Wi-Fi/magnetic fingerprinting plus PDR fusion.
nodes.h: Sample data in repo; full set on Kaggle. Good for a fingerprinting + PDR fusion demo.

nodes.s: Python devkit for MILUV, a multi-UAV indoor localization dataset with UWB ranging (including inter-robot), vision and IMU data.
nodes.w: UWB plus vision data with multiple vehicles, for relative and indoor localization.
nodes.h: Download the dataset via devkit scripts; examples include UWB EKF.

nodes.s: Dataset combining stereo camera, IMU, polarization camera and high-precision GPS for polarization-aided navigation research.
nodes.w: Polarized skylight gives a GNSS-free heading reference; open data for it is rare.
nodes.h: README only links a Google Drive; check data format before planning.

nodes.s: Small Tkinter desktop app for celestial navigation on a boat: computes the Nautical Almanac daily-page data with PyEphem, reduces sights and fixes position from two LOPs, correcting for vessel motion between sights.
nodes.w: Scriptable sight reduction for a GNSS-free position fix.
nodes.h: Python 2 code (imports ConfigParser, Tkinter) with no commits since 2018; port the celnav.py core to Python 3 or use it as an algorithm reference. Pair with a camera-based sun or star altitude to automate a fix.

nodes.s: OpenCPN plugin for entering sextant sights and plotting lines of position and fixes on the chart.
nodes.w: Puts celestial fixes into a real chart plotter workflow.
nodes.h: Build against OpenCPN SDK; useful as UI reference.

nodes.s: Open star tracker software from the University of Chile space lab, flown on SUCHAI nanosatellites.
nodes.w: Flight-tested open star tracker code, a basis for attitude from stars.
nodes.h: Python prototype; compare with tetra3/LOST.

nodes.s: Blind astrometric solver that identifies star fields in arbitrary images and returns the precise sky pointing, using geometric hash indexes of star catalogs.
nodes.w: Proven lost-in-space plate solving; with a known time and gravity vector it yields attitude and coarse position.
nodes.h: apt install astrometry.net plus index files for your field of view; solve-field on a night-sky photo.

nodes.s: Python library for high-accuracy positions of stars, planets and Earth satellites, with proper time scales and reference frames.
nodes.w: Gives the ephemerides any celestial or satellite-based nav prototype needs.
nodes.h: pip install skyfield; downloads ephemeris files on first use.

nodes.s: Nautical almanac and celestial sight reduction for Unix/Linux with CLI, ncurses and web interfaces.
nodes.w: Self-contained offline almanac, handy for air-gapped demos.
nodes.h: Very new and small; verify outputs against a published almanac.

nodes.s: Radar Ego Velocity Estimator: robust 3D ego-velocity from 4D mmWave radar Doppler point clouds, the front-end used by Doer's radar-inertial odometry.
nodes.w: Radar velocity works in smoke, fog and darkness, a strong aid for GNSS-denied drones.
nodes.h: ROS1; run on the provided datasets, pairs with christopherdoer/rio.

nodes.s: Radar odometry for Navtech spinning radar that compensates motion distortion and Doppler effects.
nodes.w: Shows the corrections needed to make scanning radar odometry accurate.
nodes.h: Unmaintained; evaluated on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

nodes.s: Continuous-time lidar, radar, lidar-inertial and radar-inertial odometry built on the STEAM library.
nodes.w: Ready continuous-time radar odometry pipeline evaluated on Boreas.
nodes.h: Docker build; test on Boreas sequences.

nodes.s: Optimization-based, point-uncertainty-aware radar-inertial odometry for 4D radar.
nodes.w: Sliding-window alternative to EKF radar-inertial methods.
nodes.h: ROS1 build; run on public 4D radar datasets.

nodes.s: Graph-based, sparse radar-inertial odometry estimation from ETH ASL, using GTSAM.
nodes.w: Factor-graph radar-inertial baseline for drones in degraded visual environments.
nodes.h: ROS build; datasets linked in README.

nodes.s: Non-iterative, adaptively loosely coupled radar-inertial odometry for spinning (scanning) radar, built on the ORORA radar odometry baseline; the radar pose uncertainty from its voting step feeds a Kalman filter (T-ASE 2025).
nodes.w: Recent scanning-radar inertial method to benchmark against.
nodes.h: ROS Noetic / Ubuntu 20.04, catkin build, Sophus built manually. Replay MulRan with its file player (radar + IMU); a Boreas demo is shown.

nodes.s: Outlier-robust radar odometry using graduated non-convexity-style estimation on radar feature correspondences (ICRA 2023).
nodes.w: Robust estimation is what keeps radar odometry stable amid clutter and multipath.
nodes.h: Evaluated on MulRan and Oxford Radar; ROS build.

nodes.s: Radar SLAM with verified loop closures built on CFEAR radar odometry.
nodes.w: Full radar-only SLAM, including loop closure, for long GNSS-denied drives.
nodes.h: ROS1 + Docker; pairs with CFEAR.

nodes.s: Lightweight radar global descriptor for radar place recognition (RA-L 2024).
nodes.w: Cheap loop-closure and relocalization for radar-only navigation.
nodes.h: Small codebase; test on MulRan/Oxford Radar.

nodes.s: Fast radar place recognition using VLAD-style aggregation over radar polar scans.
nodes.w: Simple radar relocalization baseline.
nodes.h: Evaluate on Oxford Radar RobotCar.

nodes.s: 4D radar dataset and benchmark for object detection in diverse weather, with raw 4D tensors, lidar, cameras and GNSS.
nodes.w: Bad-weather 4D radar data, also usable for radar odometry and perception experiments.
nodes.h: Very large dataset; request access and use subsets.

nodes.s: Learns to generate high-resolution, lidar-like point clouds from low-cost single-chip mmWave radar.
nodes.w: Makes cheap radar usable for mapping and localization in smoke or darkness.
nodes.h: Pretrained model and data provided; GPU needed.

nodes.s: Playground GNSS positioning code in Python/numpy that computes a static GPS position (50-100 m accuracy per the README) from RINEX 2.11 observations, with parsers for RINEX nav/obs, SP3 and IONEX plus Klobuchar, IONEX and VMF1 delay models. Works on RINEX files, not raw IF samples, so there is no acquisition or tracking stage.
nodes.w: Python-readable receiver chain for teaching and quick experiments.
nodes.h: Unmaintained since 2020; use for learning.

nodes.s: Python code generators, acquisition and tracking scripts for GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou and Xona Pulsar LEO signals, operating on IQ recordings.
nodes.w: Broadest signal coverage among lightweight SDR toolkits; quick to test a new recording.
nodes.h: Install numpy, scipy and numba (conda is the easy route), then run acquire-<system>-<signal>.py or track-*.py on an IQ file from any SDR. No compile step beyond Numba's JIT.

nodes.s: MATLAB code to generate GNSS PRN and secondary codes, dataless signals and spectra, with real captures.
nodes.w: Reference signal generation for interference and receiver studies.
nodes.h: Old but self-contained; MATLAB needed.

nodes.s: MATLAB particle filtering examples for terrain-referenced navigation, comparing standard, auxiliary, mixture and out-of-sequence measurement particle filters (accompanies an IEEE TAES 2018 paper).
nodes.w: Directly addresses the ambiguous-terrain problem that breaks naive TRN.
nodes.h: Runs in MATLAB with simulated terrain; port the update logic to Python for a DEM demo.

nodes.s: Deep-learning-based terrain-referenced navigation and localization project from ITU Aerospace Research Center, with particle filter baselines.
nodes.w: Learning-based TRN reference from an aerospace lab.
nodes.h: Partial code; read with the project website.

nodes.s: Terrain relative navigation for planetary landing that detects craters with a Mask R-CNN and matches them to a catalog using projective invariants.
nodes.w: Crater-based TRN, the space analogue of map-matching navigation.
nodes.h: Thesis code; TensorFlow 2 and pretrained weights needed.

nodes.s: Event-based stereo visual-inertial odometry combining stereo event and image streams with IMU (RA-L/IROS 2023).
nodes.w: Event cameras keep tracking under fast motion and HDR where frame VIO fails.
nodes.h: ROS1; run on provided event datasets.

nodes.s: Asynchronous photometric feature tracking that combines events and frames (IJCV 2019).
nodes.w: Feature tracks with very low latency, a front-end for event VIO.
nodes.h: Old ROS1 code; use for reference.

nodes.s: Event-based multi-view stereo: semi-dense 3D reconstruction from a moving event camera with known poses (IJCV 2018).
nodes.w: Mapping from event cameras for depth in HDR scenes.
nodes.h: ROS1; reference implementation.

nodes.s: Deep Event Visual Odometry: learned monocular event-only VO trained on simulated events, generalizing to real benchmarks (3DV 2024).
nodes.w: Event-only odometry without frames, useful at night or under strobing light.
nodes.h: PyTorch + CUDA; pretrained checkpoint available.

nodes.s: ROS drivers and tools for DVS/DAVIS event cameras, including calibration and rendering.
nodes.w: Standard way to get event-camera data into ROS 1.
nodes.h: ROS1 only; for ROS 2 look at vendor drivers.

nodes.s: Prophesee's open SDK for event-based vision: camera drivers, data formats, visualization and algorithm building blocks.
nodes.w: Entry point for the most common commercial event sensors.
nodes.h: Build from source or packages; sample recordings available without hardware.

nodes.s: Python library for event-based datasets and transforms, in the style of torchvision.
nodes.w: Fast access to many event datasets for learning-based event navigation.
nodes.h: pip install tonic (or conda-forge); use transforms such as ToFrame or voxel grids. The project is looking for a new maintainer, so pin a version.

nodes.s: Converts conventional video into realistic synthetic DVS event streams with sensor noise modeling.
nodes.w: Lets you produce event data for training/testing without owning an event camera.
nodes.h: Not on PyPI: create a conda env, install CUDA PyTorch, then `pip install -e .` from a clone (or use the Colab notebook). Needs a GPU; conversion runs far slower than real time, so test with --stop on a short clip of drone footage first.

nodes.s: Reconstructs intensity video from event streams with a recurrent network, enabling frame-based methods on event data.
nodes.w: Bridge that lets standard VO/feature pipelines consume event camera data.
nodes.h: Pretrained model; PyTorch.

nodes.s: MATLAB implementations of event-based feature tracking methods from the Penn GRASP lab.
nodes.w: Reference algorithms for event-based VIO front-ends.
nodes.h: MATLAB; pair with MVSEC data.

nodes.s: Hobby project to build a DSP-based Loran-C receiver that can also lock onto the Russian Chayka chain. The published repo holds only KiCad hardware designs (loop antenna preamp, power supply, processing board, RF prototype); no DSP firmware or software.
nodes.w: One of very few open receivers for low-frequency hyperbolic navigation, the basis of eLoran.
nodes.h: Hardware reference only, last touched 2014: the loop-antenna preamp and RF front-end schematics are the useful part for an LF receiver build. No signal processing code to reuse.

nodes.s: NumPy API that generates Loran-C master and secondary station pulse groups with phase codes for simulation (Korean docs).
nodes.w: Synthetic Loran/eLoran signals for testing receivers without LF hardware.
nodes.h: Small; translate README; combine with a tracking loop for a toy eLoran receiver.

nodes.s: Converts PyTorch models to TensorRT engines with a single call, aimed at Jetson deployment.
nodes.w: Simplest path to fast onboard inference for learned nav models.
nodes.h: Install on a Jetson with JetPack; not every layer converts - check supported ops.

nodes.s: NVIDIA's guide and library for deploying detection, segmentation and depth networks with TensorRT on Jetson, with camera streaming.
nodes.w: Get onboard perception running on a Jetson in hours.
nodes.h: Use the Docker container; works with CSI/USB cameras.

nodes.s: Build system and prebuilt containers for ML on Jetson (PyTorch, ROS, LLMs, VLMs) matched to JetPack versions.
nodes.w: Avoids the dependency hell of getting ROS and PyTorch onto a Jetson.
nodes.h: Use autotag to pull a container matching your JetPack.

nodes.s: ROS/ROS 2 nodes wrapping jetson-inference for detection, classification and segmentation with TensorRT.
nodes.w: Drop-in onboard perception topics for a ROS robot on Jetson.
nodes.h: Build inside jetson-containers ROS image.

nodes.s: GPU-accelerated 3D reconstruction (TSDF/ESDF) that provides Nav2 local costmaps from depth cameras.
nodes.w: Real-time onboard mapping for obstacle avoidance without lidar.
nodes.h: Isaac ROS dev container; RealSense quickstart.

nodes.s: ROS 2 packages for TensorRT and Triton inference on Jetson and x86, with encoder/decoder nodes for common model types.
nodes.w: Standard ROS 2 path to run custom learned models onboard.
nodes.h: Use with an ONNX model; dev container required.

nodes.s: NVIDIA's CUDA-accelerated visual odometry and SLAM library supporting mono to multi-camera rigs with optional IMU, with Python bindings.
nodes.w: The engine behind Isaac ROS Visual SLAM, now usable directly from Python.
nodes.h: Download the prebuilt wheel (cuvslam-cu12 or -cu13) from the GitHub releases page, not PyPI; wheels cover x86_64, Jetson Orin (JetPack 6) and Jetson Thor with Python 3.10+, other combos need a source build. Needs CUDA Toolkit libraries; examples include EuRoC and KITTI.

nodes.s: ONNX export and inference of LightGlue matching with SuperPoint, DISK and ALIKED extractors (including RaCo-ALIKED-LightGlue+), with TensorRT, OpenVINO and FP8 quantization workflows.
nodes.w: Fast learned matching on embedded hardware for visual geolocalization and VO.
nodes.h: Download prebuilt ONNX models from Releases and run with onnxruntime-gpu or TensorRT; for export, the repo now uses uv (uv sync with export/cuda/trt groups) and a lightglue-onnx CLI.

nodes.s: Large collection of models converted between TensorFlow, TFLite, ONNX, OpenVINO, TensorRT and others.
nodes.w: Saves conversion time when a needed model must run on an edge accelerator.
nodes.h: Use the download scripts per model; check licences per model.

nodes.s: Rockchip's examples and converted models for its NPU (RK3588 and similar), with deployment code.
nodes.w: Low-cost non-NVIDIA edge AI option common on small drones and UGVs.
nodes.h: Needs rknn-toolkit2 for conversion; run demos on an RK3588 board.

nodes.s: Landing repository for Luxonis OAK cameras, which run neural networks and stereo depth on the camera; the default branch now only points to the docs, and the old examples live on the `main` branch. The current Python API (DepthAI v3) is built from luxonis/depthai-core.
nodes.w: Puts inference and depth on the sensor, freeing the companion computer.
nodes.h: `pip install depthai` (v3 API; examples in luxonis/depthai-core). OAK camera required. Older v2 tutorials and examples will not run unchanged on v3.

nodes.s: ROS 1/2 driver for Luxonis OAK cameras publishing depth, detections and IMU.
nodes.w: Plug OAK cameras into a ROS nav stack.
nodes.h: Binary packages for major ROS 2 distros.

nodes.s: Examples for Hailo-8/8L accelerators on Raspberry Pi 5 (AI Kit/HAT): detection, pose and segmentation pipelines; marked outdated in favor of hailo-apps.
nodes.w: Cheapest route to real-time onboard inference on a Pi-based vehicle.
nodes.h: Repo points to hailo-ai/hailo-apps for current code; start there.

nodes.s: The original open-source GNSS positioning package by T. Takasu: SPP, DGNSS, RTK, PPK and PPP engines in portable C, plus CLI tools (rnx2rtkp, rtkrcv, str2str, convbin) and Windows GUIs.
nodes.w: The reference implementation most GNSS research and low-cost RTK work is built on; reading its rtkpos.c is the fastest way to understand RTK.
nodes.h: Use str2str to relay NTRIP/serial streams and rnx2rtkp for post-processing. Upstream is quiet since 2024; prefer the demo5 fork for current receivers.

nodes.s: Actively maintained RTKLIB fork tuned for low-cost receivers (especially u-blox), with many robustness fixes to ambiguity resolution, cycle-slip handling and receiver decoders.
nodes.w: The practical default for RTK/PPK with cheap F9P-class hardware; well documented through the rtklibexplorer blog.
nodes.h: Prebuilt Windows binaries and Linux builds are easy. Pair with a u-blox F9P and a free NTRIP caster for cm-level fixes in an afternoon.

nodes.s: Python port of the demo5 RTKLIB positioning core, currently focused on post-processed kinematic (PPK) solutions.
nodes.w: Readable Python version of RTK math, good for teaching, prototyping new filters or swapping in ML components.
nodes.h: Slow compared to C RTKLIB and PPK only; last pushed 2023. Ideal for instrumenting or modifying the filter during a hackathon.

nodes.s: MATLAB wrapper exposing RTKLIB functions and data structures (observations, navigation data, solutions) as MATLAB objects.
nodes.w: Lets MATLAB users script RTKLIB processing and analysis without writing C.
nodes.h: Requires MATLAB. Useful if the team already lives in MATLAB for analysis plots. Since January 2025 the backend is MALIB (the RTKLIB successor), not RTKLIB 2.4.3; pre-compiled mex files ship for Windows, Ubuntu and macOS.

nodes.s: Full software-defined GNSS receiver built on GNU Radio: acquisition, tracking, navigation message decoding and PVT for GPS, Galileo, GLONASS and BeiDou signals from SDR front-ends or IQ files, including Galileo OSNMA support.
nodes.w: The most complete open receiver for experimenting with signal-level defenses (tracking monitors, authentication, interference) on real or simulated IQ.
nodes.h: Install from distro packages (apt install gnss-sdr) to skip a long build. Feed it GPS-SDR-SIM or recorded IQ files; works with HackRF/USRP/RTL-SDR front-ends.

nodes.s: Open hardware GNSS front-end plus a software receiver (Python and C) by the RTKLIB author, supporting a wide range of GNSS signals across L1/L2/L5/L6 bands.
nodes.w: Cheap path to multi-band raw IF capture and a readable receiver implementation, ideal for signal-level research.
nodes.h: Software runs on recorded IF without the hardware; building the board is out of hackathon scope unless pre-built.

nodes.s: Older open-source GNSS software receiver library in C with a GUI, supporting several front-ends and real-time RTKLIB output.
nodes.w: Compact receiver codebase that is easier to read than GNSS-SDR; historically a common teaching receiver.
nodes.h: Not updated since 2015 (repo not formally archived). v2.0 only runs on 64-bit Windows (Visual Studio 2012 build). Use for reference only; prefer PocketSDR or GNSS-SDR for live work.

nodes.s: Multi-GNSS software receiver in MATLAB from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute, with modular acquisition, tracking and navigation stages.
nodes.w: MATLAB receiver suitable for quick algorithm swaps (e.g. new tracking or interference mitigation) with readable code.
nodes.h: Needs MATLAB and IQ files; slow but transparent.

nodes.s: Maintained copy of the classic Borre/Akos SoftGNSS MATLAB GPS L1 receiver with updates for several sampler front-ends.
nodes.w: The receiver code that accompanies the standard textbook on software GPS receivers; the canonical teaching codebase.
nodes.h: Good for learning acquisition and tracking loops on a sample data file.

nodes.s: Python port of the SoftGNSS software-defined GPS receiver toolkit.
nodes.w: Python version of the textbook receiver; easier for teams without MATLAB.
nodes.h: Not updated since 2023 and written for Python 2.7 (README system requirements; installation section says 'Coming soon'). Expect porting work before offline IQ experiments.

nodes.n: GPS L1 Direct Position Estimation module
nodes.s: Plug-in module adding Direct Position Estimation (positioning directly in the correlation domain) to MATLAB two-step software receivers such as SoftGNSS.
nodes.w: DPE is studied for robustness in weak-signal, multipath and interference conditions; this is one of few open implementations.
nodes.h: Research code; computationally heavy. Useful as a stretch comparison against conventional tracking.

nodes.s: Python GNSS processing library from comma.ai that fetches orbits, clocks and atmospheric corrections automatically and computes corrected pseudoranges and positions from raw measurements.
nodes.w: Quickest way to go from raw pseudoranges to a corrected fix in Python; it powered openpilot's laikad GNSS localizer until that was removed in October 2023.
nodes.h: Install from a clone (`pip install .`); the PyPI 'laika' package is a 2018 0.0.1 stub. Correction downloads need internet, and NASA CDDIS needs an Earthdata login in a .netrc. Good backend for Android raw data experiments.

nodes.s: Modular Python library from Stanford NavLab for parsing, analyzing and visualizing GNSS data (Android logs, RINEX, NMEA, SP3/CLK) with baseline positioning algorithms and fault detection examples.
nodes.w: Strong Python base for smartphone GNSS work and for prototyping integrity/fault detection.
nodes.h: pip install gnss-lib-py; tutorials load GSDC data directly. Very good fit for a 24h spoofing-detection or integrity notebook.

nodes.s: Fast Python reader for RINEX 2/3/4 observation and navigation files (plain, gzip/Z/bz2/zip or Hatanaka-compressed) and SP3 orbits into xarray, with batch conversion to NetCDF4/HDF5.
nodes.w: Makes RINEX data accessible in the scientific Python stack without writing parsers.
nodes.h: pip install georinex. Use it to load public CORS/IGS RINEX for analysis or ML features.

nodes.s: Geoscience Australia Python module of utilities for reading and comparing GNSS products (SP3, CLK, SINEX, Ginan outputs) and computing differences/statistics.
nodes.w: Companion tooling for evaluating precise orbit/clock products and PPP outputs.
nodes.h: Niche; useful if comparing PPP solutions or product quality.

nodes.s: Wuhan University's open-source multi-GNSS precise point positioning package with ambiguity resolution, aimed at geodetic-grade post-processing.
nodes.w: Free PPP-AR gives cm-level positions without a local base station, a key capability where RTK networks are unavailable.
nodes.h: Command-line build via install.sh on Linux and macOS, plus a Windows GUI version; needs precise products downloaded. Post-processing only, so plan for hours of data.

nodes.s: Geoscience Australia's GNSS analysis toolkit for precise orbit determination and real-time/post-processed PPP, producing and consuming correction products.
nodes.w: Government-backed open PPP and product-generation engine; relevant for sovereign correction services.
nodes.h: Heavy build and configuration; Docker images help. Overkill for most 48h builds.

nodes.s: C++ library (successor to GPSTk) from UT Austin ARL for GNSS data formats, time systems, ephemeris handling and positioning algorithms, with Python bindings.
nodes.w: Long-lived, carefully engineered GNSS core library used in US research and monitoring work.
nodes.h: Build is CMake-heavy; use for robust format and time handling rather than quick demos.

nodes.s: Python library for parsing and generating u-blox UBX protocol messages, including configuration (CFG-VALSET) and raw measurement (RXM-RAWX) messages.
nodes.w: Standard way to talk to u-blox receivers from Python: configure, log raw data and read jamming/spoofing status fields (MON-HW, NAV-STATUS).
nodes.h: pip install pyubx2. Read MON-RF jamming indicators and NAV-STATUS spoof flags to build a live interference monitor quickly.

nodes.s: Python parser for RTCM 3 messages (MSM observations, station info, ephemerides, SSR).
nodes.w: Lets teams inspect and manipulate correction streams from NTRIP casters in Python.
nodes.h: pip install pyrtcm. Combine with pygnssutils' NTRIP client for live streams.

nodes.s: Python library for parsing and generating NMEA 0183 GNSS sentences, including proprietary variants.
nodes.w: NMEA is what most autopilots and COTS receivers emit; this is a well-maintained parser/generator.
nodes.h: pip install pynmeagps. Can also generate NMEA to feed test positions into a downstream system.

nodes.s: Cross-platform Python GUI GNSS client that displays and configures receivers over NMEA, UBX, RTCM3 and other protocols, with built-in NTRIP and SPARTN clients.
nodes.w: Fast visual tool for checking receiver state, satellite C/N0 and corrections during field tests.
nodes.h: pip install pygpsclient. Good bench tool to watch C/N0 drop during a jamming test in a shielded setup.

nodes.s: Python CLI and library utilities for reading, parsing and broadcasting GNSS streams, including an NTRIP client and caster/server and a socket server.
nodes.w: Glue for building correction pipelines and logging tools without writing protocol code.
nodes.h: pip install pygnssutils; gnssntripclient gets you RTCM from a caster in one command.

nodes.s: Lightweight Python library for parsing NMEA 0183 sentences.
nodes.w: Widely used minimal NMEA parser.
nodes.h: pip install pynmea2; simpler than pynmeagps but less coverage.

nodes.s: Service daemon that monitors GNSS receivers over serial/USB/network and serves decoded fixes, satellites and timing to client applications via JSON over TCP.
nodes.w: The standard Linux GNSS middleware; used for timing (with ntpd/chrony and PPS) and for multiplexing receivers to multiple apps.
nodes.h: apt install gpsd gpsd-clients; cgps/gpsmon give instant status. Use it for PPS timing demos.

nodes.s: ROS driver for u-blox receivers that publishes fixes, raw measurements and receiver status as ROS messages.
nodes.w: Common bridge from u-blox hardware into ROS-based autonomy stacks.
nodes.h: Available as a ROS package; check the branch for ROS 1 vs ROS 2.

nodes.n: SparkFun u-blox GNSS v3 Arduino library
nodes.s: Arduino library for u-blox GNSS modules over I2C/SPI/serial, covering configuration, high-precision fixes and RTK correction input.
nodes.w: Easiest embedded route to an RTK-capable microcontroller node (ESP32 + F9P).
nodes.h: Many examples, including NTRIP over Wi-Fi on ESP32. Good for a low-cost rover or base station.

nodes.s: u-blox's portable C libraries for building applications on their GNSS and cellular modules across MCU platforms.
nodes.w: Vendor-maintained abstraction for u-blox hardware on embedded targets.
nodes.h: Repository is archived; prefer the SparkFun library or pyubx2.

nodes.s: Maintained mirror of the BKG standard NTRIP broadcaster in C for distributing RTCM correction streams over HTTP.
nodes.w: Self-hosted correction distribution for a private RTK network, e.g. in a contested area without public casters.
nodes.h: Builds with autotools; pair with str2str from RTKLIB as the source.

nodes.s: Dockerfile and instructions to build and run the BKG NTRIP caster in a container.
nodes.w: Fastest way to stand up your own caster.
nodes.h: docker build and go; last updated 2024.

nodes.s: Go library implementing NTRIP client, server and caster components.
nodes.w: Modern, embeddable NTRIP implementation for building custom correction services.
nodes.h: Use as a library inside a Go backend; smaller community than BKG caster.

nodes.s: ROS/ROS 2 node that connects to an NTRIP caster and publishes RTCM corrections, forwarding NMEA position back to the caster.
nodes.w: Standard glue to get RTK corrections into a ROS robot.
nodes.h: apt-installable ROS package; works with any receiver driver accepting RTCM topics.

nodes.s: Command-line tool that fetches and displays an NTRIP caster's source table, optionally filtered by distance from a coordinate.
nodes.w: Quick way to find the nearest public base station mountpoint.
nodes.h: Needs libcurl. pip install ntripbrowser still installs the 2021 release (2.2.3); the repo is at 4.0.0 (2025, Python 3.11+), so install from a clone with make install for current code. Point at rtk2go or a national caster.

nodes.s: TypeScript/Node.js NTRIP caster library supporting NTRIP v1 and v2.
nodes.w: JS option for web-stack teams building a correction relay.
nodes.h: Last updated 2023; fine for demos.

nodes.s: Google's Android raw GNSS measurement tooling: the GnssLogger app source, MATLAB analysis tools for pseudorange processing (including a RINEX nav reader), and NMEA utilities.
nodes.w: The canonical way to capture raw pseudoranges and carrier phase from phones, the basis for smartphone spoofing and integrity research.
nodes.h: Install GnssLogger from the Play Store and log on any recent Android phone; parse logs with gnss_lib_py.

nodes.s: Code reproducing Taro Suzuki's Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023 entry (1st on the public leaderboard, 2nd on the private one), using factor graph optimization of smartphone GNSS and IMU in MATLAB.
nodes.w: Shows what state-of-the-art smartphone positioning looks like on a public benchmark.
nodes.h: MATLAB required. Read it for the pipeline design even if you reimplement in Python.

nodes.s: Generates GPS L1 C/A baseband IQ sample files for a user-defined static or moving trajectory from a broadcast ephemeris file, for playback through an SDR.
nodes.w: The standard open test-signal generator for evaluating receiver behavior under simulated or spoofed conditions. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
nodes.h: Generate IQ files and feed GNSS-SDR directly (no RF needed) to test detectors. Repository archived in 2025 but still works. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant of GPS-SDR-SIM for bladeRF hardware.
nodes.w: Real-time variant for interactive receiver testing. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
nodes.h: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant for LimeSDR.
nodes.w: Same as bladeGPS for LimeSDR users. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
nodes.h: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Maintained derivative of GPS-SDR-SIM that streams GPS L1 baseband on the fly to HackRF or ADALM-Pluto, or to a binary IQ file, with a curses text UI.
nodes.w: More current option than the archived original for building test rigs. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
nodes.h: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Galileo E1-B/E5b signal simulator with OSNMA authentication data embedded, configurable OSNMA parameters and USRP or file output, tested against GNSS-SDR and OSNMAlib.
nodes.w: Rare open tool to generate authenticated (and deliberately broken) Galileo signals for testing OSNMA-aware receivers.
nodes.h: Use file sink output into GNSS-SDR plus OSNMAlib for a full authenticate-or-alarm pipeline without RF. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Open-source generator for BeiDou B1C baseband signals for SDR playback or file output.
nodes.w: Extends signal simulation testing beyond GPS to BeiDou.
nodes.h: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

nodes.s: Python implementation of the Galileo OSNMA receiver protocol: verifies TESLA key chains and MACs on navigation data from several input formats (u-blox, Septentrio, GNSS-SDR, files).
nodes.w: Most practical open tool to add navigation message authentication to a Galileo-capable receiver pipeline.
nodes.h: Works live with a u-blox receiver outputting SFRBX; needs the public key and Merkle root from the GSC. Good basis for an 'authenticated position' demo.

nodes.s: Rust implementation of Galileo OSNMA that can run on embedded no_std targets, with examples for live receivers.
nodes.w: Lightweight, memory-safe OSNMA verifier suitable for embedding in drones or edge devices.
nodes.h: Cargo build; includes a u-blox-based example. Embedded angle is a differentiator.

nodes.s: Python OSNMA implementation from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute designed for flexibility and integration with receivers.
nodes.w: Second independent Python OSNMA implementation for cross-checking.
nodes.h: Not updated since 2023; check against current ICD version.

nodes.s: Jupyter-based real-time OSNMA authentication of u-blox receiver data in Python.
nodes.w: Small, readable OSNMA example from the test phase.
nodes.h: Inactive since 2022, predates OSNMA public service; use for learning only.

nodes.s: Open-source GNSS monitoring network and software that collects navigation data from volunteer receivers worldwide and publishes live health, ephemeris and timing statistics for Galileo, GPS, BeiDou and GLONASS.
nodes.w: Independent constellation monitoring, valuable for spotting anomalies and checking broadcast data integrity.
nodes.h: Run a feeder with a u-blox receiver, or just consume the public galmon.eu data.

nodes.s: Python implementation of GPS jamming detection from receiver signal-to-noise ratio, following a published real-time jamming detection method.
nodes.w: Simple, explainable C/N0-based jamming detector to start from.
nodes.h: Small codebase from 2021; adapt to read C/N0 from pyubx2 or Android logs.

nodes.s: Raw GNSS measurement logs from Android phones and smartwatches recorded under spoofing scenarios on L1, L5 and dual-band.
nodes.w: Labelled smartphone spoofing data is scarce; this enables training and testing detectors without generating signals.
nodes.h: Load logs with gnss_lib_py and build a consistency-check or ML detector. Verify labelling and scenario details in the README before trusting results.

nodes.s: Stanford GPS Lab MATLAB toolset that evaluates Advanced RAIM availability and protection levels over service areas.
nodes.w: Reference-grade integrity tooling from the lab behind much ARAIM research.
nodes.h: MATLAB; heavy on aviation integrity concepts. Use for coverage maps of integrity availability.

nodes.s: MATLAB implementation of classic receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (fault detection and exclusion) for GNSS positioning.
nodes.w: Compact RAIM example to adapt for spoofing/fault detection logic.
nodes.h: Small and readable; port the residual test to Python for a quick FDE demo.

nodes.s: Custom GTSAM factors and MATLAB wrappers for GNSS factor-graph positioning, including pseudorange, Doppler and carrier-phase factors with ambiguity estimation.
nodes.w: Factor graphs are a robust way to fuse GNSS with other sensors and reject outliers.
nodes.h: Requires the author's GTSAM fork and MATLAB; under active development.

nodes.s: Open-source GNSS positioning and RTK package using factor graph optimization, built on RTKLIB data handling and ROS.
nodes.w: Shows FGO-based GNSS positioning outperforming filters in urban canyons; good research baseline.
nodes.h: ROS 1 + Ceres; uses RTKLIB internals for observation handling.

nodes.s: C++/ROS definitions and utilities for raw GNSS measurement processing (ephemeris, satellite positions, pseudorange models) used by GVINS.
nodes.w: Reusable raw GNSS building blocks for tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial fusion.
nodes.h: ROS 1; stable but unmaintained since 2022.

nodes.s: MATLAB utility functions from UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab for simulating Starlink Ku-band downlink signals (OFDM frames, PSS/SSS, Doppler and path-loss histories), with MATLAB live-script playground examples.
nodes.w: Lets teams experiment with Starlink as a signal of opportunity for PNT without capturing real Ku-band data.
nodes.h: Small MATLAB codebase, MIT licensed, last commit January 2024 and marked work in progress. The companion paper is Komodromos, Qin and Humphreys, 'Signal Simulator for Starlink Ku-Band Downlink' (ION GNSS+ 2023).

nodes.s: Proposal for RINEX format modifications to carry LEO-PNT observables and ephemeris.
nodes.w: Shows how LEO-PNT data might be standardized into existing GNSS tooling.
nodes.h: Archived; read-only reference.

nodes.s: Web application showing current GNSS satellite positions (sky plot) for a location and time across constellations.
nodes.w: Quick visibility planning tool for field tests.
nodes.h: Use the hosted site or run locally for offline sky plots.

nodes.s: Open driver-assistance robotics stack. Its current locationd fuses IMU and camera odometry in a pose Kalman filter; GNSS is still read and logged (ubloxd, qcomgpsd) but the laika-based GNSS fusion has been removed.
nodes.w: Real-world example of a production fusion pipeline on consumer hardware, and of a stack that dropped GNSS from its localizer in favour of vision and IMU.
nodes.h: Large codebase; study locationd (pose_kf) and the ubloxd GNSS parsing rather than running the full stack. For laika-style GNSS processing, look at the standalone commaai/laika repo or older openpilot releases.

nodes.s: Georgia Tech factor-graph library for smoothing and mapping, with incremental solvers (iSAM2) and a full IMU preintegration factor set. Ships Python bindings and navigation examples combining IMU with GPS-style measurements.
nodes.w: The default backbone for building a custom GNSS/INS or multi-sensor navigation estimator where you add or drop sensor factors as GNSS degrades.
nodes.h: pip install gtsam gives Python bindings; start from the ImuFactor examples and add a GNSS position factor. Noise model tuning is where time goes.

nodes.s: Google's nonlinear least-squares and general optimization library with automatic differentiation and robust loss functions.
nodes.w: Used as the solver under many VIO and GNSS/INS optimizers (VINS-Fusion, OB_GINS); good for writing your own sliding-window estimator.
nodes.h: Solid but you write the residuals yourself. Pair with an existing IMU preintegration residual (e.g. from OB_GINS) rather than deriving from scratch.

nodes.s: General framework for graph optimization, widely used for pose-graph SLAM back ends.
nodes.w: Lightweight pose-graph back end when you need loop closure or map alignment on top of an inertial front end.
nodes.h: Best for pose graphs; IMU factors are less turnkey than in GTSAM.

nodes.s: ROS package with EKF and UKF state estimation nodes that fuse any number of odometry, IMU, pose and GNSS inputs, plus a navsat_transform node for GPS-to-map conversion.
nodes.w: Fastest route to a working fused odometry on a ROS ground robot or drone; the usual baseline before writing a custom filter.
nodes.h: apt install on ROS 2; mostly YAML config. Common gotcha: frame conventions (REP-103/105) and double-counting velocities.

nodes.s: Python library of Kalman filters (linear, extended, unscented, ensemble), smoothers, particle filtering helpers and related estimators.
nodes.w: Quick prototyping of filters in notebooks before porting to embedded code.
nodes.h: pip install filterpy. Not Lie-group aware, so handle attitude error states manually or use navlie/manif for that.

nodes.n: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python (book)
nodes.s: Free interactive book of Jupyter notebooks teaching Kalman, EKF, UKF and particle filters with an intuition-first approach.
nodes.w: Fastest onboarding for team members new to estimation.
nodes.h: Run the notebooks locally or in Binder; chapters on UKF and EKF are enough for a hackathon.

nodes.s: Templated C++ unscented Kalman filter library for state and parameter estimation, including square-root variants, aimed at embedded use.
nodes.w: Option for an embedded UKF attitude/navigation filter with compile-time state definitions.
nodes.h: Heavy template code; worth it only if you specifically need a UKF on a microcontroller-class target.

nodes.s: Modular EKF framework from ETH ASL for fusing IMU propagation with pose, position and other sensor updates, with delayed-measurement handling.
nodes.w: Classic MAV state estimator that shows how to fuse delayed vision/GPS measurements into an IMU-driven filter.
nodes.h: ROS 1 era; building on modern distros takes effort. Read it for the design more than to run it.

nodes.s: Modular IMU-driven sensor-fusion framework from University of Klagenfurt designed so sensors can be added, removed or fail at runtime without reworking the core filter.
nodes.w: Directly relevant to graceful degradation when GNSS or another aiding sensor drops out.
