nodes.s: Direct monocular visual odometry that optimizes photometric error over a sparse set of pixels with joint photometric calibration.
nodes.w: Works in low-texture scenes where feature-based methods fail; the basis for DM-VIO and many direct methods.
nodes.h: No IMU, no loop closure, scale-ambiguous; mostly useful as a building block or comparison.

nodes.s: Monocular visual-inertial odometry built on DSO using delayed marginalization and pose-graph bundle adjustment for IMU initialization.
nodes.w: Strong monocular VIO accuracy; good for single-camera drones.
nodes.h: Standalone build with an optional ROS wrapper repo. Expects photometrically calibrated input for best results.

nodes.s: Robust visual-inertial odometry using an iterated EKF directly on image-patch photometric errors.
nodes.w: Long a go-to VIO on PX4/MAV research platforms because it is cheap to run.
nodes.h: ROS 1 / catkin. Lightweight; tuning of patch and feature counts matters.

nodes.s: Stereo multi-state constraint Kalman filter VIO designed for fast autonomous flight.
nodes.w: Lean filter-based stereo VIO that runs comfortably on embedded CPUs.
nodes.h: ROS 1; unmaintained. Tested heavily on EuRoC; good comparison point to OpenVINS. Licence: Penn Software License - non-profit research use only, no redistribution without Penn's approval; commercial use needs a separate licence.

nodes.s: Keyframe-based visual-inertial SLAM with loop closure and a realtime scalable factor-graph design; second generation of OKVIS.
nodes.w: Mature research VI-SLAM from the ETH/TUM lineage with active maintenance.
nodes.h: CMake build; check the README for ROS integration and the camera/IMU config format for your sensor.

nodes.s: Extension of OKVIS2 that can additionally use dense depth or LiDAR and fuse GNSS.
nodes.w: Recent (2025-2026) multi-sensor VI-SLAM that includes GNSS fusion, matching assured-PNT architectures.
nodes.h: New codebase; expect some setup friction. Good showcase for switching GNSS on/off.

nodes.s: Point-and-line visual(-inertial) SLAM using learned features, designed for illumination-robust operation, with TensorRT acceleration; successor to AirVO.
nodes.w: Targets lighting changes (dawn/dusk/night), a common failure mode for camera navigation.
nodes.h: Needs an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT). Docker recommended.

nodes.s: Modular multi-session, multi-modal mapping framework with map merging, optimization and localization against saved maps.
nodes.w: Build a map once, then localize repeatedly against it; supports multi-robot and multi-session merges.
nodes.h: Large ROS 1 codebase; only worth it if you need persistent map management.

nodes.s: Graph-based SLAM library and app supporting RGB-D, stereo and LiDAR, with memory management for large-scale loop closure and map reuse.
nodes.w: Practical all-rounder with GUI, database and localization modes; easiest way to get a working 3D map on a ground robot.
nodes.h: Install via apt binaries (ROS) or the standalone app. Supports phone/iPad LiDAR capture. Save a map, then switch to localization mode.

nodes.s: ROS and ROS 2 integration for RTAB-Map, exposing SLAM, localization and odometry nodes.
nodes.w: Drop-in SLAM for ROS 2 Nav2 stacks.
nodes.h: apt-installable for supported distros; launch examples cover common sensors.

nodes.s: Deep visual SLAM that iterates dense bundle adjustment through a recurrent update operator, for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
nodes.w: Much more robust than classic pipelines on hard sequences; strong learned baseline.
nodes.h: Needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU; not real-time on embedded. Pretrained weights available.

nodes.s: Deep Patch Visual Odometry: learned sparse patch tracking for VO, plus DPV-SLAM with loop closure.
nodes.w: Lighter learned VO than DROID-SLAM, closer to real-time on a desktop GPU.
nodes.h: CUDA build of custom kernels; follow the conda instructions.

nodes.s: Real-time dense monocular SLAM built on the MASt3R two-view 3D reconstruction prior, needing no fixed camera model (CVPR 2025).
nodes.w: Works with uncalibrated cameras, useful for opportunistic imagery from unknown cameras.
nodes.h: Requires a capable NVIDIA GPU and model checkpoint downloads. Great demo value on handheld video. Licence: the code is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the MASt3R checkpoints are also non-commercial - research and demo use only.

nodes.s: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer: a feed-forward network predicting camera poses, depth and point maps from one or many images (CVPR 2025 best paper).
nodes.w: Instant pose and geometry from a handful of frames; a building block for learned relocalization and mapping.
nodes.h: GPU inference via PyTorch; Hugging Face demo for quick tests. Not a full SLAM system by itself. Licence: LICENSE.txt prohibits military, warfare and ITAR-controlled uses; the default VGGT-1B checkpoint is non-commercial and only the gated VGGT-1B-Commercial checkpoint allows commercial use.

nodes.s: Gaussian-splatting SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras that tracks and maps directly against a 3D Gaussian representation.
nodes.w: Produces photorealistic maps useful for operator situational awareness and later simulation.
nodes.h: Needs a strong GPU; not real-time on embedded hardware. Best as an offline mapping demo. Licence: Imperial College MonoGS licence - non-commercial, internal or academic research use only.

nodes.s: Dense RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps using 3D Gaussians and differentiable rendering (CVPR 2024).
nodes.w: Reference Gaussian-splatting SLAM for RGB-D sensors.
nodes.h: GPU-heavy and slower than real time; good for offline indoor captures. The repo is BSD-3, but it depends on diff-gaussian-rasterization-w-depth, which carries the Inria Gaussian-Splatting licence (non-commercial research use only).

nodes.s: Couples ORB-SLAM3-style geometric tracking with a photorealistic Gaussian map for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras (CVPR 2024).
nodes.w: Classic robust tracking plus a nice-looking map, closer to real time than pure splatting SLAM.
nodes.h: LibTorch + CUDA build; check version pins carefully. Licence: GPL-3.0 overall, but the repo also ships the Inria Gaussian-Splatting licence (LICENSE.md), which limits that code to non-commercial research use.

nodes.s: Event-based stereo visual odometry using spatio-temporal consistency of two event cameras for mapping and tracking.
nodes.w: Event cameras keep working under high dynamic range and fast motion, where frame cameras blur or saturate.
nodes.h: Needs stereo event cameras or recorded datasets; ROS 1.

nodes.s: Open-source release of Ultimate SLAM, combining events, standard frames and IMU for VIO in HDR and high-speed scenarios (RA-L 2018).
nodes.w: Template for fusing event cameras with frames and IMU for robust flight state estimation.
nodes.h: ROS 1 / catkin; test on event datasets before buying hardware.

nodes.s: Community-curated list of event-camera papers, datasets, drivers, simulators and code.
nodes.w: Fastest way to find event-camera datasets and odometry code.
nodes.h: Use as a discovery index; not runnable code.

nodes.s: Dataset and index of event-based VO, VIO and SLAM work from HKU ArcLab, including stereo event sequences.
nodes.w: Ready-made event data for testing event odometry without hardware.
nodes.h: Download sequences as rosbags from OneDrive or Baidu Disk. The README warns that ESVO, EVO and Ultimate SLAM fail on most of the stereo sequences, so expect a hard benchmark. Licence: MIT, but the README says the data is provided for academic purposes and commercial use needs contact with the lab.

nodes.s: Visual-thermal-inertial odometry extending ROVIO to fuse asynchronous thermal and visual images with IMU, switching to whichever camera is informative.
nodes.w: Thermal keeps odometry alive in darkness and smoke; NTNU ARL targets subterranean and degraded environments.
nodes.h: Needs a thermal camera synced to IMU (or their datasets). Thermal calibration targets need a heated pattern.

nodes.s: Edge-based monocular thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal edges for visually degraded environments.
nodes.w: Low-cost night/smoke navigation from a single thermal camera plus IMU.
nodes.h: Code released with the paper; try on public thermal datasets first.

nodes.s: Radar visual/thermal inertial odometry fusing 4D mmWave radar with a visual or thermal camera and IMU for degraded visual conditions.
nodes.w: Radar plus thermal is a strong combination for fog, smoke and darkness.
nodes.h: ROS 1; datasets released by the author. Good for a degraded-visibility demo.

nodes.s: EKF-based radar-inertial odometry using 4D mmWave radar ego-velocity measurements.
nodes.w: Cheap automotive radars give velocity in fog/smoke/darkness; a minimal radar odometry template.
nodes.h: ROS 1; uses the author's radar ego-velocity estimator. Works with TI mmWave-class sensors.

nodes.s: 4D radar SLAM with scan-to-scan registration, loop closure and pose-graph optimization, released with an NTU 4D radar dataset.
nodes.w: One of the few full SLAM pipelines for 4D imaging radar, the all-weather sensor for ground vehicles.
nodes.h: ROS 1; structured like hdl_graph_slam. Test on their dataset first.

nodes.s: Landing page for CFEAR, learning-free spinning-radar odometry that filters returns to sparse oriented surface points and registers against keyframes. This repo holds only a README and LICENSE; the code is in dan11003/CFEAR_Radarodometry_code_public.
nodes.w: Strong baseline for spinning (Navtech-style) radar odometry; robust in weather that defeats LiDAR.
nodes.h: Clone CFEAR_Radarodometry_code_public for the ROS 1 code (Melodic or later; Oxford Radar RobotCar demo bag provided). Benchmarked on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas. GPL-3.0.

nodes.s: Ground-optimized 4D radar-inertial odometry integrating continuous velocity via Gaussian processes (ICRA 2025 best paper finalist).
nodes.w: Recent state of the art for 4D radar odometry on ground vehicles.
nodes.h: Recent code; check sensor assumptions against your radar.

nodes.s: 4D radar-inertial odometry using Gaussian modeling of radar points and multi-hypothesis scan matching.
nodes.w: Another recent open 4D radar odometry baseline, useful for comparison.
nodes.h: Small research codebase; read the paper before integrating.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry via factor-graph smoothing, with optional GPS factors and loop closure.
nodes.w: Popular LIO with built-in GNSS factors; the template for LiDAR+INS+intermittent GNSS.
nodes.h: ROS 1 main branch, community ROS 2 branch. Needs a 9-axis IMU and careful extrinsics.

nodes.s: Computationally efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry using an iterated error-state Kalman filter and incremental k-d tree map, mapping raw points directly.
nodes.w: The default LIO in many field robots; runs on ARM boards and supports solid-state and spinning LiDARs.
nodes.h: Easiest LIO to get running; Livox drivers supported. No loop closure; pair with a localization or loop-closure add-on.

nodes.s: High-bandwidth LiDAR-inertial odometry that updates the state point by point, tolerating aggressive motion and IMU saturation.
nodes.w: Handles violent motion (agile drones, vibration) where frame-based LIO breaks.
nodes.h: Same ecosystem as FAST-LIO; try when FAST-LIO diverges on aggressive motion.

nodes.s: Direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry fusing LiDAR, camera and IMU in a sequential ESIKF update with a unified voxel map.
nodes.w: High-accuracy colored mapping that stays robust when either LiDAR or camera degrades.
nodes.h: Needs hardware-synced LiDAR+camera; datasets available.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-visual estimation and RGB-colored mapping package.
nodes.w: Produces dense colored maps useful for operator displays and mapping.
nodes.h: ROS 1, heavy on dependencies; FAST-LIVO2 is the newer alternative. Licence: GPLv2 but the README allows it free only for personal and academic use; commercial use needs a separately negotiated licence.

nodes.s: Minimal LiDAR odometry based on point-to-point ICP with adaptive thresholding, working across sensors with few parameters.
nodes.w: Works out of the box on almost any LiDAR without IMU; ideal hackathon starting point.
nodes.h: `pip install kiss-icp` and run on a rosbag or KITTI folder in minutes. Add KISS-SLAM for loop closure.

nodes.s: LiDAR SLAM that adds loop closure and pose-graph optimization on top of KISS-ICP odometry.
nodes.w: Full LiDAR SLAM with the same low-configuration philosophy.
nodes.h: Pip-installable; quick to demo on outdoor bags.

nodes.s: Loop-closure detection using bird's-eye-view density images of local LiDAR maps.
nodes.w: Sensor-agnostic loop closure that plugs into any LiDAR odometry.
nodes.h: Python bindings via pip.

nodes.s: LiDAR-inertial odometry aiming to work without sensor-specific modelling or heavy tuning.
nodes.w: Recent (2025-2026) LIO from the KISS-ICP group; good for unknown hardware.
nodes.h: `pip install "rko_lio[all]"` then `rko_lio -v /path/to/bags` runs on ROS 1 or ROS 2 bags with a rerun viewer; a ROS 2 node is also available. You must supply IMU and LiDAR extrinsics if the bag's TF tree lacks them. No loop closure - see rko_slam for that.

nodes.s: Lightweight ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping that segments ground to speed up feature extraction on UGVs.
nodes.w: Classic UGV LiDAR SLAM for rough terrain on modest compute.
nodes.h: ROS 1 only, unmaintained, tuned for Velodyne VLP-16. Use LIO-SAM or KISS-ICP instead unless reproducing baselines.

nodes.s: Real-time 2D and 3D SLAM with submaps and branch-and-bound loop closure across many sensor configurations.
nodes.w: Widely deployed 2D LiDAR SLAM for indoor and warehouse robots.
nodes.h: Project is in maintenance mode with little activity. Still available via ROS packages and works for 2D indoor mapping.

nodes.s: Versatile point-cloud localization and mapping framework with GPU-accelerated factor graphs, supporting many range sensors and optional IMU.
nodes.w: Modern, maintained 3D mapping with GPU speedups and an extensible module system.
nodes.h: Prebuilt packages exist for ROS 2; GPU optional but recommended.

nodes.s: Collection of fast GICP and VGICP point-cloud registration implementations, multithreaded and CUDA.
nodes.w: Fast scan registration building block used by many LiDAR and radar SLAM systems.
nodes.h: Successor library small_gicp is more actively maintained.

nodes.s: Efficient, parallel point-cloud registration library (GICP, ICP variants) with C++ and Python APIs.
nodes.w: Pip-installable registration to build your own LiDAR odometry or map-based relocalization fast.
nodes.h: `pip install small_gicp`; good for scan-to-map localization prototypes.

nodes.s: Lightweight tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry using parallel sparse incremental voxels instead of a k-d tree.
nodes.w: Faster variant of the FAST-LIO design for constrained compute.
nodes.h: ROS 1; same config style as FAST-LIO.

nodes.s: Lightweight LiDAR-inertial odometry with coarse-to-fine continuous-time motion correction (ICRA 2023).
nodes.w: Accurate and compute-light LIO for aerial and ground robots.
nodes.h: ROS 1 on master; ROS 2 is supported on the repo's feature/ros2 branch.

nodes.s: Relocalization in a prebuilt map using FAST-LIO odometry plus global scan-to-map registration.
nodes.w: Localize in a map you surveyed earlier, the standard pattern for GNSS-denied ground ops in known areas.
nodes.h: ROS 1; build a map with FAST-LIO first, then localize. Needs a rough initial pose (RViz or another sensor). The global-localization node needs Python 2.7 and Open3D 0.9, so plan for a Melodic-era environment or a container.

nodes.s: LiDAR global place descriptor for loop detection and relocalization (backup of the original IRAP KAIST repo).
nodes.w: Simple, widely used LiDAR loop-closure descriptor; plugs into most LiDAR SLAM.
nodes.h: Header-only style C++; SC-LIO-SAM shows integration.

nodes.s: LIO-SAM combined with Scan Context loop closure for more reliable large-scale LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
nodes.w: Practical recipe for adding a global descriptor to an existing LIO.
nodes.h: ROS 1; same setup as LIO-SAM.

nodes.s: Stable Triangle Descriptor for 3D point-cloud place recognition and loop closure.
nodes.w: Works with solid-state LiDARs and small fields of view where Scan Context struggles.
nodes.h: ROS 1 demos; integrates with FAST-LIO. Licence: GPLv2 but the README allows it free only for personal and academic use; commercial use needs a separate licence.

nodes.s: Certifiable, outlier-robust point-cloud registration library with C++, Python and MATLAB bindings.
nodes.w: Global registration that tolerates extreme outlier rates, useful for map-to-map alignment and relocalization.
nodes.h: Needs correspondences (e.g. FPFH) as input; Python bindings make it quick to prototype.

nodes.s: Fast, robust global registration for terrestrial robots that assumes near-planar motion to cut degrees of freedom.
nodes.w: Faster global relocalization for ground vehicles.
nodes.h: Smaller research codebase; pair with KISS-ICP.

nodes.s: Tightly coupled sliding-window factor-graph fusion of IMU with LiDAR (geometric and photometric), radar radial-speed factors and external odometry such as VIO.
nodes.w: From the group behind DARPA SubT field robots; relevant to smoke/dark/dust scenarios.
nodes.h: ROS Noetic; publishes nav_msgs/Odometry. Radar factor lets you keep velocity constraints when LiDAR is blinded by dust or smoke.

nodes.s: ROS 1/ROS 2 driver for Livox LiDARs such as Mid-360 and HAP.
nodes.w: Mid-360 is a common cheap LiDAR for drones; you need this driver to feed FAST-LIO and friends.
nodes.h: Build with the Livox SDK2; set the custom message format expected by FAST-LIO.

nodes.s: 3D LiDAR graph SLAM with NDT/GICP scan matching odometry, loop detection and optional GPS, IMU and floor-plane constraints.
nodes.w: Simple, hackable graph SLAM that 4DRadarSLAM and others build on; GPS constraints make it handy for mixed GNSS/denied runs.
nodes.h: ROS 1; GLIM is the author's newer framework.

nodes.s: Distributed front end of Kimera-Multi: handles the inter-robot communication protocol and pose-graph coarsening; the robust distributed optimization back end is DPGO.
nodes.w: Reusable distributed SLAM back end.
nodes.h: Used through Kimera-Multi.

nodes.s: Distributed pose-graph optimization library with certifiably correct solutions for multi-robot SLAM.
nodes.w: Solver core for decentralized multi-robot SLAM.
nodes.h: Library only; feed it pose graphs from each robot.

nodes.s: ROS 2 decentralized collaborative SLAM supporting LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D, with sparse inter-robot communication.
nodes.w: Designed for bandwidth-limited swarms, a realistic constraint under jamming.
nodes.h: This repo is only the core cslam ROS 2 package (loop closure detection front end and pose-graph back end); setup, launch files and docs live in the main MISTLab/Swarm-SLAM repo. Experiments run on recorded multi-robot datasets. Pick one sensor type to start.

nodes.s: Centralized collaborative visual-inertial SLAM where agents run VIO and a server merges maps; COVINS-G is VIO-front-end agnostic.
nodes.w: Pattern for drones sharing maps through a ground station.
nodes.h: ROS 1 + Docker; COVINS-G can take poses from any VIO such as OpenVINS.

nodes.s: English edition of Gao Xiang's open textbook on visual SLAM, from geometry and Lie groups to back-end optimization.
nodes.w: Best free practical intro for a team ramping up on SLAM in a weekend.
nodes.h: PDF and code exercises (slambook2 repo).

nodes.s: The standard Linux implementation of IEEE 1588 PTP: ptp4l (boundary/ordinary/transparent clock), phc2sys (sync system clock to a NIC hardware clock), ts2phc (discipline a PHC from 1PPS + NMEA), pmc for management queries, and timemaster. richardcochran/linuxptp on GitHub carries the same tree.
nodes.w: If a hackathon build needs sub-microsecond time across several computers (sensor nodes, TDOA receivers, a radar array), this is the off-the-shelf way to get it on Linux with hardware timestamping.
nodes.h: apt install linuxptp. Needs NICs with hardware timestamping (check `ethtool -T`); Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 and Intel i210/i225 work. Use ts2phc with a GNSS 1PPS to build a grandmaster, ptp4l -S for software timestamping in a demo. Log `pmc` offsets to show holdover and attack behaviour.

nodes.s: NTP client and server that also disciplines the system clock from reference clocks (1PPS, gpsd shared memory, PHC). Supports NTS, hardware timestamping on NTP packets, and source selection with outlier rejection. GitHub mirror: mlichvar/chrony.
nodes.w: The default Linux time daemon on most distributions; combining a GNSS refclock with several NTS servers is the quickest way to get a clock that notices when one source lies.
nodes.h: Configure `refclock PPS /dev/pps0 lock NMEA` plus `refclock SHM 0` from gpsd, add `server ... nts` lines, then `chronyc sources -v` and `chronyc tracking` show offset, frequency and which sources are rejected. Good live demo of source selection when one GNSS source is walked off.

nodes.s: A security-focused refactor of the reference NTP implementation with much of the legacy code removed, NTS support and the classic refclock drivers. GitHub mirror: ntpsec/ntpsec.
nodes.w: Keeps the reference-implementation refclock drivers (useful for odd timing receivers) while dropping much of the attack surface of classic ntpd.
nodes.h: Use when a specific refclock driver is needed that chrony lacks; otherwise chrony is easier. ntpviz plots offsets and frequency from its logs.

nodes.s: The Network Time Foundation's reference implementation of NTPv4 (ntpd, ntpq, ntpdate and refclock drivers).
nodes.w: The baseline that NTP attack papers were written against; useful to reproduce published time-shifting attacks in a lab.
nodes.h: Mostly a reference for behaviour comparisons; prefer chrony or ntpd-rs for new builds.

nodes.s: A memory-safe NTP client and server in Rust with NTS support, from the Pendulum project (Trifecta Tech Foundation).
nodes.w: NTS-authenticated time from a small Rust daemon: a reasonable second time source to cross-check GNSS time on an edge box.
nodes.h: Packages and a container exist; configure NTS sources and read offsets via ntp-ctl. Its source-selection behaviour is a useful comparison with chrony.

nodes.s: A PTP (IEEE 1588-2019) implementation in Rust: a platform-agnostic library with a Linux daemon and an STM32 example for embedded targets.
nodes.w: A second PTP stack to compare against linuxptp, and a route to PTP on embedded targets.
nodes.h: Try the Linux daemon against a linuxptp grandmaster; library use needs more effort.

nodes.s: Server side for a pool of NTS time servers: a key-exchange front end that hands clients to member servers while keeping authentication end to end.
nodes.w: Authenticated public time at pool scale is a prerequisite for using network time as an anti-spoofing cross-check.
nodes.h: Background reading for the authenticated-time story; not needed to build a demo.

nodes.s: Meta's Go libraries and tools for NTP and PTP: protocol implementations, PTP hardware clock and timestamping helpers, a PTP server (ptp4u), the simple-PTP client sptp, ptpcheck/ntpcheck diagnostics, a Calnex API client, leap-second utilities and the oscillatord monitoring protocol. Formerly facebook/time.
nodes.w: Production code from a large-scale PTP deployment, including tools to inspect PTP clients and to monitor time cards.
nodes.h: Go build; `ptpcheck` and `ntpcheck` are the quickest wins for diagnosing a lab setup.

nodes.s: Open Compute Project Time Appliance Project hardware: a PCIe card with a GNSS receiver and an atomic or OCXO holdover oscillator that turns a server into a PTP grandmaster, plus specs and drivers.
nodes.w: An open reference design for exactly the GNSS + holdover-oscillator architecture resilient timing guidance recommends.
nodes.h: Hardware, not a 48 h build; read the architecture and holdover sections for design ideas.

nodes.s: OCP specification for an open time server: COTS server, a NIC with hardware timestamps and PPS in/out, and the Time Card as the GNSS/oscillator source.
nodes.w: A concise architecture document for a GNSS-backed time server with holdover; useful as a slide template for a resilient-timing pitch.
nodes.h: Read-only spec. Use the block diagram and responsibilities split when designing your own time node.

nodes.s: Daemon that disciplines the oscillator on the Orolia (Safran) Atomic Reference Time Card from a PPS reference and exposes monitoring.
nodes.w: Real disciplining code for a miniature atomic clock on a time card, to compare with toy GPSDO loops.
nodes.h: Needs the hardware; read the disciplining code for the loop design.

nodes.s: Go implementation of Roughtime, a protocol that returns signed coarse timestamps so a client can prove a server lied and can combine several servers.
nodes.w: Gives a cryptographically checkable, coarse sanity bound on time, useful to catch large GNSS or NTP time shifts at boot.
nodes.h: Query several public Roughtime servers at startup; reject GNSS time if it is outside their bound. Accuracy is seconds-level by design, not a fine timing source.

nodes.s: Cloudflare's Rust implementation of Network Time Security (NTS) key exchange and NTP server/client. Archived.
nodes.w: Readable NTS reference code; for running NTS use chrony, ntpd-rs or NTPsec.
nodes.h: Archived; read only.

nodes.s: Python library for time and frequency stability statistics: Allan, modified Allan, overlapping, Hadamard and time deviation, plus confidence intervals and power-law noise generators.
nodes.w: The tool to turn a logged clock offset series into an ADEV/TDEV plot and to read holdover performance off it.
nodes.h: pip install allantools; feed phase data from chronyc tracking logs, ptp4l offsets or a TICC. Plot ADEV per oscillator and compare with datasheet curves.

nodes.s: Firmware and design files for TAPR's Arduino-based sub-nanosecond time interval counter, used to compare 1PPS outputs.
nodes.w: Cheap way to measure a GPSDO or GNSS receiver PPS against a reference and get the phase data ADEV tools need.
nodes.h: Needs the board; output is a text stream of timestamps that pipes into allantools.

nodes.s: Experimental GPS-disciplined oscillator: STM32 Black Pill, u-blox NEO-M8, a DAC and a used 10 MHz OCXO, with Arduino-framework firmware counting the OCXO against the 1PPS.
nodes.w: Low-cost build that shows the full GPSDO loop on hobby parts; a starting point for adding holdover and spoof-detection logic.
nodes.h: Parts are cheap and available; the loop is frequency-counting with long averaging, so expect hours to settle. felixd/STM32-GPSDO is a fork.

nodes.s: Archive of Lars Walenius' Arduino GPSDO from the EEVblog forum: a PI loop with a simple 1 ns resolution time-interval phase detector between the GPS 1PPS and the divided OCXO.
nodes.w: The design many hobby GPSDOs copy; its loop and time-interval counter trick are a compact reference.
nodes.h: Reference files only; derivatives such as paulvee/Lars-GPSDO-V4.2 and W3AXL/Simple-GPSDO are maintained builds.

nodes.s: Replacement firmware for a widely sold BH3SAP GPSDO module, with menus for PPB trend, PWM value storage and PPS resync.
nodes.w: Turns a cheap off-the-shelf GPSDO into something whose discipline and holdover behaviour you can read and modify.
nodes.h: Buy the module, flash over SWD. fredzo/gpsdo-fw is an active fork.

nodes.s: RP2040-based GPS-disciplined OCXO: firmware steers the OCXO via PWM from u-blox UBX timing messages (coarse from clock bias, fine from TIM-TP quantization error) and a Flask dashboard plots telemetry.
nodes.w: A modern open GPSDO that uses the receiver's quantization-error correction, the step most hobby designs skip.
nodes.h: Needs Pico SDK and the board; the web dashboard is a good pattern for a demo.

nodes.s: Minimal GPSDO: Arduino Nano steers an SI5351 synthesizer from the GPS 1PPS, with measurement time scaled to the observed stability and an optional phase detector.
nodes.w: Shows that a usable disciplined reference needs only a PPS and a few dollars of parts, and why the crystal's temperature sensitivity dominates.
nodes.h: Fast to build; replace the SI5351 crystal with a TCXO as the README advises.

nodes.s: A GPS-disciplined PTP grandmaster on a TI MSP432E4 MCU: u-blox receiver, software-disciplined crystal, PPS output, and NTP, PTP and SNMP servers on PoE with battery backup.
nodes.w: A single-board GNSS time server for a sensor network, the kind of node a distributed-sensing build needs.
nodes.h: Hardware specific; read for architecture of a small grandmaster.

nodes.s: Command-line utilities to read and write the configuration of Leo Bodnar GPSDO devices over USB HID.
nodes.w: Leo Bodnar units are a common lab GPS reference; scripting them helps a team set up repeatable reference outputs.
nodes.h: Only useful if you own the hardware.

nodes.s: Software for using a GNSS receiver on a computer for precise time: stratum-1 NTP with chrony, ntpd-rs or NTPsec, a PTP grandmaster on Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 or Intel NICs via linuxptp, RTK base/rover, and a web GUI to configure and monitor receivers.
nodes.w: The shortest path from a GNSS timing receiver to a working NTP/PTP time server with monitoring, on cheap hardware.
nodes.h: Install on a Pi CM4/CM5 with a u-blox timing receiver; follow satpulse.net. The GUI makes receiver state visible during a jamming or spoofing demo.

nodes.s: Configuration for a Raspberry Pi stratum-1 PTP and NTP time server built from a GNSS module with PPS.
nodes.w: A documented recipe a team can reproduce in hours for a local GNSS time reference.
nodes.h: Ansible-driven; budget an afternoon including GNSS antenna placement.

nodes.s: User-space tools and headers for the Linux PPS API (ppstest, ppsctl, ppswatch).
nodes.w: First thing to run when wiring a GNSS 1PPS into a Linux box: confirms pulses arrive and shows their jitter.
nodes.h: apt install pps-tools; `ppstest /dev/pps0`.

nodes.s: Older open-source PTPv2 daemon; the repository has been inactive since 2022.
nodes.w: Sometimes the only option on platforms without linuxptp hardware support; also appears in older PTP security papers.
nodes.h: Prefer linuxptp or statime.

nodes.s: Research implementation, based on linuxptp 3.1.1, that detects and mitigates PTP time-delay attacks by checking path asymmetry around cyclic redundant paths; includes a DPDK man-in-the-middle delay attacker for testing.
nodes.w: Shows how to defend the network time path, the part a GNSS-vs-PTP cross-check silently trusts.
nodes.h: Needs two NICs with hardware timestamping per node and DPDK for the attacker; plan a day of setup. The detection idea can be reproduced in software on logged offsets.

nodes.s: Proof-of-concept that feeds crafted NMEA sentences to a GPS-referenced NTP server to move its time; a red-team tool, inactive since 2017.
nodes.w: A ready-made test input for a time-spoofing detector: it reproduces the 'trusted serial GNSS time' weakness without RF.
nodes.h: Only for a closed lab against your own time server; no RF needed. Use it to show the detector alarm, not to attack anything.

nodes.s: Clock and network simulator from the chrony author: runs real NTP/PTP daemons against simulated clocks and network delays to test synchronization behaviour. Mirror of gitlab.com/chrony/clknetsim.
nodes.w: Lets a team test a time daemon's reaction to delay changes, steps or a lying server without hardware.
nodes.h: Linux only (LD_PRELOAD); the chrony test suite shows usage patterns.

nodes.s: Prometheus exporter for chrony tracking, sources and server statistics.
nodes.w: Puts clock offset, frequency and source health on a dashboard: the monitoring half of a timing-resilience demo.
nodes.h: Run next to chronyd, scrape with Prometheus, chart in Grafana; enable the sources collector to see each reference.

nodes.s: CERN Open Hardware Repository HDL cores for White Rabbit nodes and switches, including the White Rabbit PTP Core that gives sub-nanosecond synchronization over fibre Ethernet.
nodes.w: White Rabbit is the open route to sub-ns time across a distributed array (radio telescopes, accelerators) and an alternative to GNSS time inside a facility.
nodes.h: FPGA work; buy WR nodes/switches if you need it in a build.

nodes.s: Portable PTP stack ('PTP Ported to Silicon') used in White Rabbit nodes and switches; one source tree builds for bare metal and Linux.
nodes.w: A PTP stack that runs on soft-core CPUs, with the White Rabbit extension.
nodes.h: Read for embedded PTP design.

nodes.s: Embedded Linux software for the White Rabbit switch, including the PTP daemon integration and management.
nodes.w: Completes the White Rabbit picture for teams evaluating it as a distribution network.
nodes.h: Hardware specific.

nodes.s: GNU Radio receiver and live decoder for the DCF77 77.5 kHz time signal, covering both the OOK and phase-modulated channels, with a simulated transmitter and channel for testing without hardware.
nodes.w: Time from a terrestrial LF signal of opportunity, independent of GNSS; the simulator lets a team test without an LF front end.
nodes.h: Needs an SDR that reaches 77.5 kHz (e.g. Airspy HF+, or an upconverter). Docker CI image exists. Outside Europe swap to WWVB/MSF.

nodes.s: C library that decodes the DCF77 time code bitstream (from a cheap AM receiver module) covering most of the public standard.
nodes.w: A tiny GNSS-independent coarse time source for a microcontroller.
nodes.h: Pair with a DCF77 receiver module; accuracy is limited by the AM envelope.

nodes.s: General SDR receive/transmit application with many demodulator plugins; its Radio Clock plugin decodes LF time broadcasts including MSF, DCF77, TDF, WWVB, JJY and RBU.
nodes.w: One GUI that decodes several LF time broadcasts and many other signals, useful for a signals-of-opportunity timing demo.
nodes.h: Install packages or the Docker image; add the Radio Clock channel.

nodes.s: MATLAB scripts that localize a transmitter by TDOA from three RTL-SDR receivers, synchronizing them on a known reference transmitter instead of GNSS time.
nodes.w: Shows that distributed RF sensing needs nanosecond-level relative timing and one way to get it without GNSS disciplining.
nodes.h: Three Pis with RTL-SDRs plus the modified librtlsdr; MATLAB or port to Octave/NumPy.

nodes.s: Modified librtlsdr that switches between two frequencies during one recording without losing samples, so a reference transmitter and the target land in the same stream.
nodes.w: The trick that makes reference-transmitter synchronization of cheap TDOA receivers work.
nodes.h: Build on the Pi receivers; see the companion evaluation scripts.

nodes.s: Python clients for KiwiSDR receivers, including recorders that save IQ with GNSS timestamps from the receiver.
nodes.w: GNSS-timestamped IQ from a public network of receivers is the input for HF TDOA; it also shows what breaks when the receivers' GNSS time is denied.
nodes.h: Pure Python; record from public KiwiSDRs. Timestamps are only as good as each receiver's GNSS.

nodes.s: ROS algorithms that translate a sensor's own hardware timestamps into host system time from one-way timing, estimating skew and offset.
nodes.w: Multi-sensor fusion (camera, IMU, LiDAR) breaks quietly when timestamps are off; this is the lightweight fix when PTP is not available on the sensor.
nodes.h: ROS1 catkin package; inactive since 2022, port the algorithm if on ROS 2.

nodes.n: KROT (Где мы, Бариста?) - terrain correlation from radar altimeter
nodes.s: Team 'Где мы, Бариста?' solution to the 2026 'Полёт вслепую' (Blind flight) hackathon case: 'КРОТ' (Корреляционный Рельефный Определитель Траектории) turns a radar-altimeter NMEA-0183 log flown at a constant 1500 m MSL into a terrain profile, correlates it against a Copernicus GLO-30 GeoTIFF, and outputs map position, WGS-84 coordinates, ground speed, azimuth and match-quality metrics. React/Three.js operator panel plus separate C++ and Rust compute cores. README in Russian also records what the organisers' technical expert clarified (no IMU/camera, final-day validation log, bonus for speed and noise robustness).
nodes.w: The most complete public write-up of the TERCOM-style hackathon problem: input format, organiser constraints and a quality/confidence readout, which is exactly what a judge asks for.
nodes.h: Read the README section on expert clarifications first: it is the closest thing to a published spec of the case. The C++/Rust cores are the parts to lift; the web UI is a demo shell. Works offline against a GeoTIFF, no flight hardware needed.

nodes.n: Gagarin - TERCOM for UAVs without GNSS
nodes.s: Python TERCOM pipeline from the June 2026 'Полёт вслепую' hackathon, continued into July: correlates radar-altimeter profiles with a DEM using a coarse-to-fine 360-degree search, a hybrid MAD+NCC metric, minima-ratio discrimination, pre-rejection gates and an error-state Kalman filter with dead-reckoning fallback. Adds pre-flight terrain-informativeness analysis along a route, flags false-correlation risk segments, and tabulates expected search time on companion computers (RPi, Jetson, Orange Pi). README (Russian) reports per-region errors honestly, including failures where the azimuth was wrong.
nodes.w: Shows the failure modes of altimeter TERCOM in practice (wrong-azimuth peaks, flat terrain) and the engineering answers: quality grading, ambiguity detection and pre-flight route fingerprinting.
nodes.h: Best starting point if the brief is altimeter + DEM: the NCC/MAD search, quality gates and pre-flight terrain analyzer are separable. Performance table gives realistic onboard budgets. Self-reported errors are 50 m to 1.5 km depending on region, so treat as a baseline, not a result to quote.

nodes.n: Полёт вслепую - GCS with terrain-referenced navigation
nodes.s: Another team's take on the 2026 'Полёт вслепую' case, built as a ground control station for a UAV swarm: a Go telemetry ingestion gateway feeds RabbitMQ, a Python worker runs a particle-filter terrain-referenced navigation core on a DEM (rasterio) with Qdrant used for relocalisation, and MAVSDK-Python bridges to MAVLink vehicles. Full Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL, Redis, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki.
nodes.w: An architecture reference for putting a TRN estimator behind a real telemetry pipeline and operator panel rather than in a notebook.
nodes.h: docker compose up brings the whole stack; heavy for a 24-48h build. Useful mainly for the particle-filter TRN module and the MAVSDK bridge pattern. Docs in docs/ (domain.md covers TRN).

nodes.s: Hackathon code from team SKB 'ФИЗ-ТЕХ' for the June 2026 blind-flight case: takes NMEA, sample rate, barometric altitude and a height map, and estimates track by profile correlation. Post-processing is the stable mode (multithreaded, vectorised); a sliding-window real-time mode adds Kalman filtering. Outputs include true vs estimated tracks over the map, profile comparisons and speed/azimuth correlation heatmaps; a Webots simulation was used to generate test data.
nodes.w: A compact Python baseline with heatmaps over speed and azimuth, handy for visualising why altimeter matching is ambiguous.
nodes.h: Run gui.py. README says post-processing is more stable than real time and that a 10 m altimeter error was tested. Demo videos are on Yandex Disk links.

nodes.s: Personal Python prototype of terrain-relative navigation: matches a height profile along the route against a DEM and estimates position with a particle filter from an imprecise start. Simulates altimeter noise, bias and outliers, and was exercised on synthetic maps and Copernicus GLO-30 tiles for three Bulgarian areas from flat to mountainous. README in Russian.
nodes.w: Clean, self-contained particle-filter TRN with a noise model, a good teaching companion to the hackathon correlation solutions.
nodes.h: Laptop-only; load a GeoTIFF or generate a synthetic DEM. Swap its measurement model for real radar-altimeter logs to compare against NCC-based TERCOM.

nodes.s: C firmware for a microcontroller-based simulator of the A-053 aircraft radio altimeter; part 1 of 2, with PC software as the second part. README is a one-line Russian description.
nodes.w: Niche, but relevant to TERCOM work: hardware-in-the-loop testing needs something that emits realistic altimeter output.
nodes.h: Little documentation; read the source to see the output interface before planning HIL use. Last push 2022.

nodes.n: aerial-nav - GPS-denied navigation via Siamese network
nodes.s: Matches onboard camera frames to a pre-built satellite map of the route: a ResNet-18 Siamese network with SAFA spatial aggregation ranks map tiles indexed at 13 altitude levels (0-1200 m), then SuperPoint/LightGlue with RANSAC homography refines position and heading. README in Russian.
nodes.w: A full coarse-retrieval plus fine-registration VPS pipeline, the same structure fielded visual positioning products describe.
nodes.h: Good template for a two-stage VPS demo: retrieval narrows the search, LightGlue gives the fix. Check what weights and data are shipped before relying on it.

nodes.s: Diploma project: autonomous quadcopter navigation in PX4 SITL + Gazebo with ROS 2, RTAB-Map visual SLAM for mapping and localisation, A* global planning, VFH plus a custom 3D manoeuvre for obstacle avoidance, and YOLO person detection. README in Russian.
nodes.w: An integrated sim stack that wires SLAM, planning and avoidance to PX4, which is the glue most teams lose time on.
nodes.h: Needs a working ROS 2 + PX4 SITL + Gazebo setup (hours, not minutes). Reuse the node layout and the SLAM-to-planner wiring.

nodes.n: MVIO - monocular visual-inertial odometry in C++
nodes.s: C++ monocular VIO: ORB features tracked with Lucas-Kanade flow, parallax-based keyframes, essential-matrix initialisation then PnP, IMU preintegration, least-squares scale and gravity estimation, and a 15-state error-state Kalman filter. Built on OpenCV 4.6 and Eigen 3.4. Companion to a Russian Habr article.
nodes.w: A small, readable VIO you can actually step through, unlike the large research systems.
nodes.h: CMake build; configs in configs/. Calibrate your own camera (camera.yaml) as the article insists. No accuracy numbers are published.

nodes.s: Minimal Python project: essential-matrix visual odometry fused with IMU in an EKF to estimate position without GPS. README is two lines in Russian.
nodes.w: Smallest possible VO+IMU EKF skeleton, useful as a starting file rather than a system.
nodes.h: Read the code directly; there is no documentation of inputs or datasets.

nodes.s: PyTorch CNN+RNN network that predicts relative pose between frames from a monocular camera and 6-axis IMU, trained on data collected in Microsoft AirSim with ground-truth poses and a composite loss to limit drift. README in Russian.
nodes.w: A learned-VIO baseline with a simulator data loop, relevant if the team wants to compare deep and geometric odometry.
nodes.h: Needs AirSim to regenerate data; notebooks otherwise. Expect sim-to-real gaps.

nodes.s: Diploma C++ code modelling a moving user, GNSS operation and an astro-corrector (star-tracker style celestial correction), with integrator and linear-algebra helpers. No README; description in Russian.
nodes.w: Rare open code pairing GNSS with celestial correction, the classic long-range fallback when GNSS is degraded.
nodes.h: Undocumented; useful only as a reference for structuring a GNSS + celestial simulation.

nodes.s: Archived fork of the Clover framework holding team V-NAV's CopterHack 2022 entry (article in docs/ru/v-nav.md on branch v-nav_article): a multi-camera plus IMU optical navigation module using graph-based SLAM with CNN-extracted features, aimed at indoor and GNSS-denied industrial-site flights, with a companion Pixhawk FMUv6U + CM4 + Coral board concept.
nodes.w: Shows how a Russian student team scoped GNSS-free navigation on the Clover/PX4 stack; a design reference more than working code.
nodes.h: Read the article on the v-nav_article branch; the fork itself is mostly upstream Clover.

nodes.s: Fork of Clover with Tomsk Polytechnic team TPU_2's CopterHack 2023 entry (docs/ru/tpu_2.md on branch tpu_2): an algorithm for autonomous flight through dense forest using empirical search plus classic planners such as Dijkstra and RRT.
nodes.w: Under-canopy flight is a GNSS-degraded case; the article frames planning in clutter on an educational stack.
nodes.h: Article-level material; check the branch for code before planning around it.

nodes.s: Drone-side backend of the Clover Rescue project (CopterHack 2022, third place), which the team describes as returning the Clover to the user or takeoff point with one click when radio contact is lost.
nodes.w: Lost-link return-home is the same behaviour EW-resilience work needs; this is a small worked example on Clover.
nodes.h: Pair with DevMBS/CRTClient. Old (2022) and tied to the Clover image.

nodes.n: Приемники ГНСС - GNSS receiver design handbook (MPEI)
nodes.s: Source of a Russian-language textbook for the MPEI course on satellite navigation user equipment by I. Korogodin (NavSysLab): signals, acquisition, tracking loops, positioning and practical receiver design.
nodes.w: One of the few open, maintained Russian-language GNSS receiver textbooks; useful to understand why jamming and spoofing break tracking loops.
nodes.h: Reading material, not code. Pair with gnss-sdr for hands-on work.

nodes.s: Assignments and lab reports for the first semester of the MPEI navigation receivers course (2020): signal model, statistical correlator equivalent, positioning accuracy and further labs. Russian.
nodes.w: Structured exercises for building intuition about correlators and positioning accuracy.
nodes.h: Good pre-hackathon homework for whoever owns the GNSS side.

nodes.s: MPEI student project template for computing GLONASS satellite positions from broadcast ephemerides. Russian.
nodes.w: GLONASS ephemerides use a different (numerical integration) model than GPS; this is a compact way to learn it.
nodes.h: Pair with the GPS twin exercise (Korogodin/gpsephexercise).

nodes.s: Python homework for a course on GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou: GLONASS satellite position and velocity from the almanac, a GLONASS L3OCp signal generator and Galileo E1-B/C signal shaping.
nodes.w: Small, runnable examples of modern GLONASS CDMA and Galileo E1 signal structure.
nodes.h: Needs almanac and code files as described in the README.

nodes.n: note-outdoor - knowledge base on GNSS-free autonomous navigation
nodes.s: Russian-language markdown knowledge base on navigation, data fusion, data links, hardware and system designs for platforms operating without GNSS, internet or cellular coverage and under possible EW, with worked selection scenarios by platform, range and budget.
nodes.w: A structured checklist for trading off navigation and comms options; useful for a design slide, not as evidence.
nodes.h: Use the 'quick choice by task' tables as a starting point, then verify claims against primary sources; authorship and sourcing are not documented.

nodes.n: Stone Nav - car navigation without GPS (iOS)
nodes.s: Ukrainian iPhone (Swift) car navigator that keeps guiding along a stored route when GPS disappears or is spoofed: it advances the position along the route by itself, and the driver corrects it by changing speed, pausing, nudging the point or tapping a landmark. Apple Maps, offline route storage, Ukrainian voice prompts. README in Ukrainian.
nodes.w: A pragmatic human-in-the-loop answer to spoofing: route-constrained dead reckoning with landmark resets.
nodes.h: Not on the App Store; sideload via Xcode. Useful idea for a dismounted or vehicle demo: snap to route and let the user re-anchor.

nodes.n: bsu-science - BSU diploma on camera-based UAV navigation
nodes.s: LaTeX sources of science reports from BSU (Belarus, FAMCS), including a diploma 'Разработка алгоритмов навигации БПЛА' that compares SIFT/SURF/ORB, surveys SLAM and SfM 3D mapping, and demonstrates SLAM + ROS + webcam + SfM to localise a UAV on a 3D terrain map without GPS.
nodes.w: A short student-level map of the visual-navigation design space in Russian.
nodes.h: Slides only (see the GitHub Pages presentation); no runnable pipeline.

nodes.s: ROS-based software stack and Raspberry Pi image for the Clover educational quadcopter (PX4 underneath). Ships ArUco marker detection, marker-map navigation published to PX4 as a vision position estimate, downward optical-flow position hold, and a Gazebo simulator. Documentation is written in Russian first, with English translations.
nodes.w: One of the most complete Russian-language open stacks for GNSS-free indoor/outdoor flight: optical flow plus marker maps fed into the autopilot EKF, with documented parameter sets.
nodes.h: Use the Docker/VM simulator image to fly ArUco-map navigation without hardware in hours. The marker-map => VPE path is a ready template for any external position source into PX4. ROS1 (Noetic) based; ROS2 only via community ports. Canonical repo is CopterExpress/clover; klever-coex/clover is a recent fork.

nodes.s: Python/OpenCV return-to-home for a quadcopter with a downward camera and no GPS. Instead of integrating optical flow, it stores keyframes ('rungs') on the way out and, on the way back, matches the nearest rung and truncates history, sending the residual offset to the controller. README and the companion Habr article are in Russian.
nodes.w: A small, readable alternative to drift-prone flow integration for the specific job of getting home when GNSS is gone; the same idea as teach-and-repeat.
nodes.h: Pure Python + OpenCV, runs on a laptop against recorded downward video. Integration with a flight controller is left to the user (README sends offsets; no MAVLink bridge verified). Good seed for a 'return home under jamming' demo.

nodes.s: Russian-language hackathon solution for 'Полёт вслепую' (Blind flight): estimate aircraft position, ground speed and heading without GNSS by reconstructing a terrain profile (barometric altitude minus radar altimeter) and matching it against a DEM, TERCOM style.
nodes.w: A compact, documented TERCOM pipeline on real DEM data; shows how a GNSS-denied hackathon problem was posed and solved in 2026.
nodes.h: Reads DEM + altimeter series; small dependency set. Useful as a baseline if a hackathon gives altimeter/DEM data. Accuracy figures are not independently checked here.

nodes.s: Second public solution to the same 'Полёт вслепую' hackathon task: web prototype that reads a GeoTIFF DEM and NMEA-0183 radar-altimeter messages, searches start point, speed and azimuth hypotheses by RMSE/correlation, and reports a confidence and a flat-terrain check.
nodes.w: Shows the practical details (UTM projection, bilinear DEM sampling, weighted scoring for informative relief, flat-terrain rejection) that a TERCOM demo needs.
nodes.h: Streamlit app on rasterio + pyproj; an optional Rust core (built automatically if cargo is installed) speeds up the hypothesis search. Includes a synthetic NMEA generator from a real DEM, which is handy for building test data fast. Small repo (about a dozen commits).

nodes.s: Controller for an autonomous ground cargo platform in the amr-sim simulator plus an operator workstation, built for the 'Безопасный маршрут' case of KosmoHackathon 2026 (2nd place in the final). A Kalman filter fuses wheel odometry, gyro and lidar-to-wall-map matching to keep position in GNSS shadow, and speed is set from a 3 s pedestrian motion forecast.
nodes.w: Worked example of GNSS-shadow ground navigation with a scored simulator benchmark, written in Russian.
nodes.h: README reports position error and collision results against the organisers' baseline (their numbers, not verified here). Depends on the organisers' amr-sim, which may not be public.

nodes.s: Pet project for local UAV navigation without GNSS: AirSim video streamed over ZeroMQ into monocular ORB-SLAM3, a ROS node converts NED/ENU frames, IMU data corrects monocular scale, and a PID controller tracks a trajectory. Russian README.
nodes.w: A minimal end-to-end sim loop (simulator => SLAM => control) that a team can copy to test VO under GNSS loss.
nodes.h: Needs ORB-SLAM3 built separately and AirSim (archived upstream). Useful mainly as an architecture reference.

nodes.s: Russian graduate thesis code: 'Development of a UAV inertial navigation module using auxiliary navigation data'. C++ client for INS/GNSS fusion, a C# flight simulator with sensor emulation, a Node.js telemetry server and a Vue web UI.
nodes.w: Small, self-contained INS + aiding simulator with a visual front-end; good for teaching drift and aiding.
nodes.h: Mixed C++/C#/Node stack; setup cost moderate. Treat as reference, not a library.

nodes.s: MIPT (FAKT) 2026 diploma: local navigation for a UAV under GNSS suppression, correcting a strapdown INS with LoRa two-way-ranging (TWR) distances to ground beacons. Python code includes INS mechanization, an error-state EKF, a tightly coupled MSCKF variant, least-squares triangulation, an IMU simulator and parameter studies; thesis and slides are in Russian (.docx/.pptx).
nodes.w: Open, inspectable version of the 'ground beacons instead of satellites' approach that Ukrainian vendors also describe publicly (see Vyriy beacon navigation).
nodes.h: Pure Python simulation, no hardware needed; good basis for a beacon-ranging + INS demo. No README; read Code/main.py and the thesis.

nodes.s: Scripts (packaged as an agent skill) that repair Garmin/Strava .fit activities corrupted by GNSS spoofing or jamming: tracks that teleport to a fixed far-away location, impossible speed spikes, phantom distance. Bilingual English/Ukrainian README written from the Ukrainian civilian experience of EW.
nodes.w: Encodes practical spoof signatures seen by civilians in Ukraine (position jumps, speed outliers) as simple detection rules; a quick start for track-level spoof detection.
nodes.h: Tiny Python codebase; the detection heuristics can be lifted into any trajectory plausibility checker. Very new (Oct 2026).

nodes.s: Unofficial Ukrainian translation of key sections of the ArduPilot Copter documentation, with a translation-status file and a built site. CC BY-SA 3.0 like the original.
nodes.w: Lowers the entry barrier for Ukrainian-speaking teams and operators configuring ArduPilot, including non-GPS navigation sections.
nodes.h: Reference only. May lag the English wiki; the original wins on conflicts.

nodes.s: Student project from SPbU (CITEC) on returning a UAV to its launch point when both GNSS and the ground-station link are lost, targeting a RockPi 4 companion computer. Description in Russian; README is minimal and points to an external Notion board.
nodes.w: Same problem statement as many Ukrainian field requirements (lost link + lost GNSS => come home), from the Russian academic side.
nodes.h: Sparse docs; read the C sources directly. Reference value only.

nodes.s: Meta-repository from Russian vendor Geoscan for the Pioneer Max educational quadcopter: system images, ROS workspace, web control apps and guides, documented in Russian.
nodes.w: Shows how a Russian educational drone ecosystem packages ROS, mission tools and indoor positioning for schools and competitions.
nodes.h: Hardware-specific; useful only as reference for packaging and docs. Last push March 2024.

nodes.n: Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild
nodes.s: Proposes matching drone camera frames to open satellite imagery with learned feature matching to get absolute position without GNSS, evaluated on flights over non-urban areas.
nodes.kt: Satellite tiles + learned matcher is a workable visual GPS baseline Failure cases cluster over low-texture and changed terrain

nodes.n: AnyLoc: Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: Shows that unsupervised aggregation of foundation-model (DINOv2) features gives place recognition that generalizes across domains including aerial imagery, without VPR-specific training.
nodes.kt: Foundation features + VLAD work training-free Aerial domain included in the evaluation

nodes.n: Exploring the best way for UAV visual localization under Low-altitude Multi-view Observation Condition: a Benchmark
nodes.s: Builds a benchmark for low-altitude, oblique-view UAV absolute visual localization and systematically compares retrieval, matching and refinement choices.
nodes.kt: Low-altitude oblique views are much harder than nadir Gives evidence for picking retrieval/matcher combos

nodes.n: UAV-VisLoc: A Large-scale Dataset for UAV Visual Localization
nodes.s: Introduces a dataset of real UAV flight images paired with satellite maps over varied terrain for evaluating UAV visual localization.
nodes.kt: Real flights with ground truth Covers terrain types beyond cities

nodes.n: Long-range UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
nodes.s: Matches night-time UAV thermal imagery to satellite RGB maps using domain adaptation to cope with scarce paired thermal-satellite data; releases code and a nighttime dataset.
nodes.kt: Night visual GPS is possible via thermal-to-RGB matching Domain adaptation offsets missing paired data

nodes.n: STHN: Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
nodes.s: Refines thermal-to-satellite localization with learned homography estimation for precise alignment.
nodes.kt: Coarse-to-fine: retrieval then homography

nodes.n: UASTHN: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Satellite-Thermal Geo-localization
nodes.s: Adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography so a navigation filter can weight or reject visual fixes.
nodes.kt: Uncertainty makes visual fixes filter-ready

nodes.n: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization
nodes.s: Introduces the drone/satellite/ground benchmark that most drone cross-view geo-localization work evaluates on.
nodes.kt: Defines drone->satellite and satellite->drone retrieval tasks

nodes.n: SUES-200: A Multi-height Multi-scene Cross-view Image Benchmark Across Drone and Satellite
nodes.s: Drone-satellite benchmark with imagery at several flight heights across varied scenes.
nodes.kt: Altitude changes strongly affect retrieval accuracy

nodes.n: Sample4Geo: Hard Negative Sampling For Cross-View Geo-Localisation
nodes.s: Shows that a simple contrastive setup with careful hard-negative sampling performs strongly on cross-view geo-localization benchmarks.
nodes.kt: Data sampling matters as much as architecture

nodes.n: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
nodes.s: Redesigns SuperGlue-style attention matching to be faster and adaptive, stopping early on easy pairs.
nodes.kt: Adaptive depth trades compute for difficulty Permissive license, easy to deploy

nodes.s: Dense matcher combining foundation-model coarse features with fine refinement, robust to large appearance change.
nodes.kt: Dense warps + certainty help on cross-season, cross-sensor pairs

nodes.n: Grounding Image Matching in 3D with MASt3R
nodes.s: Frames matching as a 3D problem on top of DUSt3R, producing dense matches robust to extreme viewpoint change.
nodes.kt: 3D reasoning handles oblique-vs-nadir gaps

nodes.n: XFeat: Accelerated Features for Lightweight Image Matching
nodes.s: Lightweight feature extraction and matching architecture aimed at real-time use on constrained hardware.
nodes.kt: Real-time matching without a big GPU

nodes.n: Optimal Transport Aggregation for Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: Introduces SALAD, aggregating DINOv2 local features into a global descriptor via optimal transport.
nodes.kt: Strong retrieval descriptor for the coarse localization stage

nodes.n: From Coarse to Fine: Robust Hierarchical Localization at Large Scale
nodes.s: The HF-Net paper and foundation of hloc: global retrieval to find candidate places, then local matching for precise pose.
nodes.kt: Retrieve-then-match is the scalable pattern

nodes.n: A Review on Deep Learning for UAV Absolute Visual Localization
nodes.s: Survey of deep-learning approaches to UAV absolute visual localization against reference maps since 2019, in the journal Drones.
nodes.kt: Good map of methods, datasets and open problems Follows the same authors' 2021 review

nodes.n: Signal Enhancement for Magnetic Navigation Challenge Problem
nodes.s: Defines the AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge: remove the aircraft's own magnetic field from airborne magnetometer data so the Earth's anomaly field can be used for navigation, with released flight data and a scientific-ML baseline.
nodes.kt: Aircraft magnetic compensation is the core difficulty Provides real survey-flight data and a baseline Problem is compensation, the hard step before map matching Physics (Tolles-Lawson) plus ML beat either alone Data and baseline code are open Tolles-Lawson is the classical baseline to beat Scalar magnetometer mixes Earth core, crustal anomaly and aircraft fields Dataset released on Zenodo

nodes.s: Documentation and examples for MagNav.jl covering data loading, compensation models, map handling and navigation filters.
nodes.kt: Fastest route to running MagNav examples

nodes.s: Overview page for MagNav as an open-source technology from the DAF-MIT AI Accelerator.
nodes.kt: Context on program origin and goals

nodes.n: Absolute Positioning Using the Earth's Magnetic Anomaly Field
nodes.s: AFIT dissertation establishing airborne magnetic anomaly navigation methods and flight-test evaluation, the basis for later AFRL/MIT MagNav work.
nodes.kt: Map-matching filter design for scalar magnetometers Flight-test evidence of absolute positioning from anomaly maps

nodes.n: Magnetic Sensors in Flight Tests as Alternative PNT to GNSS
nodes.s: Trade-press overview of Air Force magnetic navigation flight testing and the research path from AFIT to operational trials.
nodes.kt: MagNav moved from lab to aircraft tests

nodes.n: Quantum-assured magnetic navigation achieves positioning accuracy better than a strategic-grade INS in airborne and ground-based field trials
nodes.s: Reports airborne and ground field trials of magnetic anomaly navigation using quantum magnetometers with map-matching, comparing against strategic-grade inertial navigation.
nodes.kt: Recent field evidence that MagNav is a practical GNSS alternative Sensor quality and noise rejection drive performance

nodes.s: DARPA program page for ANS, which pursued GPS-quality PNT in denied environments through precision inertial sensors (PINS) and the All Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN) sensor-fusion effort.
nodes.kt: ASPN aimed at plug-and-play fusion of many nav sensors Framed GNSS denial as a core military problem Combined ASPN-style sensor fusion with new IMU technology Explicit focus on reconfigurable multi-sensor navigation

nodes.n: DARPA Seeks PNT Robustness, Flexibility with All Source Positioning and Navigation Program
nodes.s: Background article on DARPA ASPN: a navigation architecture that accepts arbitrary combinations of sensors (cameras, magnetometers, radios, IMUs) with rapid reconfiguration.
nodes.kt: Shows the plug-and-play sensor-fusion goal that later GNSS-denied architectures inherit Phase 1 built algorithms and a software architecture Phase 2 targeted real-time fusion on SWaP-representative hardware

nodes.n: Navigation using carrier Doppler shift from a LEO constellation: TRANSIT on steroids
nodes.s: Analyzes positioning from carrier Doppler measurements of a large LEO constellation with a batch filter estimating position, velocity and clock terms, showing accuracy potentially comparable to pseudorange GNSS.
nodes.kt: Doppler-only LEO positioning is geometrically viable Needs many satellites in view; mega-constellations supply them

nodes.n: Exploiting Starlink Signals for Navigation: First Results
nodes.s: Early experimental demonstration of opportunistic positioning by tracking Doppler from Starlink satellites, without cooperation from the operator.
nodes.kt: Starlink can be used as an uncooperative PNT source Ephemeris error is a dominant limitation

nodes.n: Positioning with Starlink LEO Satellites: A Blind Doppler Spectral Approach
nodes.s: Estimates Doppler from Starlink downlinks blindly in the frequency domain without knowing the signal structure, and uses it for positioning from a poor initial estimate.
nodes.kt: Blind spectral Doppler avoids needing proprietary signal details

nodes.n: Initialization-Free LEO Doppler Positioning via Semidefinite Relaxation: A Cold-Start Approach
nodes.s: Formulates LEO Doppler positioning as an optimization solvable by semidefinite relaxation so it does not need a good initial position guess.
nodes.kt: Removes the initialization problem in Doppler positioning

nodes.n: Complementary PNT and GPS Backup Technologies Demonstration Report
nodes.s: Field demonstration of 11 GPS-backup technologies (including eLoran, terrestrial beacons, LEO and fiber timing) against defined scenarios, delivered to Congress.
nodes.kt: No single technology fully backs up GPS eLoran fails differently from GNSS, which is its value

nodes.s: Usage and API documentation for the tetra3 lost-in-space star plate solver, including database generation and solving images.
nodes.kt: Database generation controls speed vs field-of-view range

nodes.n: OpenSky: A Modular and Open-Source Simulator of Sky Polarization Measurements
nodes.s: Open simulator of what a polarimetric camera sees of the sky (intensity, angle and degree of polarization), validated against real captures, for developing polarization compasses.
nodes.kt: Lets you test sky-polarization heading without field data

nodes.n: Ukraine's Autonomous Killer Drones Defeat Electronic Warfare
nodes.s: Reporting on how Ukrainian drone developers respond to pervasive jamming of radio links and satellite navigation, including onboard optical navigation that keeps the drone flying after links are lost.
nodes.kt: Jamming makes onboard, map-based navigation a front-line requirement Optical navigation is spreading to cheap drones

nodes.n: UAVs: ISR, Deterrence and War (IISS Strategic Dossier)
nodes.s: IISS dossier on military UAV use, noting that GNSS is often effectively unavailable near the front line in Ukraine and that visual scene-matching navigation is a growing response.
nodes.kt: GNSS denial is the operating norm near the front Scene-matching navigation has decades of lineage

nodes.n: Ukrainian Drones Use Vermeer Optical Navigation System
nodes.s: Ukrainian defense outlet reporting that a US company's optical (visual) navigation system is being integrated into Ukrainian reconnaissance and strike drones.
nodes.kt: Commercial visual-navigation modules are reaching the field Vision-based absolute positioning against reference imagery is being fielded Vendor claims are not independently tested

nodes.s: ArduPilot Copter documentation hub for flying without GPS: optical flow, visual odometry cameras (RealSense T265, OAK-D, ModalAI VOXL), motion capture (OptiTrack, Vicon, Nokov), beacons/UWB (Marvelmind, Pozyx, Nooploop), ROS with Cartographer, GPS/non-GPS transitions and EKF origin handling.
nodes.kt: Single index of all ArduPilot GPS-free position sources Each method links to its sensor-specific setup page Menu of supported GPS-free aiding sources Guides for feeding external pose into EKF3

nodes.kt: Cartographer SLAM feeding EKF3 Basis for later ardupilot_ros work

nodes.n: Sam Hyams's GPS-denied RTH for MAVLink systems using LoRa radio ranging
nodes.s: Blog (shared on ArduPilot Discourse) on returning a plane home without GPS using range measurements from a LoRa radio to a ground beacon; discussion covers multilateration and EKF3 range fusion.
nodes.kt: Radio ranging as a cheap GNSS backup for RTH Needs multiple beacons for a full position fix

nodes.n: A non-divergent estimation algorithm in the presence of unknown correlations
nodes.s: The original covariance intersection (CI) paper (American Control Conference 1997). It fuses two estimates whose cross-correlation is unknown by taking a convex combination of their information matrices, which stays consistent whatever the true correlation is. This is the building block behind most decentralized cooperative localization filters that cannot track inter-agent correlations.
nodes.kt: CI gives a consistent fused estimate without knowing cross-covariance Motivated by decentralized estimation, where a plain Kalman update double-counts shared information Trades some conservatism for guaranteed consistency

nodes.n: Decentralized multi-robot cooperative localization using covariance intersection
nodes.s: IROS 2013 paper applying covariance intersection to multi-robot cooperative localization so that each robot only keeps its own state and covariance. Processing and communication scale linearly with team size, and the authors compare against the earlier split-CI method in simulation and experiments.
nodes.kt: Each robot estimates only its own pose; CI absorbs unknown inter-robot correlations Linear cost in the number of robots Standard reference baseline for CI-based cooperative localization

nodes.n: Recursive decentralized localization for multi-robot systems with asynchronous pairwise communication
nodes.s: IJRR 37(10) paper describing a fully decentralized EKF for collaborative localization that approximates inter-robot cross-correlations. Only the two robots involved in a relative measurement need to talk, no measurement history is stored, and generic measurement models are supported. Builds on the authors' RSS 2016 paper and is evaluated on real-world datasets.
nodes.kt: Pairwise, asynchronous communication only Keeps just the latest pose estimate per robot Approximates cross-correlations instead of dropping them

nodes.s: IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation 18(5) paper that decomposes the centralized cooperative-localization Kalman filter into one modified filter per robot ('collective localization'). Demonstrated on three robots and compared with a decentralized information filter. A foundational reference for exact (non-CI) distributed cooperative localization.
nodes.kt: Centralized-equivalent estimator split across robots Cross-correlations are handled exactly, at a communication cost Shows accuracy gain from relative robot-to-robot measurements

nodes.n: Decentralized Localization of Sparsely-Communicating Robot Networks: A Centralized-Equivalent Approach
nodes.s: IEEE T-RO 26(1) paper on decentralized state estimation for robot teams that are not always fully connected. The central result is that a robot can reproduce the centralized estimate using only its own knowledge of the communication history, whenever that estimate is attainable.
nodes.kt: Targets intermittent, sparse communication Centralized-equivalent result when the information has actually reached the robot Extended to cooperative SLAM in later work by the same group

nodes.s: Proceedings of the IEEE 97(2) tutorial on cooperative localization in wireless networks, applied to ultra-wideband ranging. It surveys the approaches and introduces SPAWN, a fully distributed message-passing (factor graph) algorithm with low communication overhead.
nodes.kt: Good tutorial entry point for range-based cooperative positioning SPAWN: distributed belief propagation over the network UWB ranging used as the running application

nodes.n: A Probabilistic Approach to Collaborative Multi-Robot Localization
nodes.s: Autonomous Robots 8(3) paper extending sample-based Markov (Monte Carlo) localization to robot teams: when one robot detects another, both robots' beliefs are updated. Real-robot and simulation experiments show faster and more accurate global localization than single-robot localization.
nodes.kt: Particle-filter view of cooperative localization Robot-to-robot detections synchronize beliefs Handles global localization, not only tracking

nodes.n: Cooperative localization for mobile agents: a recursive decentralized algorithm based on Kalman filter decoupling
nodes.s: Published in IEEE Control Systems Magazine 36(2), 2016. Reviews decentralization strategies for cooperative localization with a focus on how each keeps track of inter-agent correlations, then presents a decentralized implementation of the centralized EKF in which agents propagate local intermediate variables instead of cross-covariances, and the agent that takes a relative measurement acts as an interim master for the update.
nodes.kt: Readable survey of CL decentralization strategies Exact centralized-equivalent EKF without propagating cross-covariances Open arXiv version

nodes.s: IEEE T-RO 35(6) paper with two decentralized cooperative localization algorithms that do not maintain inter-agent correlations: one bounds the joint covariance to stay consistent, the other estimates the unknown cross-covariance by optimization. Only the two agents involved in a relative measurement communicate, with no network-wide connectivity requirement.
nodes.kt: Consistent CL without tracking correlations Pairwise communication only Demonstrated in simulation and a robot experiment

nodes.n: Resilient and consistent multirobot cooperative localization with covariance intersection
nodes.s: IEEE T-RO 38(1) paper that uses covariance intersection to separate an explicit communication update from the observation update in multirobot cooperative localization, keeping estimates consistent. It analyses when the covariance stays bounded as a function of the communication and observation graphs, and tests resilience on simulated and benchmark physical data.
nodes.kt: Decouples communication from observation so either can fail Covariance boundedness conditions in terms of graph topology Directly relevant to lossy tactical links

nodes.s: IROS 2021 paper on a consistent distributed visual-inertial estimator for multi-robot cooperative localization. Covariance intersection lets each robot keep only its own state and autocovariance while using common SLAM features and loop closures to other robots' past poses. Validated against a centralized counterpart in simulation and real experiments.
nodes.kt: CI applied to visual-inertial teams, not just range sensors Uses shared map features and inter-robot loop closures From the RPNG group behind OpenVINS

nodes.n: Weighted Covariance Intersection for Range-based Distributed Cooperative Localization of Multi-Vehicle Systems
nodes.s: Published in IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (2026). Argues that standard CI weighting criteria break down for 3D range-based distributed cooperative localization, where state components differ strongly in scale and observability, and proposes a weighted CI criterion for GNSS-denied multi-vehicle systems.
nodes.kt: Targets 3D range-only cooperative localization Shows why plug-in CI criteria give unbalanced estimates Recent (2025-2026) follow-up to the classic CI line

nodes.n: Consistent Distributed Cooperative Localization for Ultra Large-Scale Multi-agent Systems
nodes.s: Preprint on cooperative localization for very large networks (the paper's example is satellite mega-constellations) where per-agent resources must not grow with network size. It uses overlapping covariance intersection to exploit limited structure in the cross-correlations while staying consistent, and is fully distributed.
nodes.kt: Per-agent cost independent of team size Overlapping CI: less conservative than plain CI Relevant to large drone swarms as well as constellations

nodes.n: Autonomous GPS Integrity Monitoring Using the Pseudorange Residual
nodes.s: NAVIGATION 35(2) paper proposing satellite failure detection and isolation from the least-squares pseudorange residual, one of the founding RAIM formulations. Detection uses the range residual test statistic when six or more satellites are in view.
nodes.kt: Residual-based RAIM origin Detection and isolation from the over-determined solution Background for every later FDE scheme

nodes.n: A Baseline GPS RAIM Scheme and a Note on the Equivalence of Three RAIM Methods
nodes.s: NAVIGATION 39(3) paper written as the RTCA GPS MOPS were released. It proposes a baseline RAIM scheme for performance comparisons and shows that, at equal alarm rates, the range-comparison, least-squares-residual and parity methods give identical results.
nodes.kt: Range comparison, LS residual and parity RAIM are equivalent at equal alarm rate Intended as a simple standard baseline, not an optimal scheme Ties RAIM to the aviation MOPS context

nodes.s: NAVIGATION 61(4) paper with a step-by-step derivation of residual-based and solution-separation RAIM from common integrity and continuity risk definitions, including a parity-space view of solution separation. Solution separation can monitor better because its statistics are tailored to each fault hypothesis, but residual-based RAIM gives tighter integrity bounds in conventional efficient implementations.
nodes.kt: Side-by-side derivation of the two main RAIM families Parity-space interpretation of solution separation Useful when choosing an FDE scheme for a fused alt-PNT filter

nodes.n: Baseline advanced RAIM user algorithm and possible improvements
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 51(1) description of the baseline multi-fault, multi-constellation ARAIM user algorithm for LPV-200 vertical guidance. It covers pseudorange processing, nominal error models and prior fault probabilities to compute protection levels, how to choose which fault modes to monitor, fault exclusion, and a list of possible improvements.
nodes.kt: The reference ARAIM user algorithm in journal form Protection levels from solution separation over monitored fault modes Implemented in Stanford's MAAST tool

nodes.n: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C, ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Interim Report (Issue 1.0)
nodes.s: First (Milestone 1) report of the EU-US ARAIM subgroup, dated 19 December 2012, prepared by FAA, Stanford, MITRE, IIT, DLR, UniBW Munich, ESA and the European Commission. It gives an ARAIM overview, the requirements analysis for global LPV-200 vertical guidance, a reference user algorithm, first performance evaluation and the identified threats.
nodes.kt: Why ARAIM: multi-constellation integrity with ground-supplied fault rates LPV-200 as the driving requirement First reference air algorithm

nodes.n: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C-ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Milestone 2 Report
nodes.s: Final version dated 11 February 2015. Describes the candidate ARAIM architectures (Horizontal ARAIM and Offline and Online Vertical ARAIM), the Integrity Support Message (ISM) concept that lets a ground system update constellation fault rates and error models, threat allocation, and extended availability results, for comment by the aviation community.
nodes.kt: Horizontal vs offline vs online vertical ARAIM ISM: ground-provided integrity parameters without avionics changes Wider URE/SISE and constellation scenarios

nodes.n: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C - ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Milestone 3 Report
nodes.s: Final version dated 25 February 2016, concluding the three-phase effort. Adds the proposed ARAIM implementation roadmap, message types for H-ARAIM and for offline and online vertical ARAIM, institutional issues, the relation to SBAS, H-ARAIM availability results and the updated reference user algorithm (Annex A). Also hosted by the European Commission.
nodes.kt: Roadmap toward ARAIM standards Message definitions per ARAIM mode Latest reference user algorithm in Annex A

nodes.n: Stanford WAAS Laboratory - system metrics (the integrity/availability histogram behind the 'Stanford plot')
