nodes.s: Stanford GPS Lab page that explains the 2D histogram of true position error against protection level from its real-time WAAS implementation on the National Satellite Test Bed. It defines the normal-operation, alarm (PL above alert limit) and integrity-failure regions and offers the MATLAB plotting scripts (hplstat.m, vplstat.m). Secondary sources credit the Stanford WAAS lab with this diagram; the page itself is undated.
nodes.kt: Axes: true error (x) vs protection level (y), log-scaled counts Points with error above PL are integrity failures Original MATLAB scripts for drawing the plot

nodes.n: The Stanford - ESA Integrity Diagram: Focusing on SBAS Integrity
nodes.s: ION GNSS 2006 paper (UPC UPCommons repository record, behind a bot check) that modifies the classical Stanford plot to focus strictly on integrity, since the classical plot is not always conservative for that purpose. Also proposes an 'all-geometries' diagram and reports EGNOS measurement results under this stricter test. The Stanford-ESA diagram became a main integrity assessment tool for EGNOS.
nodes.kt: Stanford-ESA variant is the integrity-conservative version of the Stanford plot Used for EGNOS safety assessment Good template for plotting alt-PNT protection levels

nodes.n: Navipedia: The Stanford - ESA Integrity Diagram: Focusing on SBAS Integrity
nodes.s: ESA Navipedia article explaining the Stanford plot (position error vs protection level) and its Stanford-ESA modification, including the definitions of misleading and hazardously misleading information used to read the diagram.
nodes.kt: MI: error not bounded by PL while the system is available HMI: error also exceeds the alert limit Short open explainer to share with a team

nodes.n: GNSS Position Integrity in Urban Environments: A Review of Literature
nodes.s: IEEE T-ITS 19(9) review of GNSS integrity monitoring for urban transport, contrasting it with aviation integrity (multipath, NLOS, different risk definitions) and listing open research issues. Open copy on HAL.
nodes.kt: Why aviation RAIM does not carry over directly to urban ground vehicles Survey of urban FDE and protection-level methods Open research problems list

nodes.n: Integrity monitoring of Graph-SLAM using GPS and fish-eye camera
nodes.s: NAVIGATION 67(3) paper (journal version of ION GNSS+ 2019 / arXiv 1910.02165) that computes protection levels for a graph-SLAM estimator fusing GPS pseudoranges and fish-eye camera pixel intensities. Vision faults are isolated with a superpixel-based piecewise RANSAC, and protection levels come from worst-case failure slope analysis. Tested in urban and semi-urban driving.
nodes.kt: Multi-fault integrity for joint GPS + vision Protection levels from failure-slope analysis on linearized graph SLAM Open arXiv preprint: 1910.02165

nodes.n: Integrity of Visual Navigation - Developments, Challenges, and Prospects
nodes.s: Open-access NAVIGATION 69(2) review arguing that the lack of an integrity framework is the main obstacle to using visual navigation in safety-critical roles. It reviews the state of the art and sketches a preliminary integrity description framework for feature-based visual positioning, noting that learning-based methods still lack one.
nodes.kt: Best single review of vision integrity Proposes how to describe integrity for feature-based VO/VIO Flags ML-based vision as an open integrity problem

nodes.n: Data-Driven Protection Levels for Camera and 3D Map-based Safe Urban Localization
nodes.s: Computes protection levels for localization that matches camera images to a LiDAR-built 3D map, for urban areas where GNSS is unreliable. Position error is modelled as a Gaussian mixture from deep-network data-driven models with outlier weighting, and the PL is found by numerical line search. Submitted to NAVIGATION.
nodes.kt: Protection levels for map-based visual localization, no GNSS Learned error model plus statistical outlier weighting Template for PLs on visual geolocalization fixes

nodes.n: Safety-Critical LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with On-Manifold Deterministic Protection Level
nodes.s: LiDAR-inertial odometry built on an on-manifold ellipsoidal set-membership filter under an unknown-but-bounded noise assumption. The filter's feasible sets serve as deterministic online protection levels for robot navigation.
nodes.kt: Set-membership (bounded-error) alternative to probabilistic PLs Closed-form link between point-cloud noise and ICP uncertainty Online safety bound for LIO

nodes.n: Terrain Contour Matching (TERCOM): A Cruise Missile Guidance Aid
nodes.s: Proc. SPIE 0238 paper giving a brief history of TERCOM, how terrain contour matching works (correlating a measured altitude profile against stored elevation data) and its status in 1980. It is the standard English citation for the origin of terrain-correlation navigation; this index uses it only for the navigation-update concept.
nodes.kt: Batch profile correlation against a stored elevation map Historic baseline that later sequential filters (SITAN, PMF, PF) improved on Abstract only without SPIE access

nodes.n: Nonlinear Kalman filtering techniques for terrain-aided navigation
nodes.s: IEEE TAC 28(3) paper from Sandia (the SITAN line of work) on updating an INS with radar terrain-clearance measurements. It compares an EKF using local terrain slopes, a stochastic linearization fitting a least-squares plane to the terrain, and a bank of parallel reduced-order filters for large initial position uncertainty.
nodes.kt: Sequential (Kalman) terrain aiding, unlike batch TERCOM Terrain linearization is the core difficulty Parallel filter bank for acquisition

nodes.n: Recursive Bayesian Estimation: Navigation and Tracking Applications
nodes.s: Linkoping University PhD thesis (Dissertation No. 579) on nonlinear, non-Gaussian recursive estimation motivated by terrain-aided aircraft navigation and target tracking. Covers the point-mass filter and particle filters for terrain navigation, compared with the Cramer-Rao bound. A standard English-language TRN reference with free full text.
nodes.kt: Point-mass filter and particle filter for TRN in one place Cramer-Rao bounds for terrain navigation Free PDF from Linkoping

nodes.s: IEEE Control Systems Magazine 19(3) article presenting the point-mass filter for terrain-aided aircraft navigation: a grid approximation of the position density propagated recursively. Monte Carlo and realistic simulations show near-optimal performance across terrain types; the main limit is that cost explodes with state dimension. An open copy is in Linkoping's DiVA.
nodes.kt: The PMF handles arbitrary nonlinearity and noise in low dimension Density shape tells you estimate quality Real time for 2D, sometimes 3D

nodes.n: Marginalized Particle Filter for Accurate and Reliable Terrain-Aided Navigation
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 45(4) paper integrating INS and terrain-aided positioning in one marginalized (Rao-Blackwellized) particle filter: particles for the nonlinear part, Kalman filters for the conditionally linear part, plus a jointly estimated discrete mode. Simulations reach near Cramer-Rao accuracy. Open copy in Linkoping's DiVA.
nodes.kt: Joint INS + TAP design instead of a separate TRN fix Marginalized PF keeps the particle count manageable Handles multimodal terrain via a mode variable

nodes.n: Accurate Measurement Calculation Method for Interferometric Radar Altimeter-Based Terrain Referenced Navigation
nodes.s: Open-access Sensors paper on TRN with an interferometric radar altimeter, which outputs slant range and cross-track look angle to the closest terrain point. It derives a formula for that point's 3D relative position using angle of attack and sideslip instead of Euler angles, checks it on real flight data, and shows in TRN simulation that wind otherwise biases the result.
nodes.kt: Interferometric altimeters give range plus look angle, not just height Wind (alpha/beta) matters for the measurement model Real flight data used for validation

nodes.n: Ant-Mutated Immune Particle Filter Design for Terrain Referenced Navigation with Interferometric Radar Altimeter
nodes.s: Open-access Remote Sensing paper proposing a particle filter variant (ant-colony mutation inside an immune auxiliary particle filter) to cope with low-grade interferometric radar altimeter errors in TRN. Evaluated by Monte Carlo TRN simulation on a UAV.
nodes.kt: Targets low-cost IRA measurement errors Particle diversity management for TRN Simulation-only evaluation

nodes.n: Design of Efficient Point-Mass Filter with Application in Terrain Aided Navigation
nodes.s: FUSION 2023 paper on speeding up the time-update (prediction) step of the grid-based point-mass filter for models with linear dynamics, unifying continuous and discrete formulations. The authors report large time-complexity reductions without accuracy loss in a terrain-aided navigation example, and release MATLAB code.
nodes.kt: Makes the PMF cheap enough for real-time TAN MATLAB code on GitHub Good modern successor to Bergman's PMF

nodes.n: Tensor Decompositions for Online Grid-Based Terrain-Aided Navigation
nodes.s: Preprint (in review for FUSION 2026) that scales grid-based filters to higher state dimensions with a Lagrangian time update and low-rank tensor decompositions, exploiting block-diagonal dynamics and sparsely coupled measurements. Demonstrated on terrain-aided navigation, with reproducible MATLAB code.
nodes.kt: Pushes grid filters beyond 2-3 dimensions Fully reproducible experiments Code: pesslovany/Matlab-LagrangianPMF

nodes.n: Contours-Seeking Proposal Density Particle Filter and Resilient Terrain-Referenced Navigation
nodes.s: Author's accepted version of an IEEE TAES 61(6) (Dec 2025) paper. Proposes a particle-filter proposal that nudges particles along terrain slopes toward the most probable terrain contours (Gaussian mixture random forcing plus auxiliary sampling) to fight degeneracy under multimodal likelihoods and unknown prediction bias.
nodes.kt: Addresses PF degeneracy, the classic TRN failure mode Robust to unknown INS bias and multimodal noise Simulation study

nodes.n: Terrain-Aided Navigation Without Raycasting: A Sliding Grid Approach for Point Cloud Processing
nodes.s: Compares two DEM-based measurement models for point-cloud (lidar-style) terrain-aided INS: classic ray casting versus a 'sliding grid' that needs no ray casting. The sliding grid gives comparable accuracy, especially at higher altitude, at much lower compute, targeting embedded hardware.
nodes.kt: Point-cloud TAN beyond a single altimeter beam Avoids GPU-hungry ray casting Relevant to scanning lidar or radar altimeters

nodes.n: Vision-Based Terrain Relative Navigation on High-Altitude Balloon and Sub-Orbital Rocket
nodes.s: AIAA SciTech 2023 paper evaluating camera-based TRN that matches landmarks from a satellite image database and uses inertial data between frames. Tested on a World View high-altitude balloon descending from 33 km and on Blue Origin New Shepard NS-23 camera data, with robustness to fast rotation and cloud obstruction.
nodes.kt: Real flight data, not simulation Visual TRN across a large altitude range Draper/MIT work

nodes.n: Advanced Aeromagnetic Compensation Models for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
nodes.s: MIT AeroAstro PhD thesis (advisor Alan Edelman) on removing the aircraft's own magnetic field so magnetic anomaly maps can be used for navigation. It studies four groups of methods: linear compensation, nonlinear (neural) compensation, online compensation and covariance-adaptive filtering. The models are implemented in MagNav.jl. DSpace terms: in copyright, educational use permitted.
nodes.kt: The full technical background behind MagNav.jl Compares Tolles-Lawson, neural and online compensation Free PDF on DSpace@MIT

nodes.n: Derivation and Extensions of the Tolles-Lawson Model for Aeromagnetic Compensation
nodes.s: Short open reference note that re-derives the Tolles-Lawson aircraft magnetic field model (permanent, induced and eddy-current terms), states where the assumptions enter, describes the calibration procedure, and adds a second-order correction and a way to build the vector aircraft field.
nodes.kt: Clear derivation of the standard compensation model Explains the calibration-box flight Pairs with the MagNav challenge data

nodes.n: Absolute Positioning Using the Earth's Magnetic Anomaly Field
nodes.s: NAVIGATION 63(2) journal paper: a particle-filter framework that aids an aircraft INS with optically pumped cesium magnetometer measurements compared against an anomaly map, while estimating the temporal variations of the field. Analyses altitude and magnetic-storm dependence with flight-test and observatory data. The article is a U.S. Government work, public domain in the USA; the related AFIT dissertation is freely available.
nodes.kt: Particle filter on scalar anomaly measurements Models temporal (diurnal/storm) field variation Public-domain US Government work

nodes.s: IEEE TAES 53(1) paper describing a passive airborne navigation system (scalar magnetometer, INS, barometer, anomaly map) with a particle filter and a full measurement equation linking magnetometer readings to the map. Flight-tested over Louisa, Virginia; the authors call the reported accuracy a best case under ideal conditions.
nodes.kt: First flight-test validation of the AFIT MagNav filter Complete measurement equation Best-case result, survey aircraft conditions

nodes.n: Magnetic Navigation on an F-16 Aircraft Using Online Calibration
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 58(1) paper on magnetic anomaly navigation flown on an F-16, where the platform's magnetic interference is far larger than on survey aircraft and drifts. A combined batch and online calibration gives better accuracy than batch-only calibration on 1.5-hour flights.
nodes.kt: Operational fighter platform, not a quiet survey aircraft Online calibration needed for drifting platform fields Key evidence for MagNav on military aircraft

nodes.n: Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation with Neural-Network-Augmented Online Calibration
nodes.s: Published in the Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics (2026). A 'cold-start' MagNav EKF that estimates kinematic states, Tolles-Lawson coefficients and the weights of a residual neural network in flight, so no calibration flight or pre-training is needed. Validated on the MagNav Challenge dataset.
nodes.kt: No prior calibration flight EKF update equivalent to online natural-gradient training Physics model first, NN only for residuals

nodes.n: Acquisition, Doppler Tracking, and Positioning With Starlink LEO Satellites: First Results
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 58(3) letter with the first acquisition, Doppler tracking and positioning results from Starlink downlinks without knowing the signal structure: a generalized-likelihood-ratio acquisition test and a Kalman-filter Doppler tracker, with six satellites tracked.
nodes.kt: Blind acquisition of undisclosed Starlink signals Doppler-only positioning works with a handful of satellites Received the IEEE M. Barry Carlton Award

nodes.n: Unveiling Starlink LEO Satellite OFDM-Like Signal Structure Enabling Precise Positioning
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 60(2) letter that estimates the structure of Starlink's OFDM-like reference signals and frame length, and proposes a blind receiver that acquires multiple satellites, estimates their reference signals and Doppler, and tracks carrier and code phase. Of six tracked satellites, three sent pure tones and three OFDM-like signals.
nodes.kt: Blind reference-signal estimation Carrier and code phase from Starlink Bridges pure-tone Doppler to OFDM ranging

nodes.s: Open-access NAVIGATION 72(1) paper describing the full Starlink OFDM beacon via blind beacon estimation, the processing gain this gives over previously published sequences, achievable C/N0 for different reception setups, and the first carrier phase, Doppler and code phase observables from Starlink OFDM. Uses signal collections from 2021 to 2024 and notes step-like corrections that contaminate OFDM observables. Won the ION Samuel Burka Award.
nodes.kt: Full beacon gives large processing gain for low-gain antennas Pilot-tone vs OFDM observable quality compared Open access, with an ION webinar companion

nodes.s: Accepted to IEEE TAES. Proposes 'fused LEO GNSS': a cooperative PNT service hosted on a broadband mega-constellation's own transmitters, clocks and spectrum. Assesses the opportunity cost to the operator in time-space-bandwidth product and energy, concluding that a near-instantaneous-fix service would cost a small fraction of Starlink downlink capacity.
nodes.kt: Cooperative (operator-supported) LEO PNT vs opportunistic use Opportunity-cost argument in downlink capacity Foundation for the UT group's LEO PNT work

nodes.n: Timing Properties of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
nodes.s: IEEE TAES 62 (2026) paper characterizing Starlink frame timing for pseudorange-based opportunistic PNT. It finds ns-level jitter periods (good) but also abrupt timing adjustments, episodic high-jitter periods and only loose disciplining to GPS time, which the authors judge incompatible with GPS-like PNT unless corrected, and attribute to software choices.
nodes.kt: Starlink frame timing is disciplined to GPS time only loosely Abrupt per-second timing jumps on v1.0/v1.5 satellites Third-party corrections could fix it

nodes.n: Pilots and Other Predictable Elements of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
nodes.s: Identifies dedicated edge-pilot symbols and other predictable elements in the Starlink Ku-band waveform, publishes the edge-pilot sequences, and shows most QPSK symbols follow a regular template rather than carrying user data. Exploiting these elements gives a large processing gain so compact low-gain receivers can get precise time of arrival even from side beams.
nodes.kt: Explicit Starlink pilot sequences disclosed Predictable frame content enables TOA with small antennas UT Austin with Psiaki (Virginia Tech)

nodes.n: OFDM-Based Positioning with Unknown Data Payloads: Bounds and Applications to LEO PNT
nodes.s: Derives the Ziv-Zakai bound on time-of-arrival estimation for OFDM signals with both known pilots and unknown data, capturing low-SNR threshold effects that Cramer-Rao bounds miss. Evaluates maximum-likelihood and decision-directed estimators on simulated LEO non-terrestrial-network channels.
nodes.kt: Unknown payload symbols still carry ranging information ZZB vs CRB at low SNR Theory for opportunistic OFDM ranging

nodes.n: LEO-PNT With Starlink: Development of a Burst Detection Algorithm Based on Signal Measurements
nodes.s: Measures Starlink signals and builds a correlation-based burst detector, then measures burst carrier frequency (Doppler) and estimates attainable positioning accuracy. The authors argue it works with an omnidirectional antenna in an operationally relevant setup.
nodes.kt: Burst detection as the first step of Doppler positioning Omnidirectional antenna, no dish European (UniBw Munich) LEO-PNT work

nodes.n: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
nodes.s: Associates unlabeled Doppler traces in passive SDR spectrum-monitoring scans (no raw IQ) with TLE-predicted Starlink/OneWeb satellites, using slope-consistent segments, a clock-offset search and multi-metric matching, then runs batch Doppler positioning on open UK monitoring data. Submitted to IEEE NAVICON 2026.
nodes.kt: Positioning from spectrum waterfalls, not IQ samples Receiver clock offset search is the key step Uses open monitoring data

nodes.s: NAVIGATION 65(2) paper analysing how broadband LEO mega-constellations could provide navigation: stronger signals against jamming, much better satellite geometry from sheer numbers, which lets the signal-in-space range error be relaxed, and a benign radiation environment that allows COTS payloads.
nodes.kt: Early quantitative case for LEO PNT Geometry gain offsets worse clocks and orbits

nodes.n: Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Through Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites: A Survey on Current Status, Challenges, and Opportunities
nodes.s: Open-access IEEE Access survey of LEO-PNT: system design steps and challenges, candidate physical-layer parameters, design tools and simulators, satellite-ground channel models, and commercial prospects, written by a multidisciplinary Finnish-led team.
nodes.kt: Broad map of the LEO-PNT design space Lists simulators and channel models Good starting reading for a LEO-PNT hackathon track

nodes.n: GNSS Timing Spoofing Detection: Methods and Analysis using Jammertest data
nodes.s: University of Vaasa master's thesis (supervised by Heidi Kuusniemi) analysing u-blox ZED-F9P data from a Jammertest 2024 timing-spoofing event. C/N0 monitoring was ineffective; pseudorange RMS and NMEA validity flags caught anomalies with false positives; an Isolation Forest model detected the spoofing with very few false alarms. Recommends validity flags as a trigger plus ML verification. The repository page sits behind a bot check.
nodes.kt: Uses real live-spoofing data, not simulation C/N0 alone does not reveal timing spoofing Cheap receiver-side detection recipe

nodes.n: Empirical Evaluation of GNSS Timing Spoofing and Detection Using Machine Learning
nodes.s: IPIN 2025 paper on timing spoofing detection with Jammertest 2024 data. Position parameters were compromised at lower spoofing power than timing parameters, which could give early warning; NMEA validity flags detected much but not all of the attack; an unsupervised Isolation Forest closed the gap. Self-archived copies exist in the Vaasa and Tampere repositories.
nodes.kt: Position degrades before time: use it as an early warning Unsupervised detector, no labelled spoofing needed Targets critical-infrastructure timing receivers

nodes.n: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Framework for Zero-Day Time-Push GNSS Spoofing Detection
nodes.s: Preprint on detecting time-push spoofing against static GNSS receivers with an autoencoder (hybrid quantum-classical) trained only on authentic tracking-stage features, so it can flag unseen attack types. Compared with classical autoencoders and supervised models across simplistic, intermediate and sophisticated time-push scenarios.
nodes.kt: Anomaly detection trained on clean data only Focus on time-push attacks on static timing receivers Quantum part is optional for a hackathon; the classical baseline is the useful bit

nodes.n: MILUV: A Multi-UAV Indoor Localization dataset with UWB and Vision
nodes.s: Multi-UAV indoor dataset (three quadcopters, 36 experiments) with UWB ranging including raw timestamps, channel impulse response and inter-robot ranges, stereo and downward cameras, IMU, laser height, magnetometer and motion-capture ground truth, in LOS and NLOS. Data on Figshare+ under CC BY 4.0; the devkit (decargroup/miluv) is MIT. Paper: arXiv 2504.14376.
nodes.kt: CC BY 4.0 data, MIT devkit Inter-robot UWB for cooperative localization tests CIR data for NLOS classification

nodes.n: Addressing Relative Pose Impact on UWB Localization: Dataset Introduction and Analysis
nodes.s: Short paper introducing a drone UWB dataset that isolates how the relative pose between UWB devices affects ranging: six flight sequences with two-way ranging to four anchors, a stereo VIO setup, and motion-capture ground truth for both the drone and the anchors. Data in the cjhhalla/RCV_uwb_dataset GitHub repo (rosbags on Google Drive), which has no licence file, so reuse terms are unstated.
nodes.kt: Characterizes antenna-orientation effects on UWB range error Useful for building a realistic UWB noise model No explicit licence

nodes.n: UWB-based system for UAV Localization in GNSS-Denied Environments: Characterization and Dataset
nodes.s: IROS 2020 paper characterizing a low-cost, portable Decawave DWM1001 UWB system for indoor UAV flight, including anchor placement, altitude and speed effects and anchor self-calibration, with open data and methods. Data in the TIERS/uwb-drone-dataset GitHub repo, which has no licence file.
nodes.kt: Cheap DWM1001 hardware, movable anchors Accuracy vs anchor geometry and altitude No explicit licence

nodes.n: GSV-Cities: Toward Appropriate Supervised Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: Neurocomputing 2022 paper introducing GSV-Cities, a street-level training set covering 40+ cities over 14 years with accurate place labels, and a study of metric-learning losses for VPR training. It is the training set used by MixVPR, BoQ and several later methods. Licence: the Kaggle dataset is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial, no derivatives); the GitHub code repo has no licence file.
nodes.kt: Standard training set for modern VPR CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: research use only Hosted on Kaggle

nodes.n: Rethinking Visual Geo-localization for Large-Scale Applications
nodes.s: CVPR 2022 paper introducing San Francisco eXtra Large (SF-XL), a city-wide geo-localization dataset, and CosPlace, which casts VPR training as classification to avoid expensive negative mining. SF-XL is obtained through a request form that states it is 'publicly available for research purposes'; no formal licence is given. The CosPlace code is MIT.
nodes.kt: Classification training scales to city-size data SF-XL access via form, research use CosPlace code: MIT

nodes.n: EigenPlaces: Training Viewpoint Robust Models for Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: ICCV 2023 paper that clusters training data to show the network the same points of interest from different viewpoints, building viewpoint robustness into global descriptors without extra supervision. Trained on SF-XL.
nodes.kt: Viewpoint robustness, relevant to oblique aerial views No extra labels needed MIT-licensed code

nodes.n: MixVPR: Feature Mixing for Visual Place Recognition
nodes.s: WACV 2023 paper proposing a holistic aggregation that mixes backbone feature maps through a cascade of feature-mixing blocks instead of NetVLAD-style local aggregation, aiming at accuracy with low latency. Trained on GSV-Cities.
nodes.kt: Simple, fast global descriptor Trained on GSV-Cities Good baseline for onboard VPR

nodes.s: CVPR 2022 oral presenting an open framework to build, train and test visual geo-localization pipelines with swappable backbones, aggregation and negative mining, plus a large experimental study of how each choice affects recall, runtime and memory.
nodes.kt: Systematic guide to VPR design choices Common evaluation protocol MIT-licensed framework

nodes.n: VPAIR - Aerial Visual Place Recognition and Localization in Large-scale Outdoor Environments
nodes.s: ICRA 2022 aerial-robotics workshop paper introducing VPAIR: downward camera images from a light aircraft flying above 300 m, each paired with a reference render with depth and a 6-DoF pose, over 100+ km of urban, farmland and forest terrain. Licence: the README says academic use only, commercial use prohibited (the small Zenodo sample is tagged CC BY 4.0).
nodes.kt: Medium-altitude aerial VPR benchmark Reference renders with depth Academic use only

nodes.n: ALTO: A Large-Scale Dataset for UAV Visual Place Recognition and Localization
nodes.s: Helicopter-flown aerial dataset over Ohio and Pennsylvania (two long trajectories) with GPS-INS ground truth, accelerometer, laser altimeter and downward RGB imagery, plus reference imagery for VPR benchmarking. The MetaSLAM/ALTO repo is BSD-3-Clause; no separate data licence is stated.
nodes.kt: Long-range aerial VPR and registration benchmark Includes laser altimeter (TRN-adjacent) Repo BSD-3-Clause

nodes.n: Visual place recognition for aerial imagery: A survey
nodes.s: Robotics and Autonomous Systems 183 (2025) survey and evaluation methodology for VPR on aerial imagery. Benchmarks several VPR methods and shows that the zoom level and overlap chosen when cutting satellite map tiles strongly affect results. Code in prime-slam/aero-vloc.
nodes.kt: How to tile satellite maps for VPR matters Hands-on benchmark with code Directly useful for drone-to-satellite geolocalization

nodes.n: Visual Place Recognition for Large-Scale UAV Applications
nodes.s: Introduces LASED, a large aerial VPR training set of about a million images from 170,000 locations across Estonia sampled over a decade, and uses steerable (rotation-equivariant) CNNs to handle the heading ambiguity of nadir UAV images.
nodes.kt: Multi-year aerial imagery for cross-season training Rotation-equivariant networks for unknown heading Aerial counterpart to GSV-Cities

nodes.n: Are State-of-the-art Visual Place Recognition Techniques any Good for Aerial Robotics?
nodes.s: Early benchmark of eight ground-robot VPR techniques on two aerial place-recognition datasets, comparing matching performance, processing power and memory, and laying out why aerial VPR differs (viewpoint change, payload-limited compute).
nodes.kt: Ground VPR does not transfer directly to aerial Compute and memory as first-class metrics Good framing for an onboard VPR budget

nodes.n: Danish Maritime Authority historical AIS data
nodes.s: Daily zip files, one CSV per UTC day, holding every AIS report received by the Danish shore network across Danish waters and approaches (Skagerrak, Kattegat, the belts, western Baltic). Free download over plain HTTP from aisdata.ais.dk with no account; a day is roughly 0.5-0.9 GB zipped. Positions are whatever each ship's own GNSS reported, stamped with base-station receive time.
nodes.kt: No login, one zip per day; a single deflate stream lets you HTTP-Range the first N MB and inflate a partial day Heavy duplication (one report heard by several stations) and 91/181/0,0 'not available' positions need cleaning first No ground truth for spoofing: inject episodes yourself; receive-time stamps create speed and jump artefacts Reuse under Danish public-data conditions with the DMA attribution sentence

nodes.n: NAIP aerial imagery on Microsoft Planetary Computer
nodes.s: USDA National Agriculture Imagery Program leaf-on orthophotos (RGB + NIR) of the contiguous US, re-flown per state every few years, served as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs behind a STAC API. Windows of a few square km can be read straight from the COGs after fetching a free SAS token. Resolution depends on state and year (0.3-1 m in the Ohio scenes the samples use).
nodes.kt: Public-domain-with-attribution reference map you can redistribute, unlike most satellite basemaps Several epochs of the same area make map-age experiments for visual geolocalization easy Unsigned blob URLs return HTTP 409; sign with planetary_computer or the SAS token endpoint US only; quarter-quad files are 0.4-1.4 GB, so read windows or overviews

nodes.s: An open catalogue of user-contributed aerial and drone orthomosaics, each stored as a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF on a public S3 bucket under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is patchy but global, which makes it a quick source of centimetre-level drone orthos outside the US with no login.
nodes.kt: Non-US, redistributable drone orthos for a visual-geolocalization demo map Scenes are EPSG:3857; convert units to ground metres (cos latitude) before quoting GSD Quality, date and georeference vary per uploader; check each scene Synthetic frames cut from the same ortho as the map are a best case, not a flight result

nodes.n: Geobasis NRW DOM1 / DGM1 1 m airborne LiDAR surface and terrain models
nodes.s: North Rhine-Westphalia's open-data 1 m digital surface model (DOM1, buildings and vegetation included) and 1 m bare-earth terrain model (DGM1) for the whole state, delivered as 1 x 1 km GeoTIFF tiles in ETRS89 / UTM 32N with no login. Licensed dl-de/zero-2.0, so no attribution is required.
nodes.kt: A real high-resolution prior map for terrain or heightmap navigation in a European setting In the terrain-heightmap sample, edge-based matching that failed on 30 m GLO-30 worked on the 1 m surface model Tile names carry the flight year, which differs by area; list the directory if a name 404s NRW only; DOM1 vegetation changes with season

nodes.n: ADS-B Exchange free monthly sample data (readsb-hist)
nodes.s: ADS-B Exchange publishes its complete global feed for the 1st day of each month free of charge, as gzipped readsb aircraft.json snapshots every 5 s. Each aircraft entry carries quality fields such as NACp and NIC plus MLAT flags, which is enough to rebuild a GPSJam-style GNSS interference map for any past 1st-of-month. No open licence is named; the site's terms of use apply.
nodes.kt: Only the 1st of each month is published, appearing about 1.5 days later Each global snapshot is about 5 MB gzipped; filter to a bbox while downloading Low NACp says 'degraded', not why; under spoofing the reported position is itself false Check the terms before redistributing raw snapshots; commit derived aggregates instead

nodes.n: Sentinel-1 Level-1 GRD on Microsoft Planetary Computer
nodes.s: Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band SAR Ground Range Detected scenes mirrored as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (VV, VH) together with the SAFE XML annotations, which include ESA's per-swath RF interference report. Readable anonymously after URL signing, no Copernicus account needed. Free and open under the Copernicus data policy.
nodes.kt: ESA's rfiDetected annotation plus a temporal z-score over a stack gives a C-band RF-activity context layer C-band, not L-band: it sees radars and broadband emissions, not a GNSS jammer's intended signal One snapshot per pass, every 6 days per orbit track in the 2026 stack; read COG overviews, full VH is about 0.5 GB Some scenes can be missing from the mirror

nodes.s: A real 76-minute Septentrio SBF GALRawINAV recording of live Galileo E1 I/NAV pages with OSNMA, shipped in the OSNMAlib repository alongside the matching GSC public key and Merkle tree, plus an older recording from the previous public-key period. About 2.6 MB: the smallest real OSNMA input available, no receiver or account needed. EUPL-1.2 as part of the repo.
nodes.kt: Runs OSNMA authentication offline in seconds; attacks can be injected by manipulating pages File mode trusts the signal's own GST, so a months-old replay still authenticates: replay demos need an independent clock No DSM-PKR in the recording, so cold start with only the Merkle tree cannot be shown The bundled key and tree go stale at the next GSC renewal

nodes.n: DroneRF dataset: A dataset of drones for RF-based detection, classification, and identification
nodes.s: RF recordings of drone-to-controller communications from three consumer drones (Bebop, AR Drone, Phantom) in several flight modes, plus background recordings with no drone, collected at Qatar University. Published on Mendeley Data under CC BY 4.0 as segmented RAR archives of CSV sample text.
nodes.kt: Classic baseline for RF-based drone detection and type identification Archives expand a lot: the cuas-classifiers sample's 4-archive subset is about 0.7 GB packed and 6.6 GB of CSV Mendeley's API rejects the default urllib user agent; set one explicitly Detection and classification only; the sample rate is not stated in the dataset description

nodes.n: University of Toronto Foot-Mounted Inertial Navigation Dataset
nodes.s: Foot-mounted IMU recordings from five subjects over more than 7.6 km with ground-truth positioning, built to evaluate zero-velocity-aided pedestrian INS. Includes non-walking motions such as running, crawling and stair climbing, and mixed walk/run trials. Open access on IEEE DataPort (DOI 10.21227/v1z6-9z84) under a Creative Commons Attribution licence.
nodes.kt: Ground truth plus varied gaits makes it a test bed for adaptive zero-velocity detectors Companion code is the pyshoe repository Crawling and running trials are the relevant ones for dismounted-soldier scenarios

nodes.n: NOAA NGS CORS network RINEX data archive
nodes.s: Public archive of RINEX observation and navigation files from the US Continuously Operating Reference Station network, organised by year and day of year. Station coordinates are precisely known and fixed, so any positioning error computed from these files is solution error, which makes them a clean test input for SPP, PPP and RTK pipelines. US government data, no login.
nodes.kt: Fixed, surveyed antennas give free truth for positioning-algorithm benchmarks Files are daily 30 s RINEX, often Hatanaka-compressed; pair with broadcast or precise orbits Pairs of nearby stations give a ready-made baseline for RTK tests

nodes.n: IGS daily merged broadcast navigation files (BKG mirror)
nodes.s: Daily multi-GNSS RINEX navigation files that merge the broadcast ephemerides collected across the IGS network, mirrored by BKG over HTTPS and organised by year and day of year. The standard way to get a real ephemeris for a past date when simulating GNSS signals or reprocessing recorded observations.
nodes.kt: Feed a past date's ephemeris to a signal simulator such as gps-sdr-sim or to an SPP solver No account needed on the BKG HTTPS mirror Broadcast orbits, not precise products; use IGS final orbits when centimetre accuracy matters

nodes.n: USGS 3DEP seamless DEMs on Microsoft Planetary Computer
nodes.s: The USGS 3D Elevation Program seamless bare-earth DEMs for the US, served as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs through Planetary Computer's STAC API with the same SAS signing as NAIP. Licensed PDDL-1.0 per the STAC collection; the vpr-large-area sample uses it to get ground elevation under each drone frame.
nodes.kt: Same STAC search and signing flow as NAIP, so one helper covers imagery and terrain Gives ground height under a frame to turn barometric or GNSS altitude into height above ground US only; outside the US use Copernicus GLO-30

nodes.n: OpenDroneMap Aukerman Park eBee image set
nodes.s: A CC0 set of nadir photos from a senseFly eBee survey of Aukerman Park, Ohio, distributed by OpenDroneMap as a photogrammetry test dataset, with EXIF GPS in each frame. The geolocalization samples use these real drone frames as queries against NAIP orthophotos of the same park.
nodes.kt: Real fixed-wing drone frames with a public-domain licence and EXIF positions as approximate truth Overlaps several NAIP epochs, so map-age effects can be measured on real imagery EXIF GPS is a consumer-grade fix, not survey truth

nodes.s: A NASA service that cuts FITS images with a reference WCS from many all-sky surveys at any position, scale and projection. The celestial star-tracker sample pulls cutouts of the Mellinger optical all-sky mosaic to score plate-solving accuracy against a known attitude.
nodes.kt: Free reference star fields with known pointing for testing lost-in-space star trackers Under load it can answer with an HTML 'Too Many Processes' page instead of FITS; retry and validate Survey mosaics are not camera frames: no lens distortion, noise or stray light of a real sensor

nodes.n: JPL DE421 planetary ephemeris (NAIF SPK kernel)
nodes.s: The DE421 planetary and lunar ephemeris as a NAIF SPK binary kernel (de421.bsp, about 16 MB), an older but compact JPL Development Ephemeris commonly loaded with Skyfield. Celestial navigation code needs it to place the Sun, Moon and planets and to compute observer geometry.
nodes.kt: Small, offline ephemeris adequate for celestial fixes; newer DE files exist under the same NAIF tree Load with Skyfield; no account needed Kept under a_old_versions on the NAIF server

nodes.s: Public-domain world vector layers (land, coastline, countries) at 1:10m, 1:50m and 1:110m scales. Samples use the 10 m land polygon as an 'is this position on land' mask for AIS plausibility checks and the 50 m country borders as a basemap for interference maps.
nodes.kt: Public domain, small downloads, no login At 1:10m, canals, fjord heads and harbours are drawn as land: most 'on land' AIS alerts in the sample were coastline resolution Use a large-scale water mask for harbour-level checks

nodes.n: OpenStreetMap data via the Overpass API
nodes.s: A read-only query API over the OpenStreetMap database that returns features (coastlines, bridges, wind turbines, buoys) inside a bounding box. The USV GNSS-denied sample builds its radar chart and landmark set from Overpass queries; OSM data is under ODbL with attribution.
nodes.kt: Quick way to build a real chart or landmark map for any region Public endpoints rate-limit; keep fallbacks and cache results If the simulated sensor sees the same OSM map the matcher uses, error numbers are optimistic

nodes.s: Crowd-sourced industry report from a six-week OPSGROUP workgroup of pilots, controllers, regulators and manufacturers on GPS spoofing hitting civil flights, mainly near Middle East and Black Sea / Baltic conflict areas. Comes with crew guidance and a technical guide.
nodes.kt: Spoofing degrades terrain-warning (EGPWS) functions, which may stay wrong after GPS returns No quick fix: mitigation is crew awareness, procedures and keeping ground navaids Strong evidence that integrity monitoring and 'is my position plausible?' checks matter more than raw accuracy Spoofing can leave systems like terrain warning degraded after GPS returns Receivers may retain corrupted data after an event Argues for retaining ground-based navaids

nodes.n: EASA SIB 2022-02R3: Global Navigation Satellite System Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
nodes.s: EASA's safety information bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aircraft, revised repeatedly since 2022 as interference spread around conflict zones. Lists symptoms and recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers; later revisions (R4) followed.
nodes.kt: Spoofing is harder for crews to detect than jamming and so the bigger safety risk Recommends cross-checking with non-GNSS navaids and reporting events Affected flight information regions are tracked on EASA's GNSS page

nodes.n: EASA - Global Navigation Satellite System outages and alterations
nodes.s: EASA's landing page for GNSS interference: current SIB revision, affected regions and related guidance and workshops.
nodes.kt: Single place to check the current bulletin revision Links civil-aviation guidance to the interference geography

nodes.n: EASA and IATA comprehensive plan to mitigate the risks of GNSS interference
nodes.s: Joint plan from a May 2025 EASA/IATA workshop setting out actions on reporting and monitoring, prevention and mitigation, airspace/infrastructure (backup navaids) and civil-military coordination against GNSS interference.
nodes.kt: Four pillars: reporting, prevention, infrastructure, coordination Retaining conventional navaids is explicitly part of resilience Calls for better civil-military sharing of interference data Standard radio calls and NOTAM Q-codes for interference Tighter controls on jammer sales Keep a minimum network of conventional navaids as backup

nodes.n: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
nodes.s: FAA Safety Alert for Operators describing jamming vs spoofing effects on aircraft systems, typical locations near conflict and counter-UAS areas, and recommended crew and operator actions.
nodes.kt: Hybrid GPS/inertial solutions can also be corrupted by spoofing Revert to conventional procedures and report to ATC Disruptions cluster around conflict zones and C-UAS protection areas

nodes.s: Aviation safety wiki article explaining jamming vs spoofing, their effects on aircraft systems and the regulatory material around them, with links to bulletins and incident reports.
nodes.kt: Good primer on how interference propagates through avionics Collects links to EASA, FAA and ICAO material Plain-language intro to the aviation impact Links to EASA/FAA/ICAO references

nodes.n: Above Us Only Stars: Exposing GPS Spoofing in Russia and Syria
nodes.s: Open-source investigation using AIS ship tracks, public records and ISS-based measurements to map thousands of GNSS spoofing events around Russia, Crimea and Syria, many linked to protection of VIPs and bases.
nodes.kt: Shows how public data (AIS) reveals spoofing via impossible tracks Spoofing used for airspace denial around military facilities A model for OSINT-style interference detection projects AIS position anomalies reveal spoofing at scale Methodology is reproducible with public data

nodes.s: Daily world map of likely GPS interference derived from ADS-B navigation-integrity reports (NIC/NACp) aggregated into hexagons from community flight-tracking data. The FAQ documents the method and its blind spots.
nodes.kt: Interference is inferred from aircraft self-reported integrity, not measured RF Empty cells mean no data, not no jamming Easy to reproduce with your own ADS-B receiver Derived from ADS-B NIC/NACp degradation Hex-binned daily snapshots Shows persistent interference zones (Baltic, Middle East, Black Sea) Method is indirect: inferred from aircraft-reported accuracy

nodes.s: Bellingcat's toolkit entry on using GPSJam for open-source investigations, with notes on limitations and interpretation.
nodes.kt: Frames interference maps as OSINT evidence with caveats Useful for teams building verification workflows

nodes.n: ADS-B Data Analysis for GNSS Interference Mapping
nodes.s: Trade-press article on using ADS-B integrity data to detect and map GNSS interference regions.
nodes.kt: ADS-B is an existing, free sensor network for interference awareness Method details help design your own detector

nodes.n: GNSS interference report: Russia 2024/2025 - Part 1: Kaliningrad and the Baltic Sea
nodes.s: Spire analysis using satellite-received ADS-B integrity metrics and RF data to characterize persistent interference around Kaliningrad and over the Baltic.
nodes.kt: Satellite ADS-B extends interference monitoring over sea areas Kaliningrad is a persistent Baltic interference zone

nodes.n: Researchers home in on origins of Russia's Baltic GPS jamming
nodes.s: Reporting on Gdynia Maritime University research tracing Baltic jamming to Russian sites such as Baltiysk in Kaliningrad, DLR comment on how cheap and mobile jammers are, and an analyst's heatmap of likely jammer locations built from aircraft ADS-B integrity data.
nodes.kt: Emitter localization from distributed monitors plus ADS-B is feasible Baltic interference has shifted to include spoofing Emitter localization from distributed measurements Shows the Baltic as a persistent interference zone

nodes.s: Post from Todd Humphreys' lab on spoofing incidents hitting commercial aircraft and what they show about receiver and avionics vulnerability.
nodes.kt: Academic view on why civil receivers accept spoofed signals Points toward authentication and cross-checks as defenses

nodes.n: GPS Spoofing in the Civil Aviation Sector (RIN 2024)
nodes.s: Royal Institute of Navigation event microsite gathering expert talks on spoofing affecting airlines and possible mitigations.
nodes.kt: UK navigation-community perspective Covers detection, operations and policy angles

nodes.n: 2025 Was a Stress Test & Maritime AI™ Is the Only Way to Pass
nodes.s: Windward's quarter-by-quarter review of 2025 maritime risk: sanctions, dark fleet growth, flag-registry fraud and GNSS interference. Reports GPS jamming affecting more than 24,000 vessels across Q1-Q3, with hotspots in the Arabian Gulf, Mediterranean and Baltic, and false port calls near Iranian terminals during the Iran conflict.
nodes.kt: GPS jamming affected more than 24,000 vessels in Q1-Q3 2025, over 13,000 in Q2 alone AIS anomalies are the main public signal of GNSS manipulation at sea

nodes.n: Meatgrinder: Russian Tactics in the Second Year of Its Invasion of Ukraine
nodes.s: RUSI special report on Russian battlefield adaptation, including the density of Russian electronic warfare and its heavy effect on Ukrainian UAVs, with a widely cited estimate of around 10,000 drone losses per month.
nodes.kt: Dense EW coverage along the front is weighted toward defeating UAVs Loss figures came from interviews and are contested Explains why EW-resilient navigation became a top Ukrainian requirement Describes dense, layered Russian EW deployment Drone attrition to EW drives demand for non-GNSS navigation

nodes.s: Annual CSIS Aerospace Security Project review of counterspace capabilities, with sections on GPS jamming and spoofing in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.
nodes.kt: Puts terrestrial GNSS jamming in the wider counterspace picture Useful citation for problem framing in pitches Country-by-country counterspace inventory Tracks GNSS electronic attack incidents year over year

nodes.n: The Invisible War: Inside the electronic warfare arms race that could shape course of war in Ukraine
nodes.s: Long-form reporting on the EW and counter-EW cycle in Ukraine, covering jamming of drones and navigation and the rapid iteration of countermeasures.
nodes.kt: GPS-guided Excalibur shells and JDAM bombs lost accuracy to Russian jamming within months to a year of delivery Ukraine's Pokrova system jams and spoofs satellite navigation; officials claim it cut the accuracy of spoofed missiles by 40%

nodes.n: Ukrainian military's anti-drone GPS spoofing spills into civilians' phones
nodes.s: Report on Ukraine's nationwide defensive spoofing against incoming drones and missiles, and its side effects on civilian devices' location and time.
nodes.kt: Defensive spoofing has collateral effects on civil PNT and timing Any consumer-grade nav stack must tolerate wrong GNSS

nodes.n: NATO DIANA unveils 10 new challenges to accelerate dual-use technology breakthroughs
nodes.s: Announcement of DIANA's 2026 challenge programme topics, including operating in contested electromagnetic environments, with problem statements that describe what NATO wants solved.
nodes.kt: Problem statements stress dual-use and resilience in contested spectrum Good template for writing a hackathon pitch in NATO language

nodes.n: NATO DIANA's breakthrough solutions for secure communication and navigation
nodes.s: DIANA feature on cohort companies working on resilient navigation and secure communications, illustrating which approaches made it through selection.
nodes.kt: Shows the spread of selected approaches: magnetic, quantum, LEO PNT, vision Selection favors deployable, testable dual-use products

nodes.n: Ukraine's Brave1, NATO Launch €10M Competition for Counter-Drone Technology
nodes.s: Coverage of a Brave1-NATO competition funding counter-drone technology and navigation that works under electronic warfare.
nodes.kt: Brave1 frames navigation under EW as a top battlefield need Competitions emphasize rapid field testing

nodes.n: В Україні провели хакатон зі створення антидронових рішень (Anti-drone hackathon held in Ukraine)
nodes.s: Ukrainian-language report on a defense hackathon focused on counter-drone solutions.
nodes.kt: Ukrainian hackathons are short, problem-driven and tied to frontline users Detection and EW-resilience recur as tracks

nodes.n: DIU launches new emerging tech portfolio, solicits industry for quantum sensing capabilities
nodes.s: Coverage of DIU's Transition of Quantum Sensing call seeking quantum inertial sensors and magnetometers to extend navigation holdover when GPS is unavailable.
nodes.kt: DIU's stated value: reduced drift means longer holdover without GPS Lines of effort: inertial, magnetometers, technology insertion Magnetic anomaly navigation is a funded transition path

nodes.n: DARPA eyeing new quantum sensing program
nodes.s: Report on DARPA's RoQS program to make quantum sensors robust to platform interference so they can support navigation without GPS on real vehicles.
nodes.kt: Platform noise, not lab sensitivity, is the barrier DARPA targets Context for why classical magnetic compensation still matters

nodes.n: DARPA Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Technology and their Impacts on GPS users
nodes.s: DARPA slide deck summarizing its PNT portfolio, including All Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN), a plug-and-play architecture for fusing non-traditional sensors when GPS is denied.
nodes.kt: ASPN pushes sensor-agnostic, plug-and-play fusion Shows the long-running DoD interest in all-source navigation

nodes.n: EDF-2024-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-SENS-RADNP: Multi-sensor integration for robust autonomous drone navigation
nodes.s: European Defence Fund technological-challenge topic on multi-sensor integration for autonomous drone navigation in GNSS-denied or contested environments, run as an organized competition with evaluation campaigns. Listing via an aggregator; confirm details on the EU Funding and Tenders portal.
nodes.kt: EU frames GNSS-denied drone navigation as a benchmarked challenge Multi-sensor fusion, not a single sensor, is the ask

nodes.s: Factsheet for an EDF-funded project developing ground and space-based detection of illegitimate activity in GNSS bands.
nodes.kt: Interference detection and monitoring is a funded European priority Pairs well with ADS-B/SDR monitoring hackathon ideas

nodes.n: Advanced Radio Frequency Sensing, Integrated Effects and PNT
nodes.s: UK DASA themed competition (for the Bright Corvus project) seeking RF sensing and resilient PNT innovations.
nodes.kt: UK MOD treats RF sensing and PNT as one problem space Example of UK-style challenge framing

nodes.n: Positioning, Navigation and Timing Growth: government response
nodes.s: UK government response on growing the resilient PNT sector, following its national PNT framework work.
nodes.kt: UK policy treats resilient PNT as both security and export opportunity Useful framing for dual-use pitches

nodes.s: Defines four cumulative resilience levels for PNT user equipment based on prevent, respond and recover behaviours, so buyers and vendors can describe how a receiver behaves under jamming or spoofing.
nodes.kt: Gives vocabulary to grade your solution: prevent, respond, recover Solution-agnostic, so it fits any sensor mix Later versions and an IEEE standards effort followed Levels escalate from basic recovery to full prevention and response Scope is PNT-producing equipment, not downstream consumers A later v2.0 was reported in 2022 with evaluation guidance

nodes.n: NISTIR 8323: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
nodes.s: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework onto systems that consume PNT, giving identify/protect/detect/respond/recover practices for GNSS dependence.
nodes.kt: Treats GNSS as an untrusted external input Detection and recovery practices map directly to hackathon features

nodes.s: US Navy prize challenge on unmanned and autonomous systems with tracks on securing a simulated autopilot, separating benign from malicious data, and model-based mission requirements.
nodes.kt: Navy judges reward working prototypes on realistic simulated systems Cyber-resilience of autopilots is treated as part of autonomy

nodes.s: AFRL/Space Force capture-the-flag on satellite and ground-segment security; challenge code from several editions has been released publicly.
nodes.kt: Space-segment security is part of assured PNT Released challenges are good training material

nodes.s: DARPA's 2018-2021 challenge for autonomous robot teams mapping and searching tunnels, urban underground and caves with no GNSS and degraded comms; systems and virtual tracks.
nodes.kt: Scoring rewarded accurate localization of reported artifacts, not just coverage Heterogeneous teams (legged + aerial) won Communication-denied autonomy was decisive

nodes.s: DARPA challenge for autonomous systems that find and assess casualties in mass-casualty scenes, combining drones and ground robots navigating degraded, GNSS-unreliable environments.
nodes.kt: Humanitarian defense use-case with navigation plus perception Team directory helps find open contributions

nodes.n: A Multi-Robot Platform for Robotic Triage Combining Onboard Sensing and Foundation Models
nodes.s: Technical report from a DARPA Triage Challenge team describing a multi-robot system and fine-tuned open vision-language models for injury identification.
nodes.kt: Shows how a challenge team integrates navigation, perception and VLMs Open-model fine-tuning is viable under challenge time budgets

nodes.n: DAF-MIT AIA Open Flight Data for Magnetic Navigation Research
nodes.s: Zenodo record of airborne magnetometer, INS and GNSS flight data with datasheets, collected for the MagNav challenge.
nodes.kt: Real flight lines with multiple magnetometers Ground truth from GNSS for evaluating nav error

nodes.n: Team CERBERUS Wins the DARPA Subterranean Challenge: Technical Overview and Lessons Learned
nodes.s: Winning team's description of its legged-plus-aerial system: multi-modal perception, robust localization and mapping, exploration planning and artifact detection, with lessons from the final.
nodes.kt: Robust multi-sensor odometry and exploration were key Field-hardening and operator workflow mattered as much as algorithms

nodes.n: CERBERUS: Autonomous Legged and Aerial Robotic Exploration in the Tunnel and Urban Circuits of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
nodes.s: Field Robotics paper covering CERBERUS' systems and results in the earlier SubT circuits, including perception, planning and artifact reporting.
nodes.kt: Documents the iteration path to the winning system

nodes.n: NeBula: Quest for Robotic Autonomy in Challenging Environments; TEAM CoSTAR at the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
nodes.s: Describes the NeBula belief-space autonomy stack: multi-modal positioning, mapping, traversability, risk-aware mission planning and multi-robot reasoning; CoSTAR won the Urban circuit.
nodes.kt: Reasoning over uncertainty in localization improves mission decisions Redundant odometry sources were essential underground

nodes.s: UZH's second-place AlphaPilot system: learned gate detection, nonlinear filtering of visual-inertial state and time-optimal trajectory planning for GPS-free racing.
nodes.kt: Vision-inertial state estimation, not GNSS, drove the race Splitting perception and planning made it robust

nodes.n: MAVLab wins the AlphaPilot AI challenge
nodes.s: TU Delft MAVLab's account of winning the 2019 Lockheed Martin AlphaPilot / AIRR autonomous drone race.
nodes.kt: Lightweight onboard estimation can beat heavier stacks Same lab later won A2RL 2025

nodes.n: Champion-level drone racing using deep reinforcement learning
nodes.s: Swift, a quadrotor using only onboard camera and IMU with an RL-trained policy, beat human world-champion pilots in head-to-head races.
nodes.kt: Onboard VIO plus learned control reached human-champion level Sim-to-real with residual models from real data

nodes.s: Summary of the A2RL x DCL autonomous drone championship, won by TU Delft MAVLab ahead of TII Racing and KAIST, including races against human pilots.
nodes.kt: Standardized drone and camera-only sensing put the focus on estimation and control University labs still beat well-funded teams

nodes.n: Satellite Pose Estimation Challenge: Dataset, Competition Design and Results
nodes.s: ESA Kelvins / Stanford competition on monocular spacecraft pose estimation, analyzing 48 entries.
nodes.kt: Keypoint detection plus PnP beat direct pose regression Shows how ESA designs and scores a navigation competition

nodes.n: ESA Kelvins Satellite Pose Estimation Competition 2021 (SPEED+)
nodes.s: Follow-up Kelvins challenge focused on bridging the domain gap: train on synthetic images, test on hardware-in-the-loop lightbox and sunlamp images.
nodes.kt: Sim-to-real gap is the core difficulty judges scored Kelvins pages document rules and metrics

nodes.s: Official docs for the Stone Soup tracking framework with step-by-step tutorials from a single-target Kalman filter through data association (PDA, JPDA), multi-hypothesis tracking, GM-PHD, track initiation/deletion, sensor management and performance metrics.
nodes.kt: Tutorial path from single-target Kalman to multi-target Metrics module helps score your fusion objectively Tutorials double as a self-paced multi-target tracking course Metrics module (OSPA, SIAP) gives defensible evaluation numbers Sensor and simulator components let you test without real radar

nodes.n: Drone Security and the Mysterious Case of DJI's DroneID
nodes.s: Security analysis of DJI drones that reverse-engineers the DroneID broadcast and shows it is unencrypted, with an open receiver released.
nodes.kt: Passive decoding enables detection and localization of DJI drones Security analysis of drone firmware and protocols DroneID leaks drone and pilot position in the clear Decoding needs SDR captures at high sample rates

nodes.s: FAA guidance on the Remote ID rule: what drones must broadcast, standard vs broadcast-module compliance and operator obligations.
nodes.kt: Remote ID gives a lawful, cooperative signal for drone awareness Defines what fields you can expect to decode Standard Remote ID broadcasts drone and control station location Non-compliant drones need non-cooperative detection

nodes.n: The EAR and Open Source Software
nodes.s: Practical guide to how US Export Administration Regulations treat published open-source code, including the separate notification step for encryption.
nodes.kt: Code published without restriction is generally outside the EAR Encryption source has an extra BIS/NSA notification step Private repos shared with foreign nationals can count as exports

nodes.s: The regulation text defining when information and software count as 'published' and therefore not subject to the EAR.
nodes.kt: Primary source to cite in an export-control slide Read with 734.3(b)(3) and 742.15(b)

nodes.n: U.S. Export Controls and "Published" Encryption Source Code Explained
nodes.s: EFF explainer on the 2016-era EAR changes for published encryption source and when email notification is still needed.
nodes.kt: Relevant if your PNT code includes signal authentication crypto

nodes.n: Overview of Regulatory Definitions of Publicly Available, Public Domain, and Published
nodes.s: University compliance guide comparing ITAR public-domain (22 CFR 120.34) and EAR published definitions and the fundamental-research exclusion.
nodes.kt: ITAR-controlled data cannot simply be put in the public domain by an individual Fundamental-research protection can be lost via publication restrictions Military GNSS items (e.g. M-code receivers, some anti-jam antenna tech) may be ITAR or EAR controlled - keep hackathon code on public civil signals and published methods

nodes.n: DOD adopts 5 principles of artificial intelligence ethics
nodes.s: Announcement of the DoD's AI ethical principles - responsible, equitable, traceable, reliable, governable - recommended by the Defense Innovation Board.
nodes.kt: Traceable and governable map to logging and safe fallback in nav autonomy Judges increasingly ask how an AI component can be disengaged

nodes.n: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy
nodes.s: NATO's 2021 AI strategy summary setting six principles of responsible use: lawfulness, responsibility and accountability, explainability and traceability, reliability, governability, bias mitigation.
nodes.kt: Applies across the whole AI lifecycle Expect a NATO-flavored jury to probe reliability and governability

nodes.n: DoD Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems (2023 reissue)
nodes.s: DoD policy governing development and use of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems, reissued January 2023. Cited here as the boundary marker: navigation and awareness tools are outside its scope, weapon autonomy is not.
nodes.kt: Clear line between navigation/autonomy for mobility and weapon autonomy Keep hackathon scope on the navigation and awareness side

nodes.s: The EU's recast dual-use export control regulation covering items, software and technology including navigation and avionics categories, with public-domain and basic-research de-control notes.
nodes.kt: Category 7 covers navigation and avionics items Public-domain and basic scientific research notes protect open publication

nodes.n: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/1700 on internal compliance programmes for controls of research involving dual-use items
nodes.s: Non-binding guidance helping universities and researchers spot and manage dual-use export risks, with scenarios, red flags and FAQs.
nodes.kt: Practical red-flag checklist for collaborative or international teams Contact national authority when control status is unclear

nodes.n: IS-GPS-200N: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Segment Interfaces
nodes.s: The master interface specification for the legacy GPS L1 C/A and L2C (and P(Y) at the public level) signals: code generation, signal structure, and the full LNAV/CNAV navigation message bit layouts. Every GPS receiver, simulator and spoofing detector ultimately decodes against this document.
nodes.kt: Defines LNAV subframe and CNAV message formats bit-for-bit Ephemeris, clock and ionosphere parameter algorithms live here Revisions are managed through the public ICWG process Authoritative source for ephemeris and clock equations Defines L1 C/A and L2C signal structure Needed to build or audit any navigation message decoder

nodes.n: IS-GPS-705J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L5 Interfaces
nodes.s: Interface specification for the GPS L5 safety-of-life band signal: I5/Q5 codes, the L5 CNAV message, and signal characteristics. L5's higher chipping rate and wider band make it more robust to narrowband interference than L1 C/A.
nodes.kt: Defines the L5 dataless pilot (Q5) and data (I5) channels CNAV message types shared with L2C Draft uprevisions were discussed at the 2025 public ICWG

nodes.n: IS-GPS-800J: NAVSTAR GPS Space Segment / User Segment L1C Interfaces
nodes.s: Interface specification for the modernized L1C civil signal designed for interoperability with Galileo E1 and other GNSS: BOC/TMBOC modulation, Weil-code ranging codes, and the CNAV-2 message.
nodes.kt: L1C uses a pilot plus data component, like Galileo E1 CNAV-2 adds FEC-coded subframes Key reference for multi-GNSS L1 receiver design

nodes.s: Index page for the public GPS ICDs and ISs (200, 705, 800, 870 etc.), change notices and public ICWG meeting material. Useful to find the current revision and pending changes such as integrity support message formats.
nodes.kt: Single place to check which revision is in force Hosts proposed change notices and meeting redlines Single entry point for all GPS signal ICDs Historic versions also linked Archive site, frozen since February 2025 per its own banner

nodes.n: GPS Standard Positioning Service (SPS) Performance Standard, 5th Edition
nodes.s: The formal commitment the US government makes about civil GPS signal-in-space accuracy, availability, continuity and integrity. It is the baseline to compare against when judging whether a receiver anomaly is the signal or interference.
nodes.kt: States guaranteed SIS user range error and availability levels Defines what counts as a major service failure Basis for RAIM and integrity assumptions in aviation

nodes.n: Galileo Open Service Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document (OS SIS ICD) Issue 2.1
nodes.s: Specification of the Galileo open service signals (E1, E5a, E5b, E6 at the structure level) and the F/NAV and I/NAV navigation messages. Needed for any multi-constellation receiver or Galileo decoder.
nodes.kt: Defines I/NAV and F/NAV page layouts Ranging code and modulation details for E1 and E5 Newer issues are listed in the GSC reference documents library Required for decoding Galileo navigation data I/NAV is the carrier for OSNMA bits

nodes.n: Galileo OSNMA Signal-In-Space Interface Control Document Issue 1.1
nodes.s: Defines Open Service Navigation Message Authentication: how TESLA-chain MACs and keys are embedded in spare I/NAV bits so a receiver can cryptographically verify that navigation data came from Galileo. It is the first civil GNSS data-authentication service in operation.
nodes.kt: Uses a TESLA key chain with delayed key disclosure Authenticates navigation data, not the ranging signal itself Requires loose time sync and a public key obtained out of band Civil signal authentication is available today on Galileo E1-B Receivers need loose time synchronization to verify TESLA keys Defines what an authenticated vs unauthenticated navigation message means

nodes.s: Companion to the OSNMA ICD describing how a receiver should process OSNMA: time-sync requirements, key and Merkle-tree handling, verification procedures and how to report authentication status to the user.
nodes.kt: Spells out the receiver time-sync assumption that OSNMA security depends on Covers cold start, key renewal and chain transitions Practical checklist for implementing OSNMA in software Explains which attacks OSNMA does and does not stop (e.g. replay/meaconing limits) Covers key renewal and alert handling

nodes.n: Galileo Open Service Navigation Message Authentication (OSNMA) - service page
nodes.s: Official landing page for the OSNMA service with status, public key and Merkle tree downloads, and links to the ICD and guidelines.
nodes.kt: Where to get the current OSNMA public key and Merkle root Links to service notices and documentation Where to download the cryptographic material receivers need

nodes.n: Galileo High Accuracy Service Signal-In-Space ICD (HAS SIS ICD) Issue 1.0
nodes.s: Defines the free Galileo High Accuracy Service: PPP orbit, clock and bias corrections broadcast on E6-B (and via internet), including message structure and Reed-Solomon encoding.
nodes.kt: Free PPP corrections broadcast from the satellites themselves Enables decimetre-level PPP without a ground subscription E6-B message decoding details for receiver builders

nodes.n: European GNSS Service Centre - Programme Reference Documents
nodes.s: Library of current Galileo ICDs, service definition documents and receiver guidelines (OS, HAS, OSNMA, SAR). Check here for the latest issue numbers before implementing.
nodes.kt: Authoritative versions of all public Galileo specs Includes service definition documents with committed performance Includes the HAS (High Accuracy Service) ICD for free PPP corrections

nodes.n: BeiDou Navigation Satellite System Signal-In-Space ICDs (B1I, B3I, B1C, B2a, B2b)
nodes.s: Official English-language ICD library for BeiDou open service signals, including the BDS-3 B1C and B2a signals that are interoperable with GPS L1C/L5 and Galileo E1/E5a, plus PPP-B2b.
nodes.kt: BDS-3 B1C and B2a are designed for multi-GNSS interoperability PPP-B2b carries free regional precise corrections The BeiDou site is the official distribution channel

nodes.n: QZSS Performance Standards and Interface Specifications (IS-QZSS)
nodes.s: Japan's QZSS interface specifications covering GPS-compatible signals, the L6 CLAS centimetre-level augmentation and MADOCA PPP services.
nodes.kt: QZSS signals are GPS-interoperable and improve urban-canyon availability in Asia-Oceania CLAS and MADOCA give free precise positioning corrections Specs are published openly by the Cabinet Office

nodes.s: The paid-access RTCM v3 standard that defines the binary messages used to stream GNSS corrections and observations (legacy RTK 1001-1012, MSM 1-7 per constellation, ephemerides, SSR). Practically every NTRIP caster and RTK base station speaks it.
nodes.kt: MSM messages replaced legacy observation messages and align with RINEX 3 MSM4/MSM7 are the common choices for RTK Standard itself is purchased; open parsers document much of it

nodes.s: Free encyclopedia overview of the RTCM correction message families and transport (NTRIP) used for real-time kinematic positioning. A good orientation before buying or parsing the RTCM standard.
nodes.kt: Explains the role of RTCM 2.x vs 3.x messages Covers NTRIP for internet transport

nodes.s: The ASCII serial sentence standard (GGA, RMC, GSA, GSV, VTG...) used by nearly all GNSS receivers and marine electronics. The official standard is sold; open references cover the common sentences.
nodes.kt: Talker IDs distinguish GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and multi-GNSS output Checksummed ASCII over serial, easy to parse and to fake Still the lowest-common-denominator GNSS output

nodes.s: CAN bus based marine network standard that carries position, heading, AIS and engine data as PGNs between devices. Paid standard; the community has reverse-documented many PGNs.
nodes.kt: PGNs carry GNSS position, COG/SOG, heading and AIS Plug-and-play backbone on modern vessels Unauthenticated bus, relevant to maritime spoofing resilience

nodes.s: A free, detailed field-by-field reference to NMEA 0183 sentences as actually emitted by real receivers, including vendor quirks and version differences. The practical substitute for the paywalled standard.
nodes.kt: Documents real-world deviations from the standard Covers talker IDs for multi-GNSS output Written by gpsd maintainers who parse these daily

nodes.s: Official documentation for the MAVLink micro air vehicle messaging protocol: message definitions, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, FTP), dialects and code generators.
nodes.kt: Lightweight binary protocol between autopilots, GCS and companion computers Microservices define stateful exchanges like mission upload Generators produce bindings for C, Python, Rust and more

nodes.s: Reference of all messages and commands in the common dialect, including GPS_RAW_INT, GPS_INPUT for injecting external position, ODOMETRY and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE for non-GNSS navigation sources.
nodes.kt: GPS_INPUT and VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE are the hooks for feeding alternative PNT into an autopilot ODOMETRY carries full pose plus covariance Enumerations document EKF and GPS fix status flags

nodes.s: Describes MAVLink 2 packet signing: a shared-secret SHA-256 based signature and timestamp appended to frames to authenticate the link and resist replay.
nodes.kt: Signing authenticates but does not encrypt traffic Key distribution is left to the integrator Relevant for hardening drone C2 links against injection

nodes.s: The microservice used to upload, download and clear waypoint missions, geofences and rally points between a GCS and an autopilot, with its handshake and retry rules.
nodes.kt: Defines MISSION_COUNT / MISSION_ITEM_INT handshake Same protocol carries geofence and rally point plans

nodes.s: Briefing introducing the Cursor on Target XML event schema: the minimal event/point/detail model for exchanging what-when-where of tracked entities between C2 systems.
nodes.kt: Base schema is tiny: event, point, detail Type strings follow a hierarchical a-f-G-... code derived from symbology Extensibility lives in the detail element

nodes.n: TAK Protocol (takproto) - protobuf encoding of CoT
nodes.s: Documentation of the TAK protocol used by ATAK and TAK Server: how CoT events are framed and carried as protocol buffers over mesh (UDP multicast) and streaming (TCP/TLS) transports, alongside legacy XML.
nodes.kt: Explains version negotiation between XML and protobuf CoT Mesh vs streaming framing headers Essential to get a custom app talking to ATAK

nodes.n: STANAG 4586 - Standard Interfaces of UAV Control System (UCS) for NATO UAV Interoperability
nodes.s: Public overview of NATO's UAS interoperability standard, which defines a core UCS, a vehicle-specific module and five levels of interoperability from receiving payload data up to full flight control including launch and recovery.
nodes.kt: LOI 1-3 cover payload data and control; LOI 4-5 cover flight control Vehicle Specific Module isolates proprietary air vehicle interfaces Full text distributed via NATO / national channels

nodes.s: NATO's public explanation of how STANAGs and Allied publications are produced and ratified, and how interoperability standards flow into national forces. Starting point for locating public STANAG/AP summaries.
nodes.kt: STANAGs record national agreement to implement an Allied publication Most full texts are restricted; summaries and some APs are public

nodes.s: Overview of APP-6, the NATO standard for map symbols of units, equipment and tactical graphics, now at edition E and aligned with the US MIL-STD-2525 family. Explains frames, affiliation colours and the symbol identification code.
nodes.kt: Affiliation (friend/hostile/neutral/unknown) is encoded by frame shape and colour APP-6 and MIL-STD-2525 share a common symbol code structure Open renderers implement it for COP displays

nodes.s: Summary of the US military symbology standard and its revisions (2525B through E), including the SIDC code formats that symbol renderers and CoT type strings map onto.
nodes.kt: 2525D/E moved to a numeric 20/30-digit SIDC Basis for symbology in TAK and many C2 tools

nodes.n: Executive Order 13905: Strengthening National Resilience Through Responsible Use of PNT Services
nodes.s: US executive order that defines 'responsible use of PNT' and tasks Commerce/NIST, DHS and others to produce PNT profiles, identify critical infrastructure dependencies and pilot-test resilience. It is the root of NIST IR 8323 and the DHS conformance framework.
nodes.kt: Treats PNT disruption as a critical infrastructure risk Directs creation of voluntary PNT profiles Calls for testing PNT resilience in federal contracts

nodes.n: NIST IR 8323r1: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
nodes.s: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) onto systems that produce or consume PNT data. A checklist-style profile for building resilient PNT into an architecture.
nodes.kt: Revision 1 supersedes the 2021 original Organized around CSF functions, applicable to both GNSS and non-GNSS sources NIST has signalled alignment with CSF 2.0

nodes.s: Companion to the conformance framework describing architectural patterns (source diversity, integrity checking, holdover) that map to its resilience levels.
nodes.kt: Architectural guidance for multi-source PNT Mapped to conformance framework levels

nodes.n: DHS S&T Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Program
nodes.s: Program hub for DHS PNT work: conformance framework, reference architecture, timing guidance and test events for critical infrastructure.
nodes.kt: Links all DHS resilient PNT publications Shows the civil critical-infrastructure angle of PNT resilience

nodes.n: DoD Directive 4650.05: Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)
nodes.s: DoD policy directive governing the department's PNT enterprise, including the PNT Oversight Council and responsibilities for assured PNT and navigation warfare. Change 3 (2023) updated the oversight structure.
nodes.kt: Establishes the DoD PNT Oversight Council Assigns responsibilities for PNT and navigation warfare

nodes.n: GAO-21-320SP: Defense Navigation Capabilities - DOD Is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
nodes.s: Technology assessment of DoD's alternative PNT efforts (inertial, vision, celestial, magnetic, signals of opportunity, clocks), with maturity status and challenges. A concise government map of the alt-PNT landscape.
nodes.kt: DOD keeps GPS at the core and adds complements Reviews maturity of many alt-PNT technology families Flags integration and testing as recurring challenges

nodes.n: National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Resilience R&D Plan
nodes.s: Federal R&D plan responding to EO 13905, laying out research priorities for resilient PNT: threat detection, alternative sources, timing distribution and integrity.
nodes.kt: Identifies federal R&D priorities for PNT resilience Ties research areas back to EO 13905

nodes.s: US DOT plan to drive adoption of complementary PNT for transportation and critical infrastructure via stakeholder engagement, specifications, field trials and test ranges.
nodes.kt: Five lines of effort starting with engagement and standards Leads to field testing of commercial CPNT technologies

nodes.n: Analyzing a More Resilient National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Capability (RR-2970)
