nodes.s: DHS-sponsored RAND study of civil US PNT dependence that argues GPS is not the only PNT source in practice and that no single system is a perfect backup. It is a deliberately contrarian counterweight to the 'GPS loss is catastrophic' framing.
nodes.kt: Realistic adaptation lowers estimated economic cost of GPS loss High bar for a large government-funded GPS backup Recommends modest investment in threat detection

nodes.n: Assessing Alternative Positioning, Navigation and Timing Technologies for Potential Deployment in the EU
nodes.s: JRC test campaign at Ispra of commercial alternative PNT systems (terrestrial beacons, LEO, eLoran-like, fibre timing and others) for DG DEFIS. One of the few side-by-side public evaluations of A-PNT products.
nodes.kt: Mature commercial A-PNT already exists for positioning or timing Recommends a system-of-systems approach Warns the diverse tests do not allow a fair head-to-head ranking

nodes.n: JRC Complementary Position, Navigation and Timing
nodes.s: JRC activity page hosting the A-PNT assessment report with per-vendor appendices and related EU complementary PNT work.
nodes.kt: Official host for the report and vendor appendices

nodes.s: UN forum where GNSS providers coordinate compatibility, interoperability and spectrum protection, including interference detection and mitigation work.
nodes.kt: Venue for multi-GNSS interoperability agreements Hosts work on interference detection and mitigation

nodes.n: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R4: GNSS Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
nodes.s: EASA's running bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aviation since February 2022, with recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers. Revision 4 is the current issue.
nodes.kt: Spoofing is treated as the harder-to-detect, higher-risk threat Recommendations are informational, not mandatory Affected FIRs are tracked on the EASA website

nodes.n: FAA GPS/GNSS Interference Reports and Anomaly Reporting
nodes.s: FAA page for reporting and reviewing GPS anomalies and interference events, with links to notices about planned GPS interference testing and operator guidance.
nodes.kt: Where US pilots file post-flight interference reports Links to GPS test NOTAM information

nodes.n: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
nodes.s: Safety alert for operators describing how jamming and spoofing manifest in the cockpit and what crews should do: revert to conventional procedures, report to ATC, and file written reports.
nodes.kt: Describes cockpit symptoms of jamming vs spoofing Advises readiness to use conventional navaids Later FAA guidance revisions followed in 2026

nodes.n: GNSS interference (ICAO WRC-27 Preparatory Workshop presentation)
nodes.s: French DGAC presentation at an ICAO WRC-27 preparatory workshop on GNSS RFI: definitions of RFI, jamming and spoofing, the problems they cause in flight (with OPSGROUP 2024 spoofing data), where interference happens, and the ICAO position and actions.
nodes.kt: Summarizes operational impacts on avionics Frames the ICAO-level mitigation agenda

nodes.s: Program to field low-SWaP optical atomic clocks with timing holdover beyond GPS satellite clocks, in a portable airborne variant and a transportable land/sea variant, to keep precise time without GNSS.
nodes.kt: Two technical areas: portable and transportable clocks Two two-year phases from physics package to operational clock

nodes.n: DARPA's ROCkN Program Targets GNSS-Free Precision Timing in Contested Environments
nodes.s: Progress report on ROCkN field tests, including optical clock hardware flown on aircraft and deployed aboard a ship.
nodes.kt: Reports field synchronization and platform trials Shows optical clocks leaving the lab

nodes.s: Challenge site for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: compensate the aircraft's own magnetic field out of magnetometer data so the remaining crustal anomaly can be map-matched for GPS-free navigation. Challenge is closed but data and code remain.
nodes.kt: Scored against a professionally compensated tail-stinger magnetometer Real flight data from survey aircraft Directly reusable as a hackathon benchmark Sensors: scalar and vector magnetometers, INS, GPS truth Domain: airborne Code: MagNav.jl Terms: Air Force data sharing agreement, non-profit research, education or US government use only, one-year licence

nodes.s: Zenodo record holding the MagNav challenge flight data: magnetometer, INS, GPS truth and map data from survey flights.

nodes.kt: Vendor claim: AuterionOS detects GNSS jamming/spoofing and stops trusting GNSS (Jan 2024 announcement) Vendor/press claim: used in Ukraine; no public accuracy figures found Open-source base is PX4; the visual navigation layer is proprietary

nodes.s: Hivemind is Shield AI's onboard autonomy software, flown on its V-BAT and on partner aircraft. In an interview the CTO describes a state-estimation framework fusing visual, EO/IR and inertial observations so the aircraft keeps operating without GNSS or comms.
nodes.kt: Vendor description: multi-sensor state estimation for GNSS-denied and comms-denied flight No published accuracy numbers found ViDAR (acquired with Sentient Vision, 2024) is an EO/IR detection product, not a navigation source

nodes.n: Helsing HX-2 - map/landmark-based GNSS-denied navigation (navigation aspect only)
nodes.s: Helsing's HX-2 is a loitering UAS supplied to Ukraine. Indexed here only for its navigation approach: press reporting says an onboard computer with stored map data lets it navigate by recognising landmarks when satellite navigation is denied. Helsing navigation job postings mention vision-aided, terrain-relative, celestial and signals-of-opportunity methods.
nodes.kt: Press/vendor claim: landmark recognition against stored maps; no public accuracy data Shows the European market expects map-based visual nav as a baseline feature

nodes.n: Q-CTRL Ironstone Opal quantum-assured magnetic navigation
nodes.s: Q-CTRL's navigation product pairs quantum magnetometers with its software to match measured crustal magnetic anomalies against maps (MagNav). The company reports flight, ground and maritime trials and positions it as a GNSS backup for aviation, including work with Airbus.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims (not independent): RNP 0.3 met in flight (error under 0.3 nm for 95% of a flight); the linked case study claims 50x lower positioning uncertainty than an INS over a ~500 km flight and at least 11x with the sensor inside the cabin; other Q-CTRL materials give different multipliers Vendor claim: RTCA DO-160 environmental qualification - not an airworthiness or RNP operational approval Underlying method is the same map-matching problem as the open AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge

nodes.s: AQNav is SandboxAQ's magnetic anomaly navigation system: magnetometers plus learned compensation, matched against magnetic anomaly maps. Flight-tested with Acubed (Airbus) on a Beechcraft Baron using public maps, and, per later SandboxAQ announcements, with the USAF on C-17/C-130J and in 2026 on a Northrop Grumman Lumberjack drone.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims (July 2025 Acubed campaign, 150+ flight hours on a Beechcraft Baron 58 with the public NAMAM map): within RNP 2 100% of the time and RNP 1 95%; outperformed INS without GNSS on every flight over 2 h Sept 2026 drone test announcement gave no error figures (noted by press) Accepted into the 2025 NATO DIANA cohort (vendor/press)

nodes.n: Xona Space Systems Pulsar LEO PNT constellation
nodes.s: Xona is building Pulsar, a commercial LEO constellation broadcasting dedicated L-band navigation signals with authentication. Pulsar-0 launched in June/July 2025 as an in-orbit demonstrator; production satellites and initial service were planned for 2026-2027 per later reporting, and the FCC granted conditional approval in August 2026 (initially 16 satellites, more after a debris review).
nodes.kt: LEO PNT signals are stronger at the ground than MEO GNSS, which is the anti-jam argument Service is not yet generally available; dates in press reports conflict Open work in this space uses existing LEO signals of opportunity (Starlink, Iridium Doppler) instead

nodes.s: TrustPoint is developing a commercial C-band LEO navigation constellation. Its third demonstration satellite (Time Flies) launched in June 2025 carrying a C-band payload for testing partner receivers.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: commercial GPS alternative from LEO; no independent performance reports found C-band choice moves PNT away from crowded and jammed L-band

nodes.n: Iridium PNT (Satellite Time and Location) and Iridium PNT ASIC
nodes.s: Iridium broadcasts a high-power LEO timing and location signal (STL, from the Satelles acquisition) usable as a GNSS backup and cross-check. A dedicated PNT ASIC was unveiled in October 2025 and announced commercially available in July 2026; integrators include Solace and Skyband, and VectorNav/NAL Research announced STL-aided INS work in 2025.
nodes.kt: Positioning is coarse compared to GNSS; main value is timing and an independent plausibility check Vendor claim on ASIC size: 8 x 8 mm, under 0.2 g (Iridium fact sheet, Oct 2025) Open LEO Doppler code in the index can use Iridium signals of opportunity without a subscription

nodes.n: Honeywell Vision Aided Navigation (Alternative Navigation Suite)
nodes.s: Honeywell's VAN correlates live visible or IR imagery against onboard reference maps for an absolute fix, paired with its inertial units. It sits in an Alternative Navigation Suite with magnetic-anomaly and celestial modules.
nodes.kt: Vendor description: passive, sensor-agnostic image-to-map correlation Press claim: 'GPS-like' performance on Embraer E170 and AW139 tests; no numbers published Same problem as open UAV absolute visual localization benchmarks

nodes.n: Honeywell HGuide o480 single-card INS and HGuide i700 IMU
nodes.s: HGuide o480 (May 2025) is a single-card INS for small UAVs and ground robots that accepts velocity aiding (e.g. Honeywell radar velocity sensor) and embeds a Septentrio receiver with AIM+ anti-jam/anti-spoof. The HGuide i700 IMU is marketed as near navigation grade with a no-license-required export classification.
nodes.kt: Shows the commodity pattern: tactical IMU + velocity aid + hardened GNSS in one card Export classification is a selling point, which matters for team hardware choices

nodes.n: Advanced Navigation Boreas FOG INS with LVS laser velocity sensor
nodes.s: Advanced Navigation's Boreas fibre-optic-gyro INS line, fused with its LVS laser velocity sensor or wheel odometry, is marketed for long GNSS-denied ground and maritime runs; reported trials include a US Army testbed and an underground mine.
nodes.kt: Vendor/press claims: 11.7 m error over 65 km with GNSS jammed (wheel-encoder config, US Army testbed, linked article); better than 0.1% of distance travelled in BHP's Callio mine trial (Advanced Navigation case study) Strategy is inertial-centric dead reckoning with velocity aiding, not vision

nodes.n: Inertial Labs VINS visual-aided INS (with Maxar Raptor)
nodes.s: Launched June 2025, VINS combines an Inertial Labs INS with Maxar Raptor software that matches camera frames to Maxar Precision3D satellite-derived 3D maps for absolute position on long-range UAV flights.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims: about 35 m horizontal / 5 m vertical without GNSS Options for Iridium-based PNT and M-code receivers Commercial map product (Precision3D) is the moat; open teams use free orthophotos and DEMs

nodes.n: Safran VersaPNT and Geonyx resilient PNT units
nodes.s: Safran's defense PNT range includes VersaPNT (GNSS receiver + IMU + disciplined oscillator with jamming/spoofing detection and NTP/PTP time serving) and the Geonyx HRG-based INS; GPS World reports a NAVKITE kit combining Geonyx M with VersaSync for French Navy commandos.
nodes.kt: Combined position + timing holdover in one box is the standard defense product shape Detection flags and holdover timing are reproducible in open stacks at lower grade

nodes.n: SBG Systems Ellipse INS - 2025 GNSS-denied firmware
nodes.s: A March 2025 free firmware update for SBG's Ellipse (v3 hardware) adds jamming/spoofing detection flags and lets users reject or re-enable GNSS and other aiding sensors without resetting the filter.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: improved accuracy in GNSS-denied and magnetically disturbed conditions Integrity flags plus manual sensor rejection is now an expected feature even in small INS

nodes.n: VectorNav - Iridium STL-aided INS collaboration with NAL Research
nodes.s: VectorNav makes small tactical-grade IMU/GNSS-INS units widely used on research drones (PX4 has a driver). In April 2025 it announced work with NAL Research on Iridium STL-aided INS for GNSS-denied operation.
nodes.kt: Collaboration announcement, not a shipped product feature VN-series units are a common drop-in for PX4 testbeds

nodes.n: Spirent GSS7000 and PNT X GNSS/PNT simulators
nodes.s: Spirent's lab simulators generate multi-GNSS RF with controllable interference and spoofing (meaconing, trajectory spoofing, nav data spoofing) for hardware-in-the-loop receiver testing; PNT X extends this to combined PNT/sensor simulation.
nodes.kt: Lab-grade, export-controlled tooling; judges from industry will know it Open alternatives are SDR-based signal simulators - legal only into a cable or shielded enclosure

nodes.n: Safran Skydel simulation engine / GSG-8 GNSS simulator (ex-Orolia)
nodes.s: Skydel is the SDR/GPU-based simulation engine behind Safran's GSG-8 simulators, with built-in jamming and spoofing scenarios, CRPA wavefront variants and LEO PNT signal options; Safran offers it to universities through an academic programme.
nodes.kt: Vendor datasheet: jamming and spoofing generated without extra hardware Spoofing workflows run a 'truth' and a 'spoofer' instance - a useful mental model for test design

nodes.n: infiniDome GPSdome / GPSdome 2 small-UAS anti-jam module
nodes.s: infiniDome sells retrofit anti-jam modules that sit between antenna elements and a commercial GNSS receiver on small drones and vehicles; GPSdome 2 is dual-band with up to four elements for nulling several jammer directions.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: CRPA-like protection without CRPA cost or export restrictions Weight figures differ across press releases (500 g in the linked GPS World piece, 350 g elsewhere)

nodes.n: Twist Robotics OSCAR visual navigation module (Ukraine)
nodes.s: Ukrainian company Twist Robotics announced OSCAR in January 2026: a camera-based module that recognises landmarks, matches them to a map and feeds coordinates to the UAV autopilot when GNSS is jammed.
nodes.kt: Vendor claim: platforms with the module have flown more than 500,000 km Architecture (camera => map match => coordinates into autopilot) is the same one open repos implement

nodes.n: Blue Arrow - Ukrainian visual navigation for drones (Brave1 cluster)
nodes.s: Brave1 cluster member Blue Arrow was presented by Ukraine's minister Fedorov in 2025 as having an autonomous visual navigation system that lets drones fly without GNSS under jamming and spoofing.
nodes.kt: Claim relayed from a ministerial post; no technical detail or numbers published One of many Ukrainian vendors in this niche (others named by Brave1: Norda Dynamics, The Fourth Law, ZIR)

nodes.s: US startup whose founders started at the February 2024 El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Aviation Week coverage). Its VNS uses a camera, an IMU and pre-loaded satellite imagery to estimate position and feeds the drone a substitute GPS signal.
nodes.kt: Vendor claims: six months from hackathon to a SOCOM sale (YC launch post); integration under 30 minutes (company statement relayed by press) Direct precedent that a hackathon visual-nav demo can become a product - and that judges have seen this pitch

nodes.n: Spleenlab VISIONAIRY perception and GNSS-free navigation software
nodes.s: German company Spleenlab sells VISIONAIRY, an AI perception suite for drones (vendor description: VIO, map-based relocalization, EO/IR and LiDAR SLAM) that joined the Auterion ecosystem in 2022 and integrates with PX4/Auterion and ROS. Quantum Systems later acquired Spleenlab and uses it for GNSS-denied navigation (press).
nodes.kt: Vendor description only; no published accuracy Module list mirrors what open VIO + VPR repos offer

nodes.s: UAVOS markets NavAI as an add-on vision-based navigation module for UAS in GNSS-degraded conditions (GPS World product announcement).
nodes.kt: Product announcement; performance figures not verified here

nodes.s: RoQS (solicitation DARPA-PS-25-11) aims to make quantum sensors robust to platform vibration and motion so they work on real vehicles; Phase 1 launched August 2025 with compact sensors to be tested on a government helicopter plus platform integration studies.
nodes.kt: Problem statement: quantum sensors lose their advantage on moving platforms Signals where defense money is going for GNSS-independent inertial/magnetic sensing

nodes.s: DIU programme fielding quantum sensors for PNT: lines of effort cover quantum inertial sensors, gravimeters for gravity-aided naval navigation, quantum magnetic sensing, magnetic navigation and component insertion, with more than 10 field tests planned in the first ~12 months (announced March 2025).
nodes.kt: 18 named performers including Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Q-CTRL, AOSense, Anduril, Northrop Grumman, Vector Atomic Honeywell flew a quantum MagNav test on an Embraer 170 under TQS (press)

nodes.n: DAF-MIT AI Accelerator MagNav real-time C-17 demonstration (2023)
nodes.s: In May 2023 the Air Force and MIT flew a real-time MagNav demo on a C-17A during exercise Golden Phoenix, training the compensation network in flight on a laptop. Follows the open MagNav challenge problem and dataset.
nodes.kt: No accuracy figure is public: the linked article and the official releases defer it to a government technical report. The value shown is RF independence Public dataset and Julia/Python code make this the most reproducible alt-PNT track for a hackathon

nodes.n: UK quantum navigation flight trials (Infleqtion, BAE Systems, QinetiQ)
nodes.s: In May 2024 an optical atomic clock and a cold-atom sensor flew on QinetiQ's RJ100 testbed from Boscombe Down, toward a quantum inertial navigation system concept. Linked to the UK National Quantum Strategy mission of quantum navigation on aircraft by 2030.
nodes.kt: Government claim: first publicly acknowledged in-flight tests of this kind Government funding stated as nearly GBP 8 million

nodes.n: UK DASA Early Market Engagement: PNT problem statement for uncrewed systems
nodes.s: Published September 2024. Asks for assured PNT for small UAS: low-cost, low-SWaP CRPA (multi-frequency, SDR-based), SDR/GPU GNSS receivers, AI for spoofing detection and multi-source fusion, as plug-in replacements for COTS GNSS.
nodes.kt: Explicit platform example: under 1.5 m wingspan Unit cost must suit mass use - cost is a first-class requirement

nodes.n: UK national eLoran, Timing Centre and GNSS warning investment (2025)
nodes.s: November 2025 UK announcement of about GBP 155M for a national timing centre, a sovereign eLoran system and GNSS interference warning; a Find a Tender notice targets eLoran IOC by 2028 and FOC by 2030.
nodes.kt: Terrestrial backup and GNSS warning, not only alt-nav on the vehicle

nodes.n: ESA NAVISP (Navigation Innovation and Support Programme)
nodes.s: ESA's PNT R&D programme funding industry projects including GNSS-independent PNT; 2025 examples include ALL.SPACE (EUR 950k per the October 2025 ALL.SPACE announcement, signals of opportunity from a multi-orbit terminal, with GMV NSL) and maritime alt-PNT via VDES and R-Mode.
nodes.kt: Permanent open call route for European companies Shows European emphasis on SoOP and terrestrial backups

nodes.s: EDF 2025 work programme (EUR 1.065B) closed 16 October 2025 with 410 proposals; results expected April 2026. Indexed as the current EDF cycle; the explicit drone-navigation challenge topic in the index is from EDF 2024.
nodes.kt: No 2025 topic explicitly on GNSS-denied navigation confirmed in this pass EDF 2024 challenge (multi-sensor drone navigation) is the best-matched prior topic

nodes.n: UNITE - Brave NATO: Brave1 and NATO Innovation HQ joint competition (2026)
nodes.s: March 2026 programme pairing Ukrainian and NATO-country companies on joint solutions: first round EUR 10M, up to EUR 1M per project split between partners. Focus areas are counter-UAS and navigation where EW disrupts positioning; NATO-side funding limited to non-lethal categories.
nodes.kt: Ministerial framing: 'robust navigation in GPS-denied environments' as a critical field

nodes.n: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 5th edition (Oct 2026) - GNSS-denied navigation challenge
nodes.s: EU-funded 48-hour hackathon held 15-17 October 2026 at eight sites under the theme 'Autonomy on the Battlefield'. Common challenges were GNSS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, plus one local challenge per host (e.g. counter-UAS in Cyprus).
nodes.kt: Most direct precedent for this hackathon's likely problem statement Eligibility: EU, Norway, Ukraine citizens aged 18+

nodes.n: European Defense Tech Hackathon series (Paris, London, Sheffield, Prague...)
nodes.s: Independent recurring European defense hackathon series. The December 2024 Paris edition had a second-place magnetic navigation entry for underwater drones; 2025 London and Sheffield editions listed GNSS-denied navigation tracks.
nodes.kt: Navigation tracks recur; winners skew toward working demos with real data

nodes.n: El Segundo Defense Tech Hackathon (Feb 2024) - origin of Theseus GPS-denied drone
nodes.s: Aviation Week story (March 2024) on three non-defense engineers who built a GPS-denied drone for under USD 500 at a 24-hour defense tech hackathon; the team became Theseus.
nodes.kt: Cheap visual nav prototypes are a known hackathon genre in the US

nodes.n: Online Training: Mobile Robotics (Basics + Robotics blocks)
nodes.s: A curated self-study path of short recorded lectures from Bonn's Photogrammetry & Robotics lab, going from linear algebra, rotations and least squares through Bayes filters, EKF localization, particle filters, ICP, RANSAC and graph-based SLAM. Each topic pairs a '5 Minutes with Cyrill' teaser with a full-length lecture.
nodes.kt: Fastest structured on-ramp to probabilistic state estimation Covers EKF/MCL localization and pose-graph SLAM end to end Links the older full SLAM course playlist

nodes.s: Full semester recording of the Freiburg Robot Mapping course: EKF-SLAM, sparse extended information filters, FastSLAM, grid-based mapping, least-squares and graph-based SLAM, and front-end/back-end design. Still one of the most-cited free SLAM courses.
nodes.kt: Classic derivations of EKF-SLAM and FastSLAM Graph-SLAM via least squares, robust kernels Slides and Octave exercises on the course page

nodes.n: Robot Mapping - WS 2013/14 course page (slides, exercises)
nodes.s: Course page that accompanies the Robot Mapping lecture videos, with lecture slides and programming exercises (EKF-SLAM, UKF, FastSLAM, least-squares calibration, graph-SLAM) in Octave/Matlab.
nodes.kt: Hands-on exercises missing from the video playlist Good template for a 1-day SLAM crash course

nodes.s: Recorded two-semester photogrammetry course (2015/16 playlist): camera models, direct linear transform, projective geometry, epipolar geometry, bundle adjustment, and image-based 3D reconstruction. The geometric backbone for visual navigation and map-matching against imagery.
nodes.kt: Camera calibration and orientation from first principles Bundle adjustment as used in VIO and visual geolocalization Useful before attempting aerial image-to-map registration

nodes.n: Cyrill Stachniss YouTube channel (incl. '5 Minutes with Cyrill')
nodes.s: Channel hosting Stachniss's full lecture courses plus the '5 Minutes with Cyrill' series of short explainers on single concepts (Kalman filter, factor graphs, ICP, RANSAC, SIFT, occupancy grids).
nodes.kt: Short explainers ideal for onboarding teammates during a hackathon Also hosts newer courses on LiDAR and photogrammetric vision

nodes.s: Graduate course building a monocular visual odometry pipeline step by step: image formation, calibration, feature detection, two-view geometry, P3P+RANSAC, bundle adjustment, KLT tracking, place recognition, visual-inertial fusion and event cameras. Slides and Matlab/Python exercises with solutions are public; recordings go to the UZH platform.
nodes.kt: Exercises culminate in a working mini VO pipeline Covers place recognition and VIO fusion Python templates available alongside Matlab

nodes.n: Visual Odometry: Part I - The First 30 Years and Fundamentals / Part II - Matching, Robustness, Optimization, and Applications
nodes.s: Two-part IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine tutorial (Part II at rpg.ifi.uzh.ch/docs/VO_Part_II_Scaramuzza.pdf). Explains the VO problem formulation, 2D-2D/3D-2D motion estimation, feature matching, outlier rejection and local optimization in a compact, readable form.
nodes.kt: Best single-read primer on VO design choices Part II covers RANSAC and windowed bundle adjustment

nodes.n: MIT 16.485 Visual Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles (VNAV)
nodes.s: MIT graduate course on the math and software of visual navigation: 3D geometry, Lie groups, quadrotor modelling and control, trajectory optimization, feature tracking, two-view geometry, nonlinear optimization, VIO and SLAM. Lecture slides/notes and ROS 2 based lab handouts are public, with lab code on GitHub.
nodes.kt: Labs walk from ROS basics to a quadrotor VIO stack Strong on certifiable/robust estimation Lecture notes downloadable per topic

nodes.s: Award-winning TUM lecture on making quadrotors navigate with cameras: 3D geometry, sensors, state estimation, visual motion estimation, SLAM, dense reconstruction, planning and exploration. Each lecture has slides and a recorded video.
nodes.kt: Compact quadrotor-centric syllabus Bridges control, estimation and visual SLAM

nodes.n: Autonomous Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM edX, AUTONAVx)
nodes.s: MOOC version of the TUM flying-robots lecture with lecture videos and browser-based Python exercises on quadrotor state estimation, Kalman filtering, control and visual navigation.
nodes.kt: Lighter-weight than the full lecture Python exercise format is easy to adapt

nodes.n: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python
nodes.s: Free interactive book as Jupyter notebooks: g-h filters, discrete Bayes, univariate and multivariate Kalman filters, EKF, UKF, particle filters and smoothers, all with runnable code built on the companion FilterPy library.
nodes.kt: Intuition-first, code-first; ideal for teammates new to filtering Notebooks run in Binder or locally FilterPy gives drop-in KF/EKF/UKF classes for prototypes

nodes.s: Free web tutorial deriving the Kalman filter through worked numerical examples (alpha-beta filter, 1D and multidimensional KF, EKF, UKF), written for engineers who want the equations without heavy theory.
nodes.kt: Numeric step-by-step examples you can check by hand Good companion to Labbe for tracking problems

nodes.n: SLAM Handbook: From Localization and Mapping to Spatial Intelligence
nodes.s: Community-written handbook released in three parts (Part 1 November 2024, Part 2 March 2025, Part 3 May 2025), to be published by Cambridge University Press; the free PDF (main.pdf) and LaTeX sources are in the GitHub release repo. Covers factor graphs, Lie groups, robust estimation, certifiable methods, visual/LiDAR/radar/event-based SLAM, and learned spatial representations.
nodes.kt: Most current one-stop reference on SLAM (2025) Chapters on non-visual sensors such as radar Free PDF; GitHub repo tracks newest release Single up-to-date reference spanning classic estimation and learned methods Free chapter PDFs on GitHub

nodes.n: SLAM toolbox for Matlab (EKF-SLAM teaching code)
nodes.s: Solà's Matlab EKF-SLAM toolbox, used as teaching material for his SLAM courses: modular robots, sensors, landmark parameterizations (including inverse-depth points and lines) and graph-SLAM variants. Old but clear code for learning.
nodes.kt: Readable reference implementation of EKF-SLAM Shows landmark parameterization trade-offs

nodes.n: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM: From Theory to Practice
nodes.s: English translation of the popular Chinese visual SLAM textbook, from rigid-body motion and Lie algebra through camera models, nonlinear optimization, feature/direct VO, backend optimization, loop closure and dense mapping, each with C++ examples.
nodes.kt: Code-heavy: every chapter compiles Good bridge from theory to ORB-SLAM-style systems

nodes.n: State Estimation and Localization for Self-Driving Cars (Coursera)
nodes.s: Course 2 of the UofT Self-Driving Cars specialization: least squares, KF/EKF/ES-EKF/UKF, IMU and GNSS sensor models, LiDAR scan matching with ICP, culminating in an error-state EKF that fuses IMU, GNSS and LiDAR on CARLA data.
nodes.kt: Final project is a ready template for GNSS/IMU/LiDAR fusion Explicit error-state EKF derivation Free to audit

nodes.s: Four-course specialization covering vehicle dynamics and control, state estimation and localization, visual perception, and motion planning, using the CARLA simulator for assignments.
nodes.kt: End-to-end autonomy pipeline in one program CARLA-based assignments transfer to hackathon sims

nodes.n: GPS: An Introduction to Satellite Navigation, with an interactive Worldwide Laboratory using Smartphones
nodes.s: Stanford MOOC (originally on Coursera) now freely available as a long video series: how GPS works, pseudoranges, orbits and signals, receiver design, assisted GPS and the future of GNSS, with smartphone-based labs.
nodes.kt: Best intro to pseudoranges and receiver basics Smartphone labs pair with Android raw GNSS measurements

nodes.n: Sensor Fusion and Non-linear Filtering for Automotive Systems (edX)
nodes.s: Self-paced edX course on Bayesian filtering: state-space and motion/measurement models, Kalman filter, EKF/UKF/CKF, and particle filters, with Matlab assignments building a personal filtering toolbox.
nodes.kt: Rigorous but practical nonlinear filtering Pairs with Chalmers' multi-object tracking course

nodes.s: edX course on single- and multi-object tracking: data association, GNN/JPDA/MHT, random finite sets and PMBM filters, with Matlab assignments. Relevant for situational awareness and C-UAS track management.
nodes.kt: Modern RFS/PMBM trackers explained Direct use for radar/EO track fusion

nodes.s: Free classic course by Sebastian Thrun programming robot localization (histogram filter, Kalman filter, particle filter), search/planning, PID control and GraphSLAM in Python. The original Udacity course page now redirects to Udacity's paid AI catalogue; the link points to a 2023 archive copy.
nodes.kt: Gentle, code-along intro to localization filters Particle-filter lesson is a 1-hour hackathon primer

nodes.n: Understanding Sensor Fusion and Tracking (MATLAB Tech Talks)
nodes.s: Short video series on sensor fusion for autonomous systems: what sensor fusion is, IMU/magnetometer orientation estimation, fusing GPS and IMU for pose with an asynchronous EKF, single- and multi-object tracking, and track-level fusion.
nodes.kt: Clear 10-15 minute visual explanations GPS+IMU episode maps directly to a nav-filter build

nodes.s: Annual Stanford SCPNT symposium page (8-9 October 2025) with the agenda and links to recorded student talks (Day 1) and invited speaker talks (Day 2), plus downloadable slides for many presentations.
nodes.kt: Current state of GNSS integrity, resilience and alt-PNT from leading labs Student talks are a good source of fresh project ideas

nodes.n: 2025 PNT Symposium - Day 2 Invited Speaker Presentation Videos
nodes.s: Video album of invited speaker talks from the 2025 Stanford PNT Symposium, featuring speakers such as Brad Parkinson and Jade Morton.
nodes.kt: Primary-source talks on the direction of GPS and resilient PNT

nodes.s: Page for the 28-29 October 2024 symposium with agenda, student and invited-speaker video albums, and slides; topics span GNSS, inertial sensing, timing and alternative navigation.
nodes.kt: Year-over-year view of resilient PNT research Slides downloadable for many talks

nodes.n: SCPNT Photo and Video Gallery (PNT Symposium recordings archive)
nodes.s: Archive index of Stanford PNT Symposium recordings going back to 2007, organised by year into student and invited-speaker albums.
nodes.kt: Deep back-catalogue of GNSS and PNT talks

nodes.s: Pre-conference tutorial programme of ION GNSS+, the main annual GNSS technical meeting: full-day course series taught by field experts (2026: Survey of GNSS Systems, Advanced Algorithms for Navigation, Space and Spacecraft Navigation), with a one-time on-demand recording for registered students.
nodes.kt: Expert-taught deep dives; topics change yearly Paid add-on to conference registration

nodes.n: ION GNSS+ Short Courses - Taught by ION Masters
nodes.s: Masters short course programme at ION GNSS+, complimentary for paid conference attendees: 50-minute lectures by ION Master Instructors. The 2026 line-up includes Space Applications of GNSS (Penny Axelrad), GNSS Modernization (Christopher Hegarty), LEO PNT with mega-constellations (Zak Kassas), quantum navigation (Allison Kealy, Andrew Greentree) and the first public GPS spoofer (Todd Humphreys).
nodes.kt: Short expert lectures on GNSS, LEO PNT, spoofing and quantum navigation for ION GNSS+ attendees

nodes.n: ION Online Tutorial: The Basics of Satellite Navigation
nodes.s: ION recorded online tutorial by Per Enge in four parts: Fundamentals of Satellite Navigation (45 min, viewable after ION sign-in), plus Applications, Mathematics, and Performance & Future of Satellite Navigation ($50 members / $100 non-members each). The tutorial page now redirects to the ION publications store, which sells the three paid parts.
nodes.kt: Short, authoritative intro by Per Enge; only the Fundamentals part is free (sign-in)

nodes.n: ION Webinar Series (archive and YouTube recordings)
nodes.s: Running ION webinar programme with summary pages per talk and a YouTube playlist of past recordings (youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPiP0PPIY2x4k1OemLZH8_OJPyLjGLYFY). Topics include GNSS spoofing and jamming, LEO PNT, signals of opportunity, quantum sensors and GNSS-denied robotics.
nodes.kt: Hour-long talks from active researchers, free Strong coverage of spoofing detection and LEO PNT

nodes.n: First results from three years of GNSS interference monitoring from low Earth orbit
nodes.s: UT Radionavigation Lab results from detecting and geolocating terrestrial GNSS jammers using receivers on LEO satellites, revealing persistent interference hotspots in conflict regions.
nodes.kt: Space-based RFI monitoring is practical Maps of jamming hotspots tied to conflict zones

nodes.s: Presents work on exploiting Starlink downlink signals for opportunistic positioning, including signal structure discovery and Doppler/pseudorange-based navigation results.
nodes.kt: Starlink can serve as an alt-PNT source without operator cooperation

nodes.n: Navigation using carrier Doppler shift from a LEO constellation: TRANSIT on steroids
nodes.s: Analysis of Doppler-only positioning from large LEO constellations, revisiting the TRANSIT concept with modern megaconstellations and quantifying achievable accuracy.
nodes.kt: Doppler positioning theory for LEO PNT

nodes.n: Implementation and Accuracy of Doppler Navigation with LEO Satellites
nodes.s: Talk on navigation with carrier Doppler-shift measurements from LEO satellite signals of opportunity: analytically derived Jacobian formulas for the navigation solution and a GNSS-like dilution-of-precision metric to assess accuracy, with preliminary numerical results. The paper is free in NAVIGATION (ION journal).
nodes.kt: DOP-style accuracy metric for LEO Doppler nav

nodes.n: Detecting GNSS Jamming and Spoofing on Android Devices
nodes.s: Shows how Android raw GNSS measurements (AGC, C/N0, pseudoranges) can flag jamming and spoofing on commodity phones.
nodes.kt: Phones can be cheap distributed interference sensors

nodes.n: Results on GNSS Spoofing Mitigation Using Multiple Receivers
nodes.s: Spoofing detection and mitigation using several spatially separated receivers, exploiting the fact that a single spoofer produces geometrically inconsistent measurements.
nodes.kt: Multi-antenna/multi-receiver consistency checks

nodes.n: GNSS Spoofing Detection through Spatial Processing
nodes.s: Stanford work on detecting spoofing from spatial signal characteristics (angle-of-arrival consistency) using antenna motion or arrays.
nodes.kt: Direction-of-arrival is a strong spoofing discriminator

nodes.n: Robust Interference Mitigation in GNSS Snapshot Receivers
nodes.s: Interference mitigation techniques adapted to snapshot (short-capture) GNSS receivers used in low-power and IoT devices.
nodes.kt: Snapshot receivers need different mitigation than tracking receivers

nodes.n: A Robust Approach to Vision-Based Terrain-Aided Localization
nodes.s: Vision-based terrain-aided localization for aircraft, matching onboard imagery against terrain/map references as a GNSS-independent position source.
nodes.kt: Map-matching as a GNSS-denied position fix

nodes.n: Cooperative Localization for GNSS-Denied Subterranean Navigation: A UAV-UGV Team Approach
nodes.s: West Virginia University work on UAV and UGV teams sharing ranging and odometry to localize jointly in GNSS-denied underground environments.
nodes.kt: Cooperative ranging reduces drift in heterogeneous teams

nodes.n: Relative navigation of fixed-wing aircraft in GPS-denied environments
nodes.s: AFRL perspective on relative navigation for fixed-wing aircraft without GPS, keeping estimation consistent by working in a relative frame with periodic global updates.
nodes.kt: Relative navigation frames tame unobservable global drift

nodes.n: Quantum Sensors for Navigation - From Physics to Field Deployment
nodes.s: Overview of quantum sensing for navigation (atom interferometers, quantum magnetometers, clocks) and what it takes to move them from lab to field.
nodes.kt: Realistic timeline for quantum inertial and magnetic nav

nodes.n: Should It Be TPN? Prioritizing Timing in Positioning and Navigation
nodes.s: Webinar arguing for timing as the foundation of resilient PNT, covering precision terrestrial time distribution and timing/positioning from current and future LEO constellations.
nodes.kt: Timing resilience underpins telecom and power grid LEO as a timing source

nodes.n: LTE Receiver Design and Multipath Analysis for Navigation in Urban Environments
nodes.s: Design of a software receiver that extracts navigation observables from cellular LTE signals and analysis of multipath effects in urban settings.
nodes.kt: Cellular signals of opportunity are viable in cities

nodes.n: Resilience Monitoring for Multi-Filter All-Source Navigation Framework With Assurance
nodes.s: AFIT research on all-source navigation that runs multiple filters and monitors sensor integrity to detect and isolate faulty or spoofed inputs.
nodes.kt: Plug-and-play all-source nav with integrity monitoring

nodes.n: When GNSS fails, what will you do? MarRINav!
nodes.s: UK maritime resilient navigation study (MarRINav) on backups for GNSS at sea, including eLoran and R-Mode style terrestrial systems; co-sponsored by the RNT Foundation.
nodes.kt: Maritime PNT backup architecture options

nodes.s: Accessible TEDx talk from the head of UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab on GPS jamming and spoofing and why civil GPS is trivially counterfeitable, given around the time of his lab's drone and yacht spoofing demonstrations.
nodes.kt: Why unauthenticated civil GNSS is a systemic risk Good opener for a resilient-PNT pitch

nodes.n: UT Austin Radionavigation Laboratory (talks, papers, news)
nodes.s: Lab site of Todd Humphreys' group, indexing talks, briefings and papers on GNSS spoofing detection, LEO interference monitoring, Starlink-based PNT and precise automotive positioning.
nodes.kt: Hub for Humphreys' talks on spoofing and LEO PNT Papers on spoofing detection are linked from here

nodes.n: Ad Astra: Navigation with Megaconstellation LEO Satellites (GRASP on Robotics)
nodes.s: UPenn GRASP seminar by Zak Kassas on opportunistic PNT from Starlink, OneWeb and other LEO megaconstellations, addressing unknown signal structure, poor ephemerides and clock instability with his STAN (simultaneous tracking and navigation) framework validated on ground and aerial vehicles.
nodes.kt: LEO signals of opportunity as a GNSS backup Covers SDR receiver design to navigation filter

nodes.n: Low-cost GPS simulator: GPS spoofing by SDR (DEF CON 23)
nodes.s: DEF CON 23 talk showing that open-source tools and cheap SDRs can generate counterfeit GPS L1 signals that fool phones and a consumer drone; the speakers end with defensive advice such as multi-constellation positioning and spoofing detection in chipsets.
nodes.kt: Shows how low the barrier to civil GPS spoofing is Motivates detection and multi-source fusion in any drone build

nodes.n: Who cares about the Baltic Jammer? Terrestrial Navigation in the Baltic Sea Region (39C3)
nodes.s: 39th Chaos Communication Congress talk from DLR researchers on R-Mode, a terrestrial maritime navigation backup built on existing radio beacons and coastal infrastructure, tested in the heavily jammed Baltic. Covers real-world jamming impacts, transmitter/receiver build-out and the path from research to critical infrastructure.
nodes.kt: Concrete view of Baltic jamming/spoofing effects on ships, aircraft, timing Terrestrial backups as an alternative to space-based ones

nodes.n: Detect GNSS jamming and spoofing (Android developer guide)
nodes.s: Android developer documentation on the platform APIs and signals that apps can use to detect GNSS jamming and spoofing on phones.
nodes.kt: Phone-based interference sensing for a hackathon prototype No custom hardware needed

nodes.n: Results Jammertest 2025 - Resilient GNSS in an Era of Rising Jamming & Spoofing (webinar)
nodes.s: On-demand vendor webinar reviewing receiver behaviour during the high-power interference trials of Jammertest 2025 in Norway, with speakers from Septentrio, the GPS Innovation Alliance and drone maker UVify.
nodes.kt: Field results under interference levels like Baltic/Eastern Europe Vendor view; treat claims accordingly

nodes.n: The Future of Secure Positioning and Timing: Insights from Jammertest 2025
nodes.s: u-blox webinar (25 November 2025) on Jammertest 2025 results: what multi-band receiver testing revealed about positioning continuity under interference, meaconing defence and hybrid spoofing detection with authentication. The page offers the slide deck for download rather than a recording.
nodes.kt: Multi-band receivers and spoofing detection in mass-market chips

nodes.n: Podcast: the vulnerable state of global navigation satellite systems (PolicyTracker Spectrum Podcast)
nodes.s: Spectrum-policy podcast episode with PNT consultant Logan Scott on GNSS jamming, spoofing, adjacent-band interference and mitigations, and the global rise in spoofing incidents affecting aviation.
nodes.kt: Policy and spectrum angle on GNSS interference

nodes.n: What Happens When GPS Goes Dark? (From the Crows' Nest)
nodes.s: Episode of the Association of Old Crows electronic warfare podcast in which RNT Foundation president Dana Goward discusses threats to GPS and the case for terrestrial and other backups.
nodes.kt: EW-community framing of PNT resilience

nodes.n: Dana A. Goward on Geospatial FM podcast (RNT Foundation)
nodes.s: RNT Foundation post linking Dana Goward's Geospatial FM podcast appearance on GPS vulnerability and national PNT resilience policy.
nodes.kt: Advocacy perspective on eLoran and PNT backups

nodes.n: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 3rd edition (with BraveTech EU)
nodes.s: EU defence hackathon (17-19 October 2025, eight locations) with challenges on protecting space assets, space for defence (including navigation and coordination) and sovereign aerospace including drone countermeasures; a recorded pre-hackathon webinar is on YouTube (watch?v=gLrCkk6XEuY).
nodes.kt: Shows how EU frames navigation and C-UAS challenge statements Pre-hackathon webinar recording available

nodes.n: Ukraine's DefTech at the End of 2025: From Drone Mass to Systems Warfare
nodes.s: Analysis of Ukraine's defence-tech ecosystem at the end of 2025, noting that GNSS-denied operation is now the norm and expecting broad adoption of radio-beacon, visual and fused alternative navigation in 2026.
nodes.kt: GNSS denial is a baseline requirement in current conflict Context for prioritising alt-nav in hackathon scope

nodes.s: Nav2 tutorial on outdoor navigation with GPS: fusing GNSS, IMU and odometry with robot_localization's navsat_transform, configuring Nav2 for GPS waypoints, and demonstrating it in Gazebo.
nodes.kt: Shortest working path to GPS waypoint following on a ROS 2 robot Shows datum and frame setup that trips people up

nodes.n: ROSCon UK 2025 - State Estimation for Mobile Robotics Workshop
nodes.s: Hands-on workshop material comparing two ROS 2 state-estimation approaches: Kalman filtering with robot_localization (EKF/UKF, covariance tuning, frames, rate handling) and factor-graph fixed-lag smoothing with fuse. Exercises and solutions are in a public repo.
nodes.kt: Filter vs smoother trade-offs with runnable exercises Directly reusable configs for IMU/odom/GPS fusion

nodes.n: Smoothing Odometry using Robot Localization (Nav2 first-time robot setup guide)
nodes.s: Setup guide for fusing wheel odometry and IMU with robot_localization's EKF to produce the odom frame Nav2 expects.
nodes.kt: Minimal correct EKF config for a new robot

nodes.s: Index of ROSCon talks by Nav2 developers and the community (Vimeo links), including SLAM Toolbox and large-scale indoor mapping talks.
nodes.kt: Curated entry point into ROSCon navigation videos

nodes.s: Documentation for the widely used ROS EKF/UKF state estimation package, including state-estimation node configuration, sensor integration, and navsat_transform for GPS.
nodes.kt: Explains covariance and frame conventions in depth navsat_transform page is essential for GPS fusion

nodes.s: Announcement and index of ROSCon 2023 recordings and slides, including navigation talks such as bidirectional navigation with Nav2 and localization on 3D mesh surfaces.
nodes.kt: One place to find localization/navigation ROSCon talks

nodes.s: ROSCon 2024 site with the programme and links to recorded talks, including localization talks such as Ekumen's Beluga particle-filter localization library.
nodes.kt: Recent ROS 2 localization tooling talks

nodes.s: Annual PX4 developer conference; recordings are posted on the PX4 YouTube channel. The 2025 Atlanta programme included an EKF2 session on handling multiple data sources with 'reset by fusion' rather than hard resets.
nodes.kt: Primary source on EKF2 design changes Talks on external vision/non-GNSS aiding in PX4

nodes.s: Official channel with PX4 Developer Summit recordings, dev calls and feature demos.
nodes.kt: Search 'EKF2' for estimator deep dives

nodes.s: How to run PX4 software-in-the-loop with Gazebo and other simulators, including multi-vehicle setups and connecting ROS 2 and ground stations.
nodes.kt: Fastest way to test nav changes without hardware Start here for PX4 SITL Covers Gazebo, Gazebo Classic, SIH and community sims

nodes.s: Official Gazebo (gz) docs and tutorials: building worlds, sensors (IMU, GPS/NavSat, cameras, LiDAR), ROS 2 bridging and plugins.
nodes.kt: NavSat and IMU sensors enable GNSS-denied scenario testing

nodes.s: Docs and quickstarts for NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated stereo visual-inertial odometry and SLAM package for ROS 2 on Jetson, including tutorials with Isaac Sim and RealSense cameras.
nodes.kt: Real-time VIO on Jetson with minimal setup Isaac Sim tutorials for testing without hardware

nodes.s: Documentation for the OpenVINS MSCKF-based visual-inertial estimator, including derivations of the propagation and update steps, calibration, evaluation tooling and ROS usage.
nodes.kt: Doubles as a VIO textbook with derivations Evaluation tools for comparing trajectories

nodes.s: Wiki for Kalibr covering multi-camera, camera-IMU and rolling-shutter calibration, target generation and data collection practice.
nodes.kt: Bad calibration ruins VIO; this is the standard workflow

nodes.s: Tutorials for the open-source GNSS-SDR software receiver: GNSS open-service signals, running with a low-cost RTL2832U DVB-T dongle as front end, monitoring the receiver's internal status, build-time options, cross-compiling for embedded platforms, data types and the testing framework. Acquisition, tracking and PVT blocks are documented in the site's Signal Processing Blocks section.
nodes.kt: Learn receiver internals with real IQ data Base for interference-detection experiments

nodes.s: Yearly SLAM benchmark challenge with datasets and leaderboards from 2021 to 2026. The 2026 edition provides 360-degree camera and IMU sequences captured on active construction sites with floor-plan priors, scored in SLAM and floor-plan Localization categories; the live evaluation system stays open after the challenge. Datasets are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial).
nodes.kt: Hard GNSS-denied indoor sequences with accurate ground truth Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0): fine for a hackathon demo, not for a product Sensors: lidar, cameras, IMU GNSS-denied indoor Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, non-commercial 2026 edition is the Hilti x Trimble challenge with 360 camera, IMU and floor plan priors

nodes.s: Benchmark and workshop series for 6-DoF visual localization under changing conditions (day/night, seasons), with standard datasets and an evaluation server.
nodes.kt: Standard evaluation for map-based visual relocalization

nodes.n: Image Matching: Local Features & Beyond (CVPR workshop)
nodes.s: Recurring CVPR workshop and Kaggle challenge on feature matching and structure-from-motion, with invited talks and recordings, covering the matchers used in visual geolocalization and VIO.
nodes.kt: State of the art in learned matchers (SuperPoint/LightGlue family)

nodes.n: From Sea to Space: Advancing Perception in Harsh Domains (ICRA 2026 workshop)
nodes.s: ICRA 2026 (Vienna) workshop on perception for underwater, space and terrestrial field robots, including localization and mapping in degraded sensing, GPS-denied global localization, novel sensors (sonar, radar, thermal, event) and edge-efficient perception.
nodes.kt: Cross-domain view of degraded-sensing localization Speaker list points to active groups

nodes.n: ERF26 workshop: Innovation and developments in robotic GNSS-denied localisation for inspection & maintenance
nodes.s: European Robotics Forum 2026 workshop (Stavanger) organised by SINTEF on GNSS-denied robot localisation in indoor, offshore, underground and urban-canyon settings, bringing together researchers, vendors and end users.
nodes.kt: Industry-side view of deployable GNSS-denied localisation

nodes.s: Official Nav2 documentation: concepts, configuration guides for every planner/controller/costmap plugin, tuning guide and tutorials including GPS-based navigation.
nodes.kt: Tuning guide explains planner/controller trade-offs Tutorials cover writing custom plugins and outdoor GPS waypoints

nodes.s: Curated index of ROSCon talks by the Nav2 team and community from 2018 onward, covering features such as Smac planners and the MPPI controller plus tuning and deployment advice.
nodes.kt: Single entry point for Nav2 conference talks Talks on MPPI and Smac planners explain design rationale

nodes.s: Paper introducing Nav2: behavior-tree based navigation architecture for ROS 2, its design choices and a long-duration campus deployment test.
nodes.kt: Explains why Nav2 uses behavior trees and lifecycle nodes Describes long-running real-world validation

nodes.n: From the Desks of ROS Maintainers: A Survey of Modern & Capable Mobile Robotics Algorithms in the Robot Operating System 2
nodes.s: Survey by ROS maintainers of the mobile robotics algorithms available in ROS 2: localization, SLAM, planning, control and perception packages, with their maturity and use.
nodes.kt: Map of which ROS 2 packages are production-ready Good orientation before choosing a localization or planning stack

nodes.n: The Open Motion Planning Library (OMPL) website
nodes.s: Official OMPL documentation with planner catalogue, tutorials, Python binding guide and benchmarking tools.
nodes.kt: Tutorials show how to define state spaces and validity checkers Built-in benchmarking compares planners on your problem

nodes.n: EGO-Planner: An ESDF-free Gradient-based Local Planner for Quadrotors
nodes.s: Introduces a local planner that avoids building a full Euclidean signed distance field, computing collision penalties only from obstacles the trajectory intersects, cutting onboard compute.
nodes.kt: ESDF-free collision cost reduces mapping overhead Fits small onboard computers for agile flight

nodes.n: Robust and Efficient Quadrotor Trajectory Generation for Fast Autonomous Flight
nodes.s: Fast-Planner paper: kinodynamic path search front-end plus B-spline optimization and time adjustment for fast quadrotor flight in unknown environments.
nodes.kt: Front-end/back-end split is the template many later planners follow

nodes.n: Aerostack2: A Software Framework for Developing Multi-robot Aerial Systems
nodes.s: Describes the Aerostack2 ROS 2 architecture for aerial robotics: platform abstraction, behaviors, mission specification and multi-robot support.
nodes.kt: Platform abstraction lets the same mission run on several autopilots and simulators

nodes.n: PlanSys2: A Planning System Framework for ROS2
nodes.s: Presents PlanSys2, a PDDL planning and execution framework for ROS 2 that compiles plans into behavior trees and supports multi-robot execution.
nodes.kt: Shows how symbolic task planning connects to Nav2 actions

nodes.n: Fields2Cover: An open-source coverage path planning library for unmanned agricultural vehicles
nodes.s: Paper behind the Fields2Cover library: modular coverage pipeline (headlands, swaths, route ordering, path smoothing) and benchmark of its components.
nodes.kt: Coverage planning decomposes cleanly into swath generation, ordering and turning

nodes.s: MITRE guide describing Cursor-on-Target: the base Event schema (what, where, when), its mandatory fields, sub-schema extensions and the message router used to distribute CoT.

nodes.n: Developer's Guide to Cursor on Target
nodes.s: Introductory developer guide to CoT's objectives, message structure, implementation patterns and limitations.
nodes.kt: Explains the what/where/when design philosophy Good primer before writing a CoT producer

nodes.s: Community-compiled list of CoT type strings with mappings to other message formats, useful when choosing the 'type' attribute for tracks.
nodes.kt: Pick correct atom/friend/hostile type codes for your tracks

nodes.s: US DoD standard defining military symbology (frames, icons, modifiers and the symbol identification code) for C2 displays. Revision E (2022) is current and sold through standards resellers; 2525D was published openly on jcs.mil.
nodes.kt: SIDC structure drives symbol rendering in milsymbol Know which revision your consumers expect (2525C vs D/E codes differ)

nodes.s: Official TAK portal for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK/TAK Server downloads, plugin SDKs and documentation; most materials require free registration.
nodes.kt: Register early - SDK and server downloads are behind an account

nodes.s: Installation and configuration docs for OpenTAKServer, including client enrollment, certificates and integrations.
nodes.kt: Step-by-step install on Ubuntu or Raspberry Pi

nodes.s: Docs and examples for PyTAK: configuration, transports (TCP/UDP/TLS/multicast) and writing CoT producers.
nodes.kt: Example scripts are a minimal template for pushing positions to TAK

nodes.n: The 1090 Megahertz Riddle: A Guide to Decoding Mode S and ADS-B Signals
nodes.s: Open book explaining Mode S and ADS-B message structure, position decoding (CPR), Comm-B registers and Mode S surveillance, with pyModeS examples.
nodes.kt: CPR position decoding explained step by step Covers enhanced surveillance fields beyond basic ADS-B

nodes.s: EUROCONTROL home of the ASTERIX surveillance data exchange format, with category specifications for radar, ADS-B, MLAT and system tracks.
nodes.kt: Categories (e.g. 048 radar, 021 ADS-B, 062 system tracks) define the binary layouts

nodes.s: Specification and ecosystem site for STAC, the common way to describe and search geospatial imagery and DEM assets.
nodes.kt: Public STAC APIs give key-free access to Sentinel-2 and Copernicus DEM

nodes.n: Copernicus DEM on AWS Open Data
nodes.s: Registry entry for the Copernicus global DEM (GLO-30/GLO-90) hosted as cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs on AWS, freely accessible without an account.
nodes.kt: Global 30 m DEM as COGs - sample directly with rasterio Good default terrain for terrain-referenced nav and planning

nodes.s: Documentation and background on geodesics, map projections, geoid and gravity models implemented in GeographicLib, plus online calculators.
nodes.kt: Geoid undulation matters when comparing GNSS ellipsoid heights to DEM heights

nodes.n: Pohang Canal Dataset: A Multimodal Maritime Dataset for Autonomous Navigation in Restricted Waters
nodes.s: Multimodal maritime dataset from a 7.5 km route through a narrow canal, port areas and near-coast waters, with LiDARs, marine radar, stereo, infrared and omnidirectional cameras, AHRS and RTK GPS. Also on the AWS Open Data registry.
nodes.kt: Includes marine radar and LiDAR together - good for radar odometry at sea RTK ground truth and SLAM baseline trajectory included CC BY-NC 4.0 - non-commercial use only

nodes.n: PoLaRIS Dataset: A Maritime Object Detection and Tracking Dataset in Pohang Canal
nodes.s: Inha University dataset that adds object detection and tracking labels to five Pohang Canal sequences, with annotations on RGB, thermal, LiDAR and radar data for objects as small as 10x10 pixels. No separate licence stated; the underlying Pohang Canal data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial).
nodes.kt: Adds object labels to the Pohang Canal setting Multi-modal labels for camera, thermal, LiDAR and radar detection on USVs Inherits the non-commercial terms of the Pohang Canal data

nodes.s: Paper describing a labelled LWIR maritime dataset of 2,916 images from in and around Boston Harbor, segmented into seven classes, with UNet, PSPNet and DeepLabv3 baselines. Data is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).
nodes.kt: Thermal segmentation for USV situational awareness Semantic and instance masks provided Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

nodes.n: LaRS: A Diverse Panoptic Maritime Obstacle Detection Dataset and Benchmark
nodes.s: ICCV 2023 panoptic obstacle detection benchmark from lakes, rivers and seas: over 4,000 per-pixel labelled key frames, each with nine preceding frames (40k+ frames), 11 classes and an online evaluation server. CC BY-NC 4.0, research use only, download behind a registration form.
nodes.kt: Most diverse maritime obstacle set by location and conditions Online server for objective scoring Baselines for 27 segmentation methods Non-commercial, research-only terms; no redistribution

nodes.n: SubPipe: A Submarine Pipeline Inspection Dataset for Segmentation and Visual-inertial Localization
nodes.s: Describes an AUV dataset from a real pipeline inspection mission (OceanScan LAUV) with two cameras, side-scan sonar and navigation data, with SLAM, RGB segmentation and sonar object detection baselines. Data on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 with a required copyright notice.
nodes.kt: Open underwater visual SLAM benchmark with pose ground truth from navigation sensors Side-scan sonar object detection labels (COCO and YOLO); segmentation labels are on RGB

nodes.n: Caltech Aerial RGB-Thermal Dataset in the Wild
nodes.s: Aerial RGB-thermal dataset over natural US terrain with synchronized GPS and IMU, with benchmarks for thermal segmentation, RGB-to-thermal translation and VIO.
nodes.kt: Thermal aerial data is expensive to collect - this fills a gap Includes VIO benchmark with GPS/IMU Dataset is for non-commercial use only (README: CC BY-SA 4.0 terms)

nodes.n: Cardinal RF (CardRF): An Outdoor UAV/UAS/Drone RF Signals with Bluetooth and WiFi Signals Dataset
nodes.s: Outdoor RF dataset of drone controller and telemetry signals plus Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, stored as .mat files, covering line-of-sight and beyond-line-of-sight conditions.
nodes.kt: Many controllers from several manufacturers in 2.4 GHz Includes Wi-Fi/Bluetooth confusers Large download (tens of GB); MATLAB loader provided

nodes.n: DroneDetect Dataset: A Radio Frequency dataset of Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) Signals for Machine Learning Detection & Classification
nodes.s: RF recordings of seven drones (six DJI models and the Parrot Disco) captured with a BladeRF SDR in GNU Radio, split by interference (clean, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, both) and flight mode (on, hovering, flying). CC BY licence, free IEEE login needed.
nodes.kt: Interference-labelled RF data for robust classifiers Python loader splits recordings into short samples Do not confuse with an unrelated image dataset of the same name

nodes.n: DIAT-uSAT: micro-Doppler Signature Dataset of Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (SUAV)
nodes.s: 4,849 micro-Doppler signature images from an X-band (10 GHz) continuous-wave radar of small UAV-like targets: RC plane, two rotor types, quadcopter, bionic bird and mini-helicopter plus bionic bird.
nodes.kt: Radar micro-Doppler classification of drones vs birds Access via e-mail request for education use

nodes.n: DroneRFb-Spectra: A RF spectrogram dataset for drone recognition
nodes.s: 14,460 spectrograms (512x512, from 50 ms USRP IQ captures over three ISM bands in urban settings) of drone controllers from 7 brands, tied to an IEEE TIFS 2024 open-set drone recognition paper. CC BY licence.
nodes.kt: Ready-made spectrograms - no SDR processing needed Covers 7 brands: DJI, Vbar, FrSky, Futaba, Taranis, RadioLink, Skydroid Open-set recognition angle for unknown drones

nodes.s: Kaggle drone RF classification dataset: 1.2 ms IQ vectors from 6 consumer drone remotes plus a noise class, mixed with lab noise or Gaussian noise across SNR -20 to 30 dB. CC BY 4.0.
nodes.kt: SNR labels allow robustness curves PyTorch tensor format

nodes.s: 20 ms raw IQ snapshots (E1 and E6 bands, 62.5 MHz) from a sensor on a bridge over a German highway, labelled into 8 interference and 3 non-interference classes, in .npy format with train/test and few-shot splits.
nodes.kt: Real-world interference recorded at a highway Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) Companion dataset 2 has fewer classes (2 interference, 1 non-interference)

nodes.s: Open raw IQ recordings (GPS L1 C/A and Galileo E1, LabSat 3 Wideband) from Jammertest 2023 in Norway covering a high-power jamming case, incoherent spoofing and coherent spoofing scenarios, under CC BY 4.0.
nodes.kt: Real spoofing IQ data under open licence Usable with FGI-GSRx software receiver

nodes.n: Raw IQ dataset for GNSS GPS jamming signal classification
nodes.s: Raw IQ dataset of GNSS jamming signal types (DME, narrowband, single AM, single chirp, single FM, no jamming) with 1000 training and 250 test samples, generated with a MATLAB script built on the Morales Ferre et al. 2019 jammer-classification data. CC BY 4.0.
nodes.kt: Common benchmark for jamming-type classifiers Converted to spectrogram images in follow-up work Signals are generated in MATLAB, not live over-the-air captures

nodes.n: GNSS L1 Jammed Signal 10MHz Recording - Triangular Wave (Part 1)
nodes.s: One of a series of February 2025 Zenodo records from LINKS Foundation with GNSS L1 IQ recordings at 10 and 20 MHz sample rates under several jamming waveforms (triangular, tick, linear narrow, linear wide fast) at stepped jamming powers. CC BY 4.0; Horizon Europe grant 101073909.
nodes.kt: More recent real IQ jamming captures Each file is about 10 GB of int8 complex samples

nodes.n: UAV Acoustic Localization Dataset: 24-Channel Beamformed Recordings of a DJI Air 3 Drone with Synchronized GPS Flight Logs
nodes.s: 24-channel acoustic recordings (48 kHz, four synced Zoom F6 recorders) of a DJI Air 3 drone with synchronized GPS flight logs at 100 ms, including no-drone ambient segments, under CC BY-SA 4.0.
nodes.kt: Ground-truth positions enable acoustic localization, not just detection Multi-recorder synchronized array

nodes.n: UaVirBASE: A Public-Access Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Sound Source Localization Dataset
nodes.s: Public dataset of synchronized multi-microphone UAV recordings under controlled distance, altitude, azimuth and orientation variations, for acoustic source localization.
nodes.kt: Controlled geometry for DOA algorithm testing

nodes.n: Improving Small Drone Detection Through Multi-Scale Processing and Data Augmentation
nodes.s: Entry to the 8th WOSDETC Drone-vs-Bird challenge at IJCNN 2025 using multi-scale YOLOv11 inference and copy-paste augmentation for tiny drones.
nodes.kt: Multi-scale tiling is key for tiny targets Copy-paste augmentation helps with scarce drone pixels v1 abstract says top-3; v2 (Nov 2025) says first place

nodes.n: Kilometer-Scale GNSS-Denied UAV Navigation via Heightmap Gradients: A Winning System from the SPRIN-D Challenge

nodes.kt: Heightmap gradients avoid needing reliable absolute (barometric) height Clustered particle filter handles multimodal position Runs on CPU in real time No public code found

nodes.s: German innovation agency challenge for long-range autonomous flight without GNSS; Fly4Future (CTU spin-off) won, with Beyond Vision and KopterKraft on the podium; a 2.0 edition followed.
nodes.kt: Real GNSS-denied long-range task specification Winners published method details

nodes.n: ACM MM 2024 Multi-weather Drone Satellite Matching Challenge (UAVM 2024)

nodes.s: Workshop and challenge site for the 4th UAVs in Multimedia workshop at ACM MM 2026. The challenge (29 Mar - 30 Jun 2026, on Codabench) uses the PairUAV dataset for last-meter relative pose alignment; workshop on 14 Nov 2026.

nodes.n: Last-Meter Precision Navigation for UAVs: A Diffusion-Refined Aerial Visual Servoing Approach

nodes.kt: Relative pose refinement complements global geo-localization

nodes.n: PiLoT: Neural Pixel-to-3D Registration for UAV-based Ego and Target Geo-localization
nodes.s: Registers live UAV frames against geo-referenced 3D maps to recover 6-DoF ego pose and geo-locate observed points.
nodes.kt: Map-based absolute pose for GNSS-denied flight 3DGS backends released

nodes.n: Game4Loc: A UAV Geo-Localization Benchmark from Game Data
nodes.s: Builds a large synthetic drone-satellite dataset from a video game with partial-match pairs and trains weighted contrastive geo-localization.
nodes.kt: Synthetic data transfers to real benchmarks Partial-match pairs are more realistic than perfect crops

nodes.n: A Transformer-Based Feature Segmentation and Region Alignment Method For UAV-View Geo-Localization
nodes.s: Transformer method that segments and aligns regions between drone and satellite views.
nodes.kt: Widely used University-1652 baseline

nodes.n: GNSS/GPS Spoofing and Jamming Identification Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
nodes.s: Study applying ML and DL to spoofing detection and to jamming-type classification from spectrogram images of public IQ data.
nodes.kt: Spectrogram + CNN reaches 98.93% jamming-type accuracy (ResNet18, transfer learning) on the simulated Swinney-Woods raw IQ dataset (CC BY 4.0) Code in Colab notebooks

nodes.n: Analyzing and Characterizing Multi-Source Interference Effects at Jammertest Norway 2025
nodes.s: Fraunhofer IIS dataset from Jammertest 2025 (Andøya) with a single-antenna E1/E5 receiver and a 2x2 CRPA array, benchmarking 17 ML models for interference type, bandwidth and power, plus YOLOv8s / RF-DETR detection of multiple simultaneous interferers in spectrograms.
nodes.kt: Near-99% within-area classification but large drops across test areas => domain shift is the real problem Dataset is open on Zenodo (record 21332689) under CC BY-SA 4.0

nodes.n: Trends and Challenges in Next-Generation GNSS Interference Management

nodes.kt: Good map of the field and its datasets

nodes.n: Data-Driven Analysis of PNT Resilience: Insights and Lessons from Jammertest 2024 Vehicular Data

nodes.kt: Shows how consumer and automotive stacks degrade under jamming/spoofing Data is on GitHub (UniVaasaDigiEco/VAARA) with no licence file => all rights reserved by default; ask before reuse

nodes.n: On Your Own: Pro-level Autonomous Drone Racing in Uninstrumented Arenas

nodes.n: Martin Saska - Onboard relative localization for agile aerial swarming in the wild (RSS 2024 Aerial Swarms workshop slides)

nodes.kt: Sensors: camera, IMU, GPS Use for aerial-to-street-view localization

nodes.s: Handheld lidar plus stereo and multi-camera sequences around New College, Oxford, with precise ground truth from a survey-grade prior map. Now hosted on Hugging Face.
nodes.kt: Sensors: lidar, stereo, multi-camera, IMUs Size class: large Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial academic use

nodes.kt: Sensors (simulated): stereo, depth, segmentation, flow, lidar (no IMU in v1) Size class: very large Licence: CC BY 4.0

nodes.s: Multi-robot, multi-modal SLAM data in degraded environments - caves, tunnels, urban and off-road - with RGB, lidar, thermal and inertial sensing; used in ICCV SLAM challenges.
nodes.kt: Sensors: RGB, lidar, thermal, IMU Domains: subterranean, off-road Size class: large No licence stated on the dataset page

nodes.s: Repeated drives of the same Oxford route over a year in all weather, with cameras, lidar and GPS/INS.
nodes.kt: Sensors: cameras, lidar, GPS/INS Size class: very large License: non-commercial per site

nodes.s: RobotCar route re-driven with a scanning FMCW radar plus lidars and cameras, for radar odometry and localization.

nodes.s: Urban driving in dense city areas with lidar, stereo and navigation sensors where GNSS is degraded.
nodes.kt: Sensors: lidars, stereo, GNSS, IMU, wheel encoders Size class: large Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial only; download links by request

nodes.s: Driving data from Hong Kong and California urban canyons with a full sensor suite, targeted at GNSS outliers and degraded localization.
nodes.kt: Sensors: lidar, cameras, GNSS, IMU Focus: dense urban GNSS failure Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial academic use

nodes.s: Segway robot sessions over many months on one campus with lidar, omnidirectional camera, GPS, IMU and odometry.

nodes.s: Multi-campus sequences in Asia and Europe across seasons with two lidar types, stereo, IMUs, UWB and survey-grade prior maps.
nodes.kt: Sensors: lidar, stereo, IMU, UWB Ground truth: continuous-time with prior maps Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial academic use

nodes.s: Hardware-synchronized event stereo, regular stereo, RGB-D, lidar and IMU across different motion and lighting, with 6-DoF ground truth.
nodes.kt: Sensors: event stereo, stereo, RGB-D, lidar, IMU

nodes.s: Stereo event and frame cameras plus lidar and RTK GNSS on a car, including night and challenging illumination.
nodes.kt: Sensors: stereo event, stereo RGB, lidar, RTK GNSS Good for low-light perception

nodes.s: Stereo event cameras with IMU, lidar and ground truth on several platforms including a hexacopter and a car.
nodes.kt: Sensors: stereo event, IMU, lidar, GPS Platforms: drone, car, motorcycle, handheld

nodes.n: MARS-LVIG Dataset: A multi-sensor aerial robots SLAM dataset for LiDAR-visual-inertial-GNSS fusion
nodes.s: Aerial robot SLAM dataset for lidar-visual-inertial-GNSS fusion, including sequences with raw GNSS measurements under different lighting.
nodes.kt: Sensors: lidar, camera, IMU, GNSS (incl. raw) Domain: aerial over large outdoor areas Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, academic use only

nodes.s: Developer docs for running ArduPilot vehicles in SITL, connecting GCS and external simulators.
nodes.kt: sim_vehicle.py workflow Lists supported external simulators

nodes.s: Install guide, sensor reference (sonar, DVL, IMU, depth) and examples for the HoloOcean underwater simulator.
nodes.kt: Covers sonar and DVL sensor configs Multi-agent and acoustic comms examples

nodes.s: Docs for AirSim covering setup, APIs, sensor configuration and PX4/ArduPilot integration.
nodes.kt: Sensor settings via settings.json Notes on the project's end of active development

nodes.n: Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization And Mapping: Towards the Robust-Perception Age
nodes.s: Landmark survey that frames modern SLAM as factor-graph MAP estimation and discusses robustness, scalability, representations and open problems.
nodes.kt: Standard framing of front end vs back end Robustness to outliers and long-term operation remain the hard problems

nodes.s: Compact review of visual-inertial navigation: filtering vs optimization, observability, calibration and representative systems.
nodes.kt: Explains why MSCKF-style filters and sliding-window optimizers coexist Observability and consistency drive estimator design

nodes.n: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM
nodes.s: Describes ORB-SLAM3's tightly integrated visual-inertial SLAM, MAP-based IMU initialization and the multi-map Atlas that recovers from tracking loss.
nodes.kt: Multi-map atlas lets the system restart and later merge maps Supports pinhole and fisheye models

nodes.n: VINS-Mono: A Robust and Versatile Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimator
nodes.s: Presents the VINS-Mono estimator: IMU preintegration, robust initialization, tightly coupled sliding-window optimization, relocalization and global pose graph.
nodes.kt: Monocular camera + IMU recovers metric scale Initialization is a key practical component

nodes.s: Introduces direct registration of raw LiDAR points in an iterated Kalman filter with an incremental k-d tree map, avoiding hand-crafted feature extraction.
nodes.kt: Raw-point registration generalizes across LiDAR types ikd-Tree enables efficient incremental mapping

nodes.n: LIO-SAM: Tightly-coupled Lidar Inertial Odometry via Smoothing and Mapping
nodes.s: Formulates LiDAR-inertial odometry as factor-graph smoothing with IMU preintegration, LiDAR odometry, GPS and loop-closure factors.
nodes.kt: Factor graphs make it straightforward to add or drop GNSS Keyframe-local scan matching keeps it real time

nodes.n: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP -- Simple, Accurate, and Robust Registration If Done the Right Way
nodes.s: Argues that a carefully engineered point-to-point ICP with motion compensation and adaptive thresholds matches far more complex LiDAR odometry across platforms.
nodes.kt: Few parameters, works across sensors and platforms Strong baseline before reaching for complex pipelines

nodes.s: Presents an error-state iterated Kalman filter that sequentially fuses LiDAR and image measurements against a shared voxel map, with exposure and plane-prior handling.
nodes.kt: Sequential updates handle LiDAR/camera dimension mismatch Robust when one modality degrades

nodes.n: DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
nodes.s: Learned SLAM that iteratively refines poses and depth through a differentiable dense bundle adjustment layer.
nodes.kt: Big robustness gains on hard sequences GPU-heavy

nodes.n: MASt3R-SLAM: Real-Time Dense SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors
nodes.s: Builds a real-time dense monocular SLAM system on the MASt3R two-view reconstruction prior, without assuming a fixed parametric camera model.
nodes.kt: 3D foundation models can serve as SLAM front ends Works with uncalibrated video

nodes.n: Kimera: an Open-Source Library for Real-Time Metric-Semantic Localization and Mapping
nodes.s: Describes the Kimera stack: VIO, robust pose-graph optimization, mesh reconstruction and semantic mapping in one open library.
nodes.kt: Metric-semantic maps on CPU in real time Modular: VIO, RPGO, mesher, semantics

nodes.n: Kimera-Multi: Robust, Distributed, Dense Metric-Semantic SLAM for Multi-Robot Systems
nodes.s: Distributed multi-robot SLAM where robots exchange compact information peer to peer and jointly optimize with outlier-robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
nodes.kt: Peer-to-peer, no central server Robust to bad inter-robot loop closures

nodes.s: Comprehensive survey of event cameras: sensing principle, algorithms (feature tracking, optical flow, VO/SLAM) and applications.
nodes.kt: Microsecond latency and high dynamic range Algorithms must be redesigned for asynchronous data

nodes.n: How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM: a Survey
nodes.s: Survey of SLAM methods that use neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian splatting as the map representation, organized by sensor and technique.
nodes.kt: Radiance-field maps trade compute for photorealism Most methods are GPU-bound and not yet embedded-ready

nodes.s: Monocular and RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps directly against 3D Gaussians using analytic Jacobians for camera pose optimization.
nodes.kt: Single representation for tracking, mapping and rendering

nodes.n: LiDAR Odometry Survey: Recent Advancements and Remaining Challenges
nodes.s: Survey of LiDAR-only, LiDAR-inertial and multi-sensor LiDAR odometry, with discussion of datasets, evaluation and open challenges such as degeneracy.
nodes.kt: Taxonomy of LiDAR, LiDAR-inertial and LiDAR-plus-other fusion Geometric degeneracy (tunnels, open fields) is a key open issue

nodes.n: 4D Millimeter-Wave Radar in Autonomous Driving: A Survey
nodes.s: Survey of 4D imaging radar: signal processing, datasets, calibration, perception and SLAM/odometry uses.
nodes.kt: 4D radar adds elevation and works in adverse weather Sparse, noisy point clouds need radar-specific methods

nodes.n: CFEAR Radarodometry - Conservative Filtering for Efficient and Accurate Radar Odometry
nodes.s: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that keeps the strongest returns per azimuth, builds oriented surface points and registers against a keyframe history (IROS 2021).
nodes.kt: Simple filtering beats heavier radar pipelines Runs fast on a single CPU thread per the authors

nodes.n: Edge-based Monocular Thermal-Inertial Odometry in Visually Degraded Environments
nodes.s: Thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal image edges instead of corner features, targeting darkness and smoke where visible cameras fail.
nodes.kt: Thermal edges are more stable than corners in low-contrast IR Relevant for night and obscurant operations

nodes.n: Time Guidance for Network Operators, Chief Information Officers, and Chief Information Security Officers
nodes.s: CISA guidance on making enterprise time resilient and secure: know where time comes from, use several independent sources, detect anomalies in timing sources, and test. The 2022 update added network considerations from a tabletop pilot plus self-assessment questions and a test plan.
nodes.kt: Inventory every time dependency and its upstream source Use multiple, diverse time sources and compare them Detect and handle anomalies in time sources; test the response

nodes.n: Technical-Level Resilient Timing Overview (CISA fact sheet)
nodes.s: Short fact sheet that frames time as an invisible utility, lists sectors that depend on it, and summarizes technical measures for resilient timing.
