nodes.kt: Many organizations do not know where their time comes from Short entry point before the longer CISA time guidance

nodes.n: Best Practices for Improved Robustness of Time and Frequency Sources in Fixed Locations
nodes.s: Best-practice guide for people who install and maintain time and frequency sources at fixed infrastructure sites, where GPS receivers are the usual source of time and time interval.
nodes.kt: Written for fixed sites that take time from GPS receivers Covers installation and operating practice rather than protocol design

nodes.n: Best Practices for Resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Supporting Critical Infrastructure
nodes.s: DHS S&T guide released in February 2025 under EO 13905 to help providers, owners and operators use PNT responsibly. It gives general best practices with GPS/GNSS examples and use cases including stationary timing and moving platforms, applied through risk assessment.
nodes.kt: Includes a stationary-timing use case Risk-based: assess, then choose resilience measures

nodes.n: Handbook of Frequency Stability Analysis (NIST SP 1065)
nodes.s: NIST tutorial and reference on characterizing clocks and oscillators: Allan, modified Allan, Hadamard and time deviation, power-law noise types, drift removal and confidence intervals.
nodes.kt: Identify the noise type from the ADEV slope before extrapolating Remove drift separately; ADEV alone does not show aging TDEV is the time-domain statistic for time error over an interval

nodes.s: Handbook chapter introducing accuracy vs stability, quartz, rubidium and cesium standards, and time and frequency transfer by radio and satellite signals.
nodes.kt: Accuracy and stability are different properties Overview of oscillator families and time-transfer signals

nodes.n: The Use of GPS Disciplined Oscillators as Primary Frequency Standards for Calibration and Metrology Laboratories
nodes.s: Explains how GPSDOs work, why they are attractive as self-calibrating references, and where they fall short of a cesium standard, including behaviour when the GPS signal is lost.
nodes.kt: A GPSDO is only as good as its local oscillator once GNSS is gone Discusses traceability and verification of GPSDO outputs

nodes.n: Introduction to Quartz Frequency Standards - Oscillator Comparison and Selection
nodes.s: Section of Vig's introduction to quartz frequency standards comparing TCXO, MCXO, OCXO, rubidium, RbXO and cesium on accuracy, aging, temperature stability, short-term stability, size, warm-up, power and price (table 1). Hosted on a mirror; the original is an Army technical report.
nodes.kt: One table with aging/year, temperature stability and ADEV at 1 s per oscillator class OCXO beats rubidium at 1 s; rubidium wins on aging Used as the parameter source for samples/timing-holdover

nodes.n: Microchip SA65 Chip Scale Atomic Clock datasheet (DS00003478F)
nodes.s: Datasheet for the SA65 CSAC: ADEV 3e-10 at 1 s, typical aging below 9e-10 per month, +/-3e-10 frequency change over -40 to +80 C, under 120 mW, with 1PPS input for discipline to GNSS. Third-party mirror of the 9/25 revision.
nodes.kt: Low power atomic holdover for portable and battery systems 1PPS input to discipline it from a GNSS receiver

nodes.n: RFC 5905: Network Time Protocol Version 4: Protocol and Algorithms Specification
nodes.s: The NTPv4 specification: on-wire protocol, clock filter, selection and clustering algorithms, and the clock discipline loop.
nodes.kt: Selection and clustering reject falsetickers when several servers are used The discipline algorithm is a hybrid phase/frequency loop

nodes.n: RFC 8915: Network Time Security for the Network Time Protocol
nodes.s: Specifies NTS: a TLS-based key exchange followed by authenticated NTP packets, protecting clients from on-path spoofing of time responses.
nodes.kt: Authenticates the server; does not stop delay attacks Supported by chrony, ntpd-rs and NTPsec

nodes.n: RFC 7384: Security Requirements of Time Protocols in Packet Switched Networks
nodes.s: Threat model and security requirements for NTP and PTP: packet manipulation, spoofing, replay, rogue master, delay attacks, cryptographic attacks and DoS.
nodes.kt: Delay attacks cannot be stopped by cryptography alone Useful checklist for a timing threat model slide

nodes.n: RFC 9523: A Secure Selection and Filtering Mechanism for the Network Time Protocol with Khronos
nodes.s: Informational RFC describing Khronos: an NTP client watchdog that samples many servers and uses trimming to bound how far a man-in-the-middle controlling some of them can shift time.
nodes.kt: Sample many servers, trim outliers, bound the shift Grew out of the Chronos NDSS 2018 work

nodes.s: IETF draft specifying Roughtime: signed coarse time responses that let clients chain queries across servers and prove misbehaviour.
nodes.kt: Coarse but cryptographically accountable time Good boot-time sanity bound for GNSS time

nodes.n: IEEE 1588-2019: IEEE Standard for a Precision Clock Synchronization Protocol for Networked Measurement and Control Systems
nodes.s: The PTP standard (version 2.1), approved November 2019 and published June 2020. Defines ordinary, boundary and transparent clocks, profiles and an optional security mechanism.
nodes.kt: PTP accuracy depends on hardware timestamping and symmetric paths The 2019 edition adds optional security mechanisms

nodes.n: ITU-T G.8271: Time and phase synchronization aspects of telecommunication networks
nodes.s: Telecom recommendation that sets time and phase synchronization requirements and network limits for packet networks (2020 base text with a 2024 amendment).
nodes.kt: Source of the telecom time-error budgets that PRTC/T-BC specs feed into

nodes.n: ITU-T G.8272: Timing characteristics of primary reference time clocks
nodes.s: Defines the primary reference time clock (PRTC), the GNSS-fed time source at the top of a telecom timing chain, and its output limits.
nodes.kt: PRTC = the 'grandmaster from GNSS' in telecom vocabulary

nodes.n: ITU-T G.8272.1: Timing characteristics of enhanced primary reference time clocks
nodes.s: Defines the enhanced PRTC: GNSS plus an autonomous primary reference (in practice cesium or equivalent) to hold time through long GNSS outages. Secondary summaries describe about 30 ns to UTC when locked and around 100 ns over multi-week holdover; read the Recommendation for normative values.
nodes.kt: Holdover is specified as a bound over days, not seconds The 2024 edition adds parametric holdover

nodes.s: Vendor one-page summary of the ePRTC: within 30 ns of UTC when locked to GNSS and within 100 ns of UTC for up to 40 days in holdover, depending on the locked period.
nodes.kt: Quick numbers for a pitch; check against the ITU text

nodes.n: How Precision Time Protocol is being deployed at Meta
nodes.s: Meta's PTP architecture: Time Appliance racks, unicast PTP through transparent clocks, and clients that report a window of uncertainty instead of a single time. When an appliance enters holdover its uncertainty grows with oscillator stability and clients are steered away by clock class.
nodes.kt: Publish an uncertainty bound with time, not just time Holdover is signalled to clients through clockClass

nodes.n: Open-sourcing a more precise time appliance
nodes.s: Introduces the Time Card (GNSS receiver, miniature atomic clock, FPGA time engine on PCIe) and the OCP Time Appliance Project. States a holdover target of within 1 microsecond over 24 hours and reports a 24-hour test with PPS drift within 300 ns.
nodes.kt: Atomic holdover target: 1 us per 24 h Time Card driver is in Linux 5.15+

nodes.s: Project page for White Rabbit, the CERN-led extension of PTP and synchronous Ethernet that distributes sub-nanosecond time over fibre; links to specs, hardware and users.
nodes.kt: Sub-ns time distribution inside a facility without GNSS at each node Open hardware and HDL on the Open Hardware Repository

nodes.s: NDSS 2016 paper showing on-path time shifting of NTP clients, an off-path single-packet denial of service against NTP synchronization, and related attacks that exploit unauthenticated NTP.
nodes.kt: Unauthenticated NTP can be shifted by an on-path attacker Some attacks work off-path

nodes.s: NDSS 2018 paper proposing Chronos, an NTP client that queries many servers and discards outliers to bound time-shifting by a man in the middle; basis of the later Khronos RFC.
nodes.kt: Many servers plus trimming bounds an attacker's shift

nodes.n: Evaluation of the vulnerability of phasor measurement units to GPS spoofing attacks
nodes.s: International Journal of Critical Infrastructure Protection paper that spoofed the GPS timing receivers of power-grid phasor measurement units and showed their timestamps could be shifted.
nodes.kt: Classic demonstration of GNSS time-push spoofing on infrastructure

nodes.n: Global GPS time anomaly on Tue, Jan 26th (2016)
nodes.s: Vendor note on the January 2016 event in which GPS receivers worldwide, including all of Meinberg's own, showed time jumps of about 13 microseconds; later analyses traced it to faulty UTC correction parameters uploaded to some satellites.
nodes.kt: A non-adversarial GNSS time fault hit many receivers at once Argues for holdover and cross-checks even without an attacker

nodes.n: GPS Experiences UTC Timing, IIF Satellite Launcher Problems
nodes.s: News report on the January 2016 GPS UTC timing error of about 13 microseconds, attributed by the US Air Force to an erroneous ground software upload during the retirement of SVN 23.
nodes.kt: Navigation was fine; only time was wrong

nodes.s: PTB's page on the DCF77 77.5 kHz longwave time signal: transmitter, time code and how legal time is disseminated in Germany.
nodes.kt: Terrestrial time source independent of GNSS over much of Europe

nodes.s: NIST page for WWVB, the 60 kHz time signal from Fort Collins, Colorado, with its time code formats including the phase-modulated code.
nodes.kt: US terrestrial time signal; phase modulation improves reception

nodes.s: NIST's authenticated NTP service for registered users, using symmetric keys so clients can verify that time came from NIST.
nodes.kt: An authenticated public reference for cross-checking GNSS time

nodes.s: Feature table comparing chrony, ntpd, NTPsec, OpenNTPD and others on NTS, hardware timestamping, reference clocks and other features.
nodes.kt: Fast way to pick an NTP daemon for a build

nodes.n: LeapSecond.com (Tom Van Baak time and frequency pages)
nodes.s: Long-running personal site with measurements of oscillators, GPSDOs and atomic clocks, Allan deviation tutorials and experiments.
nodes.kt: Real ADEV plots of hobby and surplus oscillators Practical measurement setups

nodes.n: Хакатон: трек «Робототехника и сенсорика», кейс «Полёт вслепую»
nodes.s: English: 'Hackathon: Robotics and sensing track, case Blind flight'. Problem-statement page of the 48-hour hackathon held 26-28 June 2026 in Krasnodar. A commercial operator of light unmanned and optionally piloted aircraft delivering cargo to taiga, Arctic and mountain sites asks teams to build a prototype that determines coordinates, speed and heading from onboard data when GNSS degrades (high latitudes, narrow sky in gorges, jamming/spoofing near industrial zones, storms). The page itself does not name the sensors; public team repos show the case data were a radar-altimeter log (NMEA-0183 or TXT), a constant 1500 m MSL altitude and a DEM (Copernicus GLO-30 / GeoTIFF).
nodes.kt: Civil framing: cargo delivery to remote areas, GNSS loss from geometry, latitude and interference Input data (radar altimeter + DEM) are documented in team READMEs, not on the page Prize fund listed as 250k/150k/100k RUB; scoring criteria not published At least six public solution repos exist; compare them before designing a TERCOM entry

nodes.n: Cистема визуально-инерциальной навигации для дрона на C++
nodes.s: English: 'A visual-inertial navigation system for a drone in C++'. Walks through a monocular VIO built with OpenCV and Eigen: per-camera intrinsic calibration, ORB detection with Lucas-Kanade tracking at 30 Hz (SIFT judged too slow on a Raspberry Pi), parallax-based keyframes, essential-matrix initialisation then PnP, IMU preintegration, QR least-squares for scale and gravity with sanity bounds, and a 15-state ESKF. Includes a demo GIF; no quantitative accuracy is reported.
nodes.kt: Track with optical flow, detect with ORB: descriptor matching every frame is too slow on small boards Accept scale/gravity solutions only inside physical bounds (gravity near 9.81) ESKF states: position, velocity, attitude error, accel and gyro biases Code: RusaUB/mvio

nodes.s: English: 'NextVision HackLab 2026: Detect. Track. Win.' Flyer for a student hackathon on drone detection held 22-24 April 2026 at NURE in Kharkiv. Teams of three build prototypes that detect and track small, fast objects including UAVs using optical, thermal, acoustic, radar or hybrid sensing, with requirements on range, day/night and all-weather operation, and trajectory tracking. Judged on accuracy with few false alarms, noise and interference robustness, novelty and practical value.
nodes.kt: Defensive C-UAS detection and tracking, not interception Explicit criteria: low false-alarm rate and robustness to noise Deliverable can be a working prototype or a conceptual model with simulation or video Useful template for scoping a 48h C-UAS detection entry

nodes.n: Аналіз методів автономної навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу
nodes.s: English: 'Analysis of autonomous UAV navigation methods in GPS-denied environments' (Technical Engineering, No. 1(95), 2025). Survey comparing optical flow, visual odometry, visual SLAM, IMU, lidar SLAM, radar SLAM, RF (Wi-Fi/UWB/BLE) and multi-sensor fusion on accuracy, latency, compute and power, with a summary table and a power-draw chart for small UAVs. Concludes no single method fits all conditions and names gaps: no unified test methodology, power cost, lack of realistic datasets and integration into flight controllers.
nodes.kt: Rule-of-thumb drift figures per method (e.g. optical flow ~5% of distance, VO ~2%, VSLAM <1% with loop closure) are the authors' rough comparisons, not measurements Recommends optical flow for small drones' stabilisation, fusion with SLAM for long missions, radar for bad weather, UWB/visual indoors Flags the dataset gap for degraded and emergency conditions Funded under Horizon Europe WIDE AcrossEU

nodes.n: Способи навігації БПЛА у складних умовах зовнішнього середовища
nodes.s: English: 'UAV navigation methods in complex environmental conditions' (Mechanics of Gyroscopic Systems, No. 49, 2025). Reviews GNSS/IMU integration, lidar navigation, geomagnetic navigation and computer-vision methods (SLAM, visual odometry) for GPS-denied flight, listing each one's weaknesses: jamming and spoofing, lidar processing load, magnetometer calibration, and visual dependence on light and texture. Concludes that a condition-specific multi-sensor combination is needed.
nodes.kt: KPI gyroscopic-systems department perspective: inertial core plus aiding sources Geomagnetic navigation is included alongside vision and lidar No single technology is universal; pick sensors per operating conditions

nodes.n: Програмна реалізація алгоритмів навігації БПЛА із використанням систем обробки телеметрії
nodes.s: English: 'Software implementation of UAV navigation algorithms using telemetry processing systems'. Master's thesis that fuses GPS, IMU, barometer and optical-camera telemetry with an EKF, a complementary filter and ML-based correction, then tests three scenarios: EKF vs IMU-only, GPS+IMU+barometer fusion, and map-matching with trajectory correction under simulated GPS jamming. Implemented in Python with NumPy, OpenCV and Matplotlib.
nodes.kt: Includes a simulated-jamming experiment measuring recovery after GPS loss Compares EKF and complementary filter on the same telemetry Student work; results are self-reported

nodes.n: Анализ проблемных направлений автономной навигации беспилотных летательных аппаратов
nodes.s: English: 'Analysis of problem areas in autonomous UAV navigation' (MLSD-2025 conference, ICS RAS). Reviews GNSS jamming and spoofing threats to small UAVs and three families of countermeasures: neural matching of camera imagery to a geo-referenced map or terrain model, lidar or stereo SLAM combined with neural models, and other options such as radar methods and RSSI trilateration from relay UAVs. Notes the common practical stack of ArduPilot or INAV plus a companion computer and lists observed problems, such as the volume of map tiles to store onboard and the cost and weight of 3D lidars.
nodes.kt: Map-tile storage on board is a real constraint for VPS Relay-UAV RSSI trilateration is mentioned as an emerging option Author affiliation is a Russian defence test centre; content is navigation-only

nodes.n: Разработка метода навигации беспилотных летательных аппаратов по изображению подстилающей поверхности в условиях отсутствия сигналов внешних навигационных систем
nodes.s: English: 'A method for UAV navigation by images of the underlying surface without external navigation signals'. Short ITMO young-scientists congress abstract (file dated January 2025): keypoint detection, FLANN matching and a transformation matrix against a reference map of the underlying surface give the UAV's local position. Tested only in Gazebo, where coordinates were fed to the flight controller and the authors report accuracy to about 2 m.
nodes.kt: Classic keypoints + FLANN + homography, not deep features Simulation-only result (Gazebo), about 2 m self-reported Reviews image-matching families: correlation-extremal, keypoints, neural

nodes.n: Беспилотники научили видеть дорогу без GPS и ГЛОНАСС: «умную» навигацию создали в МФТИ
nodes.s: English: 'Drones taught to see the road without GPS and GLONASS: MIPT built smart navigation'. News on 'Фасетка' from MIPT's robotics R&D centre (NTI Foundation support): it matches temporally stable landmarks (roads, buildings, river channels, power-line pylons) to an onboard satellite map, using thermal and radar imagery for seasonal robustness, and tolerates camera tilt up to 45 degrees thanks to training on synthesised viewpoints. Claims about 6 m accuracy at 1000 m altitude in helicopter and drone tests.
nodes.kt: Pick landmarks that change little over time Off-nadir tolerance (45 degrees) via synthetic-view training is the stated novelty Accuracy is a press claim, no paper cited

nodes.n: Разработана система автономной визуальной навигации роя дронов
nodes.s: English: 'A system for autonomous visual navigation of a drone swarm has been developed' (press release, 25 April 2025). SPC RAS describes a software prototype that navigates a UAV swarm from camera data under jamming or without satellite navigation, needing only ordinary satellite imagery (no height maps or geophysical fields) and no hardware beyond a video camera. Quotes postgraduate K. Konovalov.
nodes.kt: Same author line as the NSTU route-planning-over-landmarks paper Claims plain satellite imagery suffices as the reference Press release; no accuracy data

nodes.n: Систему для полёта дронов в «серой» зоне без GPS создали в России
nodes.s: English: 'A system for drone flight in the grey zone without GPS was created in Russia'. Kazan engineers, funded through the NTI Foundation, describe an adaptive wireless mesh of ground base stations and onboard modules in several frequency bands that provides positioning and control without GNSS. Claimed: up to 10 m positioning accuracy and 10-15 km range in open terrain; field trials with four base stations and two UAVs planned for end of 2026.
nodes.kt: Terrestrial radio positioning plus comms in one mesh Numbers are announced targets; trials not yet done at publication Positioning algorithm not described

nodes.n: «Очікую прориву в українській ракетній програмі». Прогнози українського deftech на 2026
nodes.s: English: 'Ukrainian deftech forecasts for 2026'. Industry round-up (25 Dec 2025). Navigation-relevant views: Vyriy expects mass adoption of GPS-free navigation based on radio beacons; Athlon Avia's CTO names the lack of a compact, reliable optical system that fully replaces GNSS as the year's main disappointment; Swarmer says visual SLAM, visual navigation and optic flow fused with inertial sensors passed field tests and that GPS-denied is now a baseline condition. EW vendors discuss CRPA-equipped threats and mesh-networked drones.
nodes.kt: Practitioners report optical navigation as still not a full GNSS replacement Beacon navigation expected to scale in 2026 Operators value stable links and predictable behaviour under EW over range Strike-related forecasts in the article are out of scope here

nodes.n: В Україні створили модернізовану версію РЕБ Lima для придушення новітніх CRPA-антен - командир «Нічної варти»
nodes.s: English: 'Ukraine built an upgraded Lima EW system to suppress the newest CRPA antennas'. Interview-based news (July 2026) on a counter-drone EW system: the original Lima layered navigation-antenna suppression, GNSS spoofing and anti-spoofing bypass; the Quant version is claimed to defeat multi-element CRPAs regardless of element count by exploiting that a CRPA cannot locate the source of a high-energy signal. All claims come from the unit commander; no test data.
nodes.kt: Defensive counter-UAS view of the CRPA race: element count alone is not a guarantee Claims are unverified interview statements Context for why receivers need spoofing and jamming detection, not just null steering

nodes.s: English: 'Ukrainian KORT developed a new 8-channel CRPA antenna'. September 2026 news on Orion 8, an adaptive 8-channel CRPA that KORT integrates with Septentrio GNSS receivers and tests on its own fixed-wing drones supplied to Ukraine's Defence Forces, against various jamming types; shown at MSPO in Poland.
nodes.kt: Domestic Ukrainian CRPA paired with a commercial high-end receiver In final testing at publication, no performance figures Continues the CRPA lab and element-count thread from round 1

nodes.n: 28 із 37 деталей - зі США: ГУР МО розкрило склад іноземних компонентів у російських «Кометах»
nodes.s: English: '28 of 37 parts from the US: HUR disclosed foreign components in Russian Kometa modules'. Teardown-level description of the Kometa CRPA: a patch-element array plus a processing module built around an Altera Cyclone FPGA; 16-element versions widely fielded, 20-element in preparation, and 32-element arrays documented on downed drones. Lists the origin of 37 foreign components.
nodes.kt: CRPA = antenna array + FPGA beamforming; spatial rejection grows with element count Gives a concrete architecture for anyone modelling anti-jam receivers No RF front-end or channel specs disclosed

nodes.n: Що це за українська система Sky Map яку поспіхом ставлять американці на своїх базах, щоб захиститись від «Шахедів»
nodes.s: English: 'What is the Ukrainian Sky Map system that Americans are rushing to install at their bases against Shaheds'. April 2026 article on Sky Fortress's command-and-control layer that fuses air-target data from radars and a network of more than 14,000 low-cost acoustic sensors (direction finding and triangulation) into one picture on tablets for mobile fire groups and interceptor operators. Reports, citing Reuters, US deployment in the Middle East.
nodes.kt: Low-cost distributed acoustic sensing + fusion is a proven C-UAS situational-awareness pattern Per-sensor cost quoted at roughly 400-1000 USD Tracking algorithms are not described

nodes.n: Автономний БпЛА без GPS та GNSS з візуальною навігаційною системою
nodes.s: English: 'Autonomous UAV without GPS and GNSS with a visual navigation system'. Short Warchangers interview (Dec 2024) with the AI4UAV developers: a visual navigation system positioned as a GPS/GNSS alternative that works day and night, with or without maps. Chapters cover the idea, development problems, pilot training time, Brave1 support and optimisation plans. Summary from the video description.
nodes.kt: Ukrainian VPS vendor perspective, Brave1-backed Claims map-free and map-based modes; no figures in the description Good for problem framing, not technical depth

nodes.s: English: 'Introduction to visual odometry'. Department seminar covering the main VO problem classes and methods, results on public test datasets, and the main limitations of VO. Summary from the video description.
nodes.kt: Russian-language entry point to VO concepts Covers limitations explicitly, useful before choosing VO vs VPS

nodes.s: English: 'Aerial photography without GNSS!?' Talk at the XVII 'Geodesy. Mine surveying. Aerial survey. Navigation' conference (13 Feb 2026) on doing UAV aerial survey when GNSS is unavailable. Only the title and venue are confirmed from the description; technical content not verified.
nodes.kt: Survey-industry angle: georeferencing imagery when GNSS is denied Description gives no method details; watch before citing

nodes.n: Как работать без ГНСС?! Системы лазерного сканирования
nodes.s: English: 'How to work without GNSS?! Laser scanning systems'. Talk at the XV 'Geodesy. Mine surveying. Aerial survey. Navigation' conference (15 Feb 2024) on lidar scanning workflows without GNSS. Summary from title and description only.
nodes.kt: Lidar/SLAM scanning as a GNSS-free mapping workflow in the survey industry Content not verified beyond the description

nodes.s: English: 'Drones: autonomous unmanned aerial systems'. Free self-paced Russian online course built on Geoscan competition experience: drone basics, simple programming including indoor and outdoor navigation systems, companion-computer interaction (Python, Raspberry Pi, autopilot protocol, mapping), computer vision with marker recognition and vision-based navigation, and swarm control with ROS. Lesson videos (e.g. ultrasonic local navigation, vision system) were published on YouTube in Dec 2022.
nodes.kt: Beginner path from flight basics to vision-based navigation and swarms Uses the Geoscan Pioneer ecosystem Free, including certificate

nodes.s: English: 'Development of UAV navigation algorithms'. Diploma defence slides from Belarusian State University: goal is to use the drone camera for positioning without GPS; compares SIFT, SURF and ORB, reviews SLAM and SfM 3D terrain mapping, and demonstrates SLAM + ROS + webcam + SfM localisation on a 3D map.
nodes.kt: Student-level overview of feature choice and SLAM/SfM for GPS-free localisation Slides only

nodes.n: Аналіз ефективності використання візуальної одометрії для навігації мобільної платформи у невизначеному середовищі
nodes.s: English: 'Analysis of the effectiveness of visual odometry for mobile platform navigation in an uncertain environment'. Short NURE conference paper weighing wheel odometry, laser/ultrasonic odometry, GNSS, INS and visual odometry for robot localisation in industrial interiors, arguing VO gives reliable localisation from the camera stream alone.
nodes.kt: Ground-robot framing; complements the UAV papers Brief; conceptual rather than experimental

nodes.s: English: 'MTF02 optical flow sensor'. August 2025 Habr review of the MicoAir MTF02 module, which combines an optical flow camera with a ToF rangefinder and talks MAVLink to ArduPilot and PX4, for position hold and motion sensing without GPS.
nodes.kt: Cheap off-the-shelf flow + range module for GNSS-free hover Integrates as a MAVLink sensor in ArduPilot/PX4

nodes.s: English: 'In search of autonomous flight' (15 Dec 2025). Practitioner comparison of GNSS, ultrasonic indoor positioning (Geoscan Pioneer 'Locus' as example) and optical flow plus laser rangefinder for agricultural, warehouse and indoor drones. The author picks optical flow + rangefinder on ArduPilot, mentions Holybro H-Flow and MTF-01 modules, and reports an OpenMV camera + TFMini Plus build that held autonomous hover up to 10 m.
nodes.kt: Optical flow + rangefinder judged the most universal low-cost option Ultrasonic systems are sensitive to beacon calibration (1 cm offsets matter) Civil use cases only

nodes.n: Локализовать нельзя ошибиться. Как работает локализация в автономном транспорте и почему это - самая сложная задача. 2/2
nodes.s: English: 'How localization works in autonomous transport and why it is the hardest task, part 2/2' (June 2026). Evocargo, a Russian autonomous-truck company, walks through GNSS/RTK, cameras against HD maps, lidar scan-to-map matching, IMU (bias growth example), wheel odometry and auxiliary RF sources, fused with Kalman or particle filters plus integrity monitoring and spoofing detection. Lists failure modes such as snow, featureless yards, tunnels and truck jammers near toll sites, and argues localization cannot be bought off the shelf.
nodes.kt: Localization is interpretation of conflicting data, not measurement Truck-mounted jammers near toll sites are a real ground GNSS threat Autoware, Apollo and robot_localization need heavy adaptation

nodes.n: Как фильтровать GPS-треки от ложных точек: спуфинг, заморозка координат, подмена времени
nodes.s: English: 'How to filter GPS tracks for false points: spoofing, frozen coordinates, time spoofing' (July 2026). A fleet-telematics backend developer's rule set: a reachability envelope instead of a fixed speed cutoff, altitude-gradient checks against a terrain database, teleport-segment boundaries, frozen-series detection, a longest-non-decreasing-odometer filter against timestamp spoofing, GPS-path vs odometer ratio with hysteresis, and cell-tower fallback. Trust order: CAN, then cell, then GPS.
nodes.kt: Use an independent odometer to expose spoofed GPS (honest path/odometer ratio ~1.6-1.8x, a spoofed track hit 3.3x) Judge frozen coordinates as series, not points Store raw, filter at read time, regression-test on clean days

nodes.n: Как джамминг и спуфинг GPS мешают мирному населению
nodes.s: English: 'How GPS jamming and spoofing affect civilians' (August 2024). Explainer opening with a regional GPS interference map and covering why weak GNSS signals are easy to jam and spoof, and the spill-over onto aviation and everyday users.
nodes.kt: Civil-impact framing with interference-map examples Background reading, not technical depth

nodes.n: Формування вирішальної функції кореляційно-екстремальних систем навігації за критерієм максимуму узагальненого коефіцієнта взаємної кореляції
nodes.s: English: 'Forming the decision function of correlation-extremal navigation systems by the maximum generalised cross-correlation criterion' (Bulletin of NTU KhPI, No. 50, 2016). Studies how viewing geometry, mainly perspective distortion, degrades the decision function when onboard images are matched to stored references, and proposes adapting the references: per resolution element take the peak cross-correlation and combine into a generalised correlation function. Keywords cite UAVs.
nodes.kt: 'Correlation-extremal navigation' (КЕНС) is the Soviet/Ukrainian term for map-matching navigation Perspective distortion dominates the geometric error in image matching Background theory for TERCOM/scene-matching style entries

nodes.n: An analysis of approaches to determining the type of reference image for correlation-extreme aircraft navigation systems
nodes.s: Ukrainian journal paper (Data Recording, Storage and Processing, IPRI NAS of Ukraine, 2025) on how to form reference images for correlation-extremal aircraft navigation. Argues that selective images of the Earth's surface are possible, and often preferable, as references instead of direct sighting images. Metadata from the NAS harvester record; full text not read.
nodes.kt: Reference-map design matters as much as the matcher Selective (feature-reduced) references proposed over raw imagery Same research line as the 2016 generalised CENS model by these authors

nodes.n: В Україні представили візуальний навігаційний модуль OSCAR, що забезпечує стійкість дронів до РЕБ
nodes.s: English: 'Ukraine unveils the OSCAR visual navigation module that makes drones resilient to EW'. Twist Robotics' OSCAR (Optical System of Coordinates with Automatic Relocalization) recognises terrain landmarks in camera frames, matches them to a map, computes coordinates and passes them to the autopilot. Vendor claims: up to 20 m accuracy, day and night, over 500,000 km flown in 24 months, development aided by an in-house combat simulator ('Obrii').
nodes.kt: Map-matching visual positioning is fielded as an autopilot position source, not as a research demo Vendor accuracy claim is ~20 m, which sets a realistic bar for hackathon VPS demos Simulation of combat conditions is part of the development loop Interfaces, weight and supported autopilots are not stated

nodes.n: Компанія, що постачає CRPA-антени для російських дронів, показала нову 32-елементну модель
nodes.s: English: 'Company supplying CRPA antennas for Russian drones shows a new 32-element model'. Explains CRPA (controlled reception pattern antenna) as a multi-element array with digital beamforming that nulls interference directions while keeping satellite signals, and lists vendor specs of a 32-element Harxon unit shown at DWC2026 (up to 31 simultaneous interferers, under 6.5 kg, up to 90 W).
nodes.kt: CRPA element count is escalating (4 => 16 => 24 => 32) as an arms race against jamming An N-element array can null up to N-1 interference sources Size, weight and power of high-element CRPAs limit them to larger airframes Explains why broadband jamming alone is losing effectiveness against long-range UAVs

nodes.n: Brave1 запускає лабораторію для тестування CRPA-антен
nodes.s: English: 'Brave1 launches a lab for testing CRPA antennas'. Ukraine's defense-tech cluster opened a lab with EW equipment where domestic developers can test anti-jam GNSS antenna prototypes against jamming and get feedback before fielding. Test procedures are not described.
nodes.kt: Ukraine treats anti-jam GNSS antennas as a domestic product category with a dedicated test facility Testing against real EW emitters is the gate before field use Shows the government-cluster model (Brave1) for EW-resilience hardware

nodes.n: «Інколи від РЕБ очікують більше, ніж вона може». Як радіоелектронна боротьба працює проти FPV і «Шахедів»
nodes.s: English: 'Sometimes more is expected from EW than it can deliver. How electronic warfare works against FPVs and Shaheds'. Explainer for engineers on defensive EW: control uplink, video downlink and GNSS as separate attack surfaces, why radio reconnaissance must precede jamming, why spoofing is weaker against drones with CRPA antennas and position-jump filters, and why fiber-optic and vision-autonomous drones bypass RF EW.
nodes.kt: Detection/RF reconnaissance comes before any effective jamming; protocols and frequencies shift often Plausibility filters on position jumps plus CRPA blunt GNSS spoofing Fiber-optic and onboard-vision drones remove the RF link entirely, so layered defense (EW + interceptors + fire) is the field answer Friendly-fire on own drones is a real cost of EW

nodes.n: Як модернізуються «Шахеди» і чи є там штучний інтелект. Розбір DOU
nodes.s: English: 'How Shaheds are being upgraded and whether there is AI inside. DOU breakdown'. Threat-side view of a long-range one-way UAV's navigation stack, useful for defenders: satellite navigation plus INS on pre-planned routes, 16-element CRPA antennas for jam/spoof resistance, and cellular modems used as trackers rather than as a navigation link.
nodes.kt: Upgraded long-range UAVs combine GNSS, INS and CRPA, which reduces the value of GNSS jamming as a defense Cellular modems are telemetry/tracking aids, not navigation Defensive conclusion in the article: interceptors outperform EW against these threats

nodes.n: «Ми почали будувати захищену екосистему для всіх військових застосунків». Архітектор DELTA - про розвиток системи
nodes.s: English: 'We started building a secure ecosystem for all military applications. DELTA's architect on the system's development'. Interview on Ukraine's DELTA situational-awareness system: a shared core fed by aerial recon, satellites, drones and radars; a map as one view; a synchronization matrix linking drone missions to map objects; streaming, chat with zone alerts, mobile app, AI video detection; security built on NIST 800-53 and FIDO2.
nodes.kt: SA systems in Ukraine evolved from a single map into a product ecosystem on a common data core Contrasted with the NATO model of separate systems joined by custom integration Security baseline cited: NIST 800-53 and FIDO2 phishing-resistant auth Offline/edge operation is not discussed

nodes.n: Шукають РЕБ/РЕР рішення для боротьби з ворожими дронами. Деталі про Jammer Hackathon
nodes.s: English: 'EW/ELINT solutions against enemy drones wanted: Jammer Hackathon details'. Problem statement of the Brave1 + D3 Jammer Hackathon (29 Nov - 1 Dec 2024, $100k pool). Tracks: disrupting commercial-class drones via their control protocols, and automatic drone detection and tracking.
nodes.kt: Counter-UAS detection and tracking was an explicit hackathon track Organisers named concrete commercial reference drones, so problem statements are platform-specific Shows the typical Brave1 hackathon format: short sprint, jury pitch, follow-on funding

nodes.n: Завершився Jammer Hackathon, де шукали РЕБ/РЕР рішення для фронту. Які проєкти перемогли
nodes.s: English: 'Jammer Hackathon is over: which EW/ELINT projects won'. Results page: winners include a reactive EW system, an FPV video-signal detector, and a radio-monitoring / direction-finding decision-support system (SPRMT); prizes $20k/$10k/$7k with a further $50k for one-month progress.
nodes.kt: Winning themes cluster around detection, direction finding and decision support, not only jamming Short one-line descriptions only; no technical depth published Follow-on prize for progress after a month is part of the format

nodes.n: У 17 років створив навігацію для дронів, яку не глушить РЕБ. Історія киянина, який переміг на «Олімпіаді геніїв» у США
nodes.s: English: 'Built EW-proof drone navigation at 17: the story of a Kyiv student who won the Genius Olympiad in the USA'. Describes an urban GNSS-free concept: an IMU dead-reckons, side-looking rangefinders measure distances to buildings at roughly 7th-floor height, and the ranges are matched to OpenStreetMap building geometry about once per second. Simulation in C#/MonoGame; hardware tests on a Betaflight FPV were at bench stage.
nodes.kt: Rangefinder-to-building matching against OSM is a cheap urban alternative to camera VPS Correction at ~1 Hz bounds IMU drift Status at publication: simulation plus bench tests, not flight-proven

nodes.n: Vyriy створила маякову навігацію для дронів, яка працює без GPS і зв’язку
nodes.s: English: 'Vyriy built beacon navigation for drones that works without GPS or a data link'. Ground radio beacons placed along a route in advance; an onboard board ranges to several beacons by delay or signal strength and trilaterates, like a local terrestrial GNSS. Frequencies, range and accuracy are not disclosed.
nodes.kt: Local terrestrial ranging beacons are a fielded GNSS substitute in Ukraine Works without any link to the operator once the route is confirmed No performance numbers published

nodes.n: Троє 20-річних хлопців за 24 години створили дрон, якому не потрібен GPS
nodes.s: English: 'Three 20-year-olds built a drone that needs no GPS in 24 hours'. Ukrainian retelling (citing Defense One) of a US hackathon-born build motivated by Ukrainian front-line feedback: downward camera frames matched to stored imagery, ~256 GB of compressed map tiles covering 10,000+ sq km on an SD card, under $500 of hardware.
nodes.kt: Hackathon-scale VPS is feasible with commodity compute and pre-loaded tiles Map storage and preloading time are the practical bottlenecks Body text says several days of work, not 24 hours; open problems are altitude and speed envelope

nodes.n: 12 переможців і призовий фонд у 120 000 доларів: результати Хакатону «Наступ машин»
nodes.s: English: '12 winners and a $120,000 prize pool: results of the Onslaught of Machines hackathon'. Official MoD results page: 2,000+ applications, 450 participants, 12 winners at $10k each. Winning-idea areas include advanced navigation systems, resilient communications, real-time recon data transfer, coordination of unmanned systems and network integration of heterogeneous unmanned systems.
nodes.kt: Navigation and resilient comms were named winning areas at a state-run drone hackathon Judging criteria: deployment readiness, scalability, timeline Winners are not named on the page

nodes.n: European Defense Tech Hackathon: Як стартапи в Мюнхені вирішують проблеми оборони України
nodes.s: English: 'European Defense Tech Hackathon: how startups in Munich tackle Ukraine's defense problems'. Report from the Feb 2025 Munich edition (48 h, 200+ participants). Tracks included machine vision for counter-drone use, autonomous underwater navigation and improved radio reconnaissance. Brave1's stated expectation: integrable components, not finished systems.
nodes.kt: Hackathon outputs are valued as quickly integrable components Underwater navigation appeared as a track Teams, networks and investor access are the main realistic outcomes of 48 h

nodes.n: Боротьба за координати. Глобальні навігаційні системи та їх значення у сучасних військових конфліктах
nodes.s: English: 'The fight for coordinates. GNSS and its role in modern military conflicts'. Pre-invasion (Jan 2022) Ukrainian overview of GNSS dependence, documented Russian interference during exercises in the Nordics/Baltics and Crimea, and responses: multi-constellation receivers, modernised GPS signals, quantum navigation research.
nodes.kt: Baseline for how the GNSS-interference picture looked just before 2022 Multi-constellation use is the first-line civilian mitigation Good intro context for non-specialists

nodes.s: English: 'Drone optical navigation algorithm'. Master's defense slides (Kyiv-Mohyla Academy): a GeoTIFF map is cut into field-of-view tiles with precomputed keypoints; each drone frame is matched (ORB vs SuperPoint+SuperGlue) against tiles near the current estimate, a homography gives position, and fallback strategies handle lost or repeating fixes. Reported on 930 tiles: SuperPoint+SuperGlue reached the goal in fewer steps with more matches but ~631 s run time vs ~26 s for ORB; goal reached in 30/30 runs.
nodes.kt: Tile pre-indexing plus local search around the last fix is the practical VPS structure Learned matchers win on match count but cost ~25x run time in this setup Explicit fallback behaviours (repeat detection, default heading) matter as much as the matcher Motivation cites both EW and fiber-optic range limits

nodes.n: Метод навігації БПЛА в умовах відсутності GPS-сигналу на основі візуальної одометрії
nodes.s: English: 'UAV navigation method in GPS-denied conditions based on visual odometry'. Short Ukrainian conference paper: ORB features, a modified RANSAC and Kalman refinement for frame-to-frame VO, targeting +/-5 m and 10 Hz. Authors report 4.8 m position error (33% better than their baseline) and 42 ms per frame on a 10,000-frame closed-loop flight set.
nodes.kt: Sets a concrete target spec (+/-5 m, +/-2 deg, >=10 Hz) typical of Ukrainian academic work Classic ORB + RANSAC + KF pipeline, not learned features Results are the authors'; dataset not published

nodes.n: Інтелектуальна кіберфізична система для навігації БПЛА в умовах дії засобів РЕБ противника
nodes.s: English: 'Intelligent cyber-physical system for UAV navigation under enemy EW'. Journal article fusing IMU data with optical-flow cameras via an EKF to hold position without any external radio signal, with a comparison of sparse (Lucas-Kanade), dense (Farneback) and learned (RAFT) optical flow.
nodes.kt: Side-by-side of LK, Farneback and RAFT for UAV flow is a handy reference EKF remains the default fusion choice in Ukrainian applied work Framed explicitly around full loss of external RF

nodes.s: English: 'UAV control and navigation system'. KPI authors describe an ArduPilot-based control and navigation architecture intended to keep working under EW: protected GPS module, inertial navigation, backup channels, and ArduPilot code modifications including pseudo-random frequency reassignment for the link.
nodes.kt: Ukrainian practice modifies ArduPilot rather than writing autopilots from scratch Link resilience (frequency agility) is treated together with navigation resilience System-level description; limited quantitative evaluation

nodes.n: Комбіноване керування безпілотними літальними апаратами в умовах радіоелектронної боротьби
nodes.s: English: 'Combined UAV control under electronic warfare'. Lviv Polytechnic article proposing a fiber-optic outbound leg plus anti-jam radio return leg, EO/IR fusion, and GNSS-free navigation with visual-inertial and lidar odometry corrected by baro and magnetometer, switched by a deterministic state machine. Reports prototype results over a 40 km mission (author figures: drift under 0.7%, 96% success over 50 runs).
nodes.kt: Mixed fiber + radio links appear as an EW-resilience pattern in Ukrainian research Deterministic mode switching between nav sources is emphasised Numbers are self-reported prototype results

nodes.n: Шляхи підвищення стійкості управління безпілотним літальним апаратом у завадовій обстановці
nodes.s: English: 'Ways to increase UAV control resilience in a jamming environment'. Survey-style article from the National Guard Academy: optical/landmark navigation, hybrid GPS+optics, lidar, wideband data links, swarm concepts and adaptive signal processing as resilience levers.
nodes.kt: Readable Ukrainian-language map of the resilience options considered by practitioners Lists landmark-based optical navigation systems as a key direction Survey, not new results

nodes.n: Помехи в глобальных навигационных спутниковых системах
nodes.s: English: 'Interference in global navigation satellite systems'. Habr article by a developer of interference-resistant receivers: why GNSS is below the noise floor, receiver structure (front end, 1-2 bit sampling, per-satellite correlator channels), narrowband vs wideband jamming and spoofing, and their effect on code/carrier tracking loops.
nodes.kt: Clear receiver-level explanation of how jamming breaks tracking loops Low-bit quantization trades SNR for simpler correlators, which matters under jamming Anti-jam methods were deferred to a part 2

nodes.s: English: 'GPS: jammers, spoofing and vulnerabilities'. Early Russian-language overview: how spoofing gradually walks a receiver off, the 2013 UT Austin yacht demonstration, consumer jammers sold in Russia, lab results on car jammers, and proposed defenses. The comment thread adds practitioner views (TERCOM as a GPS backup, antenna shielding limits).
nodes.kt: Gradual pull-off is the core spoofing technique Cheap personal jammers were already widespread years before 2022 Comments are a source of practitioner folklore, not verified data

nodes.s: English: 'SDR GPS receiver on a microcontroller'. Builds a real-time software GPS receiver on an STM32F4 (later ESP32) fed with 1-bit samples from a MAX2769 front end: XOR-based correlation, table bit-sums, four time-multiplexed channels with DLL/PLL, navigation decoding, RTCM 3 pseudorange output and on-chip RTKLIB positioning (author reports ~80 m indoors).
nodes.kt: A GPS receiver can run on a commodity MCU without FPGA Exposes the tracking loops that interference attacks Good hands-on companion to receiver-theory articles

nodes.s: English: 'High-precision GNSS RTK navigation'. Hands-on review of the u-blox ZED-F9P: tracing letters and spinning the antenna on a carousel to visualise RTK Fixed track quality. Comments add practical limits (lower RTK rate with more constellations, LoRa correction links, urban canyon dropouts).
nodes.kt: Simple visual tests (carousel, letters) expose RTK fix quality without survey gear RTK output rate drops with the number of constellations Comment thread has DIY base-station experience

nodes.n: RTKLib - Сантиметровая точность GPS/ГЛОНАСС в пост-обработке
nodes.s: English: 'RTKLIB: centimeter-level GPS/GLONASS accuracy in post-processing'. Step-by-step base (rooftop) + rover logging with two raw-capable receivers and processing with STRSVR, RTKCONV and RTKPOST in kinematic mode; author reports fixed solutions for 97.3% of epochs.
nodes.kt: Complete RTKLIB post-processing walk-through in Russian GLONASS enabled alongside GPS Useful for building ground truth for nav experiments

nodes.n: Как я научил квадрокоптер возвращаться домой без GPS: алгоритм «верёвочной лестницы»
nodes.s: English: 'How I taught a quadcopter to return home without GPS: the rope-ladder algorithm'. Explains why integrating optical flow velocity drifts so that the drone ends up offset after return, and replaces it with stored keyframe 'rungs' matched on the way back. Habr blocked automated fetch, so author and date are not verified (year inferred from the companion repo, created July 2025); content summarised from search snippets and the repo README.
nodes.kt: Flow integration error accumulates; keyframe matching bounds it for return-home Teach-and-repeat is a pragmatic answer when only the way back matters

nodes.n: Уловки, подсмотренные у медоносных пчёл, помогают дронам возвращаться домой без GPS
nodes.s: English: 'Tricks borrowed from honeybees help drones return home without GPS'. Russian translation of a New Atlas piece on TU Delft's Bee-Nav: after a short exploratory flight capturing panoramas, a tiny network (3.4 KB indoors, 42 KB outdoors) estimates direction and distance home. Reported outdoor runs exceeded 600 m, with ~70% success in wind.
nodes.kt: Homing can be learned with kilobyte-size models Wind tilt degrades panoramic matching Shows Russian tech media tracking GNSS-free homing closely

nodes.n: Навигация без GPS, которая уже работает
nodes.s: English: 'Navigation without GPS that already works'. Overview of deployed or demonstrated non-GNSS methods: accelerometer-based subway positioning, a star-tracker drone prototype (Raspberry Pi 5, night only, ~4 km accuracy), quantum-magnetometer map matching (AQNav), quantum accelerometers, and barometric tunnel detection.
nodes.kt: Broad menu of alternative PNT methods with honest limits (night-only, km-level) Magnetic anomaly navigation is presented as the most mature quantum-sensing use

nodes.n: Навигация квадрокоптера с использованием монокулярного зрения
nodes.s: English: 'Quadcopter navigation using monocular vision'. Walk-through of monocular navigation on a Parrot AR.Drone: building an obstacle map from a single camera and correcting the trajectory.
nodes.kt: Early Russian-language introduction to monocular VO/SLAM on a toy platform Scale ambiguity and obstacle mapping are the central difficulties

nodes.n: Технология коррекции навигационных параметров БПЛА в условиях отсутствия сигналов спутниковой навигации с использованием методов оптической одометрии
nodes.s: English: 'Technology for correcting UAV navigation parameters without satellite signals using optical odometry'. Short competition paper from Russia's state aviation systems institute on correcting micro-multicopter navigation with optical odometry when GNSS is absent, framed by autonomy-level roadmaps.
nodes.kt: Shows GNSS-denied optical odometry was an institutional priority in Russia by 2016 Framed around small multicopters

nodes.n: Навигация по снимкам местности на основе сопоставления глубоких признаков и визуальной одометрии
nodes.s: English: 'Terrain relative navigation based on deep feature template matching and visual odometry'. Belarusian journal article: self-supervised (triplet-loss) deep features for matching UAV views to satellite patches across season, weather and lighting; visual odometry bridges featureless forest/field areas; an entropy filter plus path planning steers flights over feature-rich terrain.
nodes.kt: Plan the route over informative terrain instead of only improving the matcher Self-supervised features avoid labelled cross-season data VO bridges texture-poor segments between absolute fixes

nodes.n: Разработка алгоритма абсолютной визуально-инерциальной навигации беспилотных воздушных судов
nodes.s: English: 'Development of an absolute visual-inertial navigation algorithm for unmanned aircraft'. Russian preprint comparing absolute navigation methods against preloaded satellite maps and proposing a season-invariant SIFT keypoint matching approach corrected by INS, optimised for real time and evaluated on real flight data against GNSS reference. Year inferred from the PDF (references run to 2025).
nodes.kt: Absolute map-based fixes + INS is the mainstream Russian approach too Seasonal invariance is the named key problem Evaluated against GNSS reference on real flights

nodes.n: Алгоритм планирования маршрута БПЛА в условиях недостатка визуальных ориентиров
nodes.s: English: 'UAV route planning algorithm under a shortage of visual landmarks'. Journal article (Analysis and Data Processing Systems, vol. 94 no. 2) on planning routes so a video-navigation system keeps seeing enough landmarks when satellite navigation is unavailable.
nodes.kt: Navigation-aware path planning: route choice is a resilience lever Pairs naturally with map-matching VPS that fails over texture-poor areas

nodes.n: GPS complex interference models and the possible antispoofing protective measures
nodes.s: Belarusian conference paper (BSUIR, 'Information radiosystems and radiotechnologies 2022'; English title, Russian-language repository) on GPS interference models and possible anti-spoofing protections. Only the metadata was checked; conclusions not verified.
nodes.kt: Example of the Belarusian academic literature on spoofing defences Metadata only verified

nodes.s: English: 'An ambiguous signal'. Russian-language independent journalism on GNSS interference over Europe: cites an EU states' report to ICAO (about 123k affected flights in Jan-Apr 2025), Estonian, Lithuanian and Polish statistics, jamming vs spoofing mechanics, and trackers such as gpsjam.org and gpswise.aero.
nodes.kt: Interference has spilled far beyond the front line into civil aviation Spoofing shows up as position jumps of hundreds of km and inconsistent instrument readings Public trackers are the main open data sources cited

nodes.s: English: 'Optical Flow navigation - Clover docs'. Russian-language official documentation for enabling downward-camera optical flow on the Clover quadcopter (requires a laser rangefinder), the ROS topics involved and the PX4 EKF2/flow parameters to set, plus tuning advice. Year approximate (docs are continuously updated).
nodes.kt: Concrete parameter list for optical-flow-only position hold in PX4 Rangefinder is mandatory for metric flow Max horizontal speed is limited in flow mode

nodes.s: English: 'Navigation by marker map - Clover docs'. Russian documentation for flying with a map of ArUco markers (floor or ceiling), publishing the resulting pose to the flight controller as a vision position estimate, and commanding flights in the marker-map frame. Year approximate.
nodes.kt: Fiducial maps are the fastest way to get GNSS-free indoor positioning for a demo Shows the generic pattern: external pose => VPE => autopilot EKF

nodes.s: Russian-language page of COEX's international open-source flying-robotics contest built on the Clover platform: format (teams develop open-source projects over months with expert feedback), final standings and links to projects, including a radio-navigation system entry.
nodes.kt: Open-source requirement makes finalist repos reusable Long-format contest, unlike 48 h hackathons Navigation and swarm entries recur across editions

nodes.n: Integrity monitoring for alt-PNT: solution-separation FDE, protection levels and a Stanford diagram
nodes.s: A stdlib-only simulated UAV flight with INS, VIO-like velocity, intermittent visual-geolocalization fixes (repetitive-texture outliers, map-misregistration bias, dropouts over water), optional coarse MagNav-like fixes and a GNSS that is jammed and then spoofed. An 8-state EKF with chi-square innovation gating feeds a solution-separation bank that detects, excludes or (with only two sources) alerts and resolves by dead-reckoning consistency, computes horizontal protection levels against an alert limit, and reports MI/HMI, availability, time-to-alert and an ASCII/SVG Stanford diagram. A monitor-off negative control shows the misleading-information events the monitor removes. v2 (altpnt_v2.py, calibration.py) extracts measured error models from sibling samples (OpenVINS / KISS-ICP / nadir-VO heading and scale, real visual-geoloc availability, bias and residuals, TRN confidence-vs-error), adds heading and scale states, a DeCleene/Rife-style Gaussian overbound with a bias term, per-source fault priors and TRN measurement covariance from particle spread, and shows that v1's zero-MI result fails under measured models (MI* 0 => 8901 of 12000 epochs) while v2 restores zero MI at 13-26 % availability instead of 41.7 %.
nodes.v: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: default run, --magnav, --no-gnss, --al-sweep, 20-seed Monte Carlo for 8 configurations, CSV and SVG writers (SVG rendered with macOS qlmanage and inspected); 15 unit tests pass (python3 -m unittest), and the detection tests were confirmed to fail with detection disabled. Synthetic data only; no real flight log or indexed repo was run. v2: ran with python3.14.7 and 3.12.14 stdlib on 2026-11-06: calibration.py --check reproduces calibration.json from the committed sibling results; 20-seed Monte Carlo over 29 world/filter rows (182 s), v1 rows identical to the v1 table; 10 v2 unit tests pass. Error models are measured on short real runs (27-197 s) and replayed over a synthetic 600 s flight; correlation times and fault-rate priors for GNSS are assumptions.

nodes.n: ArduPilot EKF3 source-set switch under GPS denial
nodes.s: Flies ArduCopter SITL on GPS, switches EKF3 to an external-nav source set (SITL vicon) with MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET, cuts simulated GPS, flies a 15 m leg, then restores it. A --no-switch contrast run shows the EKF losing position and the EKF failsafe landing the copter. EKF_STATUS_REPORT, GPS fix and local position are logged throughout; the flag decoder is stdlib with unit tests.
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06 against ArduCopter Copter-4.6.3 SITL in Docker (samples/sitl-docker, linux/arm64) with pymavlink 2.4.50 on python3.12: source switch accepted, EKF kept POS_HORIZ_ABS with GPS fix_type 1 for 30 s and flew the 15 m leg; --no-switch lost position after ~6 s and triggered 'EKF Failsafe: changed to LAND Mode'. Output in README. ekf_flags.py tests (6) pass on python3.14.7. --switch-via rc not run.

nodes.n: Blind-flight bench: radar altimeter + Copernicus GLO-30 TRN, six navigators on one harness
nodes.s: Benchmark harness that reproduces the 2026 'Polyot vslepuyu' (Blind flight) hackathon case on four real GLO-30 windows (Khibiny mountains, Middle Urals, Yenisei taiga, the flat Moscow-region map area): 20 km simulated flights at a constant 1500 m baro level, a leading-edge radar altimeter with a 40 deg beam footprint, range noise, dropouts, outliers, baro bias and drift, map error and canopy, delivered as checksummed $GPGGA lines. Scores dead reckoning on the hints, our TERCOM baseline (core.tercom_fix from terrain-heightmap-pf) and our particle filter, each also against a precomputed beam-aware reference map, plus clean-room re-implementations (from README text only) of the GORIZONT multi-hypothesis tracker and the Gagarin MAD/NCC gated pipeline. Leaderboard of median/p95 error at 5/10/20 km, divergence rate, CPU and worst-step latency, and a one-impairment-at-a-time ablation.
nodes.v: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 on an Apple M2 Max: regions.py fetched the four GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS through terrain-heightmap-pf/fetch_dem.py; run_bench.py produced out/results.json and the leaderboard (80 flights x 10 navigators, 349 s wall) and --ablation produced out/ablation.md (144 flights x 6 navigators); two full runs gave identical error numbers for unchanged navigators. unittest: 10 passed in the venv; with plain python3 and no third-party packages 3 metric tests pass and 7 skip. Mutating error_at_distances (bisect_left => bisect_right) or the sign of the TERCOM correction makes a test fail. Flights, altimeter, baro error, map error and canopy are simulated with assumed parameters; the GORIZONT and Gagarin navigators are our re-implementations from their README text, not their code, and no team code was run.

nodes.n: Celestial fix: cedar-solve plate solving on real star images, then position from star elevations above an IMU vertical
nodes.s: Runs cedar-solve (tetra3 API, v0.6.0 on NumPy 2) lost-in-space on 40 real SkyView Mellinger cutouts with a known WCS (12 and 20 deg FOV, random pointing and roll) and on the 20 real camera frames shipped with cedar-solve, reporting solve rate, pointing/roll error against the WCS and runtime on an M2 Max. A stdlib Marcq St Hilaire least-squares solver turns star elevations above the gravity vertical into latitude/longitude; a Skyfield-truth Monte Carlo sweeps level bias, vibration, accelerometer bias, clock error, refraction and FOV, and confirms 1 arcmin of level error = about 1.85 km. The 8 ESA tetra3 frames (mount alt/az in the file names) give a crude real-data fix.
nodes.v: ran on 2026-11-06 with Python 3.12.14 (numpy 2.5.4, cedar-solve git tag v0.6.0 installed --no-deps, skyfield 1.55, astropy 8.0.2) on an Apple M2 Max: plate_solve_eval.py with and without --fov-hint, esa_mount_fix.py, position_fix_sim.py --runs 200; outputs in results/ and quoted in the README. Plate solving uses real images (SkyView Mellinger mosaic cutouts, reference = requested WCS; cedar-solve test frames, no reference). The position-fix budget is simulation with Skyfield truth; centroid noise, vibration and bias levels are stated assumptions. The ESA-frame position has no ground truth (capture site undocumented). 11 unittest tests pass in the venv; with plain Homebrew python3 10 pass and the Skyfield test skips. A planted Jacobian sign flip fails 4 tests. No real IMU, moving camera, lens distortion, ESA tetra3, Cedar-Detect or database generation was run.

nodes.n: C-UAS classifiers on public data: radar tracks (UAV vs bird) and DroneRF spectra
nodes.s: Two defensive drone-detection baselines on openly licensed recordings. Per-track kinematic and RCS features from the NRC Echodyne radar dataset feed gradient boosting and random forest for UAV vs bird, evaluated with session-grouped CV and a cross-site split. Welch band-power and burstiness features on a DroneRF subset give drone-vs-background detection and 4-class identification with segment-grouped and temporal splits. Radar detections can be emitted as unknown-affiliation rotor-UAS Cursor-on-Target via the mavlink-to-tak-cot builder.
nodes.v: Ran on 2026-11-06 with Python 3.12.14, scikit-learn 1.9.1 on an Apple M2 Max. Radar: 510 labelled tracks (379 BIRD, 131 UAV, 42 sessions); 5-fold GroupKFold by session HistGB balanced accuracy 0.928, AUC 0.964, UAV P/R 0.913/0.885; train Alma 2019 => test Laval 2020-21 balanced accuracy 0.90-0.92 on 89 tracks. DroneRF low-band subset (73 segments, 4 classes): detection balanced accuracy 0.977-0.994 on a temporal holdout, 4-class identification 0.94 GroupKFold / 0.85 temporal holdout. cuas_cot.py produced a-u-A-M-H-Q / how m-a CoT for one Laval session (31 of 110 tracks reported: 9 labelled UAV, 1 HUMAN, 21 unlabelled). 11 unit tests on synthetic fixtures pass; mutations of the vertical axis and the R1/R2 session merge fail 4. Not verified: DroneRF sample rate, radar site geometry (CoT positions are placeholders), the H band and other flight modes, ATAK rendering. Each DroneRF class in the subset is one recording session, so identification numbers include session effects.

nodes.n: Dismounted foot-mounted INS: stdlib 15-state ZUPT EKF on the real pyshoe hallway data, cross-checked against pyshoe, with corridor heading, UWB and TAK output
nodes.s: A stdlib-only error-state EKF (position, velocity, attitude, accel and gyro bias) with SHOE, ARED, AMVD and MBGTD stance detectors, run on all 36 real foot-mounted IMU trials of the UTIAS pyshoe hallway dataset (214.6 m out-and-back route, surveyed floor markers) and compared with pyshoe's own INS on the same trials. It adds corridor-direction heading constraints, a floor-height constraint, simulated UWB ranges with NLOS outliers, and shows on the raw magnetometer logs why compass heading fails indoors. Positions go out as CoT blue-force events via samples/mavlink-to-tak-cot/cot.py and as navdash/1 tracks for templates/demo-dashboard.
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06 with python3.14.7 stdlib on all 36 real pyshoe hallway trials (downloaded from the UTIAS FTP): default 15-state filter 2.35 m mean ARMSE / 1.30 % final error of the 214.6 m route / 3.63 m mean max error vs pyshoe's own INS 2.51 m / 1.49 % / 3.92 m on the same trials (pyshoe 6bbc4df run in a Python 3.11 venv with numpy 1.23.5, scipy 1.10.1; LSTM/SVM detectors stubbed). Stdlib SHOE labels match pyshoe on 100 % of samples and the 9-state mode reproduces pyshoe to 2.7 mm at every marker. Corridor heading + floor + simulated UWB (inflated covariance + NIS gate) gives 1.07 m / 0.83 % / 2.80 m on held-out markers; magnetometer heading from the real raw logs is off by a median 14-40 deg and makes all 6 tested trials 2-9x worse. UWB ranges, anchors and NLOS are simulated, only at marker epochs; CoT/navdash export generated and parsed but not rendered in a browser or sent to a live TAK server. 18 unit tests pass; 4 planted mutations each fail at least one.

nodes.n: End-to-end GNSS-denied visual navigation on one real flight: nadir VO + DINOv2 retrieval + LightGlue fixes + multi-frame voting + altpnt integrity (VPAIR)
nodes.s: Chains four sibling samples by import on the real VPAIR light-aircraft flight (199 nadir frames, 8.98 km, ~320 m AGL): attitude-aided nadir VO (with and without a 2 deg heading error), every frame DINOv2 GeM top-5 retrieval over VPAIR's orthophoto renders (other capture time, leave-own-render-out, map thinned to 45/180/360 m tile spacing, plus 200 distractors), ALIKED+LightGlue fine matching with an inlier gate, single-frame vs multi-frame voting fixes (VO carries earlier candidates forward), fused by the altpnt-integrity v2 EKF with heading/scale states and no gate, chi-square gate or solution-separation FDE. Reports error vs distance, fix availability, false fixes produced and fused, protection level and HMI, runtime per frame on M2, and exports navdash/1 for templates/demo-dashboard.
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06 on Apple M2 Max (Python 3.12.14, torch 2.15.0 MPS, LightGlue 5a650c4, DINOv2 ViT-S/14) on the VPAIR Zenodo sample: frontend.py twice (recorded yaw and yaw +2 deg, 231 s each for strides 1/4/8), run_fusion.py 148 configurations in 16 s, screenshot.sh headless Chrome at frames 100 and 198. After GNSS loss (8.53 km): VO only with +2 deg heading 271 m final / 156 m RMS (57.7 m final with recorded yaw); VO + single-frame strict-gate fixes 4.8 m RMS, 19 m max, 149/188 frames fixed, 0 false; 360 m map spacing 9.7 m RMS, 47 % fixed. Loose match gate without the filter gate fused 15 false fixes (errors to 65 km, 151 HMI epochs); voting and the chi-square gate each removed all false fixes in every run. Solution-separation PL median 1.25 km (1.6 % available): one absolute source cannot be protected. 0.73 s per frame. Tests: venv 15 pass; plain python3 5 pass, 10 skip. Limits: one 199-frame flight, map renders posed from the same GNSS/INS truth, map tiles on the flown track, no IMU, VO error model fitted on this flight.

nodes.n: License-clean drone frame to orthophoto geolocalization (ALIKED / DISK / SIFT + LightGlue)
nodes.s: Drone frame => NAIP orthophoto => lat/lon using only permissively licensed parts: ALIKED (BSD-3), DISK and LightGlue weights (Apache-2.0), OpenCV SIFT and MAGSAC (Apache-2.0), rasterio, public-domain NAIP from Microsoft Planetary Computer and CC0 eBee frames from OpenDroneMap. Generates synthetic frames with known truth (rotation, scale, perspective, photometric change, cross-season source) and runs real UAV frames with EXIF GPS as truth. Measured error and CPU runtime per frame are in the README.
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06 on Apple M2 Max CPU (torch 2.15.0, Python 3.12.14): download_data.py fetched NAIP 2023/2019 windows from Planetary Computer and 5 CC0 eBee frames; run_eval.py on 20 synthetic frames per case: same-map median error 0.10-0.11 m for ALIKED/DISK/SIFT+LightGlue (0.28-2.8 s/frame), cross-season 1.9-4.8 m with 13-20/20 fixes; real eBee frames vs NAIP: 1 fix out of 5 (ALIKED, 2019 map, tight prior, 11.0 m error), 0/5 in all other configs. Numbers and logs in README.

nodes.n: GNSS/INS EKF through a GNSS outage and a spoofing walk-off
nodes.s: A stdlib-only 2D loosely-coupled GNSS/INS EKF (8 states, hand-written matrix helpers) on a synthetic vehicle with biased, noisy 100 Hz IMU and 1 Hz GNSS. It compares INS-only, EKF, EKF with a chi-square innovation gate, and a gated EKF that latches into holdover through a 60 s outage and a slowly walking spoofed offset. A sweep shows that the gate catches fast walk-offs but misses slow ones.
nodes.v: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (default run and --sweep), output shown in README. filterpy_crosscheck.py re-ran both with filterpy 2.0.0's ExtendedKalmanFilter doing covariance, innovation and Joseph-form update (Python 3.12.14) and reproduced the tables to the printed 0.1 m; inflating R 100x in the filterpy path changed them, so that path is live. gnss-ins-sim, KF-GINS and GTSAM were not run.

nodes.n: GNSS interference monitor from u-blox telemetry and ADS-B NACp
nodes.s: A stdlib heuristic scorer turns per-epoch receiver telemetry (C/N0 across SVs, AGC, CW jamming indicator, clock, position and velocity, receiver spoofing/jamming flags, and the navigation data the receiver decoded) into jamming and spoofing scores. Instantaneous rules are joined by power CUSUMs on the median per-SV C/N0 deviation and on AGC that catch staircase power changes, by position consistency against the best reference available (IMU/odometry/static velocity, else the receiver's own reported velocity integrated over a 10 s window so normal driving stays consistent, else a constant-velocity prior), Doppler velocity and clock-rate CUSUMs, a velocity-jump bound, and lost fix as its own alert class. Each reference learns only while its own detector is quiet; the per-SV C/N0 baseline is robust (clipped innovations), keeps learning through spoofing sub-alerts so a recovered sky is re-learned, and can drift at a bounded rate while frozen. An ephemeris module decodes GPS LNAV subframes from UBX-RXM-SFRBX and flags SVs whose decoded orbit/clock disagrees with an independent IGS broadcast file. Alerts latch until explicit clear conditions hold and every alert carries value, threshold, unit and evidence. A pyubx2 adapter feeds it from UBX NAV-PVT/SAT/STATUS/CLOCK, MON-RF and SEC-SIG; eval_real.py scores it per slot and detector on the real Jammertest 2024 VAARA logs with a tune/holdout split. A second module applies the GPSJam percentage method to readsb aircraft.json NACp for area-level maps.
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06. Tests: 53 (30 scorer, 12 real-data defect regressions, 6 ephemeris, 6 area map, 1 UBX replay) OK on /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 3.14.7 without packages (1 skipped: pyubx2) and OK with pyubx2 1.4.1 on Python 3.13.15. The defect regressions fail on the previous scorer (git dae8229) for driving, position pull, velocity jump, step drop after recovery, C/N0 and AGC staircase and spoofed ephemeris. Mutation check: 10 of 12 single mutations of the new logic fail 1-3 tests; references frozen by any alarm and the power term of the clear rule are not covered. Real data: eval_real.py on the 7 VAARA u-blox logs (13 h, 20 attack slots + 1 quiet), 4 parameters chosen on 3 tuning logs, reported on all 7 with a 4-log holdout: the quiet slot went from 98 % alerting (constant-velocity pos_drift) to 0 %, pos_drift false-alert epochs 10220 => 275, driving alarm time 86 % => 28 %, and every attack slot is detected by a C/N0 detector (before, without the latched pos_drift, 4 slots incl. the 2.4.3 staircase were missed). The ephemeris check, against IGS BRDC from the BKG mirror, decoded 267 GPS sets with 0 parity failures and flagged spoofer ephemerides (276 km to 53 000 km off) in 7 of the 8 spoofing slots, never on the jamming-only days. Synthetic: 20 h soak per reference mode 0 / 0 / 17 alert epochs (cv-prior / doppler / external static); a drag that moves position and Doppler together is not detected without an external reference (by design, drag table in README). gnss-signal-chain GNSS-SDR epochs rescored: clean 0 alerts, overpower/jam-then-spoof alert at attack onset (power CUSUM), drag-off alerts at +6 s on its power step but pos_drift only with --ref-vel 0,0. Not verified: live u-blox receiver, AGC/MON-RF on real data (VAARA has none), Galileo/GLONASS/BeiDou ephemeris checking, real readsb feed, any OSNMA processing.

nodes.n: Public CORS RINEX to SPP vs RTK with RTKLIB demo5 and gnss_lib_py
nodes.s: Downloads one day of public NOAA NGS CORS RINEX for a rover/base pair 30 km apart, runs RTKLIB demo5 rnx2rtkp in single-point and kinematic RTK modes with exact CLI flags, and scores both against the stations' published ITRF2020 coordinates (propagated for plate motion) in ENU. An optional gnss_lib_py weighted-least-squares SPP covers the same data in Python, after converting RINEX 2.11 to 3.
nodes.v: ran on 2026-11-06 on real NOAA NGS CORS data (P730 rover, P731 base, 2024-04-09 12:00-14:00 GPST, GPS only, 241 epochs): RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 built in Docker (docker/Dockerfile) gave SPP E/N/U rms 0.62/1.24/1.02 m and RTK 0.084/0.055/0.071 m with 97% fix, scored by compare_pos.py against the propagated ITRF2020 sheet; gnss_lib_py 1.1.0 WLS (glp_spp.py, after fixing a GPST-vs-UTC epoch tag, per-chunk ephemeris selection and transmit-time SV states) gave 0.65/1.28/1.10 m. compare_pos.py's 4 unit tests ran with python3.14.7. Not verified: other days/stations, multi-GNSS, PPP, antenna phase-centre models, a native (non-Docker) RTKLIB build.

nodes.n: File-based GNSS signal chain: gps-sdr-sim => GNSS-SDR => spoofing/jamming scorer
nodes.s: A Docker (arm64/amd64) testbed that never transmits: gps-sdr-sim synthesizes GPS L1 C/A IQ for a static receiver from the shipped 2022-01-01 broadcast ephemeris, a numpy mixer adds noise, a second spoofer stream (power offset, time offset, ramp) and/or a jamming burst, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 processes each file into PVT, RINEX and a PVT dump, and an adapter feeds 1 Hz epochs (position, Doppler velocity, HDOP, clock, per-SV C/N0, plus no-fix epochs when PVT stops) into the gnss-interference-monitor scorer, with and without a static velocity reference, and reports time-to-detect, silent windows and false alarms. Four scenarios: clean, unaligned overpower, jam-then-spoof, and a code/carrier-aligned drag-off that walks the fix 978 m away.
nodes.v: Ran end to end twice on 2026-11-06 with Docker arm64 on Apple Silicon (second run: image rebuilt, ./run.sh 319 s): gps-sdr-sim commit 28ca29a, GNSS-SDR 0.0.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 package), RTKLIB demo5 v2.5.1 rnx2rtkp. Real outputs of the second run are in out/ and quoted in the README. Clean: median horizontal error 2.9 m, 0 alarm epochs in both reference modes. Drag-off: PVT captured to 977.8 m off truth; the old scorer alerted at t=138 (run 1: t=67 with a 43 s silent stretch), the new scorer at t=89 (constant-velocity prior) / t=86 (static reference), 9 / 6 s after the drag began, with no silent epoch after the first alert. Unaligned overpower and jam-then-spoof caused a GNSS-SDR PVT outage, not a capture; the old scorer gave 1 and 0 alert epochs, the new one latched a lost-fix alarm at t=81 and t=76 and held it to the end. GNSS-SDR runs are not bit-identical. Not validated against a hardware receiver; the AGC input is a file-power proxy; the static velocity reference is ideal.

nodes.n: Golden demo: GPS drag (position-only or coherent) on an ArduCopter SITL AUTO mission, integrity monitoring with solution separation + protection level, real visual geolocalization, EKF3 switch to ExternalNav, Monte Carlo, dashboard replay
nodes.s: One command flies ArduCopter 4.6.3 SITL in Docker on a survey and drags its GPS east. v1 uses SIM_GPS_GLITCH (position only), simulated visual geoloc and navapp's windowed chi-square test. v2 injects the GPS from a pymavlink companion as GPS_INPUT so the drag can be coherent (position + velocity), takes visual-geoloc fixes from real ALIKED+LightGlue matching of frames rendered from a 2019 NAIP orthophoto against a 2023 NAIP map (replayed from a 425-node table, or live), runs a solution-separation FDE bank with a horizontal protection level ported from samples/altpnt-integrity plus a GNSS-vs-VIO velocity test, and on alarm commands MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET 2 with the companion's GNSS-free reference as ExternalNav. A 52-flight Monte Carlo (seed x rate 0.3/1/3 m/s x spoof type, monitor vs shadow) reports time-to-detect, misses, false alarms and deviation with and without the monitor; an experiment localises v1's EKF lane switching to the SITL GPS path. Logs convert to navdash/1 for templates/demo-dashboard (PL vs AL ring in v2).
nodes.v: Ran 2026-11-06 on Apple Silicon (linux/arm64 Docker, Copter-4.6.3 SITL image from samples/sitl-docker, pymavlink 2.4.50, Python 3.12). v1 (one run per mode, seed 7): chi-square alarm 9.4 s after onset, max cross-track deviation 7.6 m with the monitor vs 75.0 m without. v2 reference (coherent 1 m/s, replayed real geoloc): velocity-test alarm 3.0 s after onset, 6.8 m vs 75.0 m, EKF GPS_GLITCHING never set. v2 Monte Carlo, 52 flights in 1201 s wall (3 parallel SITLs, speedup 3): ss+vel detected 24/24 monitor flights with 0 pre-onset false alarms and 0/4 false alarms without spoof; median TTD 45/22.5/6.2 s (position 0.3/1/3 m/s) and 37.4/2.8/1 s (coherent); v1 chi-square false-alarmed in 4/4 no-spoof flights with real geoloc. Real geoloc table: 246/425 frames fixed, median 3.3 m. One live-matching flight completed (68% fixes after AUTO, ~3.5 s per match). Lane-switch experiment: 4-6 switches with SITL GPS, 0 with injected GPS (2 seeds each); mechanism not found. 17 unit tests pass. VIO is truth plus noise; frames are rendered nadir from a real orthophoto; amd64 and ArduPilot 4.7+ not tested.

nodes.n: Golden demo on PX4 v1.17 SIH: coherent GPS drag via HIL_GPS, integrity monitor (SS + PL, GNSS-vs-VIO velocity), EKF2 switch from GNSS to external vision, comparison with ArduPilot, dashboard replay
nodes.s: The samples/golden-demo v2 scenario on PX4 v1.17.0 SIH in Docker. A pymavlink companion (a subclass of the golden-demo companion; monitor, spoof model and replayed real visual geoloc imported unchanged) feeds the only GPS as MAVLink HIL_GPS (MAV_USEHILGPS=1, SIH sensor_gps_sim off; v1.17 has no GPS_INPUT handler), drags it east at 1 m/s from t=25 s, streams its GNSS-free VIO + visual-geoloc reference as ODOMETRY at 10 Hz (EKF2 needs EV samples < 200 ms apart), and on the first alarm sets EKF2_GPS_CTRL=0 then EKF2_EV_CTRL=5 so EKF2 resets onto external vision. Aux global position was not used because v1.17 has no MAVLink path into it (DDS only). Monitor vs no-monitor flights, a 20-flight sweep, navdash/1 output for templates/demo-dashboard, and a side-by-side with the ArduPilot reference.
